product_title: Suzuki Boulevard Embroidered Mesh Motorcycle Riding Jacket Black
review_headline: High Quality materials and construction, best summer jacket I've owned.
review_body: Nearly 1,000 miles logged with this jacket this summer, I wear it every time I get on the bike. Great summer protective jacket. Thankfully I haven't hit the ground in this yet, and can't comment about performance in the moment of need, but this is a very stylish, well made jacket, of very tough mesh, and high-quality embroidery and nylon for the reflective striping and "Boulevard" text. Removable rain insert is great as well. A lot of hooks and snaps involved to get it in/out, but solid and waterproof once in. Without the rain insert, the mesh allows for fantastic ventilation even on the hottest summer days - feels like I'm riding just in a T-shirt. Pads at elbows, shoulders, and back feel solid, substantial, and correctly placed, but not uncomfortable while wearing. I'm 5'10 and 210 pounds, barrel chested, and ordered the XXL, fits wonderfully - Stops right at my waist in front, padding overhangs a bit in back, and sleeves fall to halfway between my wrist and knuckles (I like longer sleeves). I'm usually an XL in jackets, but went one size up with good results.

review_headline: Perfect Fit - Solid piece of equipment from Curt

In addition to the socket wrench, you will also need a rubber mallet to bang this gently thing into place. I did not remove anything (Heat shields, etc.) or loosen the spare tire either, you just have to angle it up and knock it into place. Yes - this will nudge up against the heat shields when you install it, not a big deal at all.

The hitch is tucked up right below the bottom of the bumper and it does not hang down at all. This class III hitch will definitely handle my bike rack and a trailer if I need to. Great investment for my ride - Highly recommend for anyone who is considering adding this.

product_title: [Pre-sale promotion]HausBell®Brand New Car Air Station Inflator -Electric Air Compressor Portable Air Compressor 9A 12V DC 30L/MIN Max Pressure 250PSI
review_body: The Hausbell 12 volt tire pump works great, I have purchase several 12 volt pumps over the years and this pump ranks right up there with the best pumps I have owned. They are really small and If you have a big truck tire like I have to fill up takes some time to do. Not taking anything away from this pump at all. My 110 volt air compressor takes about 3 minutes to air my big truck tire up. I have a 1 ton truck and my tires require 70 to 80 lbs of air pressure in each tire. A lot of the gas stations we have around here won't even get my tire to 70 lbs.Caution these air compressors will over heat in high temps after they run for 3 or 4 minutes. You should shut it off for a while and allow it to cool down. Every pump I have had does the same thing ! Due to their size, the air pump has to work so hard to build air pressure that it does get very hot and in some case will even blow your fuse on your cigarette lighter or aux. outlet. Again let me state it is not just this air compressor it is with all brands of the small 12 volt compressors. For cars and regular trucks this will air your tires back up to 40 lbs with no problem. But with a bigger tire that requires a lot more air pressure you will need to take more time to get your tire up to pressure, due to the fact that they will get hot. In that case you just have to take your time and when it gets hot shut it off and allow it to cool off for a short amount of time. They are really made to be used in emergency situations where you have no other means of airing up your tire. I live on a farm a I am constantly having flat tires. This pump works great for that kind of situation. All in all I would say this is a good air compressor and would recommend it to any one looking for a emergency air compressor. I  am a Amazon reviewer and received this at a discounted price for my honest review. I am just like you and depend on other peoples input and reviews to decide if I am going to purchase an item. With that said, I would buyanother Hausbell 12 volt air compressor it works great for cars, and regular trucks, bikes, mowers ect. But don't think you are going to fill up a tractor tire with ANY small 12 volt pump when you need 100 pounds of air  pressure in a short amount of time. Because they will get hot and you will need to shut them down and allow them to cool off. I am not saying that it can't fill a tire to 100 to 150 lbs. of air, but your not going to just turn the pump on and walk off and expect it to fill a tire without over heating and blowing a fuse or burning up the compressor. Special thanks to Hausbell for allowing me to review their air compressor ! I think it is a great pump at a great price. Hope I have answered any concerns you may have had about this or any other small 12 volt compressor. Thanks.

product_title: Anker PowerCore Jump Starter 600 (High 600A Peak Current Car Battery Jump Starter and 15000mAh Portable Charger with Built-in Flashlight and Safety Protection) Perfect for 5L Gas and 3L Diesel Engines
review_headline: Solid build, 200A more peak current than similar compact jump starters.
review_body:
I think it's a product worth having in your car for those just in case situations for daily use. And if you're on a road trip, then it's upgraded from worth having to must have. It really covers a lot of functions in this device.
First of all, it's a jump starter. Most other compact jump starters in the market delivers 400A max peak current. They work for sure, work pretty well actually. With this one, it delivers 200A more to a whopping 600As. It gives you a lot more cushion room in situations like cold weather, battery completely dead, or handling bigger engines. I test it with V4 2.4L, V6 3.2L and V8 5.0L. In all cases, left the car light on overnight, comes morning I turn the lights off and confirm battery won't start the car. Then wait for about 30 mins for battery to build up some surface charge on its own before I tried to jump start with Anker jump starter. All 3 cars started successfully. I'm in NoCal, temp is about 65F in the morning.
2. It's got a small flash light. Not much, but it's good to have and its LED. I imagine in emergency situations, with its 15000mah built in battery, it will last this led light for a long long time.
3. 2 Power IQ power on the side up to 2.1A/ port. When needed, you'll have some back up charging power, though I'd recommend for hiking or other outings, get one of those solar chargers.
4. Anker was nice enough to include a car charge adapter, a wall adapter as well as a micro USB cable. Essentially all the accessories you need is included in the package which is kinda nice.
If you're a road warrior, college kid with a not so reliable car, definitely get one.

review_headline: 3.5 stars - added to truck for extra reverse lights; very bright, some RF
review_body:
More like 3.5 stars. Bright lights - added under rear bumper & spliced into my reverse lights for added visibility when backing my truck up at night. They do a good job for this - had to angle them down as they are very bright & I didn't want to take a chance on blinding anyone behind me. I did use silicone caulk around the entire light's joints, screw holes, etc. to ensure no water would get in; no problems so far - still dry. I do get some RF interference (esp. 105-106 MHz on radio) when I put the truck in reverse and these lights kick on. I'll look to install ferrite chokes on the wires to see if that clears up the issue.
Otherwise, they work great right out of the box - not sure if I needed to silicone seal them, but the added protection against moisture seemed prudent.

review_headline: If you have the OEM BMW top rack, look elsewhere.
review_body: I bought all four of the Bestem bags for the K1200LT (saddlebag and top case liners, and this top rack bag), and while the three liner bags have worked out fantastic - especially considering price - this top rack bag is unfortunately completely useless in my application.  If your LT has the OEM BMW top case rack (plastic with a chrome top and LED third brake light) this bag has an obvious and fundamental build flaw for that application: The four attachment straps are all much too long to go through the top rack and then attach to their Velcro attachment points on the bag body.  It is not that they are slightly long; it is that to use the bag on the OEM top rack you will either need to be content with using the bag's existing attachment straps and having the bag be extremely loose (like stick your arms in the gap loose), or you will need an outside form of attachment by way of a strap or bungee (kind of defeating the purpose altogether of buying a made to fit top case bag).  Please see the pictures attached illustrating the fatal flaw.  One shows the over-length the straps have when laced through the OEM rack and pulled taut, the other shows how much play there is between rack and bag when the Velcro on the straps and the bag body are pressed exactly on top of one another.

product_title: BESTEK Portable 300A Peak Current Car Jump Starter External Battery Charger with 5400mAh Capacity, Built-in LED Flashlight, and USB Charging Port
review_headline: BESTEK BTCS99 Portable Power Bank Kit - 5400 mAh battery - 300A vehicle battery boost - Charge phones & tablets - Recommended
review_body:
This BESTEK BTCS99 power bank is designed for maximum portability; it's not a big, rugged, powerful, beast given its 5400mAh capacity and 300 peak amp boost, but it easily fits in your glove box or center console. The unit is just 5 inches long, 3 inches wide, about 3/4 of an inch thick, and weighs in only at 7.4 ounces (per our postal scale).

The battery and all of its accessories could fit into a quart-size ziploc bag... but the manufacturer did not include a carry bag or pouch to put the battery and its accessories in. That's a shame.

This device could be an emergency power kit for many needs on an excursion or camping trip. Recommended if you are looking for lightweight battery back up power for your trip in the urban jungle, especially if in a smaller vehicle like our Saturn Vue (2.2L in-line 4 cylinder engine).

Nice concept; a portable 5400 mAh power bank with a USB power port (2.1A) allowing us to plug in a device's USB cable as needed, ports and cables for a variety of other electronic devices (tablets, laptops, etc...), and short alligator clip cables to connect to the car battery. Good tool for its size, functionality and price.

Operating this unit to charge a cell phone is a breeze -- just plug your cable (or the supplied micro-USB cable) into the USB port and do your thing. If you need the jumper cables, just open the rubber flap covering the port on the end of the unit (next to the standard USB port), plug in the jumper cables, and then connect the cable to your battery as directed in the user guide. The cables are fairly short so do be careful when using them.

The storage capacity of this battery is good and the charging times we experienced were fine. We tested it with an HTC Droid DNA and it charged quickly, about 3/4% per minute (45% per hour) using the 2.1A port... much better rate than we get from our wall outlet adapters.

The little flashlight on the back panel does not emit a great deal of light, but it does work. Holding the power button down for a few seconds turns it on (or back off); pressing the power button while the flashlight is on will cycle it from constant on, to SOS, and to medium speed strobe... again, nothing brilliant here, just a modest light.

No warranty information that I could find, so if a problem occurs within that a reasonable period of time I would return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. Smaller size battery storage and peak amps, minimal flashlight, and the lack of a storage/carry bag... four stars instead of 5.

If you are looking for a portable, lightweight power bank & car jumper kit of this style, size, price and functionality, for use similar to what I have described above, then we would recommend giving this unit a try.

review_body: I've been looking for some kind of battery jumper that would fit in my glove box or tool bag and this looked like it would.(and it does) Technology has come a long way since I bought a jump box years ago which was like carrying around a car battery. This is one of the neat things you can charge it with your cars powerpoint or with a usb port on a computer. Once charged it is just a matter of hooking the cables up to the battery, plugging the cables into the booster, pushing the on button, watching the lights and turning the ignition key on the car. It has all the safety features so if you hook it up backwards it lets you know without doing any damage. One thing I learned though if it doesn't sense at least 2 volts when you hook it to your dead battery it won't do anything unless you put it in bypass mode. The only thing that could have made this product any better is if the cover of the back of the front seats would have a slot for the pockets. But, I could alter that by cutting slits, which I may do.  Overall, I was very pleased with these seat covers. They look great in my car and are perfect for what I need them for...to keep my legs protected and the seats protected from my boys! I would recommend these car seat covers to anyone who is in the market for car seat covers.  I received these covers at a discounted rate in exchange for honest, unbiased opinion.  All pictures, videos and opinions are my own.

product_title: Carter P4070 In-Line Electric Fuel Pump
review_body:
The village elders still speak around the campfire about a time with automobiles were equipped with things called "carburetors" which were Byzantine contraptions designed to atomize gasoline for mixing with oxygen at a stoichiometric ration of 14.78 to 1. Legend has it these devices were perched atop gasoline engines for many moons, but were wiped out by the dinosaurs around 1982. There are still a few carbureted engines among the villagers to this day, but most suffer from a myriad of problems, including a proclivity for "vapor lock", a condition that my old Ford Bronco developed on the high-mountain passes of Colorado.

The elders told me to latch on to one of these Carter P4070 electric fuel pumps, and I did so in order to curry favor with the village council. I installed the Carter as directed, knowing that it's PSI rating was perfectly inline with the requirements of the carburetor. I installed a fuel pressure regulator to give me a bit more control, but I don't think I really ever needed it. Afterwards, the Paleozoic Bronco churned up those 13,000-foot passes like a asthmatic rhinoceros, no longer sidelined by the spectra of vapor lock.

Easy installation, not too noisy, rock-solid reliability. Make the elders happy, and slap one into your junk today.

review_headline: Hoping this will last as much as the original
review_body:
Finally decided to do timing belt in my 2003 Toyota Tundra; 232,000 miles on it. Yup, that's right.
The original belt was in good shape, no cracks, could have gone another 100k miles.
Bearings had a bit of play in them, but no noise it grinding, Idk how much longer they would have been good.
Pump had a leak at the bottom, but I had no overheating issues at all in the southern California sun.
The mechanic that did the job was impressed at how good the original parts were still.
He works mainly on Euro sedans, Audis, Bmws, and what not, and he said euros timing belts break at 110k miles.
Aisin stuff is dealer, I just hope the Mitsubishi timing belt will last like the Toyota one, so I don't have to do timing belt another 200k miles.
Btw, I didn't use my truck for heavy stuff, 95% of the driving was just commuting, a lot of that was on highway no traffic.
I gave it 4 stars because the belt was not original Toyota, but I'm hoping that it's actually the same belt but branded for Mitsubishi. If that's the case, then big 5 ol stars from me

product_title: Volant 15153 Cool Air Intake Kit
review_headline: It would have been better if they were something more sturdy like rubber
review_body: I installed this on my 2001 5.3L Silverado in conjunction with the Volant throttle body spacer. Installation was a nightmare. There are these 2 foam gaskets that sandwich the wall of the air box and mount up to the Mass Air Flow sensor. It would have been better if they were something more sturdy like rubber. You get 3 small allen key bolts that you have to get lined up with the MAF sensor, the 2 foam gaskets, the airbox and the filter adapter. Also, you can't see when you thread them. You're doing it by feel unless you can pull back the filter adapter enough to sort of get an idea of where you're aiming. Holes in the bottom of the airbox do not line up very well with the factory mounts on the truck. You may have to file the holes out to get a better fit. The same goes for the cover. The tubular section of this product was the worst. It doesn't fit on the truck if you also installed the Volant throttle body spacer. You don't have enough clearance between the throttle body and fan shroud. You have to cut an inch off the tube that mounts up to the throttle body to get it to fit. And after you cut it, You have to wrestle with it to get it on the throttle body. Make sure you clean the burrs off the edge where you had to cut. Once you finally get everything installed, you can see the air box is so large that you will have to remove it to get at any light bulbs on the front passenger side of the truck. Even as frustrating as the installation was, once I took the truck around the block I could see it performed quite well. Very good acceleration and faster throttle response. Truck's got some go now. I guess my biggest complaint about this product is, for the money you're spending, you shouldn't need to be modifying the kit to make it fit in the vehicle it is advertised to fit in. No arguments with performance though. Very happy on that end. Also, the large air box breathes well, and still draws air from the passenger fender where the air is cleaner.

product_title: Scrubblade SB1800 Premium All-Season Windshield Wiper Blade, 18" (Pack of 1)
review_headline: Great blades!  They work great... UNTIL THEY BREAK!!!
review_body:
I was really excited about these wipers at first. They felt really substantial and I thought they might work really well. Luckily, they did work well! My previous wipers were so streaky and when I put these on, it felt like I had a new windshield! I don't drive that often, so I didn't get caught in the rain often, but the times I did get caught in the rain, these worked well. I mostly used them to clean the windshields with wiper fluid when they got too dirty. They did a good job at cleaning them up. For those reasons, I was quite satisfied and I'd probably give them 4 or 5 stars. Unfortunately, my passenger side wiper fell off once when I tried to use it. Fortunately, I didn't lose it and was able to reattach it and it's been fine ever since. I chalked it up to user error.

Now here's the bad part. Tonight, while driving home, it began to rain. So of course, I put on my wipers. This time, my driver side wiper became unhooked and it fell loose under the wiper arm. Luckily, I was near a bridge, so I pulled over under it to stay dry. To my shock, the wiper just didn't fall off.. it BROKE. The plastic part that you hook the wiper arm onto somehow just broke off while using the blade. I took a picture because I was so in shock. I tried to put it back on. I pushed real hard and tried to snap the broken pieces together. It sorta went on, so I hoped that I'd be alright to make it home. I figured I'd use the blade sparingly, only when I really was having trouble seeing. I tried it once... it was fine! Then a few minutes later, I needed it again and POOF, it flew off while traveling 60 mph. Long story short, I did my best driving home in the dark without using my wipers. Let me tell you, it was very difficult to see and quite dangerous! Fortunately I made it home okay, but because of the experience, I can't recommend these at all. 0 stars as a result of this experience, but before it broke, I actually really liked them and would have given them 4 or 5 stars. Final verdict 2 stars (being very generous!). It's very sad, they were like new :-(

product_title: Three Bond Silicone Liquid Gasket - 3.5 oz 1211AT100
review_body:
Very very good stuff. I used it to seal up a BMW engine that I rebuilt, despite BMW's recommendation to not use any sealant. I don't believe they have much room to talk given how bad their engines usually leak oil. After the rebuild it didn't leak a drop for the year afterwards that I owned the car.

Tip: Clean the surfaces very well with acetone or something similiar. Then apply a very THIN coat. You can use a small paint brush to spread a nice even coat. You do not want to slather it on... It should pretty much be as thin as you can get it.

I also recommend letting the area sit a few days prior to use if possible. This is not the fastest drying stuff, but that was the least of my concerns.

product_title: Shaf International Women's Gauntlet Glove - Bottom Closure (Black, Medium)
review_headline: Just what I needed. Fit like they were made just for me.
review_body: I've ordered 3 other pairs of gloves I had to return, before finally finding these. I bought these for riding my Scooter. I like to protect my skin from the Sun. And since most gloves are himmed up short to the wrist joint & most of my long sleeve tops end up blowing back while I'm riding, I kept getting repeat sun exposure to my forearm area. I have been using good & strong Sunscreen, but I needed yet more protection. Before I ordered these, I read here that they are 12 inches long. I measured the tip of my middle finger back 12 inches & the length looked to be just perfect! Tried them on & rode with them & they are absolutely perfect! Do be aware that these gloves are super soft & comfortable inside, but they do get sweaty pretty quickly when worn in hot weather. And also the short sleeve cuff part widens out quite a bit. I don't think these would win me a "fashion contest", but they are just enough length & width to tuck in whatever long sleeve I'm wearing, deep enough that I get the full protection I was looking for. And I feel quite safe wearing them, in case of an accident or fall. It's also just good to know, the longer the glove, the more skin surface that is protected.  Update 12/19/15. I continue to wear these during the cold weather now & they are great! They keep my hands & finger tips cozy warm. (I tend to get cold hands & feet anyways). They are snug & movable enough that they don't take any control away from my hands while riding. But still warm, great hand protection & the perfect length, so they don't just stop right before your wrists. I rode to the Grocery store yesterday & kept the gloves on while I was shopping inside, just to continue to keep my hands warm & it was awesome.

product_title: OTC 6599 Universal Fuel Sender Lock Tool
review_body:
Works great on a 2007 Nissan Sentra, equivalent to tool part Kent-Moore #J-45722 ($120-150). Always a good idea to grease up the lock ring for ease of removing and reinstalling it. Luckily, there was an access port to the fuel pump assembly through the back seat, so that I didn't have to drop the tank. I did try the hammer and screw driver method but couldn't get enough lateral force to pop the ring off, the angle was steep enough. A good idea to disconnect the battery. Remember to wrap up the fuel line, a clean latex glove works. And, thoroughly clean and dry the areas around the fuel pump to reduce the risk of debris falling into gas tank.
With OTC brand you'll always know that you're getting a excellent quality product - very sturdy. Pretty good price, since all of the auto parts shop wanted to charge around $75-80 (on special order tool); and I am not an auto mechanic by trade.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:e6b275337aa304169a1fc70338e1e137]] I have done a full LED conversion on the inside of my Tahoe and started on the outside. I did a little research on the reverse lights and noted that the 3157 bulbs were pretty big when it comes to LED's. So I took the jump and installed this KDL Highlight LED 3157-18 set. I have provided a video review and I encourage you to watch it to see the difference in the standard incandescent 3157 bulb and the new LED bulb. I like the pure white light that LEDs offer and this is what I used on the inside. All pure white 6000k bulbs. The bulbs are about a 1/4 to 1/2 longer than standard bulbs so bare that in mind. Make sure you have ample distance between the end of the bulb and your bulb cover/lens. These bulbs do not list the K value but they are right at 5000K - 6000K pure white. I don't really see any hint of blue in them that the 6000K gives off so I am guessing they are 5000K..thats a guess. They are noticeably different from the standard brownish yellow standard bulbs..I love them. The pure white light makes it easier for me to see backing out of my long driveway. The throw light about 10 feet farther than the standard bulb did too. There was no flickering issues that I have had with other bulbs either. For the price these are spot on. These cost upwards of 20 bucks at my local parts store. These would be great in just about any 3157 location on your vehicle. I am getting 2 more sets to replace my blinkers and tail lights.

If you have any questions, please feel free to ask in the comments. I will respond. If you found my review helpful, let me know. Lets keep making better buying decisions together. Thank you and as always Be Safe & Happy Shopping!!

review_body:

product_title: Bosch 13399 Oxygen Sensor, OE Type Fitment
review_headline: Greatly improved throttle response and fuel consumption!
review_body:
This is the upstream sensor for my Mitsubishi Eclipse 97 (non-turbo). My downstream sensor died, and I had to get it replaced. After replacing it, I though it would be a good idea to replace the downstream sensor (this product) because the catalyst test was showing as "incomplete". I bought this sensor 2 days later and installed it. Reset the PCM (by disconnecting battery for 20 minutes) and started my car up. At first it was coughing up and idling inconsistently, which is normal when you replace one of these parts, after reaching normal temperature I took it for a spin and immediately noticed improved response on the throttle. The best part is that my engine idling has gotten much more consistent at 800 rpm and rarely drops below, the car feels smoother, and I can already notice improved fuel consumption. Even with my A/C turned on the engine idle is very consistent and I think it helps my A/C to perform better when driving in bumper to bumper traffic.

Next time you perform a tune-up of your car (spark plugs, filters, etc). And you still notice a surging idling or lack of throttle response, consider replacing your O2 sensors, specially if you have not replaced them in ages (mine were the car originals). This product is definitely recommended.

product_title: Saddlemen Adventure Track Seat Standard Black for Suzuki DL650/DL1000 V-Storm
review_body:
Anyone with more than an hour of saddle time on the stock Suzuki DL650 seat knows that it's an instrument of torture. By comparison, this seat makes me feel like I am riding a cloud. OK, that's a bit of an exaggeration, but it feels really, really good. Some comments:
The 'suede' part on my seat was only a little different from the rest of the 'leather' - some sort of lightly brushed vinyl I think. It looks more waterproof than real suede, but it definitely does not have the nap of real suede. I actually like this better. The suede part was not stretched tight on the seat - it sort of had the look of a comfortable leather couch though, so I am OK with that. The suede also had a mottled appearance, with spots of very dark gray on the black finish. This seems to be darkening as I ride though. Not very noticeable, but some people might object.

What I really like about it: I can move around, forwards and back. Moving sideways is easier too, because the top is somewhat flat. The slot in the middle really works to relieve discomfort from pressure on things I don't want to squish. Depending how I sit, I can get some support for my thighs. The sticky pillion leather is very sticky. Nothing should slide off of that stuff.

I was worried about added height for this seat. It did add some height, but not much. With the stock seat I was on the balls of my feet at a stop. With this seat, I still am on the balls of my feet.

Overall, in spite of the cosmetic issues (which could just be cosmetic 'features'), I would give this seat an A+.

review_headline: Do you know your wheel stud size?
review_body:
You Jeep guys realize you don't have M12 x 1.25 wheels studs, right? Not everything is made for a Jeep. (But yes, mostly everything is.)

The item description is strange: "This 5 piece wheel lock kit well help denture thieves when you Jeep is parked."

First, it's only 5 pieces if you count the bag it comes in, the staple that keeps it closed, and the label on the bag.
Second, only my fist will denture thieves...in the mouth.

Perhaps more accurate: "This 2-piece wheel lock kit will help deter thieves when your non-Jeep vehicle with M12 x 1.25 wheels studs is parked."

I bought two of these for an add-on tire carrier project for my Nissan Pathfinder. The truck is M12 x 1.25, as is the carrier, despite what the Amazon vehicle fitment chart thinks. Part of the reason for the purchase was to lock the tire, but it became apparent that I also didn't want to resort to denturing thieves when my Pathfinder is parked. Or when it's in motion....thieves these days!

As for the product itself, it does the job. The metal collar that covers the security pattern on the lock seems a little questionable...was a little crooked, but functional. The two I received appear to be of about the same quality, but not enough to dock a star.

product_title: ACDelco 251-743 GM Original Equipment Water Pump with Gasket
review_headline: Looks good and works great.  Made in Canada.
review_body:
It looks like a well made Water pump. It says made in Canada on the back of it. So it should be a quality made part. Make sure you get the new Thermostat housing to go along with this as I guess it's been updated. If you get this pump, it has 2 new bolts for the thermostat so you don't need any others.

You should need any sealer goop crap when installing this. it comes with new Gaskets that don't need any type of sealer!!! Same goes for the new thermostat!!! No sealant required. I use a razer blade scraper to scrap off any of the old gasket residue left on the engine. That was simple enough. Especially when it's not gooped all over!!! Now some people like the put a tiny amount in a couple spots and let it dry just to hold the gaskets in place. But that takes time for it to dry and if you're careful not needed. A couple bolts for each gasket to hold them in place and carefully place on engine and screw the bolts in. For my 2003 Chevy Silverado, they needed to be torqued to 22 foot pounds. For those 6 bolts that hold it on. Tighten to 11 ft pounds first and then to 22 ft pounds. I like to do things right so I don't have issues later. I wish I had gotten new belts, but they'll be fine for now. They're not to bad. The Thermostat bolts are smaller and so don't need to be as tight. I didn't look up that torque, so just tight. Again no sealant needed!!!

You'll also need a couple Gallons of Dec-Cool coolant. The orange stuff!!! Don't get the green crap!!! Not for a GM car/truck, you'll end up with other issues!!! I also like to use Distilled water and not tap water. So you'll need 2-3 gallons of it. That should be enough. Distilled water is water that has many of its impurities removed through distillation. This will keep your coolant lasting quite a bit longer!!! It's cheap at under a dollar a gallon. This is also what you want to use if you have a battery that needs to be topped off. Tap Water has Minerals and whatnotin it that can short out a battery and cause it to fail sooner. Especially when using Dex-Cool. You're aiming for a normal 50/50 mix of Dex-Cool and Distilled water.

One last thing, Make sure after you think you have it filled up, that you run for a while with the Cap off the tank and watch it. What you're waiting for is the engine to warm up fully and the thermostat to open up Once this happens the air in your coolant system will escape and your water in the tank will drop down to empty, so be ready to fill up more. DO NOT put the cap on tight and warm your engine up and then take it off!!! That's a good way to get coolant thrown into your face and burn you or worse. just leave it off. It'll keep the system from pressurizing up to around 15 PSI.

When the coolant drops and you fill it up to the full line, Remember that's the full when COLD line!!! So you want to check the level again when the engine is cold and make sure it's at that line. When it's cold, it's also safe to remove the cap. You can put the cap on when it's hot and you should be pretty close after the air is out of the system.

The hardest part for me on this job and more then likely for many others is getting the fan off!!! You need a large wrench for that fan nut that screws onto the pulley. The threads are normal Righty tighty, Lefty Loosy. For me, that took the longest to get off. It's easier to get off while the pump is still mounted they trying to do it when the pump of pulled off!!! The pump bolts are 10mm and the idler pully is 15mm. The fan, I'm not sure, I used a 1-1/2" wrench which was larger but it was the only then I had and it worked. The belt tensioner pully is also 15mm, I just used a 15mm wrench turn to the right and pop the belt off and the same to get it back on again. Other then the fan, the rest was a snap, simple. Remove a few parts. Top hose, top half of Fan shroud, Air duct from filter into engine, just need a normal screw driver. Pop it right off and some connectors and the pump is right there, easy enough to get to everything.

Like I said, looks like a well made pump, made in Canada and includes both Gaskets for the pump to the motor and 2 screws for the new Thermostat housing you also need to get if you've haven't replaced it in the past.

review_headline: I would recommend however, that you buy a better bulb

Well lets face it people. You are paying 35$ for essentially what is an LED Bulb, (with parking light and brake light mode) a socket, a wire and a drill bit. Now lets face it, that should not cost 35$. However, because the drill bit is measured, and that socket is specifically able to fit in a tC, FR-S, or BRZ, then yeah, you might want to spend money on it, so everything will fit.

I would recommend however, that you buy a better bulb, a brighter bulb. The brake light does not look as pictured and the difference between the brake light vs the running light is very minimal. You need to buy another 7444 LED Bulb, preferably one that is brighter and can still fit in the lens.

Lastly, you might know how to install HID's but this is a bit harder. You might want to get this done by more skilled people, it should cost that much. All they ought to do is take of one of the tail lights, drill a hole for the light bulb socket, wire it up, then close everything back up. A bit of work, and special tools needed. If you live in Los Angeles, theres a place called 310Kreations, they will definetly install this for you, for a reasonable price of 65% and it wont take longer than 20 min. They are very nice and friendly as well. (65$ is fair price considering it is a bit technical and because some people said they paid 90 to 100 for labor, just for a single light bulb) So if you buy this, make sure you know how to install it and perhaps look for a better bulb than the one which comes with the kit (which is a 7444 socket LED)

product_title: James King 1005-1 Warning Triangle, (Set of 3)
review_headline: Better Warning Triangles than some of the other brands.
review_body: Nice quality for the price on these safety triangles.  I specifically bought these James King 1005-1 Warning Triangles set because these have sturdier looking little plastic support legs on the ends of the triangles that help the unit resist falling over once setup and rotated perpendicular to the weighted bottom. Many of the other Warning Triangle sets available (like Sate-Lite and Blazer) have the little plastic support legs taper to a point. Seeing as the support legs are just plastic tabs with no metal reinforcements, I prefer the fact that these legs/tabs don't taper to a point. The weighted bottoms are nice and heavy to keep these triangles in place even with the gusts from passing semis at highway speeds. The bright orange triangles are easily visible from a distance, and the reflectorized sections make them even easier to see at night.  As with other reviews, I would recommend practicing opening and setting these up in broad daylight (or indoors where it's bright enough to see it clearly and what you're doing) so you can do it easily and competently should the need arise. The triangles themselves are plastic, and while practicing deploying these in the daytime the first time, I noted a couple of sticking points while opening one of the triangles. Forcing it open in the dark could potentially have broken the plastic. After familiarizing myself with how they deploy, if one of them sticks while opening it in the dark, I know which way to pull it to open it without the risk of breaking anything.  While doing my due diligence and reading all the reviews I could find for all the Warning Triangle sets available from numerous sellers/sites and sources, I read numerous reviews complaining about the red plastic box that holds the folded triangles, with some of the other options.  I saw more than one review of the other brands of Warning Triangle sets mentioning that the box/case that came with those was worthless, or easily deformed when simply trying to lift the boxwith the triangles inside, and with the box not being able to close or stay closed once it had been opened and the triangles had been taken out the first time. That was certainly NOT the experience I had with this James King 1005-1 Warning Triangle set.  While the included red plastic box that holds the 3 folded triangles is not the sturdiest box out there (it's not a Pelican case), unlike reviews of other Warning Triangle sets, the box that came with this James King set was easily sturdy enough to hold the triangles nicely while carrying them out to the car and moving them from the trunk of one car to the other without deforming or popping open etc. I also had no issues with the hinges or the tabs that hold the box closed after taking all 3 triangles out and deploying them and then putting them back in the box.  The set is well worth the money for safety and peace of mind.  I would also highly recommend getting a bright, reflective safety vest like this Neiko vest, http://www.amazon.com/Neiko-Visibility-Yellow-Zipper-Reflective/dp/B0030AA3YK/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1438236881&sr=8-1&keywords=neiko+safety+vest and very importantly, keeping it where you can get to it from inside the car. That way, you can put the vest on before stepping out of your vehicle and be highly visible to motorists while outside the relative safety of your vehicle. The last thing you want to happen is to be struck by an inattentive motorist when you step out of your vehicle to set up your warning triangles.  *** And to be completely clear, I have no affiliation whatsoever with the companies producing/selling ANY of these Warning Triangle sets. I simply read ALL the reviews I could find for all the various available sets before choosing this one and came to the realization they're not all the same and there are some small differences between them.

product_title: Xtune Toyota 4Runner Headlight
review_body: Here's the low down.. My 4Runner is almost 10 years old but runs great. Just needed new headlight for the driver side but decided to get both in black OEM "Direct" replacement. Yes, they look like the photo but if I had the time to return them and go with a different company I probably would..  Shipping was very fast and prompt and when the box was supposed to be delivered I instantly got followed up by an email from them asking if I had received them and if everything was going okay. That's definitely one for the books as I've never even heard of this before.  My issues.. 1. Driver side headlight came straight out of the box with the Low beam hub flapping around. Tried a quick fix but didn't work and I had literally just opened the box. Turns out the adjustment screw wasn't even attached properly and wasn't the exact size to fit the threads. I had a bucket of screws that I made work. 2. The caulking on the outskirts or the lens had it bleeding in more than one spot where it actually hardened to the lens, had to take a razor blade and trim it up. 3. Low/hi beam bulbs fit decent, but not waterproof tight nor does the low beam actually fasten tight, just keeps spinning. Had to use a bunch of caulk on the low beam slot. High beam sat well and tight.. 4. Side marker for both sides didn't fit the "exact" slots to twist the light in. I ended up taking a blade and trimming it to where it needed to be. 5. The exact positions of the pieces of plastic to screw into the vehicle weren't exactly lined up and there's a bunch of pressure on the lower radiator plastic piece since the only way to get it in and by a little force. (You can see the plastic turn white from stretching) 6. Had higher hopes for better craftsmanship. Interested to see how long these last.  Among these issues a usual half hour job for me quickly turned into 2 hours having to fix so much..Especially when their entire website is based on OEM this and OEM that, direct fit, yada yada.  The pro's1. These headlights do make it look new and pretty slick, even more so since mine is metallic black. 2. Very bright when you throw in some new bulbs all around. I used the Silvania Ultrabrights and they worked great. 3. Fast shipping and so far good customer service. 4. When you figure out how to work one side installation will pick up on the other.   If it wasn't for the possible "bad batch" I got and being out of time since my trip starts on Friday I would more than likely return them and order a different set/replacement. They are nice headlights but I would be cautious about buying them here

product_title: Selected 4D Black Carbon Fiber Vinyl Wrap Sticker Air Realease Bubble Free anti-wrinkle 5 x 7FT 60"x 78"
review_headline: Love the Product but wish it was shipped in better tube
review_body:
I bought this to cover up the surface of my old and worn out desk. I've had the same desk for over 10 years and with a new computer and monitor, I wanted to update my whole desk setup without having to get a completely new desk.

The tube was in surprisingly good shape given how thing it was. Upon taking out the vinyl, I noticed that some of it was crushed and wrinkled. See my photos. Since I didn't need the entire piece, I just used that part that wasn't wrinkled. I'm sure some heat and stretching would have taken the wrinkles right out.

I cleaned off and prepped my desk surface and it went on smoothly No wrinkles at all. I had the desk covered in 10 minutes. Super easy to work with, but then again it was a flat surface with no complex curves. I think doing this to a car roof or hood would take more time, a heat gun and a helper but could be done in a few hours including prep time.

It looks great! It's not a printed design but rather a finely embossed vinyl. If you run your finger nails against it, you can hear that "zip" sound (sorry don't know how to describe it) that you would get if you ran your finger across say a record. It wasn't until I got the monitor on that the light reflecting off the desk from the monitor gave it an almost 3D look from certain angles. Also has a semi-gloss look to it. Real carbon fiber items I’ve personally seen and held tends to have a much smoother gloss look to it from the epoxy resin but I don't care, it makes my desk look brand new again and for only $24!! I may use the left over to wrap other things now.

product_title: Obenauf's Leather Oil
review_headline: Highly recommended for sticky leather interior (steering wheel / car interior).
review_body:
My relatively new steering wheel began feeling sticky and deteriorating after 10 months. I've tried an array of synthetic and semi-natural products to try and repair the wheel. I've used Duragloss 221 / Lexol / Leather Nova / Leather Honey / Meguiars Leather products and they've all either made it much stickier or dried it out. I decided to give this one last try before employing more permanent alternatives. I've cleaned it with water vinegar , water and soap, and made sure it was dry and clean. Applied it generously and rubbed it in wearing gloves and let it sit in for 2-3 hours. I buffed the excess out and let it air out for the rest of the day and it looked significantly healthier. I've applied a second coat the following day (about 15-16 hours later) and repeated the same process and applied a liberal amount and rubbed it in. I let this application soak in for a bit longer, i'd say about 4 hours, and buffed the excess off with a microfiber towel.
This has brought it back to life with a sleek natural leather finish and absolutely no oily/sticky residue. It did leave a bit of a smell (not a bad one) but it's to be expected after having it soak in with the windows up for that many hours. Whatever is in this bottle is magical!

product_title: 2x 4" Arsenal 18W 6 CREE LED Brightest on the Market! SUV Off-road Boat Headlight Spot Driving Fog Light + Mounting Bracket
review_body: I now have 4 pairs of these on my Land Rover Discovery in Jamaica. Three pairs are on the front, on my ARB bullbar, and one pair on a custom made mount on the roof on the back as serious reverse lights.  The first pair went on several months ago and have gone through heavy tropical rain, with no moisture reaching the inside of the lights yet. However, I put some silicone on the seams soon after installation to be sure. They've also survived very rough roads with no problem.  One thing, don't bother buying the wiring harness. The one time I did, the relay was crap, didn't work, and you don't need a relay anyway. It's only 36w a pair, so at 12v less than 2A each. Just use decent gauge wire - I'm using thick speaker wire.  My set up is this:  One front pair pointed low to use as driving lights at night - the roads are terrible here so I need it. There's an inline fuse, and a basic house switch wrapped in electrical tape that sits on my dash. I also have two Hella LED floods low on the bullbar on a separate switch and the regular headlights to use.  Two pairs connected to my standard high beam wires instead of the regular high beams. Pointed straight down the road and wickedly bright.  The back pair also with an inline fuse and a light switch on my dash.  I'm quite happy with them so far. Would buy more but I really don't need them. Plenty light now.  Stefan (RS Stewart) Jamaican Caves Organisation www.jamaicancaves.org

product_title: Magnaflow 15110 Performance Exhaust Kit
review_body:
I purchased this system for my wife's 2010 Chevy Equinox as the factory exhaust developed a hole along the weld seam of the resonator. Prior to buying this system, I took the vehicle to the local dealership and was quoted a little over $1000 for the repair. This was due to the fact that after the catalytic converter pipe, the system is all one piece. Therefore, rather than just replacing the resonator, the whole exhaust beyond the cat-pipe would need to be replaced. For this reason started to research exhausts and came crossed this system from Magnaflow. On the MF website it does state that this system fits both the GMC Terrain and the Chevy Equinox(same platform), even though Amazon only has the Terrain listed.

The install was fairly straightforward, although the directions are somewhat sub pare compared to other exhaust manufacturers as there are no pictures to assist. The only real issue that came up was the factory band clamp that MF says to reuse to attach the intermediate pipe to the cat-pipe. This clamp was so rusted that it had seized and therefore was unusable. This was solved quickly by calling MF and requesting that they send another band clamp, which they did at no additional cost and it arrived 3 days later. Fit and finish of the system is perfect as the hanger posts line up perfectly. Also, spacing for the entire system is perfect as it does not come close to touching anything. The system is very well engineered. Of course after I completed the install, I took the vehicle on its initial test drive. Sound difference is negligible. The system sounds almost stock, which on a family vehicle like an Equinox quiete-ish is exactly what you want. In addition, the vehicle seems like it has a little more get-up-and-go, but this could all be in my head.

In summary, I would definitely purchase this system again and MF customer service helped greatly with the one issue I had with the system. The system looks great on the vehicle as it comes with a beautiful 4" stainless steel tip that should have come on the vehicle from the factory in the first place. I definately recommend giving this system consideration if your Equinox or Terrain's exhaust fails because, in my opinion, you will get a much better system for a couple hundred bucks cheaper than replacing your failed system with another factory assembly.

product_title: Rostra 250-9601 2011 Mazda 2 Cruise Control Kit
review_body:
I installed this in a 2010 Mazda 2 and it went without a hitch.

Overall, if you can install a car radio, you can install this kit. There are 3 fabricated connections that you must make (OBD port, accelerator, and the clutch - if it is a manual). These connectors are plug and play. Next, you must attach the power cable to ACC (I used the car audio wire) and the clutch sensor to the clutch switch (if it is a manual).After that, you install the control switch by drilling a hole through the steering wheel cover and running the wires through. Once you connect those wires to the control box, you secure everything, and you're done. I would estimate that installation takes about 1-2 hours if you take your time. You can google Rostra's installation manual

So far, the cruise control works fine, and makes long trips much easier. The functionality is no different than any aftermarket cruise control you may use.

I will update if something goes haywire in the future.

review_body:
These little babies are pretty sweet! I took a chance on these (less than 5 reviews) but I'm glad that I did so far. They appear to be of high quality and once they were finally installed, I absolutely love the effect they have! Similar to my Harley Daymaker LED light, they have a terrific cut-off point to truly act as a fog light (dispersing low and wide). I'll have to adjust/angle them to be even more effective but they're great out of the box. (Adjustment is easy with an allen-wrench.) When installed, they sit at the same depth as the OEM fog lights.

Be aware - they're fog lights....not crazy-bright DRLs that will blind/alert other drivers to your presence. Get an HID kit for that, BUT, if you're looking for a true "fog light" setup, these are definitely worth while!

Install on a '15 Jeep Wrangler was a little more of a pain, since I had to remove the bumper (4 bolts, not bad, just didn't expect) but it's totally worth it. For this vehicle, I'd HIGHLY recommend getting the wiring adapter to truly make it plug and plug (no splicing or other stuff) - search "H16 HID adapter 5202" on Amazon.

Attached pics - You can see the "top/bottom cutoff" points with the yellowish line. This is a great on/off point for the fog lights that doesn't let the light disperse too far up/down. They're much brighter in person, as it's hard to get the camera to capture what "you" really see.

product_title: Dorman 741-637 Buick/Oldsmobile Front Driver Side Window Regulator with Motor
review_headline: ... arrived a day early and all the parts looked good, though not the golden finish shown in the ...
review_body:
The unit arrived a day early and all the parts looked good, though not the golden finish shown in the picture. Also came with a packet of door panel clips, which would have been extremely useful had I broken a clip and not the plastic guide on the back of the panel to help line door up to the panel more easily. Anyway, the instructions called for removing the door handle, which I didn't do on my 2001 Buick Century, the mechanism is out of the way and it only takes a little bit of thought beforehand to figure out how to remove and replace the door panel without damaging anything, and the mechanism's moving parts all run along the solid steel of the door frame, which kinda made the idea of the door handle being an obstacle moot. Removal of the old parts and installation of the new was fairly easy and straightforward, a small note though, when putting the new unit in, slide the bottom end into the door behind the lower speaker first so that you can have enough play to set the motor in place, then bring up the regulator to place it. The rigidity of the wire guides coming out of the motor made trying to put the regulator in second pretty much impossible. One small problem was that the right hand hole for mounting the window to the support bracket was off center from the window a little bit, it was down and to the right of the threaded hole on the window tab. This was easily fixed with a rattail file and lowering the window to check progress a couple times. Fixing the hole took less than 5 minutes, so it wasn't off very far off, just enough to throw off aligning the bolt so that it locked up after about 1.5 turns. I didn't even need to remove the unit to fix the hole, just make sure the window is lifted back up out of the way. Being a machinist, this little defect is unsurprising given how much I've watched parts change as production runs.

All in all, it works great, installation was quick and easy, minus the little bit of filing. I will update if it fails within the next 2 or 3 years. Other than that, the whole job took less than an hour and all I needed was a 10mm socket for the door bolts and all window, motor, and regulator bolts, and a philips #2 screwdriver for the screw behind the door handle.

product_title: Reese Towpower 44675 Class III Custom-Fit Hitch with 2" Square Receiver opening
review_headline: Fit perfectly and I installed myself.
review_body: Bought for a 2012 CR-V.  I needed the two inch receiver and this one had it.  (I already owned a bike rack with a two inch requirement).  Previous reviews showed this one fit, no problems, and I found that to be the case.  I will admit that I had to put it on twice!  I pulled off the big plastic cover over the gas tank (the youtube video was very helpful) and cut it like the instructions said to cut....only I did what a couple of previous reviewers did...I cut it on three sides and created a flap.  Turned out perfect and the hitch fit right up into the hole I had creating by cutting the plastic.  I had no problems attaching the screws.  I did find that I had a wire harness running back there that was installed earlier so I could tow the CR-V. The ground wire was attached to a bolt using one of the required holes...so I had to move the ground wire.  No big deal, but I did scratch my head a while wondering why the wires were there at all.  I put the hitch in (I was able to hold it up using a BIG wooden block and get a couple of bolts in....but two people would make the job easier.  I was all done and realized I had not put the plastic cover back up, and it needed to be in place to provide strength to the rear fender wall, etc, so I had to take the hitch back off, put up the cover, and then reattach the hitch...sure went faster the second time!

When installing you must add a spring bolt between the down pipe and the high flow cat otherwise the exhaust system will become to tight and rattle when idling. The springs will allow flexibility and reduce the chances of cracking between the welds. Another thing you must consider is the noise it makes, it is very loud. Between 2.5 and 4 RPM is the loudest, athough it doesn't bother me at all. The next thing to consider is that the exhaust will be lower than stock making it easy for the exhaust to bottom out on a speed bump even when it is at stock hight

product_title: 3M 39008 Headlight Lens Restoration System
review_body:
I didn't expect this to work so well, and I didn't expect to be able to do more than two headlights. Alas, it has exceeded my expectations. I have currently restored two cars' headlights (four headlights total), and I think there's enough sandpaper/polish left to do one more car.

I must admit that sanding them down to an even haze with 500 grit sandpaper is awfully unnerving. I was still worried after moving up to 800, but the leap to 3000 was huge. I could have gotten away without the polish afterward if I wanted to! However, the polish does help add a nice shine. I finished with a blend of carnauba wax and paint sealant, which will hopefully slow down the deterioration process.

The first car I used this on had hazy headlights, but also a lot of micro-fractures throughout the lens. Naturally, this kit can't work miracles, but it comes close! The microfractures are still there, but the haze is completely gone. That made an enormous difference to the clarity of the headlights as well as the brightness of the light.

I then decided to secretly restore the headlights of a friend's car, as they looked awful. I had no idea what a difference clear headlights could make to a car's appearance, and I was surprised to see what a difference in headlight brightness it had made as well. It was fun to see their reaction; that was worth the price all by itself!

I forgot to buy automotive masking tape, so I used painters tape instead. It worked just fine, but you might want to be more careful and remember to order tape made for the job!

product_title: Turtle Wax Premium Grade Trim Restorer
review_headline: BEWARE!!!!! WILL RUIN YOUR FINISH, WILL MAKE IT LOOK WORSE
review_body:
First off I'm not a younger inexperienced person. I've owned many cars, & brand new ones also. I went off a recommendation from neighbor to use this product. I applied it last month in June to my 2010 Dodge truck, & my 2014 Hyundia Sonata. Both vehicles were getting the yearly wax & detail treatment.
First my Dodge truck I only applied it to the black plastic step pad that sits in the back bumper. Even though this truck is a 2010 it looks pristine, & only this part was showing signs of fading, not even as bad as you would think for the age. Second on my 2014 Hyundia I applied to the front grill insert which is all plastic.
After a week when the first good rain came through it looked horrible. The Hyundia looked splotchy with an almost white soap scum residue on it.
The truck was the worst it totally washed out & now made it look more faded & weathered than before. It looked like it's been sitting in the sun and never even been cared for.
Contacted Turtle Wax corp & initiated a claim for both vehicles. The rep on the phone told me it was a silicone clear base product, which made it impossible to do this. However would still send an adjuster to look at it and assess the claim. After the adjuster took his pictures & documented everything he left and said that Turtle Wax would be in touch. They called a week later a denied any culpability due to supposedly this has never occurred. Also they stuck to the theory that there silicone base product could never do this. However the adjuster candidly admitted that silicone is almost impossible to strip of surfaces making it permanent to the material. However they Turtle Wax claim that this product last for months after applying, but on both the vehicles it wash off within a week. However plastic surfaces being porous obviously absorbed only the part of this product that made it look worse. Read other reviews on here that also had bad experiences and they concur that it just washes off & makes it look worse. Also other people in the industry caution to stay away from silicone based products. So based on a recommendation I'm having to replace two parts on my vehicles. The Dodge truck replacement part $50, I did it myself. The Hyundia grill I can't do it myself for the bumper has to come off. A WHOPPER TO REPLACE AT $500!!!!!!!!!
By the way my retired neighbor from GM has 2 vehicles that look like crap also where he applied: THIS JUNK THAT WILL RUIN & COST YOU IF YOU USE !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!n the industry caution to stay away from silicone based products. The cap is very secure, so there won't be leakage.

product_title: Omega Steelmate SM-TP-71P Tire Pressure Monitoring System
review_body:
Using this on a Toyota Camry 97 with aftermarket alloy wheels. The OEM steel wheels with plastic covers may not allow for this.
The install is easy. The screen fits very neat in the cigarette lighter spot, being flush with the rest of the board. Looks like it was built for that. The great thing with the Camry is that you still have the accessories outlet for charging you electronics. The only problem is if you actually using the cigarette lighter.

The sensors are a little big for my liking but I guess the size of the battery was the deciding factor in their designed size. The fact that came with black and silver covers is a very good thing. Changing covers is easy but ... be careful not crosstreading them.

Important:
1. do secure your sensors with the provided nut. Otherwise you lose air or you lose the sensors.
2. do not lose the securing wrench and have it with you in the car. Without it you may have problems getting them off to inflate your tires.
3. if you drive the car with the sensors on in the winter make sure you apply some anti-seize compound on the securing nut. Winter road stuff (salt, etc.) is very corrosive. Also do not forget the rubber boot.
4. Be careful when changing covers/battery so you do not crosstread them. It is easy to do so and that means the water seal will not work properly, in time compromising the battery and the sensor's electronics. If it would be to name a cons this will be it.

review_body: After receiving the correct mounting package, I can say that these running boards are extremely difficult to install. At least on a 2013 Ford Explorer.  I ordered and received the correct mount package (Westin 27-1965) for these boards, but the instructions are very sketchy. And there are no online video instructions for newer Explorer installation for these running boards. the first issue is that they leave out the fact that the rocker panels have to be pulled far enough out so the front mount can be in installed beneath it. It gives the impression that you might remove the rocker panel, which I found very confusing. Then on the rear mount installation, the instructions state "use a punch to pop out the factory punch-out on the frame to install upper bolt". Well, there is no "factory punch-out" to "punch-out". 20 minutes of drill time, and two drill bits to drill through the frame to be able to run the bolt through for the upper bolt on the rear. Oh, and you must have very thin and nimble fingers to feed the washer and nut between the frame and rocker panel to secure it. There is no mention of that in the mounting instructions. So, if you have a 2011 or newer Expolorer--have the shop install these.

product_title: Standard Motor Products RU403 Blower Motor Resistor
review_headline: EXCELLENT quality, perfect fit and function.  5 stars --minimum.
review_body: OH YEAH---when its 110 degrees in Phoenix arizona, trust me, you notice it when your AC blower is not working right.  Its the difference between insanity and a psychotic episode.  One you are crazy and the other you do something crazy.  (Not really) --My blower was not quite right.  I bought a new motor and it "seemed" to blow harder, but it seemed like it was on medium.  It would go from off, to slow, to a little faster but never really blew hard.  SO I was frustrated having just wasted 30$ and spending 45 minutes in the heat changing the blower motor.  THEN---I realized that the blower motor plugs into this thing, which looks like nothing, a few coils of wire that look like springs---which in reality are like .25 ohm resistors.  I am assuming that my old one--which looked ok, was losing or gaining impedance (resistance) when it got hot, and so the motor was not getting the right amount of current to go fast.  I bought this--after seeing lesser named quality ones (standard is as good as motorcraft in my opinion), and the motorcraft are 50$.  this was 13$.  I installed it--5 minutes, put the blower motor on high, and voila--it made my hair move---(that was the test--the old one my hair never blew out of place).  So I am now cooler---and sane, and this is working perfectly.  For what its worth---aside from the OEM part number stamped into the plastic, this looks IDENTICAL to the original motorcraft so I am assuming that standard makes them for motorcraft or someone makes them for both companies.  Either way, its a very high quality part and works perfectly.  Highly recommend.  THANK YOU FOR READING

I have a 2014 GSXR-1000 and i was able to fit this kit into my bike with a splitter and extension left over so it sure comes with enough pieces.
I took some painters tape and taped the lights on everywhere i thought i wanted them and then ran all the wires FROM THE CONTROL UNIT up to the lights so that way you dont run the wires up to the control unit only to find you need a male end to connect. And then i turned the lights on to check lighting and after adjusting i finnished buttoning it all up and shrink wrapping ect. And i was done in less than 2 hours!! Will definitely go with these guys again in the future.

product_title: Noico 80 mil 36 sqft car Sound deadening mat, butyl automotive Sound Deadener, audio Noise Insulation and dampening
review_body:
I used this to soundproof the refrigerator compartment in my RV. The fridge had two OEM fans that were about a foot from my head when I worked at the computer in my dinette. There was nothing between me and the fans but 1/8" of plywood.

I now have 5 Noctua fans in the compartment and I have to put my ear up to the wall to tell if they're on or not.

This stuff is very easy to work with and I didn't notice any odor. It's also very reasonably priced compared to most soundproofing material.

One word of warning, the adhesive is very hard to clean up and when you pull off the paper backing, some of it will stick to the backing. If you drop the backing on the carpet and step on it, it's pretty tough to remove (don't ask me how I know).

Be aware that this stuff is heavy and will add some weight to whatever you stick it to.

I only wish they sold it in smaller amounts. I could use a sheet or two more of it but don't want to buy 6 sheets again.

I purchased this to program some keys into my van. Bottom line is it worked, BUT it wasn't the easy process I had hoped for. product_title: Stant 10841 Fuel Cap
review_headline: Don't damage the tether, attach it to the new STANT 10841 gas cap...
review_body:
Stant 10841 gas cap:
I bought to replace OEM gas cap on my 2005 Chevy Aveo Hatchback which had a conveniently attached tether. The original gas cap became loose, sloppy-fitting and no longer provided a secure seal. This Stant cap replacement fixed the problem providing a very solid secure solution with the single downside of not coming with any convenient tether…an inconvenience issue. I read many of the reviews addressing this issue before my purchase but chose to buy it anyway. So I was “forewarned is forearmed” prepared…and I easily could have been content. However…

I studied the original tethered gas cap and found it was designed to work by having a sliding “ring/collar” that easily slid around to accommodate the required movement when tightening and loosening the cap for refueling. If you knew this prior to getting rid of it and installing the new STANT cap you might get a reward for your attention to detail. I pried that sliding collar-ring off the original…then studied the new STANT gas cap.

The original had a 7 mm. wide, indented/recessed portion [pathway] along the outside perimeter of the cap which was designed to retain yet allow the ring-collar to slide easily. The collar was made of semi-rigid material but with perseverance it could be removed without damage. [Maybe some silicone spray might make it even easier to remove.]

The new STANT designed cap came with 16 thin “ribs” for better gripping along the outside perimeter. The original tethered collar wouldn’t slide onto the new cap…at least not yet. The ribs measured about 11mm…top to bottom…and the collar was only about 7mm wide so you see the possibilities…

Are you a craftsy person? Using a Dremmel grinding/cutting tool at lowest possible speed [and wearing eye protection] I removed the lower 7 mm of each rib and left the top remaining 4 mm intact. [OK, so I did smooth 2 of the ribs all the way so I easily fed the collar onto the new STANTcap.] Doing this I created the recessed pathway for the OEM tethered collar to be mounted onto the STANT 10841. Now, good as or better than new as received.

It worked absolutely great for my Aveo.

product_title: EM-AS-SPCD-VR
Hi-Gear NX5680e Nanotechnology Glass Treatment
review_body: Sorry, I've tried just about every glass cleaner and home concoction since I got my first car some 45 years ago.  I can honestly say.....nothing works as advertised.  Sure, on a cloudy day or when your windshield and door windows are not in direct sunlight, all the glass cleaners seem to leave the "perfect" shine.  With this particular product, I washed my car and dried it with a microfiber drying cloth. Very nice results.  Then I followed directions and began applying this product.  After applying, I wiped again with a new microfiber cloth.  Again, a second time, I used a brand new microfiber cloth to go over all the windows.  Wow!  All the windows looked great!  It was just like so many comments - "like the glass was invisible". Problem was, it was a rather cloudy day.  Later that day, driving into the setting sun, I could clearly see smudges, streaks etc.  Everything you don't want to see after you worked so hard to clean.  Just like a developing cure for male pattern baldness, a glass/windshield cleaner that truly works will be a long time coming.  I think the truth is, if you really want a smudge-free, streak-free windshield you just have to buy a brand new car right off the showroom floor.

product_title: Maxic White Car Emergency Jump Starter with Power Bank for Phones and Portable Devices (Rechargeable, LED Readout Protection, LiPo Battery, Flashlight)
review_body:
I used to drive across country a few times a year. I got in the habit of being very prepared an stocking my car with tools, lighters, blankets, etc to ensure that I was prepared for any number of emergencies. I don't drive more than 30 miles nowadays, but I still can't resist a good car gadget. Most of them go in my wife's car (whether she wants them or not) to ensure that she's prepared for any issues during her commute.

The Maxic Compass intrigued me instantly. A little white box that can jump-start my car? You've got to be kidding me. I snatched it up eager to test it out. Left my light on overnight to drain my battery (I have a full size Forney battery charger in the garage, so I wasn't worried if the Compass didn't live up to its hype). Plugged the jump adapter into the box (couldn't be simpler) and attached the alligator clips to the battery terminals. The read-out on the digital display said OK and sure enough, started right up.

It has several features that protect you, the battery and the unit. The most common you'd probably see is the NG readout on the digital display. This means that the battery is fine and it will not force current to it, which is great if you don't want to deal with a melted car battery. I do think they could've used something other than NG because, if I'm someone who hasn't read the manual, NG means nothing to me. Other than that, it's extremely straightforward, easy to operate and user friendly.

It has a nice carrying case that holds all sorts of adapters for cellphones/etc as well as the unit and the jumper cables. It easily fits under your car seat or in your spare tire.

The unit has a flashlight built in and USB and cigarette lighter outlet. You can charge your phone, etc. It seems to hold its charge very effectively, I haven't had it for more than a month so I can't say how long it lasts but I would think quite awhile.

Overall, this is a phenomenal device to have in any car. Great for kids going off to college, wives and husbands alike. You never know when you're going to be stuck somewhere and it's surprising how few people keep jumper cables in their cars these days.nds alike. review_headline: The wiring is medium duty (not bad, but not great)

I wanted to install the H4 bulb conversion kit, but without getting 12 - 14.4 volts what was the point.  I saw this and figured that it was a lot easier than making a harness myself (and cheaper too).  I took less than a hour to install with adding extra wire loom to cover any expose wiring, and now I have 14.4 volts to the lights.  The wiring is medium duty (not bad, but not great).  It works great for me with the 65/55 watt bulbs. IMO if you are going to install the offroad 100 watts bulbs I would change either make your own or replace the wiring going from the relay to the bulbs (they sell just the connector plug) with 12-14 gauge.  The rest of the wiring is fine.

product_title: Vega Altura Full Face Helmet
review_headline: A decent hlemet but order one size larger. Good construction for the $$.
review_body: I purchased this helmet for doing the MSF course at a local Tech College. I wear a size 7 1/4" hat (22 1/2" head diameter) . . . I thought a Large would fit . . . BUT - - - - - - - NOTE:  Sizes run small as others have said. I was going to order a Large, but went with the X-Large. Glad I did. It fits perfect. I can get it it on and it is snug. I tried other more expensive helmets in size Large at motor sports shops and a Large usually fir fine. So if you are ordering I suggest you go one size larger than you think.   Otherwise a very nice helmet, well made for the price, plenty of inside trim and padding and the all important shock absorbing foam. Also, I like that the shield locks in several positions. In the rain, I can lift the shield up one notch so that it is open at the bottom and it lets air in but no rain. This eliminates fogging and keeps you cooler also.  Note ALSO. . . product_title: Kinetix Racing KX-HFC-DE-Z33 High Flow Catalytic Converters, Smog Legal - Nissan 350Z 2003-2006 Z33 / Infiniti G35 03-06 Sedan / G35 03-07 Coupe V35 VQ35DE
review_headline: You need this - even if your catalytic converter is not bad
review_body:
I cannot believe how happy I am with this purchase. I was nervous at first purchasing something as important as this for my car being that it is aftermarket. Little bit about my situation. My check engine light came on so I took it to my local mechanic that has done some jobs I didn't feel like doing. They are also fairly priced. They said my Catalytic Converter was bad and that it was just shy of $1200 with parts and labor. They would need the car for a day. At first i thought it was a lot but I knew they were expensive, at least the OEM ones. I was going to have them do it until I looked around and found really good reviews online about Kinetix Racing so I decided to bite the bullet and try it.

First impression of them is that they are fairly light weight, the welds on them are very good, made in CA,USA it says so on the pipe. Very clean design compared to the OEM one. This does come with the hardware required.

Pros - Great Design, Fits perfect with no mods on my car but also fits aftermarket exhaust.
GREAT sound, Sounds beefer but nothing crazy
It did increase power, I was very surprised. My car is quite a bit more peppy. It just wants to get up and go where before it bogged a little. Throttle response is a lot better now.
Cons - I can not think of any. It has been less than 24 hours since install and I was so pleased I had to write a review. If something comes up I will update my review but I don't see any problems in my future. I did not take any pictures but I can jack the car up and take some if people need them.

The install is fairly easy. It took me and a buddy just over 2 hours taking our time. Going slow BSing while were doing it. They're a total of 8 bolts/nuts and 2 nuts that need to be taken off due to the headers coming out have one welded on each side. So 10 nuts total that need to be removed. On the video I seen online they take off the air intake on both sides due to it being dual air intakes which my car does not have. I was able to get a long extension from up top for each of the right and left sides. The rest of the bolts i was able to get from the bottom of the car. YOU WILL NEED GASKETS. I would recommend buying new ones don't try saving the old ones. Kinetex Racing does make them/sell them.

I used TEKTON 14967 3/8-Inch Drive Flex Head Bent Handle Ratchet - this wrench was a LIFE SAVER. My buddy kept saying it was made for this job. It really was the only reason I did not have to remove the air intake and some radiator hoses and such. BIG HELP. Excellent quality and you can't beat the price.

TEKTON 1610 3/8-Inch Drive Extra Long Extension Bar Set, 3-Piece - This was essential for getting the bolt from each side up top unless you want
to put a bunch of extensions together. It was also helpful on the bottom nuts that you can put this on it cause they are in tight spots and use a ratcheting wrench to loosen instead of getting just a few clicks and having to go back.

Powerbuilt 648691 Oxygen Sensor Offset Puller - This is a great tool to have, Worked perfect. Fits all o2 sensors and worked great for this job.

TEKTON 1919 Stubby Combination Wrench Set, Metric, 10-Piece - Just needed the 14mm from this but it is a great set.

Only tools needed for this is 3/8 14mm Deep Socket, Shallow Socket,
3/8 Ratcheting Wrench, 14mm wrench(ratcheting is nice , not needed)
3/8 Extensions - 1/4 10mm Deep Socket for oxygen sensor clip so you can easily get the sensor off.
I had an impact wrench just to tighten the bolts. It is a 12v Milwaukee, Wow was i surprised with its power. You obviously don't need this. But nice.
Is a good idea to have a breaker bar. I have a 18" craftsman that worked great.

Be happy to answer any questions. If you are in need of a new Cat, you NEED this. Even if you don't need one but want another few HP and better sound and little more pep to you vehicle.Get this. You will not be disappointed.

Before this job I had no Tekton tools just craftsman and I will be purchasing more from them. I feel like I could be a salesmen for Kinetex Racing & Tekton.
