These are solid, durable tape measures. We have a basic metal tape measure, but I like these better because of their use of rubber around the edge. It helps hold the tape measure better. It has both a manual and a lock button. The manual prevents the tape from disappearing on you. The lock makes it stay where it is.

Why have all three rather than just have the biggest one for all jobs? I'd only use the big one for big jobs because it's hard to keep the manual button down due to its larger size. The tape slides right out, but it took work pull the large one out once I get past 10 feet. Was afraid it'd give me a paper cut ( can just tell it'll cut me if I'm not careful) or swallow it up and hit me. I bravely pulled it all the way out to 26 feet and let go. It didn't slap me.

Obviously, smallest one is easiest to manage. Then why not just have small and large? Having worked with all three, it makes sense to have multiple sizes. Most people probably keep the smallest one in their desk drawer while the other two would sit somewhere in the garage for occasional projects.

Be careful about pulling out the tape all the way to the very end. It can get stuck. It has a STOP mark to prevent you from going too far. Like any other measuring tape, the tape itself has clear markings using black and red. It uses red to mark every 10 millimeters. It also marks feet using a red or black background (it's black on 16') for every feet and a red font for pointing out feet and inches as in 1'1" and 5'5" so you do have to do the math to convert inches to feet.

I have a 16-feet WorkForce Auto-Stop. I like the grip of the Ford better. The WorkForce, however, is stiff to let you control its movement.This can be an advantage over the Ford because it can be hard to prevent the tape from slipping back in. The manual lock doesn't always hold effortlessly. It's probably a matter of preference. People who have dexterity issues will prefer the Auto-Stop version.

The tape is nylon coated on the top side. Not sure of the benefit, but it's good quality. The labeling looks like good quality. A reviewer complained it looked like something printed on a home printer. I don't see that, but in comparison to the WorkForce the Ford's tape is wider and printing is bigger and more readable. (See photos.)

Each one comes with a belt clip and a wrist strap. The wrist strap can get caught. You can either remove it or tie it into a knot to prevent catching.

A couple reviewers commented on the Ford branding. I don't really care about the brand. Just want it to do the job. It's not like I'm wearing this out in public and want people to see what tape measure I drive :)top version.

review_headline: KENSUN HID H11 with Slim Ballast
review_body:
Got these as a Father's Day gift from the GF. Had these installed within 20 mins on my 2015 Toyota Camry. There is no need for any modification to the existing vehicle or wiring harness. There another reviews from another buyer stating the received the wrong bulb. Unfortunately, he does not know what bulbs are for the high beams and what bulbs are for the low beams.

Pros:
* Light spectrum match OE HID (bought the 6K). Compared this HID to my brother's OE 2010 Evo Lancer.
* Way brighter than the OE halogen.
* Plug and play. No mods to the current harness
* Aluminum shipping box. Very good presentation before opening the box.
* Assurance of excellent customer service.

Cons:
* Wished the description of the product informed me of getting 20A fuses to replace the OE 15A fuses. Found that the HID install required 20A replacement when reading the install manual.
* Although my vehicle didn't require the optional relay, they should probably have the HID with relay all in one package for those that are not technical on what items they need.
* Better layout of product when you open the box. Seems like they just threw all the items in the box.

Anyways, love these lights and will update this review later on down the road on how they perform in the long run.

review_body:
I have a 2007 Lincoln Navigator with a 5.4 3v V-8. My driver side cam phaser started to rattle at 800rpm once the engine reached optimal running temperature. So I replaced both cam phasers and both valve solenoids. So the only part I used was the wedge but wanted the entire kit for the price.
Now the tool only works IF your timing chain guides and tensioner haven't failed. If your guides are broke, you will not need this since you will have to disassemble the entire timing set anyway.
Make you have it wedged well in between the chain so it doesn't fall. This part of changing the phasers is easy compared to disassembling the top of the motor just to get the valve covers off.
I am mechanically inclined and this took me about 8-10 hours to complete.
DONT BUY THE DORMAN PHASERS OR SOLENIODS. You WILL be redoing this once they fail in 3000 miles. Get them from Ford!

product_title: Air Power America 5060TS Topsider Multi-Purpose Fluid Removing System
review_body:
I used this on a 2006 Mini Cooper S.
My vehicle has very low clearance so it's difficult to jack it up and even when I do there is little clearance. I also have a skid plate installed on the subframe so it makes the oil draining a mess (a lot will go on top of the skid plate). This oil extractor is something I needed to buy when I got this car. It's so easy to use and so clean. The directions are very straightforward. Warm up the engine (I drove mine around the block but it got a little too warm), aim for 1/4 to 1/3 (maybe 160 F) on the temp gauge. Clamp the hose and hand pump 30-40 times to form a nice vacuum. Insert the hose down the dipstick until you feel it stop, pull it back 1/4" or so and release the clamp. The oil should suck out (it will take a 10-15+ min depending on how much you have). When I did it the oil was a little too cool (was too hot at first and let it sit for too long) and it took around 1/2 hour. Then I was a little anxious and pulled the oil filter too early and made a mess anyway. :(
Next time I'll do a better job.

product_title: Flowmaster 17129 Header-back System - Dual Rear Exit - American Thunder - Moderate/Aggressive
review_body:
I installed this system on a '68 Firebird convertable. The Flowmaster description says "will not fit convertable". It will. There is an "X" brace on the convertable's that you have to remove. You can either leave it off, ( The brace is designed to keep the trans tunnel from crushing in the event of a side impact. It has no effect on the floor pan flexing, as some may suggest. ) or you can buy a modified brace from Pypes exhaust systems. DON'T BOTHER !!! I bought one and it was a joke. It didn't even come close to mounting up. The bolt holes were a mile off, and even if they were in the right place, once bolted up it was so low that it would drag the ground constantly !!! The pipes don't need that much clearance, as there brace was spaced so far from the floor pan there was 2" between the brace and the pipes in some spots. Just a bad, not well designed product. I did put the "X" brace back on the Firebird I installed this kit on by using longer bolts and 3/8" inside diameter thick wall spacers I cut to the appropriate lengths needed for the brace to mount back up and clear the pipes. ( Longer in the front, shorter in the rear.)
As far as the quality and fit of this kit, It is excellent !!!! It does install fairly easy if you have mechanical skills, as there is cutting to fit the front pipes. Both for length and width. Other than that it bolts right up and clears everything very well. The tubing is thick walled and aluminized coated, all the hardware needed is supplied. The mufflers are the Super 44 series, are they sound awesome. For some people this system may bit a bit loud. My customer changed the mufflers out to the 50 series after he and his wife drove the car a few times. They loved the sound of the car, but after cruising around for several hours they wanted it a little quieter. Keep in mind that was a convertable.
I have always loved Flowmasters products and this was no exception. I am using this same kit on my own '68 Camaro SS 350 hardtop.

Very happy this is sold as a complete unit - easy swap - and again, the price was a no-brainer. Search for video to see the tricks on install - would normally take 30 minutes start to finish - key for me was to tilt the passenger-side "up" first to rotate the unit out... otherwise, you need to push / flex the radiator hose out of the way to get one of the mounting brackets to clear (literally, that was the hardest part.).

product_title: Kensun® Portable Power Bank and Car Jump Starter
review_headline: An essential product for today's mobile-driven world
review_body:
Almost everyone in modern civilization as of 2015 has a cell phone, tablet device, or other portable technology. And 99% of all mobile devices out there depend on USB technology for their power source. Albeit USB technology is getting a bit dated, it has become the universal standard for many companies to depend on for charging the internal battery of their products. To make matters worse, products made by companies like Apple (and now even Samsung) design their devices in ways where they cannot be disassembled to change the battery easily. That is where a product like Kensun's Portable Mini USB mobile power bank supply comes in!

As in its name, the Kensun USB power bank supply is exactly that; a portable power bank that contains a USB port for all your mobile technology needs. You can pretty much plug in any device that depends on USB technology to charge and this device will charge it! I would say in most common cases that is going to be a mobile cell phone or tablet. For my testing, I tested this device with the HTC One X, Apple iPhone 6, Samsung Galaxy S5, and an iPad generation 2 tablet. I am much pleased to say that, after an average of at least 3+ charges on each device with lower than 30% battery life, this device typically charged on average under an impressive 30 minutes! The product on average takes about 2-3 hours to charge plugged into my high-end desktop computer. I would say, about as long as your phone or tablet takes is how long this product takes to charge. Even during running apps, games, and other high end applications of all these products, this product still charged in roughly 30 minutes for me, faster than it would in a computer or other device.

With all that being said, this is Kensun's smaller power supply, so you most typically will only get one charge out of it before having to recharge as it's power bank holds 2600mAh. But, in practicality, this device doubles the battery life of all your mobile technology. Also, I highly recommend this as a safety and emergency device. Whether you are a common traveler or not, this is a vital and important product to carry with you wherever you go. USB charging is not always at hand and this product makes up for that. This is especially nice technology to have on air flights and bus trips.

I own other Kensun products including their portable tire inflator. I would not leave home without either of these products in my car for emergencies. For an astoundingly low price of $14.99, this thing is a steal. You can have double the battery life for any of your mobile products at hand. Lastly as an IT professional, I highly recommend this product as an emergency and safety device that you should always carry with you if you are ever put into a predicament where you need your cellphone and the batter is dead.

product_title: Beck Arnley 103-2964 Constant Velocity Joint Boot Kit
review_headline: Prof Automotive Tech with 30+years exp says 5 STARS!
review_body:
I have a 2005 Subaru Forester 2.5x. I also have a ton of automotive experience as a professional, in case that carries any weight.

I virtually NEVER buy parts that aren't OEM anymore. 30 years ago it was a whole different story, but nowadays, a lifetime warranty just means a lifetime of changing the same inferior part over and over again in most cases. These boots are a whole different animal though.

When I replaced the clutch in my Forrester a few years ago, I replaced the half-shafts in the front as well, given both boots were torn, and I had no idea how long they had been run that way. (I'd just purchased the car used) There are a LOT of real bad reman halfshafts out there. I bought my shafts from Annapolis Subaru. (I get real decent pricing thought them and they ship worldwide. If you want to give them a whirl, talk to Jackie in the parts department. She's a sweet gal, and a WIZ KID TOO!)

4 months later, wasn't I dealing with a cross-ship on the passenger side shaft again? There is nothing cutting that boot, it just failed for some odd reason. New shaft goes in, and doesn't the same (outer) boot fail again in 8 months?! Needless to say, I was NOT a happy camper, but one definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again, expecting a different result. I decided to take a different tack just to see what would happen.

I bought this boot right here on Amazon and re-booted the affected CV joint right away. 1 year 10 months later, still working just fine.

Why people give a product that works properly three star reviews and say, "It probably this and probably that," based on NO ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE is beyond me. That kind of review, or, "help," is in no way helpful to me at ALL.

If you do not know how to install the bands properly, you are NOT going to be happy with the result.

If you buy dental tools and are not qualified to use them, but do so anyway, you're probably not going to be real happy there either, but really, PLEASE DON'T WRITE A REVIEW ABOUT THE PRODUCT IF YOU NEVER SHOULD HAVE BEEN USING IT IN THE FIRST PLACE!

Anyhow, I had an OEM installed boot fail once in 4 months, and again in 8. This boot has been running fro 22 months without issue, so as far as I'm concerned, yeah, 5 stars! Why would it rate any less?

product_title: 40mm Dia Self-Adhesive Back Car Rearview Blindspot Mirror Black 2 Pcs
review_body:
On my last truck, I had adjustable blind spot mirrors due to the very large blind spots it had up the side of the vehicle.

When I got my new Jeep Grand Cherokee, I found that not only was visibility poor, but the side mirrors did nothing useful to help me see. While the Jeep has an option to tilt the side mirrors down when reversing, I found that was a pain and it didn't solve the issue of seeing properly when changing lanes. I decided I needed another set of blind spot mirrors.

The problem is, unlike my truck, the mirrors on the GC are kind of small. The 2\\" mirrors I previously used would have covered too much of the mirror surface.

After searching, I finally found these mirrors.

So far, they are working great. While small, they work perfectly to allow me to see when changing lanes as well as view lines and curbs when parking.

The only issue is, unlike my larger adjustable mirrors I previously had, these are easier to accidentally move out of position when cleaning the mirrors. After the first time it happened, I simply started being more careful and it hasn't been an issue since.

Since I have heated mirrors, only time will tell how the hold up in extreme cold, then heat of the mirror warmer. At least I don't have to scrape the mirrors, which should prevent accidentally knocking them off.

product_title: 2PCS CARCHET CREE-XPE Q5 LED Festoon Light Lamp Bulb White Car Interior 31MM
review_headline: These Carchet LEDs are on a whole nother level. VERY, VERY, VERY bright. All other LED interior bulbs pale in comparison.
review_body:
OMG these are the real deal!

I had already changed from the factory bulbs to another brand LED for my dome and map lights. On those, the BEST I could find increased the light 50% over stock. This was using a digital light meter I bought on Amazon a few years ago. With these, its a whole new level. Here the details:

Testing the overhead map lights:

Stock bulbs: 10-15 Lux at the console/shifter area, both maps lights on
Prev. LED: 20-25 Lux at the console/shifter area, both maps lights on
These Carchet LEDs, 80-95 Lux at the console/shifter area, both maps lights on

(this is with the diffuser off in all cases. When you put the diffuser back in, it drops all the light output by about 40%. Its not really dropping it, but spreading it out, but the light meter can only measure one place at a time.

When I put these in my wife's Rav4 (2006), rear dome light:

At the seat cushion level:

Factory: 7-11 Lux
Prev. LEDs: 10-15 Lux
These: 40+ Lux

No joke. These are the real deal. In my car (Subaru Impreza) Having the dome light on (1 unit) and both map lights on (2), the interior of the car is like an office in any building. You could do lab experiments with the light these things put out.

Now the down side:

#1, I have NO IDEA how long these will last. In my experience, super bright LEDs only last a very short time. However, based on how long your dome light and map lights are on, and the fact these have heat sinks on them, these could last years. Only time will tell.

Another selling point is that, since the GOOFIT starter relay is designed for ATVs and DirtBikes, it fits well with student projects. It is not heavy on the pocket when compared with other car-related relays but can easily fire up engines with lesser displacement.

product_title: Nissan Altima Spoiler Painted in the Factory Paint Code of Your Choice
review_body:
If you have a nice car get nice stuff for it. I bought this thinking that it couldn't be that bad because of all the good reviews. The stock Nissan spoiler or wing or whatever you want to call it sits flush on the trunk lid and is sealed off. This one comes with 6 screws and no weather seal. It doesn't come with the 35¢ plug for the brake harness so you either have to splice the wires in or track down the connector which is a pain in the butt to find. After about 2 weeks I noticed some white powder at the edge of the spoiler, it was vibrating and rubbed through the paint on the trunk lid on both ends at the forward lip of the wing. I ended up having to take it off and fix it before it started to rust then sealed the forward edge to the trunk lid to try to keep it from vibrating and keep water from collecting under the wing. There are spots where the paint was so thin that you can see the black plastic through it as well. For less than $100 you get what you pay for.

It would be a really good deal for a 1992 Honda Civic but I would never suggest putting this on a newer car. Spend the extra $300 to get the factory wing, it may look the same but it mounts to the trunk lid securely and won't cause issues later on.

product_title: ClipperCreek LCS-20, 240V, 16 Amp, Level 2 EV Charging Station, Hardwired, 25 Ft Cable, SAFETY CERTIFIED, Made in America
review_headline: Completely adequate and well built charging station - MADE IN USA!
review_body:
How can I not love this charge station? It's less than $400, and you can install it yourself. Originally I thought of buying the unit that comes with a connecting cable and plug for 240VAC, but the only plug offered by ClipperCreek is the NEMA 14-30 which is a 30 amp plug and of course requires a 30 amp matching socket. I have 240VAC on my wall in my garage, with a NEMA 6-20R receptacle, and I saw no need to change that out when all you use for this device is a steady 15 amp draw, well within the capacity of the 20 amp breakers. ClipperCreek's decision to use the 30 amp plug is confusing, to say the least.

I was pleased to find, when I opened the box, that a 36 inch power source cable is already attached, with plastic armor. The 12 gauge red, green, and black wires are stranded copper, and easy to form. All I had to do was find a NEMA 6-20P plug that would clamp the armor and wires properly, attach the plug, and mount the charge station on a plywood board and I was ready to go. I saved hundreds of dollars in the final cost.

As far as the speed of charge is concerned, when you are at home, why spend money on a fast charge cable when you can get a full charge in just a few hours with this 240VAC cable at considerably less expense? You can always get the fast charge on the road.

Finally, to check my installation, I used a thermal meter during charge to check for any resistivity problems, as you can see in the photos. The highest temp was from the unwound cable bundle during a charge, which was 105.4 degrees Fahrenheit, no problem. All in all I am very happy with this product.

product_title: WeatherTech Trim to Fit Front Rubber Mats (Black)
review_headline: Pros Thick Rubber Easy to Clean Holds well Cons They didn’t fit in ...
review_body:
Pros
Thick Rubber
Easy to Clean
Holds well

Cons
They didn’t fit in more than 5 places
Rubber mats do not look or feel good on carpeted flooring
Bad customer service
Bad return policy

I needed both mats for a 2003 Nissan 350Z. The website has all sorts of claims about how well their mats fit. This is not true in my case.

They were not a perfect laser-measured fit. They were not even a good fit. They gapped in more than 5 places. I had no intentions to return the mats, and I wanted Weathertech to succeed, so I contacted them by email just to let them know the mats do not fit the 350Z well.
When I contacted Weathertech by email, Mr Heisler told me in several emails that I was reviewing the website incorrectly, and if they weren’t a perfect fit, they were most certainly a very good fit. I responded that the website should really make it clearer. He then sent me screenshots of the website with areas circled where I was quite obviously wrong. After his 3rd demeaning email on how wrong I was, I showed the mats and emails to several friends who told me flat out to return the mats.
They did take the mats back, however I had to eat the shipping, and I didn’t see the partial refund for weeks. For the same amount of money, I bought mats from Nissan. They were of better quality, and they fit perfectly.
Summary: Had Weathertech treated me better through email, or even returned my shipping (as this was clearly not my fault they sent me mats that didn’t fit), I would not have returned the mats, even though they didn’t fit. In addition, I’ve talked to others interested in mats, and my experience has cost Weathertech more sales.

product_title: MotorKote 1gal Hyper Lubricant
review_body: So after using this stuff in 4 different vehicles engine oil and transmission, I think its about time to leave a review.  For starters, I build airsoft guns on the side, (gear driven & ball bearings).  Motorkote grease and lube has exceeded everything else I have tried (including militech-1) on ball bearings and continuous (dry) lubrication.  So after passing that test I used it in my current vehicle's oil at the time (2003 saab 9-3ss 2.0t)  it idled noticeably smoother and felt smoother to drive, definitely helped on cold starts, however I was still scared to put it in my transmission.  The first transmission I treated was a 1998 dodge intrepid that shifted pretty rough, when i first added we noticed the transmission slipping just ever so slightly, ~300 miles later you don't even know its shifting.  After that I treated a ~2002 f150 transmission, it immediately improved and got even better after a couple hundred miles, and finally my saab 9-3, I treated the transission, and it slipped pretty bad a couple of times (literally 2 times, once at high rpm and once going up an incline)  needless to say I was pretty upset, but after a few hundred miles its in the same boat as the other two.  So yes I definitely recommend it.

product_title: Lisle Drake Off Road Tools 56650 Adjustable Seal Puller
review_headline: This tool may cause more grief than joy
review_body: Oil seals are a pain to extract (especially if they've been in there for a decade or more) because of the oxidation that builds around them and because they are fit in very tightly for good reason.  When using this tool, you can't see how deep the sharp hook goes.  In my case, it went through the wall of the seal and into the bearing carrier of my outboard's lower unit gauging it badly.  Don't use the top of the bearing carrier as fulcrum or the bearing carrier top will break as it did for me.  Bearing carriers aren't made of steel but an aluminum allow, it seems, which is soft yet brittle.  I used an epoxy compound paste to fix the gauges and luckily the top of the carrier didn't break deep enough to expose the new bearing seals so I should be OK there.  But after sanding the walls of the carrier to prepare for the epoxy and again sanding the epoxy after setting, my seals may fit too losely in there.  If that turns out to be the case, I'll have to replace the bearing carrier.  Instead of using this tool (especially if you haven't used it before), go to youtube and look for a 3-part "how to replace oil seals on a lower unit" and use that guy's method (drill 2 holes in each of the seals, drive screws through them, and use a slide hammer to pull them out.  This way you will have no damage to the walls and top of the carrier, or the shaft.  Good luck!

product_title: OPT7 Fluxbeam LED Headlight Kit - All Bulb Sizes - 60w 7,000Lms 6K Cool White CREE - 2 Yr Warranty
review_body:
Less bright than the 4300k HID headlights. Also the beam is not as clear and far as HID headlights. I know many say "oh you get instant brightness" but ask yourself is waiting maybe 30 seconds (max) worth losing about 30% brightness permanently? I mean HID gets brighter as it lights on, it is not like it takes 30seconds for light to come on. During the wait time the light is equal to or even brighter than these LED headlights. Also the lights give a blue tint which makes it almost unless in rain/fog. Beam pattern is wide and bright close to your car but further away it is weak and cannot light up the road very good (I have projector housing not sure about reflectors). If you are upgrading from Halogens then you will really see a big difference in brightness. If you are changing from HIDs 4300k or 5000k you will be 20-30% less brightness.

They claim 7000lm and that is because each bulb gives raw output of 3500lm. There are 2 LED diodes per bulb which means each LED diode puts out 1750lm. Remember this is raw output which means if you factor in losses from positioning of the LED diode, beam pattern losses, and loss of light from your headlight housing, it really does not give you 7000Lumens of usable light to the road. You cannot simply add up all the Lumens each LED puts out and think you will have the same usable light. I think that is a marketing tactic to make us think it is super bright.

For 99$ I do not believe it is worth it. Also guys beware as the HB3 (9005) bulbs do not fit the same in all cars. It fit nicely on my one of my cars but does not fit in the other. Also these WILL NOT WORK if you are trying to do a DRL/HIGH Beam set up. The LEDs will stay lit and bright. It will be as if you have high beams on at all time. It will also flicker because LED's are not meant to run a set up like this. There are other same quality items other there for cheaper if you want to run LED highlights. Only benefit is OPT7 offers a nice return policy. Warranty, mostly all other sellers offer the same free replacement.

product_title: XtremepowerUS 12v Fluid Oil Diesel Extractor + Tubes Truck Rv Boat ATV
review_headline: Malibu VLX Oil Change made easy!
review_body:
I purchased this oil extractor after trying to build one myself with an expensive 100 pump and failing because I did not realize oil would clog it. I didn't have high hopes for this pump as it is cheap and there are bad reviews for similar style/looking pumps on amazon. I bit the bullet and made the purchase anyway because I wanted a more efficient way of draining the oil and other fluids from my boat.

I have a 2006 Malibu VLX with a Monsoon 340 Engine. There are 2 ways to drain the oil that I know of. 1 using an oil extractor, electric or hand pump style sticking a small tube through your dip stick and letting the oil drain into a bucket. The other by taking the hose that is connected to the bottom of the oil pan and running it through the hull, unscrew the cap and wait over night and your oil should be drained. I don't care for running the smaller tube through the dip stick as I feel there is still some oil left. I'm not patient enough for option 2.

I took this pump and added my own tubing that I connected to the hose via a series of adapters and it works wonderfully! Couldn't be happier, this has saved me a lot of time and money from taking the boat to the stealership. Be sure to warm up the boat, if its in your driveway like mine I used a Moeller Flushrite Boat Motor Flusher which gets the job done.

product_title: Dorman 590-001 Fuel Pump Driver Module
review_headline: Excellent replacement for a problem/part FORD should have recalled in the first place.
review_body:
I did not actually receive this item - I needed it next day, yet due to winter storm it got delayed so I had to buy it from local parts store. Its the exact same item and model number that I purchased. I would have rather of purchased through Amazon because it was ~$80 cheaper.

This was used for a 2007 Ford F150. If your ford stops delivering fuel (will not start with good battery, ie: keeps turning over) replace this. Some mechanics misdiagnose this problem as a faulty fuel pump, which is VERY expensive to replace (fuel pump is inside fuel tank, so you can imagine the labor, etc to get a fuel pump replaced).

The original part that Ford uses for a Fuel Pump Driver Module ends up degrading and falling apart from the backside (part that is mounted against metal) - most likely you can not tell the original part's overall seal has been breached by just looking at it because the plastic part faces outwards and will look fine.

This is a -VERY SIMPLE- fix that I feel ANYONE can replace - two bolts, most common local is next to spare tire in back (look for videos if needed).

This product comes with spacers so that THIS Fuel Pump Driver Model does NOT sit against metal directly and will (most likely) not degrade and malfunction.

Excellent replacement product that FORD should have put out a recall for (along with their spark plugs), in regards to the 2004-2008 model years (although I believe they used this part for the next model as well, at least for most of that models year makes.

Under $100 (OVER $100 at local store) fix that involves two bolts and a quick connect wire harness. Simple fix, big problem solved.

Unless you live in an area with NO humidity (usually it is salt - in the air or on the road to melt snow - that causes the original to start its metal/metal chemical degradation process) I would recommend buying this even if you DONT need it yet (and, of course, you own a Ford F150, Explorer (etc) 2004-2008, 2009-2010). You WILL need it along with replacing the spark plugs with a special tool because they will break off in the engine (replace the 100k mile plugs before 75k if possible).

product_title: Moonet Fuel Brake Foot Rest MT Pedals Fit BMW X1 E30 E36 E46 E90 E91 E92 E93 M3
review_headline: Cool idea, terrible unsafe execution IMO
review_body:
Upside: They look really good, and I think are much better looking overall than the OWM metal pedals you can order from BMW.

Downside:

1. To install, you need to drill the pedals, which is fine, except the problem of the screws and nuts showing through the on the back of the pedal - which even if cut down - create a space where you can't put the gas pedal all the way down as before, nor the brake pedal. Which scares me a great deal. I bought a performance car so I could accelerate fast and brake fast. But if I can't get the full throw of the pedals, what's the point? You might be able to re-map the pedal travel if you are a car coder, but I'm not. And even if you used self tapping screws and cut them off right at the end of the pre-existing metal plate, I'm not sure I have the confidence they'll stay in place with so little thread to hold them in place into the thin metal pedals. If I mash the pedals or torque my feet as I move between them due to error or intent, perhaps while practicing my best heal-toe rev-matching downshifts, a loose pedal that moves, slides, or otherwise gets jammed is very very bad news. Even if you thought you could lock these in palce with some super-epoxy, the problem is that these are really two piece items, the rubber that sticks through is actually the full sizer of the metal pad, with ridges that stick out between the grooves, so glueing the pedals in place wouldn't work either.
2. For my E90 2008 M3 6MT, the foot rest (far left in image) was about an inch too short.
3. It looks close to the M logo, but it's not quite there. Not a big deal, but you'd notice it.

product_title: MotoBatt MBTX16U (12V 19 Amp) 250CCA Factory Activated QuadFlex AGM Battery
review_headline: the battery in my motorcycle went bad. My bike is a Suzuki Intruder 1500cc and ...
review_body:
This is my second MotoBatt. A little over two years ago, the battery in my motorcycle went bad. My bike is a Suzuki Intruder 1500cc and needs a lot of power to crank over the motor. I searched the web and Amazon before deciding to buy this battery. My main reason for buying this battery was the CCA rating and the price. Yes, there were batteries with a higher CCA but the cost was outrageous.

I bought the battery in Feb of 2013 and it finely gave up on me in May of 2015 (just out of warranty). I would be upset about it dying in 2 years, but this seems to be the norm.

I was searching for a replacement and again I could not find a battery with a higher CCA rating for this price or less. I did find a Lithium Iron battery from battery tender (higher CCA but more expensive), but I read a lot of negative reviews about that type of battery in cold weather. Being that I do drive in 30 degree weather, I decided to stay with what I knew worked. Also, I just got a battery tender a few months ago which should make this new battery live further past the two year mark. Note, if you get a Lithium Iron battery you need a special battery tender for it. The one I have would not work which is another reason I decided not to go with Lithium Iron.

I put the battery in the bike, hooked up the charger (it did take a little charge) and fired the bike right up. A good battery at a great price (plus I know it works).

It rained overnight. The next morning, the rotors were covered in rust. I've dealt with this crap for quite some time and the rust is unbelievable. The worst offense happened as I was trying to replace these. They had rusted onto the hub (understandable). There are two threaded holes that are used to drive bolts through to break the rotor off the hub. I was HAND tightening these bolts with a ratchet thinking, "These should be breaking off soon." when I noticed what looked like three cracks forming around the one bolt hole. After a few more cranks, sure enough, there WERE cracks forming. The other threaded hole did the same. I decided to continue to tighten in the hopes that this stupid rotor would come off my hub. I BROKE the rotor. The metal is so cheap, it continued to crack and distort like modeling clay. I have NEVER had this happen before, no matter how old the vehicle. In the end, the holes were utterly useless (stripped) and I had to revert to other means of removal.

review_headline: Long but worth the read, 6 month post-purchase review
review_body:
Initially I'd purchased a set of these bulbs. They arrived quickly and installed easily, looked great. Such a deal compared to the nearly $200 that Autozone/Napa had charged. I was thrilled.

About 6 months into owning them, one bulb began to flicker. Shortly after that started, it would flicker then go out after hitting bumps in the road. I swapped it to the passenger side to rule out bad housing/connection, but nope, it's the bulb.

Upset, I left a mediocre review here, voicing my displeasure in the longevity of the bulb. Within an hour I received an email from Bradley from their customer service team asking me to explain the circumstances of the failure a bit better. He quickly responded again and shipped a replacement pair to my house. In 4 days I had them replaced, and they look great.

Now I can say that this seller absolutely values his reputation here. He is prompt, stands behind this product, and aims to please us as customers.

I was shocked that he'd replace a 6 month old product under no obligation of Amazon. These bulbs were a fantastic alternative to the ripoffs that the auto stores offered, and I'm certain that I wouldn't have received half of the customer service in the store!

Don't hesitate, buy these, and if they're defective, contact the seller, he responds, and he cares.

review_headline: These large KDs cover my face much better and protect better against wind/dirt/sand etc while riding but ...
review_body:
I bought a pair of the large and a pair of the regular size KDs. These large KDs cover my face much better and protect better against wind/dirt/sand etc while riding but they feel very loose and in high winds they move around on my face as if they are going to be blown off. I'm not talking about fitment when I say loose here. The arms of the glasses are wobbly and loose. I've tried tightening them a bit but it doesn't seem to help much. The smaller KDs felt like they were manufactured better, but they are smaller and don't provide as much protection.

I still like these glasses and wear them whenever I ride at night but they seem to work best when worn with a helmet or strap to hold them in place.

UPDATE 7-19-16

I have ordered another pair of these because my old one got crushed (my fault). I'm greatly impressed in the new pair as they are much tighter fitting and much more solid than the first pair I ordered some time back. Highly recommended and upgraded my rating from 3 stars to 5.

This Meguiar's also ran in a few spots as it was difficult to get an even application with the sprayer. It also did not restore a few of the really faded areas on the truck's black plastic grill. I could not believe that the issue could be resolved by simply changing a seemingly identical plug to the OEM counterpart but it worked. The bad side is that I had to go back to the same crappy design/ manufacturer who stuck us with the infamous plug dilemma to begin with but I countered that with some nickel anti-seize this time around. product_title: HID Xenon DC Headlight "Slim" Conversion Kit by SDX
review_body:
For my 1999 Plymouth Voyager Espresso, headlight brightness (to see and to be seen) has always been an issue with me. Several times while driving on dark roads, the way ahead of me would be lit up by late model cars with HID headlights behind me. I thought about getting brighter halogen bulbs but those are usually about double the cost of standard-brightness halogen bulbs while having a shorter life expectancy. Next, I “discovered” headlight lens restoration kits which removed the haze on my headlight lenses. My lights were brighter. But until I browsed Amazon and then discovered HID conversion kits, I didn’t think I could upgrade my car headlights to HID for a few dollars more (at Amazon prices) than “ultra” halogen bulbs.

While Kensun, that company that sells the kit, says the HID conversion installation is a “20 minute” job, that’s only if you’ve done it before and are familiar with all the connections. For the first-timer, plan on an evening of getting familiar with the steps, with planning the layout of your wiring, and then with making the actual connections. It takes a while to read through the kit instructions (the manual is somewhat helpful but it is a “universal” manual for different types of HID kits; you have to know which kit you have and which kit the manual is referring to). Kensun’s website is more helpful with printable installation instructions plus a pdf download of illustrated instructions, plus pictures of the kit and the connections. (Arguably, though, they could have done a better job with their online pictures, which basically shows the kit spread out on a tiled floor and taped to pieces of blank paper. The connectors are labelled with letters, but close-ups of the connectors would be even more helpful. Better yet, the kit itself should have matching letters attached to the various connectors.)

Most of the connections are fairly logical after examining the connecting ends. They only fit one way to a matching connector. The kit includes: two xenon HID bulbs (of the particular color temperature that you ordered, which was 6000K in my case), two ballasts (one for each headlight), one controller (which controls both headlights), two mounting brackets (one for each ballast), and each ballast and the controller has multiple wire leads. The controller connects to the battery, to each ballast, to ground, and to the bulb socket from the car (usually the one closets to the battery, and only one such connection is needed since both ballasts connect to the controller). The ballasts connect to each bulb, and to the controller. The brackets are optional and connect to the ballasts and help to secure the ballasts to the car. However, the brackets are only useful if you have a properly-positioned and –sized hole in which to attach it with the proper size screw or bolt.

Some Youtube videos showing how others have installed conversion kits show the installers drilling holes into the car frame to attach the ballasts. Good luck with that if you have a car which gives you enough room to even hold a drill under the hood where you could drill a hole at the right spot for the ballast. An easier choice would be to use double-stick mounting tape or squares and/or nylon cable ties (“zip” ties). I used a combination of double-stick mounting squares and nylon ties. There were holes already in the car frame which I could use to attach the zip ties, and there were also enough flat area where I could stick the ballasts with the mounting squares. I did attach the brackets anyway, but the thickness of the heads of the screws used to mount the brackets also prevented me from laying one of the ballasts flat against the frame, so I had to use a double layer of mounting squares to overcome the gap created by the thickness of the screw head.

The first problem I encountered was that the Voyager uses a bulb holder to secure the bulb in the socket, but the base of the HIDbulb was too big to fit through the holder. I thought I had to return the kit, but then I called the troubleshooting line at Kensun explaining the problem and got a call back to pull the base apart from the bulb. (Actually it is a twist-and-pull movement similar to other car bulbs that have two pins on the base.) This is not documented anywhere in the instructions in the booklet or online. Anyway, once I got the HID bulbs into the holders I was able to install the bulbs into the car. Then it was a matter of connecting the ballasts, controller, bulb socket, ground and battery wire (without fastening them to the car yet) to see if the set-up would work. The first time I did this, nothing happened. And for the second time I thought I would have to return the kit. I called Kensun, and also double-checked my procedures. I found out I had connected the power wire to the negative terminal of the battery instead of the positive terminal. Problem solved. I made the correction and the lights worked. The next step was to firmly attach all the components inside the engine compartment.

The HID bulb is basically a glass tube as thin as a stick pretzel with an exposed wire running down one side to the base. It takes 15 to 20 seconds to get to full brightness, and according to specs, it uses 35 watts compared to 55 watts for a standard halogen bulb. I bought the bi-xenon bulb, which uses the same bulb for high and low beam (The bulb is pulled inward to the base, presumably by a magnet, when the high beam is switched on.) The light output (bright white) is concentrated up close (within 20-30 feet) and widely dispersed further out. Anything with any reflective coating (including traffic signs) is lit up 200 or 300 feet away (though of course signs will still not be readable unless they are large enough). Freeway signs using reflective coatings are very brightly lit-up at night as I approach them. I understand late model cars with HID bulbs have projector lenses which focus the light output better, while my conversion kit using a headlight lens and reflector designed for halogen scatters the light.
I am less concerned now about my headlight visibility and brightness. review_body:
The metal key part of my old key fell out and would not go back in. I bought this housing, transferred everything to this one and had it cut at the honda dealership for $20.00 saving me approx $100.00. Note: the metal part of this new key CANNOT be taken out and swapped, it's like welded in there.

Also note: When you remove the transponder chip make sure you are gentle, it's easiest to just peel back the black plastic to get to it. When you add the transponder chip to the new key make sure the small* side of the chip faces toward the actual metal key (you'll see what i'm talking about when you look at the chip, one side is smaller).

The Honda dealership I went to originally gave me static about cutting the key (said it might not work bc it's aftermarket, no guarantees, yada yada), in the end they cut it and it worked. the dealerships are just money hungry and don't like when you save money.

I gave it 4 stars only because I wish you could remove the metal key part.

Good product.

product_title: Gold Stars 11560040 Replacement LED Bulb 1156/1141 Base Tower 280 Lums 12v or 24v Natural White
review_headline: Great Product - same review as I posted for the 120 Lumen bulbs
review_body: Love them.  I'm using both these 280 Lumen bulbs and Gold Stars 120 Lumen bulbs in my RV.  I base which I use where on how much light I really need, and how many hours (thus watt-hours) I will use them.  Goal it to stretch the battery life of the RV with a good balance of light and watts.  Readers should note that the SMD (surface mounted device -- the yellow things) affect the brightness both as it defines size but also refers to the technology used. The model number (5050 in this case) relates to size (5.0 mm x 5.0 mm) vs. e.g., "3528".  But also these 5050SMDs technology has 3 light emitting diodes per SMD.  Thus these are brighter than some other bulbs with more SMDs, so be careful when comparing with other brands.  Brightness is defined by the Lumen rating and you'll notice some manufacturers don't list the Lumens.  No Lumens == unknown brightness.  Still, compare watts consumed and heat generated as well as price in making a choice.

review_body: Don't be fooled with the cheap mirror film - you will be hard pressed to install the cheap stuff on anything other than a flat surface. You get what you pay for. But i was able to apply this to a pair of Mini Cooper headlight lense covers. I then applied clear plastic film to protect the mirror film. It's not perfect, but i'm satisifed with the results. As you can see from the picture, the covers are not curved that much, but you still need a stretchable complaint film. The clear plastic film dulls the mirror effect slightly. I feel it was worth a little less shine to get the extra protection.  This film is totally opaque - the headlight covers are fastened with heavy duty velcro and removable for night driving. product_title: Hellwig 7643 Rear Sway Bar
review_headline: End result makes up for hassles installing.
review_body: If you have an Excursion without a rear sway bar, you need this. This newer style helwig has better end links with more adjustment and fit great on my 2005 with no additional work. I installed this along with modified C code F350 springs, and even with a few inches of lift it still had plenty of adjustment left on the links. The instructions however are horrid. So bad in fact, that Hellwig should pull them from the box. They do nothing but ad confusion to what is really an easy install. The instructions also don't mention the need to drill out the shock mount holes to fit the bigger U-bolts. This would be nice to know beforehand. I was also sent a weird arrangement of locking hardware that I don't believe was the correct amount. I just added a few extra nuts I had to double up the locking nuts I feel were missing. The only other gripe is the bushings in the end links. They were a pain to install. I ended up using my 20 ton shop press after greasing them up and got them installed, but I find no reason other than being cheap why Hellwig would make the customer press these into the links. Star docked for these issues. All in all it has made driving a heavily loaded excursion around corners and on the highway as easy as a prius.... not that I know what that would feel like, but I imagine its that easy. It now corners very flat and feels more surefooted on the twisty roads. Great addition to the best SUV ever created.

product_title: Lead Acid Batteries 12v 24v 36v 48v Battery Regenerator 2A Auto Pulse Desulfator, Blue
review_body:
Unbelievable this works...but it is fantastic!

I had desulfators at work that we used once /week on our industrial batteries and worked well. For $1000 each.

This little $30 unit was not going to impress me...i just did it last ditch in lieu of shelling out $180 for a new mower battery (worx electric 36v deep cell). The damn thing restored my battery from 60% life to 95-100% in one day of pulsing!! I had planned on pulsing a week!

Then I put it on a bike battery that had been week all last year. Now it cranks like brand new! again only one day!

What i do is charge the battery....remove the charger and apply the pulser...it reads voltage; then tells you its setting (c12-c48); then goes blank; then the little red pulsing light starts pulsing until your battery drops to under about 90% of the rated voltage...you should be blinking for about 24hrs at least. Then you should charge the battery again for a day (the pulser runs off your battery while connected...drawing it down). Then last you should remove the charger and fire up your engine and you will be HAPPY at how fast it cranks!

dont charge and pulse at the same time. Not sure if thats good advice but I'm just telling you how i had MUCH success! I feel like its saved me $400 in battery outlays this week (i have a lot of toys)

product_title: BatteryMINDer Maintainer/Desulfater - 2.7 Amps for 36V Systems, Model# 36271
review_headline: Get anther year or so out of your batteries, perhaps?
review_body:
This "Battery Minder", used on my 36 Volt golf cart batteries, left on 'float', did bring up the open cell voltage, and seems to be helping on the ultra low hydrometer readings. My voltage readings were always OK- quasi satisfactory. (38.5 Volts) This was the voltage at which my OEM EzGo charger went into 'float'.This device, after being on 'float' for a couple of weeks brought the voltage up to 40+ vollts and seems to be slowly improving the hydrometer readings. The batteries are only two years old, but had been left in a discharged state previously. The performance of the batteries was always better than the hydrometer readings disclosed, which I found strange.
.
This also (after being on float) balanced all the batteries within .1 to .2 volts of each other. I can only say it seems to be a battery saver. I'm quite satisfied with its performance. My photo shows the maximum voltage after a 'reset'. It then drops to around 40.1 volts on float. I think this slight overvoltage upon start is what is lessening the sulphation and aiding in cell balance.
.
Update4-13-15: A MIRACLE! The specific gravity reading on all batteries is now 'full charge'. This thing evidently DID eleminate all or most sulfation over a couple of weeks. Left on, the batteries do not lose electrolite. In fact, it came up a bit, I assume as the acid was driven out of the plates.
.
Update5-10-15: I am no longer using the factory charger. This device brings the batteries up overnight, then settles in with a higher 'float' voltage. Batteries are using no water.

Boxes and the air filter were spotless and in excellent shape when it was delivered to my door (two days early!). The install was as straightforward as it gets - unscrew the two screws that hold the upper portion of the Air Box, then remove the hose clamp / hose that runs into the engine. Pull the lid off, take out the old filter, slap the new air filter in, screw everything back on nice and tight (including the hose clamp), and wah-lah.

I noticed my Dart was a little more audible on start up as well as when in motion. It's easier to hear the turbo blow-off valve as well. However, the clear coat came off with it and attempts to restore it proved futile.  Look, I'm not an auto hobbiest and I don't doubt the veracity of the reviewers when they enthused over this product.  If you're constantlt working with filler and restoration products, you accumulate more expertise.  However, for the average Joe, I really think this product is not a good idea.  The problem comes at the scratch removal stage which is to know when to call it quits.  In my case, I used light to moderate pressure and did not exceed 10 second intervals (per the mfr's instructions). There are two problems:  the foam emitted from the pad obscures the level of abrasion.  Even constantly wiping it won't do.  Also, the mfr stating that "dulling" of the finish is no problem (it will be restored later) is misleading.  I wish anyone good luck using this product.

review_body:
I just installed these on my 2010 Tacoma and they look good, little more narrow than I truly thought they might be but that is my own fault. To use these have to face foot forward on the step, but workable. It took my wife about 3 tries to feel it out (little leery at first), then once she got use to it she liked it okay.
These fit perfectly and installed in just less than an hour (but that may be just the way I work). This includes minor things like taking the plastic plugs off the truck that have the threaded holes for mounts to attach, getting the proper ratchet (use 1/2 inch socket or wrench), and reading the instructions (which called for leveling, so I had my little level ready but there is really no use for this step. They essential mount one way with no adjustments that I could see to be made).
The bolts seemed a bit hard to get started but I think this was a matter of the paint in the threads on the truck; just keep going, they do fit. This is a one man installation, I thought at first may require some support or another person to assist since there had to be a way to hold it up. Once the mounts are attached to the truck, the part that holds the step is semi round so it just lays on top. I put bolts in the center to start to make sure it didn't fall off, hand tightened all around then went back and alternated the tightening of each bolt for even fit.
These are made in China, wish I had looked a bit closer for made in U.S.A. but not looking back at this point, not the first thing I ever bought from over there. We'll see how they hold up, I will update if I have any issues at all.

product_title: Firstgear Torrent Waterproof Duffel Bag
review_body:
I have the 40L and 70L versions of this. Both have been taken on motorcycle road trips, camping trips and soon a week long sailing trip. Everything about them is sturdy, and I've never had any problems keeping stuff dry inside them.

The 40L should be small enough for airport carry on requirements IF you don't over stuff it. If the top rolls down and the clips secure with low effort, it'll fit just fine. You'll have to check the 70L though. The 40L is large enough for full-size swim fins.

They come with all the straps you'd ever need to make them safe on a motorcycle (4 pieces of webbing with double-back D rings on one end come inside the bag, not pictured).

The only thing I have ever go wrong with these is that TSA decided not to close it properly once when I checked it for a flight. So be aware that that might happen...they probably don't see roll-top bags very often. I'd recommend putting loose little things in stuff sacks inside it so that there's less likelihood of misplaced stuff when it comes open on the baggage carousel.

I would love to have bought this in yellow/white/red or orange...but that's not possible at the moment. Looking into the bottom of these is like looking into a deep dark well...

product_title: CURT 11067 Class 1 Trailer Hitch
review_headline: Fits the Fiesta ST if extra steps are taken.
review_body:
This will fit on a Fiesta ST with a major caveat. The stock exhaust's movement will hit the hitch and cause some banging noise due to the muffler's size and low clearance. There are 3 fixes. The first one is you can change the exhaust hangers (3 for this car) to a stiffer or higher durometer type. This will minimize but not completely eliminate the "banging". Freeway driving will be fine but there will be thunking on rough local roads. The second fix is to take your car to a local muffler shop to either eliminate the muffler (which is the main cause), switch to a smaller one, or have them weld you a solid mount so the exhaust will not move at all. The third fix (and most expensive) is to get an aftermarket exhaust which usually have a straight pipe or smaller muffler.

Other than the aforementioned issue, the hitch fits the rear end perfectly. There is no clearance issues with the rear bumper. Nothing is being bent out of shape or anything has to be cut.

It maybe because I changed the exhaust hangers on mine but the install went way beyond a half hour (possibly an hour and a half). I'm not sure if it's because I have the ST model but inserting the screw into the access hole to do the fish wire method took the longest time. At first glance, you will not believe the screw head will fit into the hole. I had to turn the screw every which way possible to get it in there. Even then I felt some luck was involved as it was hard to duplicate the effort and apply it to the next screw. A second set of hands will definitely help when mounting the hitch.

I bought this hitch as I needed somewhere to carry my bike easily.This will not be used for towing anything. I'd still recommend getting this if
you're willing to take the extra steps to address the muffler clearance issue. If not you can always get a roof rack.

Update: After adjusting the hitch and moving it towards the right (if facing the rear of the car), I have not heard the muffler hit the hitch whatsoever. I forgot to mention in my original review that I used a set of exhaust hangers from Cobb. product_title: Genuine  Toyota (77300-33070) Fuel Tank Cap Assembly
review_headline: Worked just like the original and it fixed the check engine lamp.
review_body:
Worked perfect. This is an OE fuel cap, so it fit and functioned just like the original.

Our 2007 4Runner was showing 2 trouble codes for an evaporative emissions leak, which was annoying. On this model truck, when the check engine lamp is lit for any reason, all traction control is turned off by default and can't be switched back on until the problem is sorted. (Which is a REALLY stupid idea, Toyota).

The fuel cap cleared the codes instantly. I've learned that the factory fuel caps are good for 100-150k miles, then have to be replaced. Seems to be a common thing with 4Runners and Tacoma's. Probably other Toyotas too. The seal dries out and it will stop holding the required pressure in the system. Replacing the cap fixed the problem instantly.

The added bonus of buying the OE equipment cap is that it comes with the teather that secures it to the vehicle when you open it. Aftermarket caps don't have that feature.

If your Toyota is throwing a trouble code for an Evap problem, start with this first.

Thanks!

product_title: Sena Bluetooth Headset Bundle
review_headline: Clear communication on sportbike at 70+, full duplex intercom, worth the money (and not even much)
review_body:
THESE are absolutely AWESOME. It's even cooler that you can listen to Pandora/spotify and just do a quick tap of the middle button on the Sena pack and open up comms with a friend. Another tap on the middle and you return to music.

So far it's been clear at speeds of 70+ even with wind. The boom mic is all I've used (due to reviews saying just use that) and I thought kissing it would be annoying but you get used to it. Moving the mic to your upper lip or lower lip is also comfortable. I ride a suzuki GSX650F and I can just barely hear the engine when going over 6k RPM. My friend with the same bike says the same, you can lightly hear our engines but the user's voice is loud and clear. Full duplex communication (you and your friend can talk at the same time) is AWESOME. Sometimes when in tight maneuvers or traffic we will keep just comms open to coordinate. Kind of scary though we thought that if one of us goes down, we will probably hear every second of it BUT I DIGRESS!

Only issue we've had (don't really care) is that when sharing music between both devices you'll occasionally get stutters and dead spots even within 10-30 feet proximity AND on latest 5.1 firmware. This maybe happens a few times every 10-20 minutes but still is badass being able to share music.

I use a full face helmet properly fitted and the volume of the speakers is never set to 100% since these things can really blast your ears (VERY high treble, given they are small speakers) so what I do in Spotify (recommend doing this if you have an equalizer on your phone/MP3 device) is to reduce treble where its comfortable. I can blast music now without highs making my ears bleed.

I tried going the cheap route before (getting radios with throat mics and PTT) but it was just bad. Bad bad bad. Unless you are using a good boom mic WITH SOFTWARE AUDIO FILTERING, you're going to have a bad time.

product_title: Evapo-Rust ER012 The Original Super Safe Rust Remover - 1 Gallon
review_headline: Great For Light Rust, Good For Heavy
review_body:
This product is fantastic for light rust and certain kinds of rusted metals, but its effectiveness varies a bit. It always eats off the rust, but the resulting surface might be totally like-new or have a new non-rust substance where the rust was. I tested it on some old tools, and the result on hand tools was remarkable. The wrenches (Craftsman steel alloy) lost the rust, but didn't look as good afterward.

Regarding the photos: the one on linoleum is the after (sorry for mediocre lighting), concrete is the before, in liquid is the during. The pilers were really spectacularly de-rusted. Same with the Craftsman philips screwdriver. The file looked much better, the prybar was great, and the needle nose pliers were successes. The wrenches were improved, but not perfect. A bit of grinding work fixed them up, though.

Pros:
-Removes rust! I'm still hoping to try it on some vehicular rust, but it works great for hand tools.
-Non-toxic, so I wasn't worried about it burning off my skin.
-I used it at below the recommended temperature one round, but it still worked great.
-Simple to use. Just soak the items, wash with water, dry, and you're done.
-Can be used multiple times.

Cons:
-Won't work every miracle you might want. For example, don't expect it to release a set of pliers that has rusted shut. It helped on one I tried, but wasn't magic (WD-40 was more effective).
-Doesn't stop rust moving forward from the treatment. You will want to put on oil or WD-40 or paint very soon, because the metal will re-rust.

Other thoughts:
-The stuff is a bit sticky and oily.

product_title: Bestop 7562615 PowerBoard NX Retractable Electric Running Board
review_body: I purchased the 7562615 powerboard for my brand new 2015 GMC Sierra 2500HD SLT Crew Cab.  Wiring it up was excellent and easy.  However the rear motor linkage is defective. The Rear Motor linkage, Part # 460.89 is held on by two bolts, An upper bolt and a lower bolt.  The lower bolt is where the issue is.  This bolt is placed too close to the rotating knuckle and as you tighten the bolt down it hits the rotating knuckle.  The rear motor linkage is what attaches to the rear of the running board and also holds the motor that moves the board.  The bolt is made out of hardened steel, the rear motor linkage is made out of aluminum.  The steel bolt threads grind into the knuckle of the rear motor linkage causing immediate damage and over a short period of time will cause catastrophic failure.  This is a massive design flaw.  I have tried to work with Bestop on this problem but to date they have sent me the exact same parts that are defective... twice!  I've sent pictures and detailed information describing the problem and described how easy it is to duplicate.  You don't have to attach the unit to the vehicle.  Just install the bolt and actuate the linkage by hand and your grinding away aluminum.  Good design but their QC sucks and there response is lacking.  I will hopefully be able to send this back and get AMP.  Amp is an American made product with a 5 year warranty.  I'm hoping the longer warranty means they make a much better product that is actually built to last.  Bestop is built to fail and the replacement parts sent directly from the mfg are built the same way. The pictures below are from the test fit installation.  They weren't installed on the truck for more than 5 minutes and a few rotations of the boards.

product_title: Depo Replacement Exterior Door Handle
review_headline: Works as advertised, slightly difficult to mount but I was able to get it installed without any extra drilling or modifications.
review_body:
Works well, I've been using this handle daily to open my driver's door for the last 3 or 4 months.

Slightly difficult fit in the stock mounting holes on my 91 Pathfinder SE, I can see why some others have said it didn't fit, but after a bit of wiggling it went in. It does seem more flimsy than the OEM but I just greased all the moving parts on the door lock/unlock mechanism and that helped.

For the price I'd recommend this, and even if it broke tomorrow I'd buy another one. Whole install took less than 1 hour total, including figuring out the tip below. I have big hands so I wasn't able to get inside the door easily but was able to maneuver things around without too much difficult.

TIP: Specific to 1991 Pathfinder. After installing you may have problems locking/unlocking your door with the power locks. If you do, DON'T FORCE THINGS - you just need to adjust the tension on the rod that opens the door a little bit. To do this, loosen the tension on the vertical threaded rod that adjusts the tension on the opening mechanism by screwing up or down the big plastic flanged nut on the end that connects the handle to the opening rod. You want it to be loose enough that it doesn't block the lock mechanism when you lock/unlock with a key or the power locks, but with enough tension that when you lift the handle the door opens easily. It took me about 4 tries and tests before things settled in and all worked as they had before the handle broke.

product_title: Dorman 425-361 Steering Shaft
review_headline: Good deal for price, wih caveat!
review_body:
Bought APDTY in lieu of the Dorman part, due to some user/reviewers saying steering wheel had play. I knew how to check for that but preferred not to have to return part for luck of the draw. ANY rotational slop is not acceptable since 1/32 at 1-2 inch radius would translate to ~ 1 inch on the steering wheel rim. So keep that in mind and return for replacement if that happens.
What I'm glad about is that I didnt take old part off to check it first. The bad joint was nowhere near 'seized up' just a little sticky but it sure affected steering and wheel return to center.

Key: spray on penetrant (PB blaster not WD40) well before working on it. Remove bolts. Tap a screwdriver blade into squeeze slot. You'll likely have no problem with either bolts or shaft connections. Apply axle grease to telescoping shaft before install and work it a little.

product_title: Bolt Power D28A 13600mAh Portable Car Jump Starter 400 AMP Peak With Air Compressor
review_headline: and laptop charging ports are fantastic features, and I like the design quality of ...
review_body:
I bought this all-purpose battery pack about a week ago, and I'm very impressed by its performance. To my pleasant surprise, it can actually start cars (even with the original car battery removed altogether!) The flashlight, emergency light, USB port, and laptop charging ports are fantastic features, and I like the design quality of the product. My primary use for this battery is actually operating a 400-watt power inverter, which runs with no complaint directly off the car starting port. The laptop charger is also useful, although it may not work well if your device has a large inrush current.

The only thing I want to note to future buyers is that the 16500 mAh figure is calculated at the LiPo cells' individual voltage of 3.7 volts, NOT the 11.1-volt output of the pack. The entire 11.1-volt pack is a 5500 mAh LiPo battery, so it holds a total of 67 watt-hours, not 201. Other than that, the product is well-designed and performs as advertised!

product_title: G2 High Temperature Brake Caliper Paint System Set YELLOW G2161
review_body:
I painted their yellow kit over the gray Brembo's that came on my car and applied a few coats. A bit of the gray is showing through in small areas, but only if you're up close to notice. Sometimes my OCD kicks-in and I think about buying another kit to add a few more layers, but then my laziness wins over the OCD. Otherwise, it's pretty good. Very shiny, still looks good after a few months. I have ceramic brake pads so I don't get any brake dust. Not sure how they'd handle it.

Since the calipers were already painted & clear-coated, I sanded them to improve the adhesion. Not sure what would happen if I hadn't but I think it's a good call.

There's a video on YouTube where someone suggests spending a buck for a 1-inch paintbrush (bristles, not foam) from Home Depot and cutting the bristles in half & at an angle, to paint faster and get a better result. I only found that video AFTER I painted, so hopefully you'll read this before you get started and make it easier on yourself.

product_title: Ford Powerstroke Diesel 7.3 1994-2003 TS Performance 6 Position Chip WITH KNOB 140+ HP
review_headline: Fantastic upgrade! Its like a whole different truck! Updated July 2015
review_body: Update July 30 2015:  TS performance chip still works great! I've put about 5000 miles on it since installing and haven't had any problems directly related to this. I did notice that when using FORScan diagnostic tools on the truck it comes up with a 2000 F-250 now instead of before installation when it came up as 2001 (the truck IS a 2001), but doesn't seem to have any running issues because of that. Don't know if that is caused by a misflashed chip or the chip for 2000-2001 trucks are flashed the same or???   I already had a small injector o-ring leak from before installing this and I finally lost enough HPOP pressure to start causing major running issues. Is that related to pushing the injectors harder because of the chip? Maybe. Is it related to me being much heavier on the pedal since installing the chip? Most likely! Bottom line, I would buy it again in a heartbeat, but beware that if you buy one, small problems could be exacerbated.   Original Review Feb 2015: "Holy S***!" That's what I said once i set it to 75 HP and took off for the first time. The change from stock power (well fairly stock) and shift points/speed to the modified shift points and power is absurd. Its like I went to the dealership and bought a new truck. Night and day. I drive a 2001 F-250 CCLB 7.3l PSD. 285k on the clock and hoping to double that!  Installation was a breeze. Because of other people's common complaints of not working or issues with reliability I made sure that I took my time and followed the instructions to a tee. Start to finish was 45 minutes with the hardest part removing the ECU from the firewall. The instructions state that you need to remove the entire ECU bracket when you only have to remove the two 7mm screws holding the plastic cover to the bracket. Then loosen the 10mm nut that holds the wiring harness to the ECU in the engine bay. Pull the harness off then go in the cab and pull the ECU along with the plastic cover out. You will probably have to turn it right and pull a bit to clear the E-brake release. The terminal did not take nearly as much "nightmarish" cleaning to remove the rubberized coating (looked like clear silicone to me) as everyone seems to say it does. A few scrapes with a flat tip screwdriver then a little scrubbing with the scratchpad with a drop of acetone on it and it was done. I installed my switch on the fuse panel cover. Drill one hole a little bigger than 1/4 inch for the actual switch and one hole just below that about 1/8 inch or slightly larger (for the tab that keeps the switch from freespinning in its mount hole).  All settings (stock, high idle, +50, +75, +100 and +140) worked great. I have heard that the +100 and +140 settings won't give you much of a boost unless you have an aftermarket HPOP capable of pushing the injectors hard enough but it sure seems to me like those settings provide extra power even with a stock pump. In any case a T500 HPOP is probably my next purchase. What a great chip!

review_headline: RAM 1500 Crew Cab - CHECK BRACKET FIT TO STEP MOUNT HOLE POSITIONS - SOME PARTS MISLABELLED!
review_body:
I put these on a 2015 RAM 1500 Crew Cab. No holes to drill. In my case the brackets labelled Driver Front (DF), Driver Center (DC) had to be swapped with the Passenger Front (PF) and Passenger Center (PC). I would recommend doing a loose top bolt mount of one side's bracket and then get approximate measurement of hole spacings (front to back) on step mount holes. Compare those measurements to the spacings on the step tubes. If the numbers are close, you're golden - if not, you need the bracket swap like I did. I also installed the deluxe molded splash guards just before I put these on. This order needs to be followed also or the lower splash guard bolt will become inaccessible due to the tube being in the way. The splash guards and the tubes can coexist - on other setups this isn't true.

I had Westin's on my prior truck for 11 years and never had any problems; hoping that is true of these. If it weren't for the mislabelled parts I would give these 5 stars.

product_title: Range Technology Active Fuel Management Disable Device
review_body: Installed this on my own 08 Silverado 5.3L, 63K 3 months ago as a test vehicle. This truck did have a complete tear down from GM for oil consumption while under powertrain warranty about 3 years back. The vehicle still had oil consumption issues. Knowing these systems are extremely problematic the oil is changed every 3K or 4 months no matter what and that is what is recommended to our customers. Plugs were replaced at 60K (which took care of the annoying light stumble at idle). With the AFM deactivated the truck has consistent power and performance. The transmission shift points are flawless now. The MPG has actually gone up about 1.3. I have since recommended this to our customers who have  DOD/AFM vehicles. 3 more have been installed in the last month. 09 Silverado 5.3L, 160K (which did have an AFM lifter collapse on #1 in January), 06 Envoy XL 5.3L, 125K (which has had very excessive oil consumption for about 1 year now) and an 08 Avalanche 5.3L, 142K (which has had the continuous #1 plug fouled and multiple repeats of oil pressure switch which is also a key sign). All 3 so far have had a big change in performance. Of course time will tell with the consumption rate but there will be an obvious reduction just due to the fact those AFM cylinders are not constantly sparying a light mist of oil non stop. The only one thus far that had an issue with the device was the 09. One time at startup all the dash lights came on and vehicle went into limp mode just when starting out. The customer knew this could occur as we advised so they turned off vehicle, unplugged Range, waited until it cleared and plugged it back in. We have definitely seen and heard that the improvement overall in how these vehicles run has been on the plus side. We will continue to highly recommend these to our customers with these systems. The jury is still out as to whether this will reduce stress on the transmission as well over time. Since it stops it from searching gears every time the vehicle goes from 4 to 8, good possiblity. There are a lot of vehicles out there that date back in years with DOD/AFM and a lot of people do not even realize they have it especially on the older models without the DIC.

product_title: Westin 57-2500 HDX Polished Grille Guard
review_body:
Last month I ordered a Westin HDX for my Dad's 2015 Chevrolet 2500 and the packing box was as clean as if I had picked it up at the factory. All welds were perfect and installation was a piece of cake. It looked so good on his truck the Dad bought one for my 2009 F150 SuperCrew Platinum 4X4.

Mine came from a different freight line. The ends of the box had been torn apart and reattached with packing tape. By some miracle nothing was missing or scraped. Installation is a two man job. I didn't take off the air dam. Nor did I do any cutting.

Once installed we took the truck out of my shop to inspect every weld, etc. It is a sold grill guard and really looks nice from a distance. Close inspection found very poor quality control allowed it through. Last week I sent 14 pictures of ugly rusting welds. So far nothing from Westin on this and how they want to proceed.
