product_title: Boliy PRO3600SIER QBlue RV Pro 3700 Wireless Remote Start Generator
review_body:
I live in AZ. Purchased my Boliy 3600Si/E on line and have done all my own servicing. My contact for help has been Northern Wholesale Supply
I have had a Boliy since 2010, the first thing I had go wrong out of the box, was a fuel leak between the fuel tank and the fuel petcock. NWS overnight'd me a new tank. The new one also leaked, I'm leaving on vacation the next day so I pulled the new tank turned it up side down and used some high tech super glue on it. It worked and is still not leaking. I purchased the Boliy to run the 15,500 AC on my America camp. It was always a struggle for it, as there has always been a delay or dead spot between needing more RPM and getting more RPM. Most of the time it just blew the breaker. After a year it quit charging it's own battery, NWS sent me a new module and harness. At 5000 ft elevation it struggled to run the microwave. I installed the lean high elevation jet,. that gave it better fuel economy but even in my new 2011 Forest River Wild Cat with a 13,500 AC it couldn't start the AC. Last year I read and article on line about trailer A/C's not having big enough starting capacitor in them To handle the starting surge. The article listed Amazone as the place to buy the capicator for the job. For under ten bucks. Iand about 20 min to install my Boliy started the A/C with no effort at all. Shure wish I had known about this simple fix five years ago.
.Boliy now mentions this in the new starting manual. Just look up RV A/C starting capicator on Amazon. The same capacitor sells from $8.00 to $20. You may need some advice as to how to hook it up. Mine was simple because a guy with a trailer and A/C like mine explained where to connect the 2 wires. It's worth an A/C service call for the difference it makes. Now my Boliy needs a new stepping motor control module. First the generator started surging, then it would run for 5 minutes after starting and quit. A couple of days latter the low side didn't work at all and finally the motor would just run at it's highest speed. Systematic of a bad control module. A new motor is only another six bucks so I will replace both at the same time. As far as noise mine has always been noisier then then I thought it should be .
Boliy has made a lot of changes since I purchased mine, a metal fuel tank hopefully with a gauge that doesn't cloud up on the first tank of fuel, a keyed ignition switch, upgraded carbaration, optional remote control , Aux. fuel tank connection and finally a set of wheels with a tow handle.
By all the good reports it sounds line Boliy has got there act together. Although most reports are from just afew hours of use. I installed an hour meter on mine before it had 2 hours on it. There are now more then 650 hrs on it. I also change the oil every 60 hrs
By comparison 4 years ago I purchased a 1000 WE Yahmaha inverter generator. Which I use mainly for TV, lights and charging my two 12 volt deep cycle batteris. It has done a Yoman's job. It runs nearly 10 hours on .six tens of gallon, ran up to ten hours a day for three months, when we were camp hosts and has never had anything more than routine maintence. I estimate it to have close to 1800 hours on it.
Both generators are set up next to each other so it's easy to switch depending whether we need microwave/AC watts or less then 1000 low power Watts.
The are a lot of competively priced 2000-3000+ watt generators out there that wern't around 5 years ago.

Shop wisely ;)

product_title: Chemical Guys WAC_808 Hybrid V7 Optical Select-High Gloss Spray Sealant and Detailer - 1 Gallon
review_headline: Works good, but not on black and not the best.
review_body:
Good spray, but not the best.

Put this up against Lucas Speed Spray Wax, which costs half as much per bottle, and you get 50% more product (24oz compared to 16oz).
Lucas held up great on a black car with little to no streaking and had a much deeper and wetter look to it.

V7 worked as advertised, but just seemed a little watered down. Great smell, just like orange sherbet ice cream or a "Push-up" pop, if you know what that is.

Tried the V7 on everything on the exterior like paint, glass, plastic, headlights, and it worked fine on everything. Great aid when drying the car, no water spots at all. Nice "just waxed look" when you got done. Very slick feeling, feels like the car was just waxed.

Overall, liked the V7 and it did everything it said it would, only thing, Lucas Speed Spray wax did it better, with no streaking, and looks better and most importantly, costs less than half as much with 50% product. Oh, and you can get Lucas OTC at locally at just about any auto store/wally world/etc.

For a black car, this product is a no-go, just streaks too much.

product_title: Peak PKC0J6 600-Amp Jump Starter
review_body:
I bought this on sale from the grocery store about October 2014. My primary use for this is jump starting lawn tractors which it does. It's difficult to tell if it's charging. I get the flashing "FL" and then the indicator goes out. I plug it in again and get a flashing "99%". Sometimes I don't get an indicator at all.

As with other users, the charging plug in the back broke off inside the unit. I called today and reported it. Apparently it's within a year of the manufacture date based on the serial number or else the rep is being wonderfully helpful considering the reviews this thing has gotten. They are sending a replacement, hopefully an improved version. The rep said they may request me to return the old unit. If it costs as much as the original to ship it I won't.

I plan to see if I can open the old one and solder in a short plug wire. I carry jumper cables for the family vehicles but sometimes it's a pain to push the lawn tractors out if the battery is weak to jump them from the truck. This works.

16 MARCH 2015 / UPDATE: Received my replacement jump starter in the mail today. First thing I noticed is the AC plug, while still a flip out design, is reinforced and hopefully more sturdy. I opened the old unit and the AC plug is nothing more than a 120VAC / 15VDC adaper "wall wart" with a two-wire plug. I assume it could be swapped out with a 220VAC for European countries. Hoping this one is better than the first. I'm keeping the old one for now.

Out of the box the mpg reading on the unit was way off showing an average of 9 mpg. When hand calculating I get about 14 mpg when driving like normal and about 15 when following the driving coach. Also occasionally it will show a false reading for a moment, for instance my trans temp will be at 90 to 100 degrees and will suddenly jump from 400 to as much as 1000 degrees. I will be switching to premium gas and the premium tune for towing this summer I will see if that makes a difference. Overall I saw no change in mileage or performance but since I wanted it mainly to monitor the truck I am not disappointed. I know they make a unit just for monitoring but I figured I would take a shot. Hope to see an improvement after switching to the premium tune.

review_body:
Put this on an 02 F250 Supercrew. Read a lot of reviews and was excited at the low cost/easy install of this product. product_title: 4.0" In/Out x 20" OAL Aero Turbine Muffler, 6" Round Body
review_headline: Your turbo will scream with this muffler!!!
review_body:
Well.. I have run two of these mufflers now (the other was the 3.5" version). I was slightly let down when I pulled this one out and looked at it, as the insides look just like the 3.5" version. I expected a larger hole through the center, and figured the 4" version should be capable of flowing more than the 3.5" version. But inside it's basically the same.

I put this on my EVO 8 that makes about 530 awhp. I have a homebuilt 3.5" downpipe to bumper exit exhaust setup. (MAP ef4 turbo, built 2.4L, lots of goodies). I am ALWAYS in search of making my turbo cars turbos louder. I have built several mufflers from scratch.. tried everything you can imagine. This muffler without a doubt wins the award for letting the most turbo sound through. Now don't get me wrong, it's pretty loud overall.. these are not quiet mufflers.. but the turbo screams. Even under normal cruising it's ridiculously loud. I love it.

However, more importantly than sound.. is how it actually performs. As a pilot, I don't buy into all this airfoil nonsense.. airplane wings do create lift with high and low pressure, however they also create drag in doing so (drag could be compared to flow- or in this case, back pressure). I was surprised that I haven't really seen a difference in power on the road dyno (which incidentally is far more accurate than you might think). Boost is actually as high, if not higher! Which means it didn't introduce any more back pressure. This really surprised me, as I expected it to flow worse.

Overall I have to say, for the money, the quality (stainless), the sound! and it appears to flow plenty for 500+ HP, probably quite a bit more (I found a video while doing research on these of a 8-900whp supra running this 4" version). I'm really pleased... Here are a couple videos showing how it sounds (and believe me, it's much louder in real life)

product_title: OPT7 Blitz H4 Bi-Xenon Replacement HID Bulbs Pair [6000K Lightning Blue] Xenon Light
review_headline: Great buy! Super bright and high quality. Definetely recommend as replacments on exisiting Opt7 kits.
review_body:
I bought these H4 Bi-xenon 6000K bulbs as a replacement for the 10000K ones I got in my full Opt7 HID relay conversion kit. The 10000K were much too dark of a color for me and with limited visibility. If you want some awesome HID bulbs that still have the blue color to them but have great visibility, go for these. While the blue color isn't super vivid, it definetely stands out on the road and isn't too ostentatious. The visibility is great. Much much better than 10000K bulbs.
This actually comes with more than is advertised. Mine came with the two bulbs, and a whole secondary wiring harness. It has almost everything you need to hook up another whole HID kit except the Ballasts, capacitors and relay. I'm not sure what I'm supossed to do with it but it was generous of them to include so much extras.
The bulbs themselves are obviously of a higher quality than the 10000k bi-xenon bulbs I got with my original Opt7 kit. The metal surround that covers the actual xenon bulb is larger and more complete, and the actuator motor on the back seems better built, larger, and sturdier than the ones included in the kit. I've had these installed for about 10 days now and have never noticed any flicker or have they ever failed to work. They do however take about 5 seconds to warm up though when first turning them on. They don't flicker, they just start dim and steadily get brighter over the course of 5 seconds or so.
I was able to just plug them right into my exisiting Opt7 HID kit and go. Took two minutes to install them on my already installed kit.
I've tried several different bulbs for my kit and feel like 6000K is definetely the way to go if you want the maximum visibility while still retaining the cool blue color. And on top of all that Opt7 warranties these bulbs for two years just like the full kit.
All in all, even though these bulbs cost almost as much as the full Opt7 conversion kit, I would highly recommend them. They are much higher quality than the ones included in the kits. Great buy.

product_title: Denso (3172) PK20PR-L13 Double Platinum Spark Plug, Pack of 1
review_headline: Replaced stock 15 year old plugs, 2000 Civic Si..
review_body:
Original owner of a 2000 Civic Si with a stock B16A2 engine. These replace the original ~15 year old spark plugs which were the NGK PFR6L-13. They came pre-gapped at .050-.051 inches which is within the spec. Side note: to be sure ('measure twice, cut once') I called my local Honda Cars service department and was told that the gap should be .028 inches. I asked if he was sure. He paused, double checked and said that it is 0.52 inches. Oops. Doesn't give me a lot of confidence in this shop. Several years ago, this same shop also replaced my transmission fluid with a transmission fluid, not the recommended 10W30. No damage fortunately. I asked what they used immediately after and caught it then. But I digress.

After coating the spark plug terminals and new wire connectors (also replaced the wires, NGK (8018) HE64) with dielectric grease, I installed and torqued them to the recommended 13 ft·lb's, Another digression: while in an Auto Zone for something else, I asked an employee about the torque requirements for my spark plugs. He insisted it was 13 inch pounds, not foot pounds. He said if I torqued to 13 foot pounds I'd strip or break the plugs. If I had torqued to inch pounds as he said, engine damage could have resulted. It was interesting how convincing he was when he was talking about this. The moral of the story is that you should always do your homework, not blindly believe what a self described pro says no matter how convincing they are.

After installing and torquing to 13 ft.lbs, the car started immediatelyand ran smoothly. Later that night, I took it out for a test drive. I ran it through the gears, took it up to the rev limiter (~8k) several times and gave it a good work out. No issues, misfires or anything out of the ordinary.

Not sure what I expected but noticed no performance difference between the new plugs and wires than I did with the 15 year old plugs and wires. Testimony I guess to how far quality control, materials and design have progressed throughout the years. Back in the day, you might have to remove and clean plugs every 15-20 thousand miles or so. I only replaced them because it seemed like a reasonable thing to do after 15 years. I haven't measured fuel mileage yet so maybe the difference will manifest itself there.

Lastly, I did not use anti-seize compound. There seems to be a lot of opinion about this. Denso's website does not recommend using anti-seize compound. They say doing so can result in overly high resistance when torquing the plug into place. My previous NGK plugs showed no evidence of having anti-seize compound on the threads and I didn't have any problems removing them after fifteen years of use.and design have progressed throughout the years. review_headline: Great little pump, but only 150 PSI

This is a neat looking little pump. It is very well-constructed and it appears to be of a very high quality. It says "made in the USA" on the package which you don't see very often these days. I really wanted to like it and keep it. The problem is, I did not read all the fine print carefully enough. I think the description needs to state more prominently that this is a pump of up to 150 psi.

150 psi is good enough to pump a front shock. But it is not sufficient for a rear shock. I have a full suspension bike, and it turns out I need a higher pressure pump. One can get a 300 psi pump for a comparable price, which would allow you to use it on a much wider variety of shocks.

The only reason why it doesn't get 5 stars from me is due to the fact that it doesn't come with an on/off switch nor does it have a standby setting, so if you have a car you rarely drive, or something like an LS motor hotrod with stock computer that you only drive once every once in a while and you keep this plugged in, your going to be draining your battery.

Beside that one little thing with it (and of course you can always mod your own on/off switch very very easily), I can't complain. It's fast, it works, it's reputable.. If you work on your own cars at all, you can't do anything but good purchasing this product.

product_title: EAG 07-17 Jeep Wrangler JK Rock Crawler Off road Front Bumper with Winch Mounting Plate (51-0328)
review_body:
I ordered this bumper directly from E-Autogrilles other online storefront because it was significantly cheaper than their Amazon listing. I'm writing a review here because there are few actual reviews of their products online, and the info in the Wrangler forums is often highly prejudiced against anything not made in the USA. That said, I purchased this bumper for my 2009 JK Wrangler. This item seems to be identical to Extreme Terrain's Barricade Trail Force HD bumper; it might not be exact, but it sure appears to be the same to me. You can definitely reference that installation guide if you really need to. Installation is pretty much a no-brainer. The bumper is very high quality; the steel is very thick and the welds look solid. The coating/paint on the bumper is slightly textured. Installation on my 2009 JK was extremely easy. Everything lined up perfectly--my installation took around 20 minutes (not counting the time to remove the old bumper). This bumper has cutouts to mount the two small lights from your factory bumper. You'll use the supplied new screws with nuts to attach the lights. On my 09 JK I had to remove some electrical tape from the wiring harness to bring the wires out a bit more--I did not have to splice to lengthen the wire. This might not be the case for other year's models. You don't need to reuse any of the bolts, brackets, or screws from your old bumper. I placed a Smittybilt XRC 9500 Winch on the bumper AFTER the bumper was mounted. The holes lined up perfectly. I decided to mount the solenoid in the upright/vertical position because the wiring was a little tight with the solenoid mounted horizontally. You could mount a winch prior to putting the bumper on; just wanted to testify that it is quite easy to mount one AFTER the bumper is already installed.

Since I ordered this bumper from another source I am not sure how they'll handle shipping via Amazon. All I can tell you is mine was shipped very quickly from California to the Southeast via FedEx. The bumper was wrapped in cardboard, styrofoam, and then wrapped with a ton of plastic shrinkwrap.

The only other thing I'll add is that removing the old bumper is the most difficult part. My advice is to buy a can of PB Blaster lubricant. I had some bolts an impact drill wouldn't budge. 5 minutes after spraying with PB Blaster and I was able to ratchet the bolts off by hand.ornia to the Southeast via FedEx. If you need a vise for machining or havy metalwork I s ggest spending a good deal more moneh. review_headline: Great Adapter for Vehicles Without A Threaded Shaft !!!
review_body: Just what I was looking for. Had to replace the shift knob on a 99 Ford Ranger. There is not much variety out there when it comes to shift knobs for Ford trucks due to their splined shaft design. But with the right adapter, you can use just about any shift knob on the market. This is that adapter. Fits right on the end of that splined shaft and fastens with set screws. Just for extra tightness, you may want to partially drill some holes in the shaft where the set screws tighten to be extra certain your new knob does not pull off. Also, some Loctite 242 is good for preventing the set screws from backing out from vibration. Once installed you can directly screw on any shift knob with a 16 x 1.5 mm thread.

As far as attracting dirt this stuff is about the same as any other oil product, it attracts some dirt. No more, no less than other oil products used.
If you buy a quart of this stuff it should last you quite a while. It will cost you about 3 dollars to buy an eye dropper at your local drugstore, which you can use to apply the gear lube to the chain. I suspect that the high price chain lubes you see at the bike shop are smaller quantities of this stuff. Save some money and buy a quart of this stuff. Share some with your friends.

Think it can still work with the factory low fuel indicators but may be off by a few miles won't bother me once I'm comfortable the low fuel is accurate on the gauge..seems to be and can be calibrated to wherever you choose. Different model bike? in the end you takes your chances but with fairly good odds I'd say.

I found the electronic monitoring is almost useless and dangerous at highway speeds.  In other words, the system warned me too late as I approached the other lane. review_body: These little LEDs are bright, and cheap. I wired them up and had one that flickered when I wiggled the wire. I decided to pop them all open and take a look. The LED capsule is soldered to a little PCB with a 220 ohm surface mount resistor on the positive side. The positive lead to the LED capsule was not soldered to the pad, and the wiggling caused the light to make and break contact with the solder. I re-soldered all of the capsules and sealed them up again. Now they work great. The lenses on these cause some prismatic coloring at the edges, so a yellow border is very evident at the periphery of the beam pattern. The studs measure 3/8\\" in diameter.    Update: In my application I needed to thread these into a fixture. For reference, the stud is an M10 x 1.0 thread.

product_title: Cobra Short Round Sissy Bar with Pad
review_headline: here is a better description of how to install them
review_body:
Very solid and performs just as advertised. It's all flat black except for the rear plate.

My sole complaint is that the directions that come with it are not very clear. It's a one paragraph statement that is very vague. I thought that it wanted me to put the cobra supports between the side cover and the swing arm, or something similar, but in fact, these go on the outside. I ended up having to Google image search other people's installs to see exactly how it goes. It took an extra 20 minutes to figure out the process, so to help future purchasers, here is a better description of how to install them:

1. No need to undo the seat, leave that on.
2. Starting with one side, undo the two 14mm bolts that attach the side rails to the rear fender. Do not do both side rails at once, otherwise the fender will fall and you will have to hold it up while you reattach everything. Not a big deal should this happen, but it's an extra step you don't need to do.
3. On the phantom, the side rails consist of the metal coming up from the swing arm and detachable side rail covers on the outside. You want to leave those side rail covers in place, but put the included spacers between the side rail cover and the cobra supports, with the cobra supports being on the outside of everything. The top of the cobra support should be angled in. If it's not, you got left and right reversed.
4. Using the included Allen wrench bolts replace the stock 14mm bolts, tighten everything down halfway until it's secure but there is still some play back and forth.
5. Repeat the process on the other side.
6. Screw in the backrest to the supports and make it tight.
7. Tighten the cobra supports and side rails down tight.
8. ???????
9. Profit!

product_title: Klasse ALL-IN-ONE Polish 10 oz
review_headline: Just like any other car material you need to use mask ...
review_body: is alright, I own a 1993  Cheyenne c1500 short bed truck. Was painted 2 months ago with championship white. I washed it in the morning and let it completely dry. In the afternoon I went to my local autozone to purchase a set of 4 Microfiber pads and some large hand gloves. Just like any other car material you should use mask or gloves if you care about your health. They don't say that is harmful but since this thing bonds hard for 6 months I imagined it can stay in your body if you breath the dried klasse while is being removed. Either way if you care about your health is nothing wrong if you use this precaution. After buying all these stuff I went home and I started to put a coat of Klasse all-in-one, I started with the hood then the fenders and then the doors and roof of the truck. So I finished putting this on half of the truck, then I started removing the dried klasse from the first part it was done and the next one so on...After It was cleaned I started with the rear part, rear fenders and tonneau cover, tail gate and roll pan. Same thing I started to remove the dried klasse from the first part I started with and the next and so on.. The instructions says\\" apply a small amount of klasse\\" and they mean it, if you add heavy coats of these stuff you will have trouble removing it. Also do not add additional coats if it been more than 2 minutes apart after you applied the first coat. I did this on a front fender and it felt dried and hard so I thought I had scratched the fender. It took me about 2 hours to add and remove the klasse all in one. I left my truck in the garage overnight to bond the klasse all in one.  The next morning I took a clean Microfiber towel and I started to clean the dust and dirt that sat over the night. Then I started to put the klasse high sealant glaze I did the same procedure I first did, it took me another 2 hours to apply it and remove it. I left it parked in the garage after I was done, I had to go to work so I asked for a ride to go towork this way the truck can stay home for the klasse high gloss sealant bonds to the klasse ALL-IN-ONE. I did notice a change on the shine but I thought it would be like supper wet as the image on the bottle of the product but obviously it doesn't look like that. Just like any other product they exaggerate so they can sell their product. I'm not saying that is not good, if it looked wet shinny I would had given this product 5 stars instead of 4.  I hope this help someone, but I know for a fact that every paint is different so don't be afraid on trying this out. It might work better than me or any other persons. Don't be afraid to try a product, just because some said it was not worth it.

product_title: Rightline Gear 100S20 Sport 2 Car Top Carrier, 15 cu ft, Waterproof, Attaches With or Without Roof Rack
review_body: The Rightline Gear Top Carrier is a Godsend for us.  We travel between two states quite often with a 100 pound dog and a cat.  We had been driving a huge truck, but our dog has problems getting in and out of the truck now so we are trying to drive our Yukon more.  The problem was space.  We purchased a Pro Series Hitch Mount Carrier for bins and cooler and purchased this top carrier for all other items.  It is fairly easy to use (with a few video reviews) and includes four straps, the carrier and a handy bag to hold the straps and carrier that has attached instructions.  The Sport 2 car top is perfect for our Yukon and holds ALOT more than we thought it would.  The top carrier is very well made with strong canvas material.  The zippers are protected because there is a flap all the way around that covers the zippers so water does not leak in.  So far we have taken 3 trips using the carrier.  On the last trip we drove 11 hours with rain and sleet during 10 of those hours.  When we opened the carrier the next day there was not a spot of water inside.  It is important to place the carrier in the middle of the roof and be sure to pack evenly.  I tend to put more square items (boxes) in the corners to help form the shape and then pack from there.  We also purchased the non-skid roof pad to keep the carrier from slipping and to protect the roof.  Great product!

product_title: YAMAHA YZF-R6 R6 1998-2015 HEALTECH SPEEDOHEALER V4
review_headline: Once I got it hooked up to the correct connector under my gas tank it worked like a charm
review_body:
I bought this for my 2008 R6, and let me go ahead and tell you: there's a few connectors that can technically fit the harness kit. My connectors were under the gas tank (I had to lift it up to access it)... make sure it's not the green ones because I think those are for your thermostat (but it's the same type of connector, just green). There's also a connector under the seat that the harness fits to, so don't use this one either. I accidentally hooked it up to the one under the seat at first, which didn't cause any problems at all except that the SH wasn't doing its job. Once I got it hooked up to the correct connector under my gas tank it worked like a charm!

I was really concerned about the size of this unit, because I have very little room (I would even say no room) under my seat, but this little guy fits perfectly anyway. It's about the size of a Zippo lighter, but slightly thicker. The actual build quality is top-notch, and the cables are extremely great quality with fantastic strain relief (for anyone that really wants to jam their cables down in there). This unit also came with the "remote" for top speed recall... I haven't used this yet, so I honestly don't know much about it, but I will say that the "remote" is extremely long (about 5 feet or so I'm guessing), and if this is appealing to you as a feature, you could run it anywhere you want to with as much wire that they give you for it.

So it's really great build quality, tiny, and obviously extremely versatile! You may wonder how hard it is to get it going after you weave the cables where you want and mount it wherever. Let me tell you, it's a breeze. You use the online calculator from Healtech's website or else you can just use a GPS with a speed function, or get someone to follow at a precise speed (I used the GPS method), and get the bike up to to 60mph via GPS speed (real speed), divide it by what the speedometer says (mine was 73mph), then subtract "1", then times 100! So "100((60/73) - 1) = -17.8".... mine was -17.8; The online calculator makes it simple by putting in two things, but in case you can't access it, it's a pretty simple equation. After you figure out the number for yours, just start the electronics, then hold the only two buttons on the SH at the same time, then push one button to change the digit, and the other button to continue to the next digit..... so mine was 1, then 7., then 8. That's it. If your speedometer is too slow vs actual speed, you'd change it to the "positive" option instead of the "-" option. Mine was negative. That's literally all I had to do and I have a perfect speed now, and let me tell you, I really regret not getting this little guy sooner!

product_title: Bussmann HHM Mini In-Line Fuse Holder
review_headline: Great connector for automotive applications! Ham essential.
review_body:
Fuse holder shipped with 12 gauge wire. It accepts automotive "mini" fuses also known as APM or ATM. This is the smaller of the two types of fuses very commonly found in newer cars. The larger fuses, which this holder does NOT accept are "regular" also known as APR, ATC, or ATO. No fuse is included, allowing the selection of the proper fuse for your application.

As I answered in the question posted on the product page...
Note that the maximum current allowed through 12 gauge wire cannot be answered simply. (See http://www.powerstream.com/Wire_Size.htm) You can feel safe with 9 Amps. Do more homework regarding specifics of your application and you may be OK with 41 Amps or more.

The holder is definitely water resistant, great for an automotive application. I would not try testing how waterproof it is by submersing it.

The ends are prepared to be connected with splices. I connected one end to my car battery using a ring terminal and the other end to 12 gauge wire using a butt splice. Heat shrink is helpful to slow oxidation.

My application was to wire an amateur radio transceiver about 6 feet away that can output 50 watts of power. I connected to the transceiver using two sets of red and black Anderson Power Pole connectors, which is almost a standard in the ham community.

product_title: RVLock V4 Keyless Handle w/ Integrated Keypad & Fob
review_headline: Great RV Upgrade to Feel More Secure
review_body:
We received a new RVLock v.4.0 keyless RV door handle with integrated keypad and key fob to review, coincidentally shortly after discovering that the key to our old fifth wheel unlocked the door to our new rig. We don't freely give out glowing product reviews to RV manufacturers but this product really lives up to its claims. I don't know if we received a newer version than the folks who gave this bad reviews, but the one we got isn't loud, and it's very well-made and solid.

The lock was easy enough to install in less than 10 minutes and it's given us a whole new appreciation for keyless entries. With 3 ways to get inside the rig (a key, a keypad and a remote), you have many options to use the product according to your needs. I really learned to appreciate it the day after we installed it when I came home from the grocery store and had my hands full of bags. Since I had the key fob in my hand all I had to do was click it to open the door, without having to drop my bags, reach out and stick a key in a lock. The remote made coming home with full hands much easier than before. It's also GREAT to have a keypad option when we go out for a morning run and don't want to carry keys or try to hide them somewhere in our outer compartments (I've always been paranoid that a thief would see me doing that).

My only complaint is that the beep noise it makes is louder than I'd like. It's kind of an announcement to your neighbors that you're leaving somewhere. However I'm guessing that with the age demographic of the average RVer, the company knew they had to something to accommodate all of those RVers with age-related hearing loss.

We really do like this product. For more details about installation and use, see our blog post http://www.liveworkdream.com/2015/01/07/keyless-rv-lock-handle/

review_body:
Chemical guys makes another competent product. I've gotten to try a couple Chemical Guy cleaners (if you count this as the second) and so far I'm liking it.

Now first off, as with many products of this nature I'm a bit skeptical as to some of the claims. For instance, the product says that it supplies Vitamin E to keep the leather healthy. Maybe your leather is different, but mine tends to come separated from the source animal, so I'm a bit confused as to how the animal (even if it were still alive) could possibly metabolize the Vitamin E in order for that Vitamin E to take up residence in the skin that my leather was made from. Seems like a bit of a gap in logic there.

Ridiculous faux-science claims aside, this is a competent leather cleaner. Normally I'm a fan of the Armor-All line merely because it's a proven brand that does well enough. Compared to Armor-All, I find this product does a better job of cleaning- it removes what blemishes my leather had- while still giving a good level of shine. This is an excellent all-around, one-stop cleaner and conditioner. Recommended.

product_title: 2x Integrated Motorcycle Bolt-On Xenon White LED License Plate Light + Brilliant Red LED Rear Brake Stop Tail Lamp Bulb
review_body: this shipped from China so prepare for the wait. Alright, Here's the assumption and its wrong. Assumption: "I can wire the white plate light to my taillights and the red lights to my brake lights". That is incorrect. Its only setup with one red and black. It works with both lights on together or nothing. So you can have your license plate light only work when you hit the brakes or you can have your brake lights on all the time with your headlights - neither are good options. These are super bright which is awesome. I might add a resistor to dim them just a bit. I'm good at electronics so I unscrewed the bolt from the light housing. pulled out the small red wire attached to the white light and separated the operations. I now need to solder a long lead to that wire and fit it back through the bolt. I noticed there is NO chance the leds are going to come out or allow water in. they are glued in there tight. I was surprised to get 4 of these but thats great so if I mess one up I have spares. I found a company in UK that sells these same modules but with a 3 wire lead which is correct but I will try my mods first as they are 3 times the price.

review_headline: These work great, but I wish they were all and inch ...
review_body: These work great, but I wish they were all and inch longer.  The short ones are 1 3/4" long and the long ones are 3" long.  I used them to seal up my fishfinder cords when I installed it.  I used them over the crimp connectors.  You can get adheasive lined heat shrink crimp connectors.  They are pretty expensive.  I tried them for one connection and there great, but I still put this tubing over them.  I am in salt water the cord will lie in the bottom of the boat and I want the connections as water proof as possible.  The big one you slide over the crimp connector won't shrink down enough to seal the small wire so before crimping I used small diameter tubing shrunk over each wire before crimping on the connector to bulk up and seal the larger tube I slid over the crimp connector.  So I used 4 different sizes in all making my connections as I built it up.  So if you plan to do as I did you need a range of sizes.  I used a Bic lighter to shrink the tubing, but be very careful not to char the insulation or shrink tubing.  I am up dating this review because another reviewer mentioned silicone tape.  I ordered some to fix a nicked up extension cord.  This might have been a better choice or I might have used it with the adheasive tubing.  Check it out. http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00004WLKT/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 This is the stuff I ordered.  Up date:  I used the silicone tape to repair a nicked up 12 gauge electrical cord.  The tape doesn't stick to the surface it is applied to, it sticks to itself.  To get a water tightness it works like a gasket under compression.  You wrap around tightly then spiral down and do another wrap around.  This would have been a poor first choice for the small diameter wires I was working with.  Maybe a wrap after the heat shrink, but I haven't done it because I don't think it is worth the bother.  I also cut some of the heat shrink in half legnth wise giving me two short pieces of "tape" which I used to do some of the repair with.  It's working pretty good to my suprise.  I cleaned and lightly sanded the cord in the repair area before applying, which was a pain.  I like the silicone tape better for this repair.

product_title: 303 (30302) UV Protectant Spray for Vinyl, Plastic, Rubber, Fiberglass, Leather & More
review_body:
It is good to try and protect those leather goods, so I ordered this to try it out. I find it to go on easily, come off cleanly, and to not affect the appearance of the leather.

The product comes in a canister that resembles the normal hand wipes you find at the store. Each wipe is about 7 inches by 8 inches, and the wet material has a slight (but not offensive)odor - it reminded me of vanilla. The canister snaps closed after use. I tried the product out on a leather chair. The wipe left a small amount of film on the surface, which I then wiped off, per the instructions). After wiping, the surface did not appear any different than before, and it felt the same. I'm pleased that it doesn't leave a shiny surface (like some products).

It will require some time to see if the product actually protects against sunlight - I'll try it on some things that get out in the sun and report back if there are any problems. One never really knows how well this sort of thing works, because once applied, there is no real way to say it has done any good - unless you have an identical item that you don't treat. The instructions say it can be used on leather, vinyl, plastic, chrome, alloy, synthetic / natural rubber, and fiberglass - but not on unfinished leathers like suede, fabrics, canvas, or flooring. They recommend reapplying every 3-5 weeks.

Summary: It does no harm to the leather; only time will tell how well it works. Recommended.

review_body: EDIT UPDATE:  Ok, so I now have had these mats for a couple of weeks and I've got some additional comments. First of all, these are NOT latex, so when they get wet, the foot area becomes slick. It's not horrible, but you do need to notice and take some care. I would've preferred that area to be textures such that it doesn't take on the slick quality. Next, though they are beige, they do not match the carpets, so it becomes really obvious they are there. This is more important because they are a whole foot-well coverage mat instead of a simple flat mat. I don't mind this, but there is no question. Overall, I'd still buy them and like them, but there are a couple of things to consider.    I've had the mats installed for a couple of days now and I wanted to say that they fit perfectly. Moreover, they look great. Durability will have to be assessed over time, but I'm pretty pleased just now. I am shocked at the size of the delivered package, but it doesn't appear to have negatively affected the mats themselves.    Two things I wanted to respond to from other reviewers:  1. The size of the retention holes for the front mats appears identical to the product pictures. I'm not sure what the issue with that reviewer is. I'm really surprised at how nice the mats look and don't get the complaint.  2. The third-row mats ARE small, but so is the footwell back there and the mats properly fill up the whole well.    I'll come back to this review in a few months to relate durability scores, but I'm quite happy with my purchase!

product_title: JT Sprockets JTC530Z1R118RL Steel 118-Link Super Heavy Duty X-Ring Drive Chain (530 Z1R)
review_headline: Happy so far - seems like a good value
review_body: Like kassf2, I'm reluctant to give this chain 5 stars yet since I've only got just shy of 2,000 miles on it.  But I am impressed so far.  I did a lot of research, and went out on a limb a bit in buying this because reviews/feedback on it were practically non-existent.  However, since JT sprockets seem to be held in high regard, I thought I'd try this chain, figuring JT wouldn't put their name on something of poor quality.  It was considerably cheaper than its better know competition, but was well packaged and looked to be well made.  My bike has a lot of torque, so I don't care if I have a chain some might describe as a boat anchor as long as it lasts.  I think it was pre-stretched, since so far I've only had to tighten it once, and that was just a tiny bit.  The last time I replaced a chain and sprockets using a D.I.D., I had to adjust it 5-6 times until I put around 1,500 miles on it, but after that it would go several thousand miles between adjustments.  Since a chain's rate of stretch is a key part of it's longevity, hopefully with good care the JT won't require frequent tensioning.  I'll probably do a follow-up to this review after I've logged more miles.

review_headline: Nice Quality, But I'll Get a Different One Next Time
review_body:
This is a nice little key cover. I bought this after the plastic case cracked where the small screw holds it together. The metal key shank was still rigid in the case, but the plastic backing kept falling off when I drove over bumps or set the key down on the counter. This silicone cover fits snugly, and holds everything together very nicely. The only thing I don't like about this cover is how thick it is around the buttons. It is sometimes hard to press the button since they are now recessed below the silicone surface. This is especially true for the concave trunk release button. I have to use my fingernail to get a good press on this button. If I had to do it again, I would get a cover that was solid over the top of the buttons such as this one http://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00K73M2J2/ref=ox_sc_sfl_title_2?ie=UTF8&psc=1&smid=AID95U58Y479R . (I also like the contrast of the white text on that unit, but it was not in stock when I ordered this one.)

All in all I'm happy with this one, but if I ever need to buy another, I'll get a different version.

product_title: Prime Choice Auto Parts FPKM136 New Fuel Pump Module Assembly
review_headline: Not a direct fit replacement for my 2000 Pontiace Montana
review_body: This fuel pump failed within 2 months. The Company did provide a complete refund (quickly and without hassle, so thumbs up on that), but the aggravation and cost of a tow and the inconvenience of tracking down another pump quickly for an emergency repair was not worth the price savings on this original purchase.This wasn't a direct drop-in replacement pump for a 2000 Pontiac Montana. I understood that the harness would need to be modified, but the new pump itself had a locator lug on it that was obviously designed to nest in the tank to prevent rotation. However, my Montana tank does not have a cutout for the lug; the original pump was perfectly circular without protuberances. I had to grind the lug off to get the mounting ring to fit over the new pump and tighten down. Also, the new supplied gasket/seal didn't fit (too large or thick), so the original was used. As far as the harness modification, the supplied crimp connectors (large gauge) were not sized properly to fit the existing wires on the car (smaller gauge), but were appropriately sized for the large gauge wire used in the new harness.

You are supposed to apply the 3rd first, then the 2nd then clean up with the 1st. You are also supposed to work the polish with a cloth, (they included a paper towel), perpendicular to the scratches, (across the scratches). My iPod had scratches going in multiple directions and even in swirls, but I gave it a shot. review_body:
These taillights look great and the bulbs are bright. They do fit tightly, so it takes a little bit of effort to install them (on my 04 Silverado 1500). But the wiring harnesses are perfect, once you get them in just plug and go. When you are removing your old wiring harness, be careful not to break the little plastic brackets that hold it to the frame and out of the way - just use a flathead screwdriver to pop them open so you can re-use them with the new wires.
One thing to note, though, is that the wiring to the bulbs is a bit different than the stock/original tail light. So if you are going to be splicing into it for any reason (for instance, if you are going to be installing an additional reverse light or LED tailgate light bar w/ reverse lights) you will definitely want to use a voltometer to make sure you are splicing into the correct positive wire. Do not assume that the wire color is the same as your stock light, because it may not be.

product_title: Oxford Heaterz Premium Adventure Heated Grip - One Size
review_body:
Easy installation - excellent quality.

Connections are so simple it's impossible to mess up. The controller cable has a Y adapter to connect each grip and a third wire that runs to the battery. Very easy. Installation was a breeze, just cut off the old grips with a utility knife and clean the bars/throttle body with a brush or some WD40. Make sure you TEST FIT the Oxford grips first!! This is extremely important as the super glue bonds instantly and DOES NOT give you the ability to twist the grips around to the correct orientation. I had no problems test fitting the grips. Make sure you align the bottoms of the grips as indicated in the instructions. Once you are certain you have the proper orientation (and there is NO WD40 residue on the contact surface), lube the bars/throttle body with some super glue (you don't need much--glue is provided) and slide the grips on fully all the way. I made the mistake of not fully seating the throttle grip and came up a tad too long at the end of the bar--long enough to prevent proper operation of the throttle. (I could turn the throttle but if I released the grip it would stay!! That is NOT good) I was able to easily fix it by trimming a sliver more off the end of the grip.

If you need to trim the grips you can. The instructions point out the trim lines on the grips, but I had to trim my throttle grip an extra 1/8 inch and it did not harm the grip or its heating function. But be careful; I wouldn't try trimming any more than that. So if you need to trim a tiny bit more if needed you can. That small 1/8 inch trim fixed my stuck throttle and the throttle worked normally after that (It also allowed me to reinstall my bar weight and hand guard on that side).

Operation of grips is simple: the controller has two large buttons that adjust the heat temp up or down. To turn on just press the large + button. It is recommended that you start out at 100% high temp to get the grips to warm up faster and then ramp it down to a comfortable setting. The controller automatically will turn itself off too if you forget to turn the unit off. (turn it off by holding down the - button for two seconds--there should be no lights on the panel when it's off) The controller comes with a thin aluminum mounting bracket to attach to your clutch assembly. Very nice and puts the controller right where you need it. You can also mount it to a fairing or elsewhere with the double faced tape supplied.

Overall I am very glad I spent the extra $ on these premium grips. You can buy grips at half the cost, but you might also get half the functionality and quality. You do not need to wire these to your ignition which was the big selling point for me. These grips are nice. They are well worth spending the extra money.

product_title: OE Aftermarket Suspension Sensor Original Equipment
review_headline: Cheap Knockoff that doesn't function properly
review_body: I purchased this sensor to replace a failed ride height sensor on my 2000 Mercedes S500.  The sensor is the same as the Mercedes spec sensor (my car has the base airmatic system not the ABC system).  However once I had it installed, I kept receiving intermittent *check suspension* warnings from the car.  After trouble shooting it (and replacing other components) I ended up taking it to a Mercedes specialist shop.  They ran several tests and determined the problem to be this sensor, apparently it was faulty (this sensor is responsible for determining the ride height of the car and it measures multiple parameters).  From the diagnosis I received, this sensor only was recording half of the parameters about the car that it should have been monitoring.  I had the shop replace the sensor with a sensor from Mercedes and it immediately fixed the problem.  If anyone is looking to purchase this sensor for installation on any Mercedes, I would highly recommend that you do not.  This sensor is cheaply made and not suitable for its designed task.  Also, since it took over one month to properly diagnose my car's problems associated with this intermittent issue, the return window on the product has passed.  So don't purchase this if you desire quality.

product_title: Basix Magic Shade Jumbo ( Styles may vary )
review_headline: Didn't make much difference on my black leather interior.
review_body:
Didn't make a huge difference in my car. I have a black leather interior and park my car in an open parking lot in North Carolina for most of the day. Car would still be very hot at the end of the day. Not sure if I even notice the difference using these things. On the plus they fold up really easily, and can't hurt to try. Might work better for a car with lighter interior.

If heat in your car is really an issue, consider getting your windows tinted. Even a slight tint can help reject heat a lot better than these can. And then if you use these WITH tinted windows, you're getting the most heat rejection possible.

product_title: Prime Choice Auto Parts PR65016R Front Passengers Side Performance Drilled And Slotted Brake Rotor
review_body: These appear pretty well made for being Chinese. The rotors were mostly machined, powder coated, and then the rotor face was finished leaving all of the rotor coated except the braking surface.  I measure the various dimensions with some quality digital dial calipers and all seemed on with in the .0005 tolerance of my caliper.  The run out on the face and diameter, when mounted to the hub, seemed to .05 inch or less, but it's hard to get a good reading.  I have no way of knowing if the balance was good, but I didn't notice any new vibrations.  As far as material quality and life span, only time will tell for sure, but I have no reason to think they won't hold up as good as the originals.

product_title: Motorcraft SP-514 Spark Plug
review_body: Hello,  I bought 8 of these to change my plugs in my pony at 84k.  I followed the instructions of UWISHPRODUCTIONS on YouTube for mustang spark plug change.  I cannot recommend enough the OTC 6900 plug socket (wrench never slipped and you can always tell when the socket is seated) and the PB Blaster, saved me the time, hassle and money of breaking a plug in the head.  Took me 3 hours, start to finish. (~1 hour was waiting.)    I used a 10 inch extension, an 8mm socket, an OTC 6900 Ford F-150 Spark Plug Socket, 1 can of PB Blaster, a 3/8 drive socket wrench and a 3/8 drive torque wrench that I borrowed.  First, I loosened the 8mm bolts on each of the coil boots.  Took each coil boot off in order and set the aside in order.  I then turned each plug about a quarter of a turn, just enough to loosen it for PB Blaster to penetrate the threads. Next, I let all the plugs soak in PB Blaster for about an hour.  Came back out to the garage and took them all out with ease without breaking any of them.  Replaced all the plugs with the Motorcraft SP-514's at 20 ft/lbs of torque (Ford TSB says 25 but I used PB which could cause overtightening).    My GT fired right up and is running smoother than ever.  It is too early to tell about any other benefits like MPG & improvements in power.

HOWEVER, this thing is SOOOO LOUD its not even worth having unless you fix it. This light bar makes a very loud whistle that sounds like a tornado siren going off when the ind blows across it. It does not appear to be caused by a head wind while driving. It seems it only whistles with a cross wind blowing in from he side of the vehicle. On windy days its really bad and will drive you insane. Now that being said for less than $10 you can fix this issue. With a clear plastic tube used to protect florescent light tubes just cut it to length of the light bar then cut a straight line down the middle to open it up and stretch it over the back of the light bar to cover the cooling fins. Use 2-3 zip ties to hold it in place or what ever means you would like. This works to quiet it down so yo do not hear any whistling. You don't even see it on the back of the bar so all in all it works out pretty well. Much better than spending $1,000 on a more expensive light bar. I gave it a 3 because of the value, the brightness and looks. The wind howling is clearly a design flaw and a big one.

product_title: 303 (30210) Speed Detailer Trigger Sprayer
review_body:
Till recently I only bought Meguiar’s car product off the shelf and this compares well.

I find this detailer spray very handy at this time of year. Here in California during the holiday we have days of sun and rain and finding the time to detail your car isn’t very practical. Especially with recent hose pipe use being rationed out. So this is where the spray comes in particularly handy with its fast and convenient usage.

It comes in what to me seems like a fairly large 32oz spray bottle. First time I used it I wasn’t sure what to expect. After a quick sponge, rinse and dry down with terry cloth I sprayed five squirts around the roof of my convertible hardtop which I want to protect from the elements.
The spray looks like a clear liquid that, when wiped over a surface with a terrycloth, looks quite waxy. I just rubbed around the whole surface and realized you don’t need a lot of it on a large flat surface. After rubbing it in I went to the laundry room for more cotton rags to wipe it down. I got extra rags for any excess. It only took a few minutes. The wax soon came off on the fresh cloths leaving a lovely bright shine. The roof looked like new with very little work. My other half noticed when they saw the car a few hours later.

So I really like the detailer. I’m a little lazy most of the year and only give the car a thorough polish once a year. With this product you don’t need a lot of time and preparation. It doesn’t go on opaque and is quick and easy to apply and rub off. It doesn’t leave opaque residue around edges and some overspray on the windows didn’t leave any noticeable residue that would normally catch the light when the sun shines through it.

So it’s very nice, quick and convenient. I probably only spent about 7 minutes on the hard top both cleaning and polishing with the speed detailer.

I recommend it.

product_title: 3M 32044 Imperial Wetordry  Sheet3
review_body:
Great product. It works by removing the outer layer of plastic with rough sand paper, smoothing the surface with a 3000 grit wet sanding process, then polishing and filling in the scratches with a rubbing compound. The protective layer comes from a synthetic wax and is not required for a crystal clear finish. If you follow the directions and take your time you will be pleased with the results. It took me about an hour and five-teen minutes per vehicle from tape-up to clean-up.
I got this kit and the hand operated kit at the same time with the intent to do 2 cars at once. I used the hand tool for the tight spaces and corners and the drill to do the bulk of the work on both cars -- just like you might do with a palm sander and sand paper when wood working. The disks are interchangeable between the hand tool and drill bit attachment and the sand paper, rubbing compound, and wax finish are the exact same in both kits. This plan works pretty good if you have more than one car to do.

product_title: Valvoline DEXRON VI Automatic Transmission Fluid - 1 Quart
review_headline: Make your BMW X3 Shift Like New !
review_body:
I used this to change out the ATF in my 2008 BMW X3 3.0si at 93,000-miles. The transmission now shifts MUCH smoother than before. Mine took almost 5-qts to drain and refill. The 2007-2010 US BMW X3's (E83 models) are equipped with a GM-GA6L45R automatic transmission and BMW recommends Dexron-IV ATF. This Valvoline Dexron-VI fits the specifications, and it is also one of the few full synthetic options on the market.

BMW says the ATF is a "lifetime fluid". I don't believe there is such a thing as a lifetime fluid. Now that I have seen what the original ATF looked like after 93,000 miles when I drained it out, I definitely don't believe in lifetime fluid...it was really dark and really in need of being changed. It's an easy job...go do it !

Remember that roughly half of the fluid will remain up in the transmission and torque converter, so most people drain and refill, then drive a few hundred miles, and then drain and refill again in order to get most of it changed out. Also, note the BMW process of having to top up the fluid level with the engine running to get the right quantity of fluid in the transmission...it's easy to mess that part up if you aren't used to doing it on other car brands. Read up on the process before you change your ATF on a BMW.

review_body: Quality of the Zamp Solar 200 Watt Portable Kit is first rate in all respects with one exception. Due to poor design, the folding aluminum legs for the 200 Watt Kit are incapable of supporting this relatively heavy unit (appx 45 pounds) in a stable manner.  The words rickety and wobbly are not out of place in describing this defect.  Any mild physical disturbance originating from right or left will cause deployed panels to sway widely from side to side, giving good reason for concern of collapse.  The legs themselves are not the problem.  The problem is over-flexibility in solar panel frame segments serving as attachment points for the legs. The user can overcome this defect by anchoring panel array to the ground via stakes or weights situated on both sides, but this should not be necessary given the high cost of this unit.  The whole point of paying premium price for a portable solar array is to get one that can be deployed on ground with reasonable stability.

product_title: Peak PKC0BU7 Wireless 7-Inch Back-up Camera Kit
review_body:
I have this unit installed in my 2007 Nissan Titan with a Leer topper. The camera is mounted on the license plate and is aimed slightly down using the provided shims. The wireless transmitter is mounted in the topper by the hinge. The 7" screen fits nicely in front of my navigation screen in the dash.

Reception is acceptable, good enough to clearly see the ball mounted on my receiver hitch and the trailer hitch as I back up to it. It will also show objects further away but I rarely use it for that. I have external LED light bars mounted under my bumper. When these lights come on at night they are very bright and wash out some of the backup camera's picture.

After about four years the camera fogged up on the inside due to moisture (one too many river crossings or trips to the car wash). It would take a couple of weeks to dry out. I contacted Peak customer support and they sent me a new camera which works fine. The failure to stay sealed is the only reason I reduced my score to four stars.

If you aren't handy with electrical stuff then this may not be for you. You'll need to tap into a power source to power the camera and transmitter. I located the wires going to my backup light in one of the tail lights and tapped into those using the provided hardware. I subsequently rewired it to not use the plastic taps and instead used a small distribution board mounted to the metal. The plastic taps, while they are the quickest and easiest method to get power, seem to be unreliable in the long term.

product_title: Sachs SG301053 Trunk Lid Lift Support
review_headline: This is correct item for MK V VW Golf models
review_body:
Exact fit for my 2009 GTI; installed with no problems in just a few minutes. How to videos on seller website very helpful.
EDIT 10/22/15 - This item ultimately did not work for my GTI. The fit seemed right, the opening pressure was strong, but the hatch would kind of bang against the hinges unless I held the hatch at the top of the lift. The seller advised that about 30 days of use should see the opening force of the struts diminish. I gave it 60 days, no change. The seller exchanged for a new set (on their dime). That set operated exactly the same. Seller advised reversing the mounting direction (essentially to mount them upside down). That seemed to have some effect, but not enough. Seller and I agreed that I should continue using the struts to see if the problem would resolve; if not the seller would refund. After several months with no change, I went to the local VW dealer and tried a pair of OEM struts. The OEM worked perfectly, but the price is higher. I bought the OEM and returned these to the seller for a full refund. While these struts did not work for me (never did figure out why; as you can see from other posts, lots of people have bought these and did not experience any problem; perhaps the mounting ball studs on my car are ever so slightly out of position, or perhaps both sets of struts provided by the seller were from a production batch slightly off spec), I continue to recommend the seller and the product. You can buy with confidence from this seller because they will stand behind the product. In my case, they made a full refund after I had used their struts for some 8 months. You cannot ask for better customer service!

product_title: Arcan ALJ3T Aluminum Floor Jack - 3 Ton Capacity
review_headline: A premium home garage tool - very good but not perfect...
review_body:
I bought this to replace a 3 ton Torin Black Jack floor jack that started leaking after 7 years. I decided to splurge on the Arcan ALJ3T (almost 3x the cost of the Torin) because I wanted something that was lighter, could pump faster, and would be easier to control on descents. The Arcan is certainly lighter (by some 30 lbs) and, therefore, easier to maneuver around the garage. It's still pretty heavy to carry, so I resort to my smaller 1.5 ton jack if I need more portability. The two pistons on the Arcan help it to get up to the jacking point much faster, but it still takes as many strokes as my old Torin to actually lift the vehicle off the ground. On the plus side, the two pistons and longer handle mean that I need less effort to jack up my SUV. It would have been more helpful for the rubber guard around the lower handle to be a little higher (the bare metal portion of the handle could still hit the bumper of my SUV when I was jacking up the rear cross member). Fortunately, this is not a deal breaker because I just applied my own home solution by wrapping some pipe insulation around the upper handle. I also like the wide saddle (about 4.5\\" diameter) with a firm solid rubber insert (unlike the Torin whose rubber insert compressed significantly under load) and dimpled surface. Finally, the knurled shaft and universal joint at the release valve help immensely with nice controlled descents (unlike the Torin which was much more difficult to control because the release valve seemed to be either \\"fully open\\" or \\"fully closed\\"). I did not notice any significant flex in the handle as noted as elsewhere. Overall, I would call this a premium home garage tool. If budget was an issue and I was only using it occasionally, I would probably still go with a much cheaper floor jack from Costco / Sam's Club (e.g. a Torin Black Jack).

P.S. I had a good chuckle at the review that subtracted a few stars because the color of the new model is completely silver rather than blue / silver as pictured. I suppose if my tools, my tool chest, my car, my work gloves, and my glasses were all blue, then I would be upset too. LOL...ue / silver as pictured. product_title: Kensun Air Compressor
review_headline: I'd easily estimate 5 minutes per tire
review_body: The air-gauge on this is off by 11 psi (It reads 11psi too high), so that's a big no-no. Sure, it'll fill my tires up, but not to the maximum psi which is what I'm using to maximize fuel efficiency. And, boy, did it take a long time to fill it up to 44psi from 28psi! I'd easily estimate 5 minutes per tire, and the whole affair took me 20 minutes. Considering that the instructions told me to run the car the entire time, I think it easily took half a gallon of gas to fill it up completely! Looking at the above comments, I can see why people thought it filled up their tires so quickly - Because they thought it filled it up to 45 psi in minutes when it was actually still at 33psi in reality. Probably would've been cheaper to pay the gas station $1 to fill up my tires. On the other-hand, considering how underpowered this thing is, that probably means it's more on the reliable side, and there's little to no risk of blowing a fuse, so that's why I'm rating this three-stars instead of the one star it'd otherwise deserve.

product_title: Jaybrake Two Button Micro Switch Clamp Chrome for Harley
review_body:
The important thing to keep in mind about this particular item is that it is specifically designed to work with the Jaybrake Classic Master Cylinder hand control. In other words these particular hand controls have cutouts for the wires and switches so that you don't have to drill anything. There is an exit channel machined into the control so that the wires can be routed around the bar and out the left side of the controls. The only reason you would have to drill a hole is if you wanted to run the wires through the bars. I actually bought this to mount on my Jaybrake classic clutch hand control, but unfortunately the clutch does not have the channels machined out for this switch, only the master cylinder has them, so I had to change my plans and mount it on the other side (It would be better if Jaybrake machined the channels in all of their hand controls).

My only major complaint against these is that the solder joints going to the micro-switch are very delicate. I broke one of them and had to re-solder it.

Waited a whole month for this to come in and when they finally did.. it was worth the wait. The material looks authentic matches my interior. The hinges were the correct ones. Build quality is what you would expect for the price paid and is really not that bad but the feeling of finally getting a replacement armrest lid is priceless. Plus I got an extra one just in case. product_title: Jump-N-Carry
review_body: Alright, in the last year, I have had to use this thing 3 times, 2 times it's failed me. Unfortunate. My roommate, however, has had to use it about 5 times, in which he said it worked great every time. So what gives? I think the key is the battery.    My car is a Toyota Avalon with the 1MZ-FE V6 3.0L engine, and the battery was definitely old. My roommate had an older cheap car from Kia, but obviously smaller amp requirements for its tiny V4 engine, and who knows about the battery. My 3 situations with my car, the Avalon, were as follows:    1- Sat in car waiting, turned car off but left key plugged in without thinking. So used to everything turning off automatically (spoiled) that I just started playing around on my phone without paying attention. The key plugged in made everything stay on (exterior, interior, and dashboard lights). This was an hour passed before I realized and turned everything off. At this point, I was thinking \\"meh\\" as an hour should be no problem on a 100% charge (which it was). Well, no such luck, the car turned over about once per second with no ignition. I was almost a little happy because I knew I had this Clore jump pakc in my trunk, and I was eager to use it (I was confident after reading all the rave reviews on here). There are few things worse than being over-confident with a smirk on your face, and quickly losing that with a swift hand of fate like getting a surprise ALS ice bucket challenge on your head. My car not only didn't start, it made absolutely no difference with this battery pack hooked up. I was dismayed to say the least, luckily I found some friendly strangers. The pack showed 3 lights when checked; should be able to jump my car no problem.    2 - I was washing my car and while cleaning the inside I left the interior lights on for about 1 hour. This drained the car to inoperable levels, and after hooking up this pack, it turned over slowly still but started back up. Probably right past the line where it wasn't able to start. This was right after I had fully charged the Clore pack the night before.    3 - Just yesterday, I stopped my car while getting some food. I checked my phone for about 10 minutes prior to getting out, during which time the car lights were on. I got out without thinking twice, locked everything just fine, and then came out after about 25 minutes. The car wouldn't start. Same symptoms as situation 1. I thought to myself \\"f!@#\\" as I knew this time, despite having the pack in my trunk, I didn't fully charge it recently. It WAS fully charged though when I put it in my trunk (3 months ago). So I hooked it up, and lo' and behold, no dice. Same thing as situation 1; not even a change in the symptoms. Once again, luckily, I was able to convince a chick to help me out while in the middle of a pitch black parking lot in which I was by happenstance parked right next to her car... Yeah...luckily she trusted me otherwise I'd have been screwed.    In all 3 situations, the status light was 3 bars (full). This means that either the lights aren't reliable at all, or the battery just doesn't have the gumption for my medium size engine (disappointing). Recharging it is not even reliable because as soon as I plug it in it says its good (4 lights), and the manual says it's not recommended to leave it plugged in that state.    At this point in time I KNEW I had some sort of battery problem. It's these kind of problems, though, that this jump pack was made for, but I was unfortunately unable to receive these amazing functions as everyone else seems to have been able to. So in a sense this product has failed me. Tonight, I took my car to Autozone, got it tested, and as suspected the battery was labelled \\"bad\\". It gave 12.7V with 100% charge on the meter, but it likely just wasn't driving the needed amperage (525 CCA rated, new of course). So I popped in a new Duralast Gold with 750 CCA and 3 year free warranty replacement (5 year total). Shouldn't ever be a problem now, but I will adjustmy rating as my experience changes with this product should I need to use it sometime again.  On a side note, this does drive my portable air compressor fairly well that I carry in my trunk.

He also smoothed the intakes going into the chamber just above the valve seats maybe an 1" or 1.5" up the intake runners. He said the Edelbrock parts were quality pieces and req'd nothing further, and should last like OEMs or better. As for street performance, I can't be more satisfied for the price, quality, and WOW the seat of the pants performance improvement over the steel OEMs. Flow out of the box beats the fully ported '65 OEMs ~240cfm to ~220cfm @ .500". With the massaging, probably closer to 250+cfm @.500 lift. I was warned not to use the 2.02 version on my stock 289 application to keep up the torque and clearance issues...EDL Performer 289, Comp Die Cast roller rockers, Dynamax X-pipe, turbo muffs, and 1 5/8" Doug's long tubes have surprised all who have ridden in it - it all seems to work together nicely. product_title: STANLEY Ll1000 Li-Ion Battery Jump Starter
review_body:
I am an Auto technician for over 20 years. I specialize in German cars and trucks.
Ive used many many jump boxes over the years. I saw this and figures foe under $60 why not give it a try.
Today it is 35deg F I disconnected the battery on my old beat up 96 suburban work truck. 5.7L V8 (It has been sitting all night and needs a tune up, cobblers kids need shoes that's how it goes) It was a little slow to get going but then cranked like a champ and started. I did this 5 times letting it sit several minutes between starts and it still read 12.5v and only dropped 1 bar on the graph
Now this thing is bigger then those pocket things, BUT the CLAMPS are METAL and the WIRE IS HEAVY GAUGE. This is very important! I have seen many plastic clamps break over the years and wires melt. It is real hard to hold a broken clamp on a battery and crank at the same time. THIS STANLEY LI000 WILL NOT HAVE THAT PROBLEM
The case is heavy with rubber around the edges. Definitely feels like it can take many drops.
I have written several reviews on amazon as I use them when buying a product and feel it definitely helps to hear fro some one who owns one. and I own one. May even get one for the shop.

on a side not you should ALWAYS connect the NEGATIVE lead to a NON moving METAL part of the ENGINE or frame, and give both connections a good wiggle to make sure you have good contact between clamps and where they connect.Some cars can be damaged by connecting it directly to the battery. This also helps give a more direct route for current to flow.

product_title: Nitro Aikido Full Face Helmet
review_headline: SHARP Helmet Safety Rating of 5 stars is all I need. Anything else is a bonus.
review_body:
This is my first helmet. I went into stores looking for a very safe helmet and to determine fit. Once I learned of this through internet research and that it was the cheapest helmet to earn a 5-star rating from SHARP (look it up online if you don't know - great information on impact protection), I bought it.

Fit: Excellent. Bought a large and it was perfect for my head. I'm 5'4, medium build, 165 pounds.

Road/Wind Noise: Good. The helmet is fairly quiet inside, except for a whistle that has developed over time. I think the vents may have broken into a given position which leads me to the next point...

Ventilation: I can't really tell. It haven't been able to notice much of a difference between the open and closed position. I would prefer a little more air when I'm hot, and would love to eliminate the wind whistling sound completely when it's cool outside.

Comfort: I have almost 2,000 miles under my belt on it now and I can't complain about comfort. Note that if you like to use earbuds while you ride, this helmet isn't for you. It's snug around the ears (as it should be), and trying to get a bud in your ear before putting it on will only result in the earbud shifting. However if you want a nice helmet with a removable, washable liner and nose guard, it's a great choice.

Safety: This is what my choice boiled down to. If all factors were equal, this would be a 4 star review. However given the helmets excellent performance in the SHARP tests, I can't mark this helmet anything less than a 5. If I'm in a high speed accident, I trust it gives me the best chance of returning to my family.

review_headline: Impairs visibility with smears, do not use
review_body:
This is an awful product - an utter engineering failure whose continued ubiquitous presence in auto parts stores is a shining triumph of marketing. Used precisely as directed, it leaves obvious smears that last for weeks and are difficult to clean off. Overall, it provides a significant reduction in night vision clarity, with no apparent effect on window fogging.

If you are a smart person who checks Amazon reviews before purchasing or using things, you can stop reading now.

On the other hand, if you are like me, and used this on impulse because it sounded neat and you thought RainX was a reputable brand, keep reading.

You are now faced with the challenge of removing this smeary crap from your windshield so you can see again. This is surprisingly tricky. I tried both soap and Windex with no luck. Fortunately there are many threads on the internet written by unfortunate folks in the same predicament, and a recommendation from one of those worked for me: First, wash the windows with full strength distilled white vinegar. Then, wash them again with Windex. My windows are clear again.

product_title: Airaid 200-996 M.I.T. Modular Intake Tube
review_headline: Pretty neat and pretty easy to install
review_body: Pretty neat and pretty easy to install.  It certainly looks like it would decrease drag on the air flowing toward the throttle body and thus obviously increase the airflow, but a guy like myself can only accept this in theory as I am not an engineer.  I put this on the pickup with a K&N filter and the sound was the biggest thing I noticed.  If accelerating or under a load at all, the truck was definitely louder, especially around 2-2.5k RPM.  Later on I installed Gibson dual exhaust and the noise changed again - different loudness and different RPM range.  I think this route is a good option for those who would rather keep their OEM airbox.  No messing with sensors (my truck has never thrown an engine light from this product), and in my opinion the OEM airbox better protects against dust and road grime or junk like when treatments have been put on the road after a snowstorm.  For what it's worth, my truck sports the filter and this intake tube with the exhaust as stated, as well as the Hypertech econ programmer, and I don't think I need any more power from a 5.3 gasoline engine (wait, did I just say that?)  Of course, a tuned-up diesel with a chip and turbo did beat me in a drag, but that's apples and oranges.
