product_title: K&N 57-9013 FIPK Performance Air Intake System
review_headline: A worthy ivestment that pays dividens in performance and cost savings
review_body:
I am a big K&N fan. I have them in all my cars. I have always been impressed with the quality and engineering that goes into their products and love that they are USA made.

It is definitely a personal thing and you have to decide yourself if this is something that works for you. It is something I have found that works for me. I like the ability to not have to replace filters all the time, saving money and getting good performance at the same time.

They stand the test of time and have really good tolerances.

This was my first air intake system. Most of the time I just get their filters and have vehicles with 150K+ miles and have gone through many recharges without issue.

I don't have a way to measure gains to HP and MPG other than the way I push the pedal to the metal and fill ups.

I am happy with the performance of the product in those aspects. I seem to have to rev less hard and seems to idle smoother and takes less effort to go places.

An obvious bonus is the way it sounds. Maybe some people buy these just for that reason alone and I am ok with that.

I think its a worthy investment to a vehicle.

I live in Arizona and have a dusty, dry environment and have never had issues fording rivers or too much moisture causing problems with my filters. That should be something you consider if you decide on a product like this is your environment you will be using it in.

I had to install and remove this system 3-4 times to do various projects on my engine and each time it mounted up nicely and stayed true to form.

If I had to give it any complaint it would be that if I don't pay enough attention to how tight I put the cone on and go off roading too hard I could find my cone loose or even disconnected bouncing around the compartment behind the shield.

Easy to fix by checking it all over by twisting everything and using good clamping locations and appropriation torque when installing.

Installation instructions were pretty easy to follow. Removal of the old intake system was the most difficult part of the process.

EDIT: Well as I suspected, after about two weeks of having this piece of junk in my car, it came loose. It wasn't the set screws that got loose, as they have blue loctite on them. Simply the entire assembly just came loose off the shifter. Don't waste your money with this pos.

..........................................

I got this for my Golf GTI MK4. Since its shifter rod is not threaded I needed an adapter.

Adapter itself is a pretty simple piece of kit. The top threading is for the shifter knob. Base has a wide opening with three holes on its side, with screws that you tighten down and clamp onto your shifter rod. The wide opening at the base then has a narrower hole that goes through the top where threads for the knob are.

The design of this adapter is pretty poor in my opinion. As you can see the base (wider part) is pretty short. That is how much this adapter will grip your shifter rod, so basically just the very tip of it. Now if your rod is thin enough, you might be able to slide the adapter further down, through the narrower hole that is on top, where the threading is.

However this also has its problems, as the side screws that come with this adapter to tighten it down on the shifter rod, are not long enough. Basically if you can fit your rod through the narrower top hole, the screws won't be able to touch it, and therefore tighten the adapter against it.

I was able to mount this on my GTI, with a blue loctite on the three clamping screws so that they don't come lose as per previous reviews. Adapter does sit securely (for now) on the rod, and there is no play. However I am still very cautious about it, and honestly do not think it will last for a long time, and will simply come lose one of these days.

The biggest change that I would do to this adapter, is to simply lengthen the base part by an inch or so and offer it in multiple inner diameters. This way it can grip more of the shifter rod, and you can find the diameter that will fit a bit tighter than what is currently is.

product_title: SiriusLED Fanless Cree XM L2 High Power Chipset 3000 Lumen LED Bulbs for Headlights Fog Lights DRL Daytime running Size H4 9003 HB2
review_headline: The quality looked good, but I decided to try another rather than ...
review_body:
This is the third LED headlight conversion kit I tried installing in my 1998 Subaru Forester. The first kit, the "Innovited LED Headlight Conversion Kit "All Bulb Size" With Cree LED - Replaces HID - H4 9003 Dual Beam" came with one of the lights not working. The quality looked good, but I decided to try another rather than risk another failure. The second kit, the "AS Vision AS-HLLEDH46KH/L H4 High-Low 6,000K Conversion LED Kit for Headlights" worked out of the box, but I sent it back.

Both those kits come with a ballast that hangs off the end of the unit. These little boxes are extremely noisy electrically - they produce a lot of radio frequency interference (RFI). When the second kit was installed, I noticed immediately that my radio sounded like the station had been moved 50 miles further away - lots of static. This made listening intolerable. I grant that this may have been because my car's radio was not designed to reject RFI that may have been present on the power inputs.

These all-in-one units are very quiet. I can't say I never get any static, but it is rare and minor when it happens. They'd get 5 stars if it never happened, but I'd recommend them otherwise. They're easy to install, very bright, and make a noticeable difference in how I see the road at night. I've only had them a month, so I can't comment on how long they last. If they fail within a year, I'll update my review. In general, they're a high quality, well-made units.

review_body:
BEWARE! Plastic tube can (and did for me yesterday) fall off nozzle into cylinder through spark plug hole. I finally googled the problem and see that I've had plenty of company for years! Why Sta-Bil hasn't put a nozzle with a non-detachable tube or at least one that securely attaches is only because Sta-Bil hasn't been paying for the subsequent required head removals. Surely, they could at least have included a warning. Too many folks having the same frustrating and costly consequence!!!!!!

UPDATE 11/24/14: Got straw out of cylinder after two partial days of disassembly of motorcycle to get better access and using a bore scope and grabber and lots of luck. I tried vacuuming, gorilla tape on a wire, and lots of fishing. I was lucky. This problem is documented for s least 7 years plus with various frustrating, time consuming results. Hold the straw when using or don't even risk it unless you really need this. Harley mechanic here in Oregon told me he hasn't fogged his during 6 month layups for the past 17 years. I'm going to just use the Sta-Bil fuel additive and avoid the fogger. If your conditions require fogging, then I would duct tape the straw and hold it to be sure it doesn't shoot off into the cylinders.

product_title: OTC 4521 Hose Removal Tool
review_body:
This tool simply rocks. I always struggle with hoses that were stuck on water pumps, thermostat housings and everything in between. It seems no matter what, the hoses stick on like they were glued in place. This thing removes the hose every time. The shape of the hook works very well at separating the hose from the any neck it is on and I am able to get around the entire neck most of the time with the way the thing is angled.

The only downside - you may not always be able to re-use the hose every time. The sharp point does allow you to get in between the hose and neck it is attached to, but because the sharp tip allows for that to occur, it will also pierce the hose without much effort if you start lifting the hose away from the neck with the tool. Don't use it as a pry tool in the hose or you will poke through the hose every time.

I did damage one hose to the point I couldn't use it again because of the sharp tip, but the time and aggravation saved working on an old truck and family vehicles is WELL WORTH damaging the one hose. The simple fact that I didn't up with bloody knuckles from the hose flying off from my hand jamming against the engine when the hose finally dislodged from the tug of war and tools flying down the street after the cussing fit was well worth it to me.

I decided to use my hands to apply product to everything, and it worked out very well. I felt that I was better able to massage the conditioner into my jacket and shoes using my hands than I would have been if I used a lint free cloth. I was a little worried about getting a thick, sticky conditioner on my hands and possibly making my nails look gunky, but the product cleaned right off very easily and left no residue. (By the way, there are very inexpensive lint free cloths available on Amazon.)

After reading a number of the reviews on Amazon and watching the how-to videos on the Leather Honey site, I felt confident enough to get to work. I applied the product to an old, distressed leather jacket (about 10 years old) that had never been cleaned or conditioned, an old pair of Camper boots (about 7 years old) that had also never been cared for, and a couple of pairs of new leather boots that I recently purchased. I found applying the product to be quite easy; it didn't take nearly as long to treat everything as I thought it would, and I didn't feel that I had to use a lot of elbow grease to work the product in. The conditioner made the jacket and boots look like new! I wasn't sure what to expect, but I am really impressed. I checked on everything the next morning and all of the products were dry with no residue on them, so I was able to wear a pair of boots to work. It happened to rain that day and the rain beaded up on the boots, just as it should.

I would absolutely recommend Leather Honey to anyone who needing a conditioner to protect their leather or bring old leather items back to life.r to protect their leather or bring old leather items back to life.

The only good story here is that Amazon was very good on taking it back, making it very simple to return.

But I needed a hitch, so went to U-Haul who had the identical hitch. Ordering it online from U-Haul gave me a $20 discount and the installation was only $40. So it cost me only $20 more than Amazon and installed. Here is the most interesting part. The U-Haul hitch was bent too but they had the equipment to re-bend it and get it to fit. I asked the mechanic if that is a common problem and he said 4 out 5 come bent and need to be adjusted.

So unless you have the equipment to bend this part, then beware.

product_title: Save A Battery 1702 12-Volt Battery Charger Maintainer and Tester
review_headline: and it has been a great addition to my garage
review_body:
I bought this Save A Battery Charger Tester Maintainer in December of 2011, and it has been a great addition to my garage. I bought it to see if the third Optima battery that has lasted just over the warranty period could be saved...it was not to be, so I bought an Interstate battery, and put this on my lawn mower battery which had needed a jump to get going. This cured that issue, and brought the charge status of my jump-starter back up to 100%. I expected to replace the mower battery by now-not necessary-it takes and holds a charge now that I have cycled it as recommended in the 1702 manual. Also takes care of all my 12V batteries...rejuvenating them to longer run times! One further note, recently, I thought I had an issue with the unit failing-the lights were doing the right thing, but the low voltage alarm and charging were not happening. A quick call to Granite tech support walked me through the obvious, and educated me as to the lower voltage limit at which the unit will charge. The customer service was outstanding, it was great to have tech support handled by an American who was so familiar with the product he did not need a script, or to put me on hold, or approval from/check with anyone else to actually take care of a customer.
Did I mention the person I was talking to in technical support was the owner of the company. Talk about a company totally invested in Customer Service! The owner answered the call-I was not transferred-there was none of the typical "Your call is important to us so please hold" after pressing one for english, 39 for techinical support and then a transfer to a very polite but hard to understand person whose native language is certianly not engilsh and who is clearly reading from a script and not equipped to handle the reason you called.....
NO, the owner of Granite aswered the call, The call was enjoyable, and best of all it quickly addressed and handled the issue! I had one connection that was visually correct, but not flowing current-not one on the unit, one I had made,

This unit has resuscitated two of the three batteries I have used it on that were consistently under-performing, and I have no doubt it has helped the two new batteries I use it on to get a good start to increasing their useful . I had replaced a Craftsman with a Shummacher, and two other brands (I went through one with each of the Optima Batteries), and I know I have a better solution with the 1702. This charger seems way to small to be as great as it is, It comes with a nice assortment of accessories, from hardware to wall mount the unit(a seriously handy thing to do), to a couple of sets of wires-a set with alligator clips, a set with post rings, and more. all of the cables are swappable, and long enough-obviously the American who designed this built it to satisfy an actual need first, and with his own ideas of product use and satisfaction in mind-this is actually built to use, instead of being built just to work... This is a great tool to add to your garage/car hobby. Easy to setup, easy to use, easy to understand-set it and forget it. If you want to buy the right tool once instead of buying the wrong tool several times, I found this to be a perfect addition and after three years it is still going strong and has outlived the other four brands I bought combined! My batteries are all in great shape-follow the instructions-they went to all the trouble of providing them so you could go to all the trouble of reading them. Between the performance of this unit and the Customer Service of the company I won't replace this one(should I ever have to) with anything but another Granite!

08/27/17 still keeping my batteries in top shape! I use it to charge my jump box, lawn mower and car batteries...just keeps doing what I bought it to do!

product_title: Akebono ACT699 ProACT Ultra-Premium Ceramic Brake Pad Set
review_headline: Definitely improved braking performance over semi-metallic pads
review_body:
I was on vacation this summer driving on an interstate through a large city. At 70 mph a driver swerved from the main lanes onto the HOV lane directly in front of the car in front of me. We both slammed on our brakes. However, his vehicle was stopping faster than my minivan. I was able to serve out of the way safely, fortunately. However, I decided at that point that my current brake pads were not doing the job. They were the semimetallic pads from Autozone. I did some research on thes Akebono brakes and it seemed like they do a good job in panic stop situations. I saw a graph of friction (stopping power) vs applied pressure (I think) on their website and that was confirmation of the nice reviews these brakes were getting on this site. I have had them installed for several months and I am very happy with the stopping power of them. I haven't had to test them out in a panic stop situation (fortunately), but I can tell the cold braking performance is substantially better than my previous pads. The warm/hot performance seems fine as well.

Also, the brake dust is very minimal. That is a nice bonus. All in all, I am very happy. Perhaps other ceramic pads could have done the trick. I don't really care. I wanted a near sure bet that my braking performance would improve. It has. My family is worth it.

product_title: STA-BIL  Fuel Stabilizer
review_headline: Excellent product for a great price
review_body:
I've purchased this product to share with my buddies for fly fishing purposes. However, I also applied it to everything else.

Car, TV, and computer:
Used it on the dashboard, any plastic surface in the car, and wow. Compared to the Amor All and Turtle Wax products I've used, I can see why this product is so freaking expensive. Dust layers formed 3 to 4 weeks after application. The other products, I would see it within a week. Simply wiped of by merely using a terry cloth towel, running lightly over the surface. 3 to 4 weeks of non-dusting again. After 2 months, exposing the car's treated surfaces to the intense sunlight, there was very little lost of luster to the surface since application. Reapplied, and luster came back for another 2 months. Can't do the same with Armor All for 2 weeks.

Glasses and exposed surfaces:
Applied to car side windows, bathroom mirrors, and house windows, 2 months later, I still haven't seen any spot formed, nor need to reapply. Water hit the surfaces, beaded up, and rolled off. So, I applied to the kitchen dish rack drain base and utensil holder for a test. Water kept on rolling of the base and holder, and into the sink for nearly 3 months on 1 application. After 2 months, finally, a few spots here and there. Without application, calcium formation within a week. With Turtle wax and Armor All, spotting and calcium build-up within a month.

review_headline: good product just not for me
review_body:
Long write up

I bought this for my 2014 VW jetta Tdi 2.0 turbo
on first install i was enthusiastic to try this filter it looked like good quality material and the whole saving money on filters it would pay for itself within a few changes i drive alot about 110 miles a day and of that 90 or more are high way. i purchased my car as a fuel saver. before i installed this filter i was getting between 54-59 mpg depending on slope wind speed ect to get closer to 60 i would hyper mile and go 64. my average in town high way was somewhere around 49-50. when installed this i reset my ecu so that the car would have to learn the air filter and adjust the air flow as needed new car mode. so i put it in did the reset and drove about 300 miles. My in town mpg dropped from 42-47 to 20 and i wasn't driving any differently. i did notice a drop in turbo lag but also the car idled extremely rough and would almost sputter at low speeds in low rpm as for the high way the results were about the same i was getting before 54-59 high way and with this filter i was lucky to get 50-51 i was confused and disappointed the filters thinner so you would think less restriction better mpg and it was the opposite. but i digress i put another Mann filter in back to my old mpg you make your own decisions what you want but for me mpg over a tiny increase in response was not worth it

product_title: ACDelco 45C1043 Professional Idler Link Arm
review_body:
My 2002 Blazer steering was a bit loose and would wander as I was driving. I figured it could be the steering box, but since the idler arm was a bit loose as well and is way easier to change, I figured I'd start with that first.

Easy to change ! Hardest part was separating the tapered stud from the center link. Thought a few taps with a hammer might loosen it, but ended up using a gear puller I already had (I don't own a pitman arm puller which is the actual item recommended for this job) which worked out just fine. In my case I had to tighten the puller further than I thought I'd need to....and when it came free it makes a loud snapping noise.

Make sure you mark where the old idler arm is mounted to the frame since the mounting holes are elongated and you need to keep the same relationship as the existing one was installed. I used a pointed scribe and scratch around the old mounting bracket and fit the new one in the exact same position. Remember to install the grease fittings and actually add grease before putting vehicle back into service.

Figured I worked at the entire job about an hour and a half from start to finish. Not difficult, just take your time and put everything back same as you took the old one off.

When riding in the boonies there is no way to know when a break down can happen and you generally aren't going to get a tow truck in the places we all like to go.
I pack a decent tool kit (Cruz Tools) for changing tires or making small repairs but having a compact tow strap is essential. This strap is 12' long and the entire strap while in the storage bag is about the size of an open hand. It weighs almost nothing and is very strong. I can't say if the MSR or the Moose is better, they are very similar and both have performed well for us in emergency situations. If you are on the fence about buying one I would say it is cheap insurance and will work well for you.

product_title: Camco "Big Red Campfire" Propane Camp Fire
review_body: Exactly as described.  We camp in a lot of places, everything from state and federal parks to true RV parks to boon docking.  Due to many of the horticultural diseases, most places are now asking that you don't bring firewood with you.  The problem with that is most "local" firewood sellers want to sell you green wood that takes a blow torch to get it started.  Couple that with burn bans, ash mess, the smoke in your/your kids faces, the smell in your clothes and hair, and having to baby sit the fire till it goes out, and we often found ourselves just skipping the campfire.  Enter the Big Red Campfire...  Quick, easy to use, easy to transport, on/off capability, clean, burn ban approved (most places), RV Park approved (most places) - It makes the campfire very convenient.  Does it have the great smell (which we all love for the first hour, but hate the next morning) and the popping of the coals, no.  Does it give you the ambiance, heat (though lower amounts) and the ability to roast marshmellows and/or hotdogs, yes!  Will we use it every time we camp, probably not, we will still want a real campfire now and then.  But I suspect this will be our preferred choice at the end of a busy hiking/boating/etc. day when we want to sit around the campfire for an hour or two before bed.  When we are doing the stay and relax in camp, campfire dinner, stay up half the night kind of campouts, I am sure we will go hunting for wood and do the real thing.

The oxidation removal with the the two sided polishing pad made a huge difference, and dint even have to use a drill!! At this point I could not ask for better results... I still haven't applied the Wipe-it!

Simple to use, great results! I recommend this product!

review_body: These are noticeably brighter than most of the stock headlight bulbs.  The color tint is unfiltered (so still a warm hue), which means less trapped heat.  So these last a while longer than the other bulbs that over-drive the bulb, as those others have a blue coating to trap heat and require even more power be pushed through.  One of these bulbs will usually last me a little over a year in my honda civic.  Since my stock bulbs were dim at best, I tried most of the minor upgrade bulbs (everything from long life, to supposed upgrade, to slight upgrade) and the "brighter white" version of bulbs (aka blue-ish), and these were the first noticeable improvement I have found.  The blue-ish version of these and others just didn't last long enough for me not to have to keep a couple spares in the trunk. These are the best mix of brightness, durability (duration) and price that I have found.  I will be sticking with these for the foreseeable future.

product_title: NOCO XGrid 4W Portable Solar Panel and Auto Kit
review_headline: Product Performed Well In Harsh Conditions
review_body:
I received the product in packaging I would rate as excellent... a complete 5-Star in that regard.

The instructions were well written, and the express start up was a graphic that was very well done.

But, in this first time out, the battery failed to charge. I contacted the support staff at NOCO who were very helpful and very familiar with their product. It was a minor problem, but it gave me a chance to grade customer service. Another 5-Star.

From there, the battery was fully charged, and did a good job charging my cell phone. One does have to be patient; at a 5V output it will charge at a similar rate as a car charger which does take a bit longer than house power.

This review is late, but it was by design. I gave this device harder service than it probably was designed for, but it stood up to the challenge, and it is my pleasure to tell you about it.

The product went with me to an undisclosed location in east Texas. One must know the area..... steady winds and very fine dust.... along with an occasional blast of salt air from the coast.... a vicious electronic device hell. Here are a couple of examples: this dust can even creep into military grade night vision equipment, and I personally suffered a cell phone casualty to the dust 2-years ago.

And there is another point... the device went to the bush. Cell phone reception is spotty in that remote area, so the phone must be tip-top charged to reach a tower. Again, the NOCO got the job done.

I can't give this product a 5-Star only because I have only used it 4-times, but I put it at 4.8, and will update this entry in the future.

Rossi

review_body:

Cons: The materials used are definitely a step down from the OEM version. The fit and finish of the product is marginal. For instance the top half and the bottom half of the housing do not completely mate together around the total circumference. This could lead to leakage or breakage in the future. The rubber used for the keypad seems to be much thinner and or softer than the OEM version. You can actually feel the heads of the switches below. The softer/thinner rubber keys may also lead to premature wear out.

As an Engineer it is really disappointing when I see company go this far to create an OK product, but with a little more work and very little added cost they could have had a really good product.

product_title: Optima Batteries 8002-002 34 RedTop Starting Battery
review_headline: I'll never buy anything but Optima again
review_body:
No introduction needed here... I was leery about buying an Optima from Amazon because of the horror stories I have read about people buying dead batteries and Optima not returning them because they were bought from a third party. I haven't had a single problem with mine. I put it in my truck to match the other Optima that was already installed in there, charged them both for a couple of hours to top them off, and they have worked like champions ever since. My other Optima has been in my truck about three years, still passes load tests past its rated output, and holds a steady charge at 12.4v. I don't drive my truck much anymore because I bought a commuter car, so sometimes it sits for three or four weeks without a charge, but every time I hop in I have a ridiculous amount of battery power on that key turn.

I also put an optima 34 in my offroad truck back in 2006. I ran around the desert with a broken battery tie down for three years, bouncing that optima all over the back of the truck. Never broke the case, never bulged, never leaked, never quit. I drained that Optima down to 2v one time by leaving a dome light on... for a month... Took the battery out of my offroad truck, stuck it in my diesel, drove around with it for a few days to force charge it back up. I couldn't believe it, but from 2 volts it came back to hold a steady charge of 12.4v and passed a load test like nothing ever happened to it. I'll never buy any other battery.

Secondly, the listing states that it's "Shinny Metal"...it is NOT shinny metal. It is Powder Coated! There is no metal exposed! Powder coating can chip and will wear down after time and lose it's gloss.

I called the company to talk to someone and their policy is that all Amazon transaction have to be through email! PERIOD!

I have returned this item and bought the "STOW and GO" from ITC which is REAL stainless!

product_title: Rough Country Suspension 664 Suspension Lift Kit
review_body:
Great kit for the Commander. It sits level and just the perfect amount taller - my Jeep looks awesome now, even with the factory Hulk wheels and tires. As soon as I get the wheels and tires in I'll post a picture. Mine is a base 2007 with the 3.7L (yeah I know, but gotta work with what you got!) going with 17x8 Pro Comp 7105's with Goodyear Duratracs, 265/70/17. Based on my research on various Jeep forums, it seems that is the most tire you can squeeze in there without rubbing after this lift goes in.

I've never installed a lift or otherwise worked on any suspension components on any vehicle before. Thankfully, I have a friend who has (Grand Cherokee, so same setup) and solicited his help/shop. With air tools and spring compressors we knocked this out in less than 3 hours. I wouldn't recommend trying it any other way. One thing we DID NOT do is grind down the unthreaded tip portion of the factory stud on the front struts. We found if you just put the spacer on the studs partway and start the nuts, there is plenty of clearance even after tightening them down all the way without grinding them down.

One thing that leaves something to be desired is the instructions, but I think that's already been covered. Wasn't too much of a hindrance obviously, but a few things, like maybe a more detailed section on how to assemble the cups on the rear, would be nice. One other thing that has already been mentioned, the coating on the spacers, I'll echo. We put the fronts in a vice to make sure we could tighten the nuts on the spacer down good, and the coating just cracked right off with very little effort. Gotta be something better they could do with that. For me it's not a big deal... you can't really see it so it's no bother, not enough for me to deduct a star.

Overall, I'd recommend this to anyone with a Commander as the FIRST mod you do to your Jeep. Makes this thing sit right, the way it should have from the factory.

product_title: Depo 330-2014N-AS Ford Driver/Passenger Side Replacement Fog Light Assembly
review_headline: I am surprised and pleased. The installation in a Ford Escape is so ...
review_body:
It has been over two years since I ordered and installed these lights. They have not broken, dimmed, or become foggy. Considering how fast the original ones broke, I am surprised and pleased.

The installation in a Ford Escape is so easy! I turned the front wheels as far as they would go and popped out the plastic fasteners that held in the front of the wheel well cover. Then I alternately peeked through the opening and reached in to turn the bolts that held the light in. Installed the new lights the same way, except for turning the bolts in the opposite direction, of course. When I was done, I replaced the plastic fasteners that held the wheel well cover in place. I did mangle one of them, but picked up a replacement for a few cents.

If you have an Escape, don't hesitate to get these because you think the install is too much trouble - it could not have been simpler.

product_title: Toshiba D4S Xenon HID Bulbs 4300K 35W for Lexus and Toyota (Pack of 2)
review_body:
Replaced both sides yesterday and it the fixed problem of pass side that would initially light, then go out. Best to replace in pairs so bulb color when lit is the same. Bulbs deteriorate with age and sometimes color shifts.
Took about 30 minutes total for both sides. Need flashlight, wire with hook on end, and small hands. (The HID unit will rotate side to side easily when you are working to remove the bulb.)
Remove underhood cover panels, unscrew plastic cap on back of headlamp (1/8th turn counterclockwise), rotate silver bulb connector about 1/4 inch counterclockwise and pull off. Release 2 bulb retainer wires...press in on loop and move away from bulb. When released, the wire retainer will fold out. Remove bulb. Note that large u shaped slot on bulb goes up and long external bulb electrode goes down.
Don't touch new bulb glass with bare fingers since that may leave oil on glass that will burn fast and locally overheat bulb leading to premature failure.
Reinstall in reverse order. Long bulb electrode goes down. After bulb is installed, rehook wire bulb retainers, place silver connector at "10 oclock" then rotate to 12 oclock. If connector dropped down after removal, use a wire hook to fish it back up where you can grab it.

product_title: Fulton 2061166 2" x 20' Stainless Steel Gunwale Max Grip Ratchet Tie Down
review_headline: Update 4-13-15. Hooks rusting when rubber covering them peeled.Best pair of straps I have ever bought and got a great price too.
review_body: Update 4-13-15.  These have held up well and I have had no problems with rusting except on the rubber covered end hooks.  Those have both peeled off and are rusting a bit now. Stainless hooks would make this a much better deal. Or even heavy galvanized covered by the rubber.    The aluminum has pitted a bit and looks worse for wear now.  Also  the ratchet mechanism has gotten a bit harder and stiffer.  Thats pretty normal though.    Overall its still a good purchase though.  However I would be willing to pay more if they had SS hooks on them.   These two inch straps are really smooth and powerful.  Almost too big, thick and smooth of action for me.  Im used to 1 inch gear that was half rusted out.  These are a pleasure to ratchet and  its worth the price I paid for all 3 of these.  I used 2 of them for transom holders and one for a motor strap because I trailer back and forth from Miami to norther Michigan.  It was super easy to cut these with some kitchen shears and then melt the ends to keep it from fraying so I could get the length I wanted.  Although that webbing is super tough and hard to cut!  They say rated for 400 lbs but thats a serious understatement.  Im sure its for liability reasons they dont tell you to crank the whole boat up, but these things could support the entire boat if I wanted them too.  Please dont sue me its just my opinion and has not been backed by the FDA, IRS or Department of Homeland security.  LoL.  I would buy them again in a heartbeat. Been using them on 4 trips to the ocean so far in the last 4 weeks.  I sure hope every single component is high grade Stainless in them though or they will start to rust sooner or later.  Even one spring thats not SS can cause problems  when you use them like I do. But so far so good.  Will let everyone know IF I have rust problems in the future.

product_title: 303 Aerospace Protectant 32 Oz Pack of 2 Anti-Fade Spray
review_headline: Matte Finish Protectant Is Best Polish/Protector On The Market, But Does Leave Slight Oily Residue
review_body:
The Aerospace 303 is a polish and UV Protectant for Vinyl (clear & opaque)/Rubber (natural & synthetic)/ Leather/Plastic/Fiberglass/Carbon Fiber/Gel Coat. It is, in my opinion, the best available product on the market due to its effective polishing, matte finish, great UV protection, low oily residue and good price point.

Application is simple. Though the directions ask to spray directly on the surface and wipe with a clean cloth, I spray the product on a very well-wrung out damp cloth, apply to surface and immediately wipe with a clean, dry cloth. This process avoids spray spots. If you choose to spray directly on the surface and manage to get streaks, wipe with a damp cloth till streaks are removed and buff with a dry cloth. The product does not air-dry, so buffing after application is required.

My go-to cloth for cleaning/polishing are the [[ASIN:B00H72YXRK Zwipes (677-6PK) Charcoal 12\\" x 25\\" Waffle Weave Stemware and Bar Towel, (Pack of 6)]]. It is a lint-free microfiber cloth that gives you a used cotton feel after the first wash.

The 303 is a matte finish product, so the finish is clean and soft, not the traditional high-gloss you get with traditional mineral oil based products (Armor All, etc.). This can be good or bad based on the condition of your surface. Though the matte finish of the 303 looks classier on undamaged surfaces, my slightly scuffed surface looks better with a high gloss products. The gloss masks the scuff marks while the 303 highlights/reveals them.

303 is advertised as having no oily/greasy residue, but in my experience there is a slight residue - might not be \\"oily\\" in the traditional mineral oil sense, but there is some residue when you touch it.

The instructions on this bottle do mention that it contains chemicals that are known to cause cancer in California. The MSDS sheets have been difficult to locate, but I do not believe that they have changed the formula, It works and seems to be the exact same product as the [[ASIN:B000XBCURW 303 Products 30350 Aerospace Protectant - 32 oz.]] with new packaging and new labeling.

Recommended - Do Not use on floor mats or control surfaces.

Pros:
* Best non-mineral oil, non-alcohol, non-silicone based polish and UV protector on the market
* Matte finish provides a classy look
* Rejuvenates Vinyl (clear & opaque)/Rubber (natural & synthetic)/ Leather/Plastic/Fiberglass/Carbon Fiber/Gel Coat
* Slight \\"oily\\" residue to touch, but fingerprints do not show
* Great price point in this product class

product_title: Devcon Flow-Mix 5-Minute Epoxy
review_body:
Do not use the provided "precision self-mixing nozzles"!

5 minute epoxy is generally two chemicals that are liquid when kept apart, but harden once mixed. What the 'precision self-mixing nozzles' do is mix the two chemicals in their ~9cm length before dispensing the mixture directly onto your surfaces to be glued.

Once you are done dispensing the epoxy you need, about 3mL of now hardened, unusable epoxy is trapped within the disposable nozzle. If you were to use both nozzles with the provided syringe of 14mL of epoxy, you will have wasted nearly half of the epoxy.

If you do purchase this epoxy, immediately throw away the mixing nozzles. But better yet, do not purchase this product and allow them to perpetrate this scam in the name of 'simplicity'.

product_title: Nokya NOK7413 Arctic White 60/55W Pro Halogen Headlight Bulb
review_body:
If you wish to forgo the other, more difficult options of "stylish"-looking headlights, these are a decent alternative! Colored halogen bulbs like these don't require special ballasts, wiring, or relays; you simply replace them as you would factory bulbs.

Nokya Arctic White Bulbs emit a beautiful shade of COOL WHITE, which is more light-blueish than pure white. These headlights look different and more aesthetically appealing than normal yellow headlights; they're the perfect color---not over-the-top "Show-off"---but not "typical," either. You can turn them on with gusto.

After installing these, however, my Toyota Tacoma's headlights' adjustment became noticeably misaligned.
Additionally, these lights seemed more diffused than the stock ones. Light diffusion means it's softer... And with headlights illuminating dark country roads for safety, you definitely don't need 'softer.' It's my theory that the coating that gives the bulbs their blue color is responsible for this.

Again, it's a theory, and I will update this review when I precisely align my headlights and compare them to a vehicle with stock bulbs in order to confirm or deny it.

If you really want cool headlights for cheap, get Nokya Arctic White Bulbs.

However, if you want more practical, brighter bulbs that look even better, then seek options like HID projectors or LED bulbs that cost more. In the end, you receive what you invest.

product_title: Camco Portable Toilet
review_body:
PROS...
No smell. Use this in your tent or camper for days. Even the Reliance chemical (purchased separately) doesn't emit an odor of its own.
Higher than other portable toilets.
Comfortable.
Comes with several packets of orange chemical that I have not yet used.
Easy to flush. I have not had the "back-splash" problem others complained about when flushing.
It's stable. You will feel and see the quality of this toilet.
Lightweight. Easy to lift and pack into the car.

CONS...
It's difficult to fill with water from a jug unless you use a funnel (not included).
It lacks a pull-out spout to make dumping easier. Prepare for splash when you empty this into a toilet. It doesn't matter how slowly you dump the contents, it splashes.

..............

I haven't filled this to the 5.3 gallon capacity because it's too heavy for me to lift and empty. I pour about two gallons into the water tank. This gives me 4 or 5 days of usage. As with any portable toilet, the solid waste tends to drop straight down, piling up in the middle of the waste tank where the chemical water level doesn't cover it unless you use copious amounts of water when flushing. When the solid waste isn't completely covered by the chemically treated water, it will smell. I solved that problem by grabbing the sides of the toilet and gently swishing it back and forth, distributing the solid waste evenly in the chemically treated water. The smell disappears.

Campers who haven't experienced a portable toilet in their own tent don't know what they are missing. Get one, especially if you're edging into your senior years. No more midnight runs to a dark, spooky campground bathroom crawling with spiders. No more picking a campsite right next to the bathroom anymore. No more "holding it" because the maintenance men are inside cleaning or fixing something.

As a side note...Do not use bleach if you're using the chemical packs. Some reviewers are complaining about a smell. Those same reviewers admit to using bleach in their toilet. Reliance Chemical instructions clearly state not to use bleach because it renders the chemical impotent, which leads to a smelly toilet. product_title: MORryde UO12-016 Heavy Duty Shackle Upgrade Kit, CRE3000 / Stock / Equaflex 2.25" Shackles - Tandem Axle
review_headline: Great shackle kit and great service from the manufacturer
review_body: I replaced the original shackles with these and these are much better with the grease fittings.  I had a lot of questions before installing the kit and MOR/ryde was very helpful answer them.  I would very much recommend them because soon or later, the plastic bushings will wear and you'll hear the squeaking and clanking noise.  I grease the fittings with a standard grease gun.  Also, when you take the original shackles out, make sure your turn the nut and not the bolt.  The bolt has ridges that lock them into place and is very difficult to turn.  When you install the new kit, ensure you turn the nuts as well and not the bolts.  Having a torque wrench will help you to properly torque down the nuts.  I lifted the whole trailer off the ground and that makes the work much easier.  The directions are pretty good, but it will take you some time to lift the whole trailer.

review_headline: DO NOT BUY THESE: They all are failing.  EDIT:  All have failed.
review_body:
Do not make the same mistake as I did by buying these. I purchased 5 thinking they will be perfect for lighting my motorhome. The bulbs are a little larger than the original bulbs are but fit. The light that these emit is sort of harsh on the eyes. The real problem is that the individual LED's (on each bulb) are failing at an alarming rate now. First it was one, then two, and then more and more until the amount of good LED's are not putting out much light. This happened on EACH AND EVERY bulb. My attempt to replace my conventional bulbs with LED's has failed miserably...and very expensively too. Take it from a guy that looks on the bright side all the time, your future will not be bright if you buy these, but your wallet will be much lighter! I sure would like to get my money back if I could.

UPDATE 2/28/2015 - Every single one of these LED bulbs has failed. Almost all LED's on each bulb is dead and those that remain are flickering badly. These bulbs were babied and installed correctly. Either it was a bad batch or bad luck. I hope I can help you avoid bad luck by looking elsewhere for an LED bulb. I am suspect of some of the "positive" reviews and think they might be shills. Buyer beware!

product_title: Smittybilt 98412 XRC Synthetic Rope Winch - 12000 lb. Load Capacity
review_headline: Great bang for the buck and much better than the typical Chinese winches I have seen.
review_body:
Update on 2/8/16: I have used this winch a lot on the back of my tractor to help with large, leaning tree removal while clearing my property for our new home. It has worked in a stellar manner each time used. One of the last times used was to "try" and keep a ~70' tall oak tree with very large limbs located more on one side than any other, from falling onto/being supported by other trees and creating a very dangerous situation. This did not work as I could not get the winch wire rope extension high enough to provide enough leverage on this very large tree, along with not being able to anchor the tractor to a tree in the now open, cleared field.

In the end the tree went in the direction I was trying to keep it from going as the leaning tree pressure on the winch caused the tractor to eventually crush four large, rubber wheel chocks behind the tractor's tires and started dragging the 7500# tractor with its brakes locked as the tree was very slowly falling away from us. The winch operator did not notice the tractor was being dragged over the winch control cable and it was ripped from the winch. The situation then went unrecoverable, quickly. I have no idea how much weight the winch was supporting as it and the tractor were being drug with what was left of the wheel chocks and with brakes engaged, but am sure at some points it was FAR more than the rated 12,000 pounds before the dragging began. I have used smaller chocks on the wheels of my Jeep GC with no chock damage with its 9,000 pound winch at maximum pull.

In the end the synthetic winch rope was embedded on the winch drum between various layers of rope and sections appeared to be melted/fused together somewhat from all of the heat generated in this greatly overloaded condition. However the winch nor the rope failed and are still functional. I need to replace the existing damaged 7/16" synthetic rope with new 1/2" I have waiting and am planning on purchasing an identical Smittybilt winch to replace the 9k unit on my Jeep GC.

Original review: By the time one purchases a less expensive Chinese winch and adds synthetic rope to it, the price is close to this Smittybilt and nowhere near the quality, performance and warranty. I have not used it yet but will update in the future after I have hauled some cut oak trees up a hill with it.

I have just installed this on a portable 2" receiver cradle to use on my tractor's 3PH. The synthetic rope is 7/16" diameter, which is pretty hefty and all of the components and construction seem to be high quality. At today's winch prices, I see no reason to purchase anything less than a 10k# class winch for automotive recovery purposes and a 12k# for just a little bit more money is the way to go as a starting point. I have a 9k winch on my Jeep GC that is ~ 8 years old and feel it is borderline in capacity. I am not an expert, but the general standard is one needs a winch capacity that is 1.0 - 1.5 times the maximum expected rolling weight capacity of the winched vehicle. And the greater the winch capacity the better the performance. I like a minimum of 1.5 times the weight, but all circumstances are different.

Pros:
- Very good quality
- 7/16" synthetic rope. I will not use wire rope for safety and weight reasons. Possible abrasion of the synthetic rope is not an issue for me.
- Waterproof
- Reasonably priced
- Efficient 6.6 HP motor with 193:1 gear ratio for relatively quick recovery speeds
- Excellent limited lifetime mechanical warranty with a 3 year electrical warranty
- Excellent remote control with a magnetic portion to latch onto anything ferrous metal. This will be really handy when using the winch and not having to look for a clean place to lay the remote while using it- just "stick" it on the vehicle.

Cons:
- There are no instructions on how to install the rope, which is no bigdeal for one experienced in doing this, but would be helpful for a newcomer. Search the Internet for instructions if you are new to this sort of thing.
- The hook on the rope is permanently attached and rated at 3.1T. It is a stout looking hook but I would not intentionally purchase a 3.1T hook for a 12k# winch. There is no easy way to remove this hook and replace with a different one. I will use it and see how it goes. The professional looking hook on my other winch's synthetic rope has no rating on it at all. I assume Smittybilt knows what they are doing.
- This is a nit really and not a con, but I was expecting this winch to have a waterproof solenoid box, which it is not. However, the solenoid is an all-in-one unit that is sealed.

product_title: ROLA 59100 Platypus Expandable Roof Top Bag
review_headline: Cannot be beat with this price. Not even close.
review_body:
Havent used this yet but its the perfect size for my Rhino Rack steel wire basket. Enough space on the sides and back for fuel tanks and shovels.

The quality is very good and very durable. It has two great exapansion features:

- The elastic cord on top to make it fit tight around the load.
- Is has a zipper on the side near the bottom that allows you to zip it up to make it compact or un zip to expand it and is the same concept that check-in suitcases/luggage such as Samsonite use.

*** One thing to note. I see a lot of people complaining that their cargo got wet. Coming from a hiking/camping background the first thing I checked is whether the seams (stitching) are seam sealed. They are not.

As anyone who is serious about staying dry while outdoors knows you need to have the seams (stitching) on your waterproof jackets or your tents or anything else that comes in contact with water, sealed with either seam sealing tape (done by the manufacturer) of seam sealing "glue" (can be done by yourself).

You can have a jacket made of 100% water rubber but if the stitching for the zippers, panels and attachment points are not seam sealed it will leak when water ingresses at the stitching points.

Having said all that what I will do and what I recommend is you get some McNett (or other brand) seam seal "glue. Its cheap so get more than you think you will need. This should work:

http://www.amazon.com/Gear-floor-sealant-brush-8-Ounce/dp/B00278BSU4/ref=sr_1_6?ie=UTF8&qid=1409032601&sr=8-6&keywords=seam+sealer

Then plan over the course of a few days to seal the bag. Do one side section at a time and allow to cure or dry before going on to the section. So for example seam seal every stitch and edge near the zippers, panel sections and strap attachment points. You paint it on like glue (rubber cement). Allow it to cure and dry. Then do the same for the bottom.

A tip before you fold it up to prevent the seam sealer from sticking dust the inside with some talcum powder or ever corn starch.

Additionally you can spray water proofing spray on the outside. In fact if you will use this a lot a UV/water proof spray would be a good idea. For example this is what I use on my tents:

http://www.amazon.com/Gear-floor-sealant-brush-8-Ounce/dp/B00278BSU4/ref=sr_1_6?ie=UTF8&qid=1409032601&sr=8-6&keywords=seam+sealer

product_title: ARB Fridge Freezer
review_headline: The king of 12 volt Freezer Fridges.  105 degree outside temps, bouncing around in the back over rough terrain? No Problem!
review_body:
The "Freezer, Fridge" of freezer fridges! I've had this for awhile and just thought this was an expensive, mediocre item that I was almost peeved about because of the price. Well, let me tell you, this sucker is damn good. I just came back from a 6700 mile journey across the states and down to Baja Mexico in 105 degree temperatures, over some of the roughest, rockiest, corrugated roads anyone could ever drive on and this thing performed flawlessly! I'm talking about frozen steaks at the bottom and milk that was still good after 2 weeks in inhumanely hot places. Let's not even talk about this thing not being mounted to anything but bouncing around in the back of my truck in Baja and through the South West with no insulating cover. Talk about cold beers, we're talking about frosty on the outside and almost icy on the inside.

Yeah, this thing works and works well. The thermostat is a little off. I don't know how it is with others but I set mine to 25 degrees to make actually 32 degrees at the bottom of the fridge. I'm sure outside temps affect it also. The neoprene covers for these things are expensive but I've seen someone use that foiled insulation/reflective fabric (or whatever it is) you can get at home depot and sewed a cover for theirs.

I bought mine on Ebay and got into a bidding war but I eventually won it at $550 brand new. After what this fridge freezer has gone through in the last month, I feel even better that I got it for such a low price. But at whatever price you purchase this, you won't be disappointed.

product_title: OTC 6575-1 Hub Grappler Puller
review_headline: Pulls out hub assemblies like a hot knife thru butter!!
review_body:
Being a mechanic, doing hub bearings are a real PITA. Remove this, take that off, put the spindle in the press, get some sockets, line this up, use some washers to get it straight, put a ton of pressure on it, and when the hub finally gives way, everything falls to the floor. Then, you do it again to push it out the rest of the way. Time consuming and frustrating.

With this, I can pull the hub assembly out in about 15 minutes. I use the hub bearing kit from Harbor Freight that I got for $70, and it works great. Total time from removing the tire to putting the tire back on is about 45 minutes. And you don't have to charge the customer for a alignment afterwords.

The only downside to this is that, you get done so fast, the customer wonders why they're paying for 3 hours of labor for 45 minutes of work.

Keep the threads well lubed when using an impact, and it should last for years to come. I use SEA-FOAM DEEP CREEP to keep the heat down and everything well lubricated.

Your going to need a 1" impact socket for the bolt, and a 1-1/4" wrench for the nut. If your in the auto repair business...you NEED THIS TOOL !!

product_title: Monroe 58620 Monroe Load Adjust Shock Absorber
review_headline: Get em if you like to haul stuff in your Dodge minivan
review_body:
We do a fair amount of cargo hauling with our 2000 Dodge Grand Caravan. The old shocks allowed the rear end to drop so much that I could stand on the back bumper and it wouldn't drop anymore. These babies make it so you can hardly tell the difference between loaded and unloaded. I haven't noticed any ride difference between these and the old ones when unloaded as the old shocks worked for bumps. The back end seems to sit a bit higher when unloaded. I docked a star because the rubber boot that keeps the spring from contacting the gas cylinder wasn't pushed all the way on and I didn't notice it before installing so it's hard to fix it now that they're on the car. It would probably be hard to fix it off the car too as the boots are pretty tight.

Installation was easy enough. Take rear tires off and then the two shock bolts and the old ones come off and install is reverse as removal. You do have to adjust the axle height while the car is suspended to get the bolts to line up with the holes in the shocks as the new shocks will not move around for you by hand like springless shocks.

product_title: Muteki SR Series SR48 Open End Lug Nut Set, (Set of 20)
review_headline: Lugs are fine, coating is garbage
review_body:
Let me start by saying that as lug nuts, these work just fine. Clean threads, no issues installing on my WRX. However, the coating is a joke. I had heard that it was thin and prone to chipping or flaking, so I took extra care when installing them on the first wheel. Torque wrench only (no impact) and I made sure to be gentle putting the socket on the nuts and avoid any angular torque on them. Still, I ended up damaging the coating on all 5 nuts.

On the next wheel I slid a few pieces of electrical tape inside the socket to avoid metal to metal contact. It worked well enough, at least for a while. By the last few nuts I was damaging the coating again as the tape had been displaced a bit. So a temporary solution at best.

I know these aren't Rays or Project Kics, but come on, for $50 they should at least last through the first install. I'll be taking my business elsewhere next time I need lugs.

review_body: I have had these on the bike for about a month now and have had no issues. I mounted these bars on my 2013 road glide. I went with the 10" bars so that I wouldn't have to lengthen any wires or cables and I'm not sure my shoulders would take an all day ride with bars even with my shoulders or over them. I ran all of the wires inside the bars which was more of a task than I thought it would be. I have done other bikes but this was the first fly by wire or throttle by wire bike I have done. To have enough room in the bars for all of the wires I had to cut off the plugs on the throttle by wire and the 2 heated grip wires and solder them together, that's not something I wanted to do but I really wanted the wires inside the bars for looks. I also added heated grips at the same time so I wouldn't have to go back in and pull more wires later and I am glad I did all of that at the same time. All in all I am happy with the looks, fit and function of the bars.

product_title: 3M 08898 Multi Purpose Spray Lubricant - 10.5 oz.
review_body:
This is a pretty good lubricant. I used it on a variety of things—including my garage door and opener, door hinges in my house and on my car. It lubricates well and eliminates squeaks. It also cleans the metal of dirt and debris. The spray stays in place well after you apply it. The small extension tube attached makes it easy to pinpoint where you want to spray it.
You need to shake it a lot before you spray it, to blend the ingredients. As with most oil, if you overspray and it drips, wipe it off or clean the area with soap and water immediately, or it could stain. It does have a slight smell, similar to old wax. It is not something you want to get on your clothes or your skin, as the odor remains even after washing with soap.
This spray contains several petroleum products, propane, paraffin and butane—all of which are highly flammable. I do not recommend using it on plastics, because it may damage them. Instead I would use a silicone based product. Over all this 3M spray lubricant works fine for most automotive and household needs, if used properly.

product_title: Roadpro RPSC-784 12-Volt Quick Cup Coffee Maker with 16 oz. Metal Carafe
review_body:
Sheesh! Good idea, good size, makes decent coffee but the Manufacturer/design engineer must have been on drugs or drunk. Bought this for our cuddy cabin 20' boat.

The first and most obvious design flaw is that it cannot sit flat. Ironic that the instructions tell you to make sure it's flat. You cannot see it in the picture but the front half of the bottom is recessed 3/8" from the back half. It will sit flat only with the water reservoir filled. Of course the whole idea of the coffee maker is that it transfers the water from the reservoir to the cup....which will tip it forward during the brewing cycle. You will need 2 of something like these to make sure it stays level: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003P4JS2Y/ref=gno_cart_title_0?ie=UTF8&psc=1&smid=A15OOFJ01NGILN. I'm sure there are much cheaper 3/8" thick stick on rubber feet somewhere but I can't seem to find them...

Secondly, the "15 min brew time" is a lie. It took 22 mins. to brew 16oz of coffee. Drink it right away because it's not all that hot.

Finally, Be aware! The 12v adapter and adapter cord gets quite warm. Once again, bad engineering. Be sure to turn off and unplug when water in reservoir is (almost) gone. It does NOT turn itself off.

It this age, one would think that we can build better stuff than this, instead they keep selling us cheap, dangerous junk from China. I would happily pay twice the price for a GOOD one.

product_title: CURT 13127 Class 3 Trailer Hitch
review_body:
Hitch is well made and nicely painted. It is heavy duty and should work well. The installation went well so read what is written below.

Before you install the hitch, look at the videos on E trailer and youtube, they are very helpful.

I installed this on my Mazda CX-5 and used a combination of all the information gathered and added my own. I did it alone so I had to work smarter!

1. I took the muffler assembly off 2 - 14 MM bolts. I used the cardboard box from the hitch under the muffler and hitch to prevent scratches.
2. Leave the rubber hangers on the vehicle! They are trapped with the hitch installed.
3. I left the wires used to install the bolts on the bolts. I trimed them to 6-8 inches to assist in locating them in the hitch bolt holes.
4. My addition - I used 2 wire ties (zips) 24\\" long to support the hitch while I raised it, aligned and tightened the bolts. Loop the wire ties over the vehicle frame and the very end of the frame. Connect the zip under the very end of the hitch at the corners. It balances the hitch and you can raise the it a few inches at a time. This allows you to work alone with no weight and helps you align the bolts and holes.
5. I also removed the 2 plastic push pins on the bottom of the bumper. This allows you to move the plastic easily to set the hitch behind the bumper.
6. Once the bolts are aligned you can tighten the wire ties completely and secure the hitch to the frame. No holding required!
7. I removed the wires from the bolts and held the bolts in place while I treaded the nuts on a few threads.
8. Tightened the bolts, reinstalled the push pins, reinstalled the muffler and removed the wire ties.
9. I recommend using 1/2\\" drive, 6 point sockets. (14MM and 3/4\\")

Actualy work time was about 1 hour. That was in my driveway, under the Mazda and alone.

Contact me with questions or comments.

review_body:
The intake fits okay on a 2001 Wolfsburg Jetta with a 1.8T engine. Given the low price compared to other competitors, I expected this intake kit to not be perfect. For the price I can live with most of the issues listed below.

2. The breather hose given with the kit is too small to connect to the one in the car so I had to run down to Autozone to get something to connect the hoses.
3.The filter is not of the best quality so I ordered a nice AEM one.
4. Instructions were marginal, they could have been more specific by adding pictures.

Other than those problems, I am happy with the intake overall. It works just fine and is hundreds of dollars cheaper than other intake systems.

product_title: Philips X-Treme Vision Headlight Bulb
review_body:
I bought these for my 2006 Peterbilt 387, and while they do fit, it's hard to determine accurately how much brighter they are. What most people fail to understand about headlight bulbs is that they get dimmer over time, so I'f you're replacing a pair of bulbs you've had in your vehicle for a year or two, even the identical make and model bulbs will be brighter than the ones that have been in use for a long time. Without a light meter and a variety of brand new bulbs to compare, it really is impossible to accurately tell whether one bulb is brighter than another.

I've put about 1,054,000 miles on my truck so far, and I've been through close to a dozen sets of headlight bulbs of varying makes and models, so I have a good point of reference, but I'd be lying if I said I could determine with certainty whether one bulb is better than another. With that being said, I do like these bulbs. The light they produce isn't as white as I'd like, but they do seem to be quite bright and illuminate a very large stretch of the road.

review_headline: I put a dab of WD40 on the O ring and they snapped in fine. Just keep in mind
review_body:
Bought these for OEM replacement for a 2012 Jeep Wrangler. Dealership wanted $36 a bulb for factory halogens. Local auto parts stores were similar in price, so I opted for these babies.

I've heard a lot about these not being identical to the factory PSX24W design, but I will tell you that they are. I did have trouble "snapping them in" because the fitment was snug on the O ring. I put a dab of WD40 on the O ring and they snapped in fine.

Just keep in mind, most bulbs twist in place, these bulbs snap in place.

As far as brightness goes, I have 6000K HID headlights and they are a perfect match of brightness. As far as light output goes, they actually do not provide great driving light. My OEM halogens provided more light on the road. However, I don't rely on my fog lights for driving, so honestly, they're just for looks.

product_title: Unity Automotive 11161 Front Complete Strut Assembly (Left Driver Side)
review_body: My '96 Intrepid with 265K miles had the original struts on it, and one of the upper bearing mounts was getting pretty noisy. I didn't want to spend a lot on a car with so many miles, but had to do something.    Started researching these types of quick struts, and found these Unity to have good backing by the company, along with a lifetime warranty. Sure, they're made in China like 90% of all aftermarket parts are, but figured I'd give these a shot.    The install is straight foreward, nothing any backyard mechanic can't handle. These went right on perfectly. I bought both the left and the right side struts, and didn't have to twist one 180 degrees like I've read about on some others. My biggest problem was removing the sway bar links from the old struts. Had to cut one off and get a new one - no biggie. One of these new struts was missing one of the three nuts that hold it to the top of the inner fender, but the old original nuts were in good shape and actually have more surface area, so I reused them.    I had the front end aligned right away. Driving and handling is noticeably improved, and no more noisy squeaky upper bearings. The only thing I am a little concerned about is when hitting harsh bumps, there is a clunking noise. There was no such noise with the old struts. I've driven over 300 miles with them so far, and it's not getting any worse.  I checked the torque on the main upper shaft nut, and it's tight. So with that, I'm holding back one star. Otherwise I'm very happy. I'll see how they do after a few thousand miles, and give an update.

review_body:
From website
Included are Timken bearings and races along with high quality seals and small parts. Included in this kit are carrier bearings and races, pinion bearings and races, pinion seal, axle seals, complete shim kit, ring gear bolts, pinion nut, crush sleeve , oil baffles and slingers , thread locker, marking compound with brush, and silicone.

Missing silicone, oilbaffles and slingers, thinner shims.

The good.
Comes with pinion shims and both pinion bearings. Comes with 2 new Diff bearings and shims. It comes with both seals however they are the old bare metal style that leak (I bought the new rubber coated style from toyota for $10 and $19).

The bad
Does not come with the 2 needle bearings for the half shafts(axle) that get worn out alot or the passenger side bearing. There are 7 side (differential) shims evenly spaced from 0.105in to 0.129in however the stock shims are about 0.096in (probably 0.095in) and the new bearings are thicker by about 0.008. After installing and tightening I found that I needed smaller shims around 0.080in because the diff bearings are too tight. The kit is also missing new ring gear bolt safety plate(thing that prevents bolts from backing out).

This kit is not worth it. The things I needed the most was the side shims and they are too thick and the needle bearings.

product_title: Dorman 934-601 Drive Shaft Center Support Bearing
review_headline: An affordable and perfect replacement for the high priced OEM bearing.
review_body: This is a typical high-quality Dorman product at the right price, and a perfect replacement for the KIA (OEM) bearing.  Working with the driveshaft on the workbench, a universal two-jaw  puller is required to remove the support bearing u-joint yoke. Removing the yoke retaining nut is quite difficult, as it is "staked" from the factory to keep it tight. I separated the front shaft from the rear shaft at the u-joint and temporarily re-installed the front shaft back into the transmission (in Park) to hold it from rotating. Then I broke the retaining nut loose using a high quality breaker bar and a short piece of pipe. Back on the bench, I replaced the support bearing. A little dressing of the threads with a thread file enabled the retaining nut to be re-installed and re-staked with a punch. A considerable amount of work, but the great price of this support bearing made it worth the effort!

product_title: Dorman 679-005 Turbocharger Up Pipe
review_body:
After researching the more expensive brand of Up-Pipes, I decided to give these a chance since I have had good luck with Dorman Door Lock Actuators. Installation is tough, however if you have researched this upgrade you will already be aware of this fact. I had the luxury of using my hoist which makes the job much easier. Be sure to give yourself plenty of time and have patience. I rate this product at four stars due to the following reasons:

1. No instructions, which I'm sure is due to the fact that if you are doing this job you most likely have an idea of how to complete the install. (Visit the expensive brands website for a great color, downloadable instruction sheet)

2. The factory pipe on the Driver Side is dimpled near where the pipe meets the manifold to provide clearance on the motor. The higher priced pipes also have this dimple, however the Dorman pipes do not. Be sure to match the new pipe with the old one and use a hammer to make the same dimple. I was lucky enough to have gone over the higher priced brands instructions while waiting for my parts to arrive.

Overall I am very satisfied with this product and believe they are well worth the savings over the "other guys" pipes. Also you can read the article in Diesel Power Magazine on their install of up-pipes on a 7.3 (lucky for them they had the transmission out for their install)

product_title: SixSixOne Core Saver Wired White/Black Articulating Armor
review_headline: It held up to intense wear/tear
review_body:
I was pleasantly surprised at how well this vest performed for me. It is well made and very lightweight for it's size. I was initially impressed when I put it on for the first time, but I held my opinions in reserve until I could try it out for myself. First I went 92 miles on my road bike with a 28 pound load on my back- I could hardly feel the weight because of the well designed pads/armor plates which helped distribute the weight evenly over my whole back.
Secondly I noticed how easy movement is for the amount of protection you receive. The spine guard does very slightly restrict side-to-side turning, but it is hardly notcicable and is a very small price to pay.
I also went on a 28 mile bike ride on a mountain trail which put the vest to test I a different way. I didn't have any weight on my back and found that I practically forgot I was even wearing a vest to begin with! It was very light a fairly breathable at that. My back did get pretty hot by the end of the ride, but I would've been shocked if it wasn't somewhat warm after a hard ride.

All in all I am entirely please with my purchase and would recommend this for biking! It suited all my needs and expectations for both road and mountain biking. I hope I works as well for anybody else who gets it.

This cook set is light and very packable. I store my Trangia alcohol stove, fire starter and dish towel in the pot while hiking. This makes for one very packable kitchen.

I get to watch other hikers cook every night using all sorts of cooking gear. I have not seen anything else that I would even remotely want over the GSI Soloist other than the GSI Dualist if you are cooking for two.

You cannot go wrong with this cook set. Just buy it.

Never again. Ok, it's a Summer and a few months down the line, and I'm modifying this review. I had stated that the end result was good, but time has shown this stuff sucks. I've got rust forming under the creeme and crumbs from the whole mess has been plugging my filter. Going to have to redo this tank, and on further investigation, there are several better choices on the market, one epoxy that works whether you've got rust in there or not, and another that has high ratings, I've found. I doubt Amazon would appreciate me just naming them, but search and ye shall find. It's worth the effort compared to this crap, in my opinion.

product_title: Vision X Lighting HIL-STW Superwhite LED Strobe and Rock Light Kit
review_headline: Work great for rock lights, multi-strobe feature is gimmicky
review_body:
The Good: Easy to install. Light output (work well for rock lights). Pods are small enough to fit virtually anywhere. Wireless remote control. LEDs (will not drain battery)

The Bad: LED pods aren't waterproof. 8 pods = 8 cables. Multi-function strobe feature is gimmicky.

The Lowdown: Out of all the big name rock light kits out there, the Tantrums are the cheapest I've seen and a great deal for what you get.

Although quite time consuming, the system is easy to install. Pods are small enough to place anywhere, just make sure to seal them up beforehand to make them waterproof (I used clear silicone).

As a result of 8 LEDs, all those cables can be a hassle and a wiring mess. They all connect to the Hub (black box shown in photo), so you'll need a safe spot for it, along with all those cables.

Pods are only 1W each, but the superwhite LEDs are just bright enough for your spotter to see, without being too bright to affect night vision. Since they're LEDs, they won't drain your battery either.

Control Unit is easy to use, each button is labeled with its function.

I totally dig the wireless remote control, but it's confusing to use. Buttons aren't labeled (only lettered). With all the different options, it's difficult to remember which one is which. I just want one button - the on/off button!

Some may like the different strobe options, but I find them unnecessary and just adds to the complexity of the system. Too gimmicky.

I've read other reviews of burnt out LEDs and other issues, but so far so good. Vision X does sell individual pods ($20 each) that can be used as replacements.

Overall, a good value for the money. Would've been perfect without the multi-strobe feature, though.

product_title: Valterra RV Hydroflush
review_headline: The Quicki Flush may be a better way to get the tank clean
review_body: I just finished trying this for the 1st time.  The instructions that came on the label stated \\"It's most effective when tank is directly in line with valve cap opening\\".  My black tank has a 90 deg bend immediately outside the opening.  Also the drain pipe is approximately 4' from tank to drain opening where the hydroflush attaches.  I was skeptical that it would work.  It took approx. 45-60 mins. to get clear water draining from the tank.  I experimented with 20-40 seconds each time running water into black tank then shutting off the water and letting it drain, then repeated till water ran clear.  The campground we are at has very high water pressure and I believe this helped.  Not sure how this will work at campgrounds with lower water pressure.  It worked and I will now see if it helps the smell we've been getting from the black tank.  The Quicki Flush may be a better way to get the tank clean.  This will be my next purchase if this doesn't work in the future.

product_title: Dorman 902-001 Engine Water Pump
review_body:
I purchased this product to replace the failing MECS pump in my 2007 Mercury Mariner Hybrid. I should have known that the price tag was too good to be true (an OEM replacement pump was $400 more). The manufacturer and Amazon claim that this pump is a replacement for the pump in my vehicle as well as in other model years of the Mercury Mariner/Ford Escape hybrids. I don't know about the other model years, but the mounting bracket on this replacement pump didn't even come close to mounting in my vehicle - it was the wrong orientation and wrong hole pattern. I discovered this late on a Friday evening and couldn't wait out the weekend to get one that actually fit, so I had to make a different mounting bracket. Once installed, the pump worked great and solved my overheating problem. In fact, if it had mounted up like it was supposed to, I would have given this 5 stars, but having to make a custom bracket when it was supposed to be a drop-in replacement only gets it 3.

All in all, it's a good pump and a much better price than an OEM replacment. If you can confirm the included bracket fits your vehicle or don't mind manufacturing your own, I'd recommend this pump as a great way to save $400.

product_title: K&N PS-7002 Pro Series Oil Filter
review_body: Excellent oil filter.  I am very, very picky about what I use in my car.  I have a 2009 Volvo S60 2.5T that I love and want to keep and pass along to my oldest daughter as her first car.  To do that I need to make sure I take care of it and use quality parts.  Prior to trying the K&N filter, the only filter I would use is the Mann filters that are European made for these cars.  The quality and fit of those filters is excellent.  I decided to give the K&N filters a try, especially since I use them on my motorcycle and really like them, AND the K&N filter comes with the rubber seal to replace the one on the filter canister.  In the Volvo's, you remove the canister and just replace the paper filter element inside, not the whole filter like many others.  The filter material on the K&N filter was really nice.  LOTS of pleats and the paper felt very high quality.  More pleats means more surface area, which means better filtering and easier time for the oil to flow thru the filter.  The price on Amazon was very close to being the same, maybe even a bit better than the Mann filters.  Both are excellent choices.  After comparing the K&N against the high quality Mann filters, I would highly recommend the K&N filters.  They also have the advantage of being the only one of the 2 brands you can generally get locally.  I really can't recommend any of the many other brands out there.  I've tried them and most look and feel very cheap and very flimsy.  I want my daughter to have this car for a good, long time so I'll take the extra step and spend the extra dollar to get the best.
