product_title: Kensun HID Xenon Conversion Kit "All Bulb Sizes and Colors" with "Slim" Digital Ballasts
review_headline: Xenon is the better choice for headlights
review_body:
Looking to upgrade your headlights? Here's the deal: I replaced all the lights in my car with LEDs. I really enjoy the 6000k white LED look. When it came to the headlights, not wanting to deal with ballasts, I wasted money on some expensive \\"White\\" halogen lights. Bad choice, no such thing as \\"White halogen\\" headlights. Compared to the other LEDs on my car, yellow(ish) halogen headlights looked terrible. So, I then got some white LED headlights. Again, bad choice, bad light disbursement. LED headlights are not advanced enough in technology to provide high brightness output without using mechanical \\"mini-fans\\" to keep them cool. I found that these fans could be heard buzzing with my windows up and the engine running. What good are LED headlights that last longer than my car, if they depend on noisy fan motors that will eventually fail? Anyway, each of the LED headlights I had were comprised of several small led modules. These modules are mostly mounted on the sides of the bulb. My car has projector lenses. The light disbursement, from these bulbs, through the projector lens was not uniform.

I finally tried the only other option left (should have done this in the first place) and installed these Xenon lights. review_headline: THIS STATOR AND SELLER ARE COMPLETE GARBAGE!!!!!!
review_body:
I will never buy one of these inferior knock-offs again. I've learned my lesson. To the point! I needed a new stator cover for my '02 ZX12R and decided the $196 was not a wise use of my money for a stator cover from the factory. I went to Amazon. I found the part for just North of $40 and decided I would risk it. My gut told me one thing, I did another.

When the stator cover arrived, it seemed to be comparable to the piece I was taking off. So, I went to work. The first problem was mounting holes for the stator were not tapped deep enough. Still thinking I had a value, I tapped the holes the rest of the way so they would receive the factory bolts. Done. BTW, I informed the seller and all they wanted was a photo of the problem. I told them a photo would not show a shallow tapped mounting hole. They insisted on a photo a second time. I declined. At this point, they had no interest in solving my problem.

Back to the cover. After installing the cover and filling the crankcase with 3 quarts of Mobil 1 synthetic oil at a cost of 10.00 a quart, I started the engine. No leaks around the cover! But wait, is that a crack right in the middle of the cover that is leaking oil???? Yes. There was a stress fracture near the top that was leaking my $30 oil.

I warn you. Don't do business with these people and don't buy these inferior products. I am out the cost of my oil, my gasket and the rotor. This is garbage! Pure cheaply made garbage from unscrupulous people.

review_headline: Finally - an RV Sewer Hose Support that works well
review_body:
I've used just about every style sewer hose support, and this is the first that I liked. Actually, it is the first that seems to have been designed by someone who actually spends time RVing. It is extremely easy to use and also easy to set up. It took me a little getting used to the first time, but now that I've figured out that you want to get the support positioned and then raise it up to get the slope right, it is super easy! It helps you maintain a constant slope from the RV to sewer connection and can be customized to fit just about any situation. It seems to be well made and I expect it will last longer than the cheep junk I have had in the past.

Unlike the accordion style sewer hose supports, this can be adjusted to accommodate uneven ground between your RV and the sewer connection (not that the ground is ever uneven in a campground - ha ha!).

Unlike the expandable gutter style sewer hose supports that collapse under the weight of the hose when fully extended, this is supported every 30" and will not collapse. The length of this can also be shortened to just 30" which is handy if you are close to the sewer connection.

product_title: Air Lift 25870 WirelessONE Compressor System
review_body:
Love the ease of changing the pressure in my air bag system while driving or while loading the truck/ trailer. It has 2 program settings so i set one for my boat and 1 for my car hauler. If I need to adjust the ride while driving, press the arrow buttons and it takes care of everything. If I am loading a different vehicle on my car hauler or towing someone elses boat, I just take the remote with me, load the truck and use the arrows to adjust pressure until I like the level.

install is easy and straight forward. Install time was about 1 hour for my 2012 toyota tundra Crew max due to taking all the interior panels off so i could run wiring behing everything and finding a body penetration that i could use to run the air lines back to the air bags at my rear axle. I also added a quick disconnect so i can plug in my air hose and fill my tires if needed. The pump is not made to be in the elements so that is why I mounted the compressor inside the cab of my truck. 3 things i will note about an interior install. DO NOT mount compressor where it touchs the truck body or plastic molding inside the vehicle. It will be VERY noisy if you do. Second, this is a compressor so it makes NOISE. granted it takes about 7 seconds to get to 25 pounds and 20 seconds to be at 75 pounds so it isnt a big deal regarding duration. finally, since it has a regulator on it and is fully automatic, weight changes and temperature changes will make it add air or remove air as needed. For instance, it was 80 degrees yesterday when i parked. This morning it was 50. As soon as i started the truck, the compressor kicked on for about 1 second to make up the difference. That is long enough to startle you if you are not used to it.

product_title: Genuine Chrysler (5083138AA) Transfer Case Switch
review_body:
Fitted to my 2003 Rubicon Tcase 241OR RockTrack. You need a 1 1/2" socket on a 3/4" ratchet to get the old one out and the new one in after disconnecting the harness plug on top of the switch sensor. Trickier without body lift (I have one). This happened after I did a clutch install, so I thought that the harness wires were pinched, checked them all , and came to conclusion that the switch bit the dust somehow during the removal and reinstall.

My symptoms were that the 4WD light didn't come on and therefore the lockers didn't engage in LOW range. After installing the new switch, I still didn't get the 4WD light to operate, I did a battery disconnect, no luck, then tried this, quoted from another website :-

1. Disconnect the POSITIVE battery Terminal and touch it to ground for 30 seconds. (This is to discharge the PCM capacitors, which maintain the Adaptive Memory.
2. Reconnect the Battery Cable
3. Turn Ignition Switch to the "ON" position but DO NOT start the engine
4. Turn Headlight "ON"
5. Turn Headlights "OFF"
6. Turn Ignition Key "OFF"
The PCM Adaptive memory has now been flashed, or erased from the PCM.

Still no 4WD light. Soooo.....

I did the dash light test routine (google it, if I remember it's hold the ODO switch and key-on the ignition switch) and then the light came back on after keying off and back on. YMMV.

product_title: Hawk Performance HB312Y.591 LTS Brake Pad
review_body: I installed these pads on a 1996 Toyota Land Cruiser, along with matching rear pads. The same time the pads were installed, new calipers x4, rotors x4, soft lines, LSPV, and a master cylinder were replaced. I also flushed the brake lines to get rid of the old fluid. During the break-in cycles, I was not surprised to experience excessive pedal travel and fade. However, even after the break-in period, these pads still don't "bite' until they are hot. Once hot, they will out perform most other brake pads that I've tried, but until they get hot enough, they don't provide much confidence. I will probably go back to using OEM pads. I may also consider using the Adaptive One pads from NAPA. I frequently install the NAPA pads at my shop as an upgrade to OEM, and my customers can usually notice the difference.

product_title: GMax GM54S Modular Helmet 2XL Flat Black
review_body: This isn't as great as I was led to believe. I got the 2XL and it still a very snug fit. Especially around the jaw. I do like the sun visor that comes down. Everyone that comments about the little vents all over allowing cool air to rush in is something I have 't personally experienced. In fact I hear the wind, but its not cool air. It just creates a lot of wind noise.    I am sure it is a safe helmet but I don't think it is as comfortable as a helmet can be.    Update.....9.30.2014    After owning this helmet for a while, I have to say my opinion of it has changed drastically. I love it. I am not so sure I get the same air flow that some other people have been raving about, but I think that might be because the helmet is a little snug on my head and no room to spare for air flow.     But as for safety and feeling safe wearing this helmet, I love it. I used to wear my half shell when I was riding on short rides and now I almost always wear this one. The ability to have a double shield provides you with so much protection and for people with contacts, you need it to block out the wind and protect your eyes from drying out.     If something happened to this I would buy another one in a heartbeat!

product_title: Infiniti Professional Grade Touch Up Clear Coat! Best on the Market!
review_headline: Good quality clear coat for your Infiniti
review_body:
Is this clear coat sold for Infiniti any different than this seller sells for other cars? I don't know. Overall, a good product. I am pretty detailed in fixing paint chips and will generally put three coats of touch-up paint followed by 2-3 coats of clear coat. In order to get a nice smooth finish, you need to sand between coats with 300+ grit wet sand paper followed up by a polish to remove all scratches and then wiping the spot with isopropol alcohol to remove any polish residue before proceeding to the next coat. The clear coat is "clear" and does seem to match the car. There is enough clear coat to perform hundreds and hundreds of touch ups.

They lose one star the the triple O (000) brush that is included. Pretty lousy brush. I have good quality 000 brushes that have a much finer tip that what is included. You will not be able to do any fine touch-ups using the included brush as it is just too fat.

Kit comes with the bottle of clear coat, the 000 brush, a plastic glove and instructions. You don't really need the glove. Be sure to pick up some lacquer thinner to clean your brush afterwards. Just pick up the Testors brand from anywhere that sells hobby paint.

product_title: RoofBag Explorer Waterproof Soft Car Top Carrier for Any Car Van or SUV - Made in the USA | 1-Year Warranty | Ships Today
review_headline: I wish I had bought it sooner.
review_body:
It's great! I was preparing for my third multi-state move (in under two years!) and this was perfect to strap on the top of my Ford Focus, especially since it was just me and I wasn't using a moving truck. It really has a lot of space and was easy enough to load. It was a bit challenging at first since I had never done it before and wasn't sure how everything would fit in. Since it is soft the top was a bit annoying while loading. I have an antennae on the top of my car that goes back at about a 45* angle so I couldn't just flip the top of the bag over onto my windshield. (I didn't even think about the antennae until after I bought it and thankfully it fits perfectly under it and does not ruin the reception.)

I will use this again and again, I'm sure. I am happy it folds down to such a small size for storage. Being a soft bag and attached with straps, it does worry me that people would mess with it if you leave it on your car overnight, so if you plan on getting a rooftop carrier that you'll use on road trips I wouldn't suggest this one unless you want to unpack everything and take it off your car each night.

It's a great value. I think it was cheaper on the actual site than on amazon. I love that it's made in America and that I didn't need a rack on my car in order to use it. Now if only the bugs wouldn't smash into it while driving...

product_title: Spyder Auto Jeep Grand Cherokee Black Halogen LED Projector Headlight - Pair
review_body:
These lights are pretty fantastic. I had originally purchased HIDs for the stock assemblies, but didn't like the pattern so I decided to go for these housings. I like the pattern of projectors MUCH more because it is very precise and even. I was able to make the stock bulbs fit with a small amount of modification to the bulbs themselves, and I was therefore able to avoid also buying a second set of HIDs.
Note: These housings come with halogen H1 bulbs and will not fit 9006 bulbs unmodified.

The halos could be brighter and could look nicer, but if it's a deal-breaker spend the extra cash on CCFL housings. The real savior for me with these were the LEDs. They give the Grand a nice, clean look day or night. Super white, not blue, bright, and easy to splice into a power source. All in all, this was a great purchase. I love Spyder products!

Just make sure you clean the metal with warm soapy water (I used dish-washing liquid) to remove any oil that might be on the metal from your hands and/or someone else's handling the metal. This will ensure that the primer adheres to the surface of the metal well.

product_title: 1 Oz Welder Professional Adhesive 730657
review_headline: the BEST all purpose glue - now only online?!
review_body:
I discovered this glue a few years back and now swear by it and recommend it whenever possible. I used to be able to find it at Lowe's and Home Depot but both have stopped carrying it. The only other place i have heard that may carry it is Wal-Mart, but who wants to go there? ;)

Let me list the greatness of this glue:

-Dries quickly, which is important no matter what the project. Objects can still be shifted for a time, but the glue holds weight great early on. Clamp it or let gravity hold it in place, work on the next part, in a few minutes your weld is gelled and solid.

-LOW ODOR -no model glue smell. Still use ventilation and common sense, but it practically has no smell.

-Cleans up easily: any glue dried (or wet) onto your fingers can be rolled or peeled off most of the time. If glue gets on the wrong part (as long as it is not fabric or carpet) you can wipe and knead it off while it is damp with no problem.

- In my experience, bonds anything to anything! -- I do mixed media sculpture work which often includes glass, metal, wood and plastic. This glue does it ALL. Few glues work well with glass, this glue will bond glass of decent weight to metal within minutes, and be fully cured by the end of the day or less.

- The foggy glue dries crystal clear- it even smooths out and contracts a little (unlike gorilla glue!) making even a copious gluing job tidy itself up as it dries. Placed properly and sparingly, you might not even see it when dried.

-If you change your mind about a weld, most times you can pull or pry them apart carefully months after they are dried, peel off the glue, and use them again. Gravity or impact alone will not break the weld, but often you can with strength and the knowledge of where you made the bond. This is convenient for crafters and sculptors who change their mind about placement, or want to use an object another way later. - this method does not work for WOOD or porous surfaces like cloth- only smooth metal, glass, hard thick plastic and ceramics.

-Perfect amount of flow: not runny or wet. best comparison is like a silicon caulk. Requires pressure to come out of the tube but applies very easily, despite looking 'rubbery'

I can't rave enough about it, and I use it for every project. When I saw the chain stores had stopped carrying it, I had to grab the 6 pack of two (12 tubes!) stuck to stock up for emergencies.

seriously, anything else you buy is going to be a waste of money. product_title: Dorman 973-416 Blower Motor Resistor Kit
review_headline: Great replacement part for likely less than half of what it would have been at my local parts store
review_body:
This worked very well to repair the vent fan for my wife's 2001 Jeep Wrangler. The vent fan was not working at all

I replaced the fan speed selector switch with the OEM Mopar part, and then the fan worked, but only at full speed. Apparently, this part was vital as well. When I took the glove box apart, and removed the kickplate beneath it, I saw that the resistor pack was charred and burnt. One of the wires had burnt itself completely free of the harness. The wiring harness was melted.

The gauge of wire on this replacement part was about #10 whereas the original was about #12. The thicker wire of this replacement part makes me think this replacement part may be better than OEM. All of the fan speed settings worked after replacing this part.

A couple of things to watch for, however:
1) the wiring harness doesn't clip into the resistor pack as tightly as the OEM, pulling on the wires can make the harness come unplugged. This isn't a big worry once all of the wiring is done and everything is put back together, but it is noticeable while doing the wiring.
2) the wires look exactly like they do in the picture--they are not color coded like the originals, so just keep the old harness or use some other method as a way to keep track.

Great replacement part for likely less than half of what it would have been at my local parts store.

review_headline: Fitting the Pace Setter Header on a B2200
review_body:
I recently installed this header on my 1989 B2200. It fit very nice and close to the engine. I had the header nickel plated locally, so I had to use a tail pipe expander tool to get the slip fit extension to fit, due to the extra thickness of the plating. I didn't bother using the clamp to join the two, since it's a pretty snug fit.
The extender has an integral threaded boss in which the original oxygen sensor can be fitted, or it can be plugged with an 18mm spark plug (old Ford type).
My existing front exhaust pipe had been bodged when the secondary catalytic convertor had been removed years ago, so I knew I would have to do a bit of custom exhaust work to assemble the exhaust.
I replaced the stock, failing carburetor with a Weber DGEV unit at the same time.
After a few days driving the truck and adjusting the carburetor, the truck is running very well now. I am very pleased with the combination. It seems to have a little more power, it is not annoyingly loud and it appears my mileage has increased, although that's probably mostly due to the carb swap.

I ordered this system to paint a car for a friend as a favor. I usually use a BASF LIMCO base-clear system but wanted to give this system a shot as it was ¼ the price. Like I said it isn’t lacquer it’s some type of vinyl paint in lacquer thinner. It sprays like crap if it’s too hot or humid. The paint does not sand well either well wet sanding with 800-1000-1200 progressively the paint kept rolling into hard balls causing scratching. It does not cover well to get it to blend you need to reduce it farther and still it looks like terrible. If you are in the south this will bleach within 2 years it will not stand up to the elements. Do yourself a favor spend a few extra dollars and purchase a descent base-clear or enamel system

review_body:

Some install load resistors inline to simulate the resistance of an incandescent bulb but this produces heat which is uncool (literally) wherever it is installed. The optimum way seems to be to replace the stock flasher module. For my truck, an '03 Yukon XL the following is the replacement part:

Tridon LM487 Flasher (approx. $33)

We'll see if I live with the hyper-flashing or replace the flasher module.

product_title: Red Line 60103 SI-1 Fuel System Cleaner
review_headline: To each his own.  Works well for my cars.
review_body: I've never been a fan of those "additives" but everyone's results will vary.  I have put this into the three cars that I own (2006 Dodge Charger 3.5l,  2003 Chevy Suburban 5.3l and 2007 Nissan Versa 1.8l).  The only car I have noticed a real difference in acceleration and fuel economy is the 2007 Nissan Versa.  As some who own these cars, they come under powered from factory, but this product seemed to have helped in aspects of fuel economy and acceleration.  I have always noted fuel mileage and after the initial treatment-say 1 tank after, I have gone from 27mpg to 28.5mpg.  It's not much but for what it's worth, I feel it did help a little and I have a lead foot.  I treat my cars at least 500 miles before my next oil change as you will notice the engine oil will get darker when you treat it.  I'm guessing the oil gets darker from all of the junk it's cleaning out from the cylinders amd washing down into the oil.  As far as my other vehicles, I don't notice much as I don't really drive them on a daily basis as I do with the Nissan Versa.

product_title: TouchUpDirect Toyota Prius Exact-Match Automotive Touch-Up Paint - 0.5 oz. Pen
review_headline: Great for small chips, useless for deep scratches.
review_body:
If you've got small chips on the edges of your door, this is the product for you! It would also be good if you don't care what your nick & scratch repair looks like; you know, if you were driving a 1972 Maverick or something.
I bought this to touch up a few small spots on a 2010 Highlander and one long (12''), perfectly straight scratch from a nail on a fence post, 3'' of which went down to the bare metal. Unless the area you are trying to fix is wide, this system simply will not suffice if you care how your care looks.
I have a tri-color finish on my car; blizzard pearl white. I'm also an artist, so I'm well-versed when it comes to painting fine lines with various sized brushes and tips. The tips on these pens are too thick for a fine scratch. I tried every trick I knew to regulate the amount of paint coming from the tip but it's all or nothing-- and all is way too much. I even taped the scratch on both sides until there was no more than a 1/32'' space; still, the paint piled up. I worked it 2'' at a time. I try free-handing. After a dozen attempts, I gave up.
This 'system' comes in three parts: the base color, the pearl topping and the clearcoat. I never made it to the cleacoat, but I did try to use the pearl topping by itself. It has the consistency of milk and was a total disaster.
The ad states: ''super accurate line-drawing capability''. It just not true. It's not super and it's not accurate. I'm sure it can draw lines because I drew several-- big, gloppy lines of inconsistent paint width and depth.
I'm giving it one star because the colors are very accurate and another star because it works well on very small chips.
However, if you think this product will be the touch-up panacea you're looking for, you will be sadly disappointed. A magic marker would most likely work just as well.

review_body: I have bought these before in the past from other venders and I usally buy a 50 to 100 foot roll. Any how I bought two boxes of these pre cut and the boxes were intact but looked very old and have been opened and closed alot. Any how the reason for the 1 star is do to that these parts are defective but I already trashed the boxes so I am just stuck with them. The reason I say they are defective is that when they were made one side the outside is longer then the inside when they made these. What I mean is that lets say u lay them flat on the ground well when u do it looks like a smile or rainbow curve. Now dont get me wrong as these do have a slight curve to them for the wheel well arch but that arch is if u are holding it up in the middle it should arch to help fit the wheel well area. Well this does that but let say u have a nice arch while holding the part and then u walk up to a flat surface then u can see that there is also a arch away from ur flat surface. So any how here at the shop we have ran into this issue before but a few years back with this same product. What my body guy did was cut v notches out of the back side were it mounts to the under side fender lip which took alot of time and messing with the part to look right on the vehicle and also u have to put a screw with washer on every single none cut v part. So it will look like this on the mounting side of the flare VVVVVVV. The reason for it is to bring it back straight as the outer flare part is longer than the inside flat part. Any how we have ran into these same defect fender flare parts before and last time we were in a rush to finish the vehicle but this time I had the time so I just ordered a 100 foot roll and my guys had each fender done in about 15 to 20 min. We also have learned when installing these as we have done alot of them and they look and work great to take the screw they send u and keep them for some thing else as we now use self tapping torques deck screws with the big flat heads built into them. They dont rust hold the flares on real good and tight and u can get all kinds of colors so they dont stick out and really look factory. Also the metal wire that comes with these will rust if u dont use a sealer on each end as we use windshiled sealer black 3m product and it just take a little bit and will nnever come out. We use on some alium wire or stainless steel wire or the wire they send us depending on what vehicle its going on. I would send these back but dont have the boxes so thats my fault.

product_title: Four Seasons 78599 New AC Compressor
review_headline: Good product, good price, beats buying locally everytime
review_body:
Installed on a 2001 Civic. Four Seasons is considered one of the biggest in aftermarket auto A/C products. The price from Amazon is extremely good and so far I've had good luck with this unit.

Installation was straight forward. Unit has OEM connector. This unit is of good quality. Judging by a slightly looser fit on the bolts, rougher casting finish, and lighter clutch components, this unit is not quite that of the OEM Denso (although the Denso failed at 128k miles so I can't say great things). These differences are pretty inconsequential. At the time, the Denso was about 25 dollars more from Amazon.

Another reviewer says the unit comes with an oil charge. My unit warned that it had "shipping oil" inside, and to drain it and fill to your specifications. Upon draining the oil, I found it had 50ml of green oil (w/leak detector) of unknown weight. If you are doing a flush (which you should, see below!), this is probably too little oil required for your system.

The results are good. Compressor seems to run smoothly and clutch engagement is smooth. Pressures and temperatures are right where they should be.

If you need to replace a failed compressor, seek help from a pro. If not, at least seek help from someone who knows how to flush an A/C system, or you'll be doing the job again sooner than you want. Consider replacing the condenser too. A new drier is mandatory.

product_title: Denso 6732302 Ignition Coil
review_headline: You might like to purchase this OEM part when you can find non-OEM parts at half the price.
review_body: I am replacing all 4 coils of my Honda 2002 GX NGV (30520PVJA01) OEM Part Number 09G16J PVJ DENSO 099700-114. I have in the past purchased non-OEM parts for this automobile and I would like to share what I have learned. The OEM part will not have the same life in the natural gas engine as you get in a gasoline fueled engine for the following reasons explained by a shop manager of a place that works on the Honda GX. The natural gas engine head runs hot and this heat causes the coil to break down. The plastic on the coil will oxidize and turn dull over time in relationship to the breakdown of the plastic as an insulator. At some point cracks will develop in the insulator and then the coil will spark to the wall and begin to misfire randomly.  The coil that is old and breaking down begins to change resistance and break down when it is hot.  So an oxidized coil without cracks can fail under load as without a visible indicator like cracks. You can’t easily check the resistance of the hot coil only the removed coil. This resistance and failure will often not be apparent when it is cold.  I have known that the coil was a week part of the Honda, and decided tor the last 40,000 that the non-OEM part at half the price could not be worse than the OEM part. This has proven to be untrue. The non-OEM parts probably use a poorer plastic and less quality control of the winding. As bad as the OEM part is they are better than the non-OEM in the GX and NGV. I am confused why the model number for this part is 099700-114 and I get Part Number 673-2302. This part goes in many Honda 1.7 liter engines. Delivery was quick and good. The part is very clearly marked DENSO on the top of the Coil. The last OEM part I had was stamped only on the bottom and it was not obvious that it was the correct manufacturer.  Some internet sellers claim to be OEM but they do not state the manufacturer.  This is a part that costs about twice what the non-OEM part costs. I’m expecting value from it, like two to three times the life of the non-OEM part. Make sure that you verify the year, engine size, make, and model in ordering a coil. It is easy to get an incorrect size on the initial search. The Amazon part is about one half of the cost at the local Honda dealer. It is an easy job for the novice mechanic; you don’t want to pay the retail price and labor for this repair. You need to be able to inspect your part for cracks and oxidation. You can afford to buy a code reader machine to read and clear the engine codes. It will pay for itself on the first coil replacement. It is hard to keep the engine coolant level properly level in the NGV. Even though the car temperature light is not unusual, you may still be running higher than normal temperatures at the head and reducing the life of your coils. There is a relationship between bad radiator maintenance and coil failure.

product_title: ACDelco 15-73596 GM Original Equipment Heating and Air Conditioning Panel Mode Door Actuator
review_headline: Great part. About an hour to replace if you figure out how to do it right.
review_body: Repair posts online are all over the place with how to replace. Mine was for a 2007 Trailblazer. Not too difficult to do but you have to be patient. Online posts everywhere were not detailed enough. Remove lower dash panels. (I also disconnected wire harnesses from one panel to make it easier to work-obd harness had 2 screws other 2 harnesses popped right out.) My trailblazer had adjustable pedals-I removed my gas pedal for easier access. Gas pedal just had 3 bolts (10mm), I didnt disconnect the wire to it that controlled the adjuster but did disconnect the other harness-Just moved it out of the way. now you can remove air ducts. Remember to pop out air temp sensor on it. Once removed the actuator is right there. Its the one closer to driver seat. Just compare part numbers visible on side. 2 screws (5.5 mm) to remove it and it comes right out. There is a notch on the white portion of the new actuator that you just line up on the other receiving end. You may need a mirror to get a good look but it basically lines right up with the mount holes. Remember to plug wire harness back in to new actuator. I plugged wire harness back into gas pedal and tested before re mounting it just in case. Don't start ac at first. Let vehicle run for about 4 minutes and shut off. Restart and turn ac on to check if working. This allows system to recalibrate. If it works like it did for me now just put air ducts back in place,  remount pedal and re install lower dash panels. Access is the main issue with installing this part. This way work great for me. Had to review the how to because I searched forever online and few posts I found were either inaccurate or didnt explain it well at all. Again Great Part, Fixed my problem. Local auto part stores wanted $60, I got it here for $30. Hour of work and prob saved alot $.

product_title: Meguiar's Hot Shine High Gloss Tire Spray and Microfiber Cloths Bundle
review_body:
I'm generally a big fan of the Meguiar's products, and use them for washing, drying, waxing, etc. Got this thinking it would be a good addition to the lineup. However, not only does it not really add much to the overall look, but the application method is all wrong.

This product comes as a spray, and is designed, as per the instructions, to spray right onto the tires. After doing so, it does make the areas where applied shiny, but the application is uneven, and even then, because it's a mist, it goes everywhere (onto the paint, the wheels, etc), which is bad. So you end up having to use something like a paper towel or a cloth to spread the product evenly, which ends up removing most of the product (and making a mess overall). Then the shine is gone.

This product would be better made as a bottle that is made to apply to a pad or some other applying tool, as the spray is too difficult to control to get it only on the tires.

Since evening it out also means removing most of the shine, whatever soaks in leaves a dull but darker look. So, in the end, the best it was able to do was darken the tires slightly. The product briefly mentions protective qualities, so a star for that, but it seems like an afterthought in the advertising materials, so I'm somewhat doubtful about that. So overall, this product doesn't seem worthwhile; it's more trouble than it's worth. It basically made a mess, made the tires darker, but duller looking, and made the logos/letters/numbers on the tires less visible, which in the end made it look less cool than before. So, I won't be using this particular product again.

Other Meguiar's products are great; but this one is not an essential. It seems like a very niche product that one would only need for special photo shoots, etc, in a controlled environment, but not as an everyday car polishing tool.

product_title: INNOVA 3612 Compression Tester - 4 Piece Kit
review_headline: Already paid for itself after a single use!
review_body:
We have an old Volvo that recently developed a misfire on cylinders 2 and 3. In fact, the cylinders were not firing at all. Given that the two cylinders are right next to each other (and the other cylinders were firing fine) I strongly suspected a failed head gasket was the cause. I didn't want to pay to have the car towed to the shop and then checked out to confirm my diagnosis, however. The tow bill and the checkout fee would have been in the hundreds of dollars and that still wouldn't have covered towing the car back home again if I didn't pay the $800+ to get it fixed.

Anyway, I have wanted one of these for a while and the need finally arose so I took a chance. In 15 minutes this device confirmed what I suspected. We found strong compression on cylinders 1 and 4 and virtually no compression on cylinders 2 and 3. So, it sure looks like a blown head gasket. At a minimum the head needs to come off and be checked with a straight-edge to make sure it isn't warped. There is always the outside chance of failed piston rings but that is a very rare occurrence on modern cars.

So, bottom line, for around $30 we now have an excellent idea of what is wrong with the car. We know it is a compression issue and not one to do with ignition or fuel delivery. Even if this gauge breaks the next time I go to use it it has already paid for itself. Very happy customer!

EDIT: pulled the head and sure enough the head gasket was gone between cylinders 2 and 3. That being said, at least 2 people have left informative comments below which should be read and considered.

product_title: 3M 39008 Headlight Lens Restoration System
review_headline: Works great! Here's a tip to save your paint.
review_body:
I love this kit, and I've used it on 3 cars so far (1 kit works well for 2 headlights, but I always end up using all of the pads - so if you want to do tail lights too I'd recommend 2 kits). If you follow the instructions and wipe away excess dust frequently, you'll get a nice smooth finish that is crystal clear after you get through all 4 stages. It takes some patience, and it normally takes me about an hour per headlight.

Here's a tip for saving your paint: take the entire headlight enclosure out of the car instead of leaving it mounted and taping around it. I don't care how much tape you use, if that drill spins you out of control a bit you're going to burn right through the tape down to the paint. It happened in a few tiny spots the first two times I used the kit. Some headlights are difficult to do when mounted since they are very short top to bottom (like my 2008 Honda Civic). The sanding pad can barely fit between the bumper and fender. It took a little extra time, but I removed the headlights first this time, and it actually helps in several ways. I can get different light angles to look at scratch detail by moving the light around instead of having it fixed in the car. I can also get a better sanding angle (vertical instead of horizontal).

Overall, this kit is fantastic for the price. I'll continue to buy/use them as needed. All 3 times I've used it, my lenses look brand new when I'm done!

review_headline: Excellent fuel pressure gauge for gas or diesel applications where nominal fuel feed pressure is 30 psi or less.
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo1GI985CO0V31K]]I purchased this gauge to go with a new FASS Titanium 95gph lift pump installed on a 98.5 Dodge 2500 Cummins diesel pickup truck. The issue with these trucks is that the small OEM Carter fuel feed pump is just barely adequate when brand new, and as it ages and starts to wear out, it's feed rate and pressure begins to fall off. As soon as it drops below 5 or 6 psi, the primary injection pump is not getting enough fuel circulation to keep it cooled and lubricated, and this will cause premature failure of the injection pump. Anyone with a diesel vehicle of any make or model, that uses a low-pressure electric feed pump to deliver fuel to the primary injection pump, should consider installing one of these gauges. The $69 investment in this gauge could save you thousands of dollars by giving you advance warning of a weak or failing electric lift pump. If you have recently installed a new lift pump, this gauge is still a good idea, as it will tell you what the nominal pressure of the fuel feed system is with a new lift pump and new clean fuel filter. If the pressure starts to drop but the pump motor still sounds normal, this is likely due to a filter that is starting to clog up, and you know it's time to change it. If pressure suddenly drops very low, or to zero, you have a serious problem with the lift pump, or maybe a clogged or broken fuel line, and if you shut down immediately you might be able to avoid damage to the injection pump. I don't know why the factories don't install either a gauge or at least a warning light for low fuel feed pressure, as it's critical to the health and longevity of the very expensive fuel injection pump and injectors on your diesel engine.

What you get in the box: The gauge is 52mm (2\\") diameter, with a 270º sweep of the needle from zero to 30 psi. The needle is red, and is internally illuminated, so it glows when the system is powered on. You do not get a mounting pod or bracket with this gauge. Those can be purchased separately from GlowShift or most auto parts stores, or right here on Amazon. A basic metal bracket is about $6.00. Pods are more expensive and can run $20 to a couple hundred dollars depending on how fancy you want it. In addition to the gauge itself, you get a wiring harness with about 9 feet of cable. This will be enough to cover installations in pickup trucks or cars where the pressure sensor is in the engine bay. If the pressure sensor is mounted on or near the lift pump, and the pump is in or near the fuel tank, this will probably NOT be enough wire, and you will have to splice in enough 18 gauge automotive wire to make up the difference. Same if you are installing this in a big rig, or in a diesel RV or boat: the 9' of supplied wire is likely not going to be enough. Please solder your splices - don't use just crimp connections, especially if the splices are exposed under the vehicle somewhere where water or road salt could splash on them.

This gauge comes with a pressure transducer that uses a 1/8\\" NPT male thread, which I think is an industry standard. It screwed right into the gauge port on my FASS Titanium lift pump. Inside the gauge is a multi-colored LED backlight. You can change the gauge backlighting to any of a dozen or so colors by pressing the button on the lower right side of the gauge face.

The gauge is a \\"stepper motor\\" type. I think this means that it has an analog-to-digital conversion chip in it. This takes the analog voltage signal from the sensor and converts it to a digital value that is used to control the rotation of the gauge needle. Watch the video: you can see that as I start the truck's engine, the gauge rotates the full 0-270º-0 range, then rotates to 17.5 psi and stays there. You can also see the gauge needle and face plate light up with a red glow. This stepper motor technology is supposed to give very accurate gauge readings, as the gauge self-calibrates it's zero to maximum rangeevery time it is powered on.

Ease of installation: No more or less difficult than any other automotive gauge. The difficult part will be routing the wire and finding or making holes in the firewall or floor to pass the wire through. In addition to the cable that goes to the pressure sensor, there are three positive connections that have to be made in the vehicle's fuse box, and a chassis ground. This ground connection can be made at the negative battery terminal, or to any point in the vehicle's frame that you can make a hole in and use your own ring terminal and a sheet metal screw. The three positive connections you need are: (1) a 12 volt \\"always on\\" circuit, (2) a 12 volt \\"switched\\" circuit that is only on when the ignition key is in the \\"run\\" position, and (3) a 12 volt Running Light circuit that is only on when the running light/headlights are on.

Quality of product: I only installed it this week, so I don't have any knowledge of it's long-term durability, but it seems to be well made. NOTE: It has a printed circuit board inside and uses at least some computer type components, so it will not be tolerant of excessive heat. With this in mind, try to install it in such a way that it won't have direct sunlight cooking it. An in-dash install would be good, or perhaps in an \\"A\\" pillar pod in a pickup truck. I like the way the gauge looks and functions, and it seems pretty accurate. For the time being, I'll give it a \\"Highly Recommended\\" rating, in hope that it will last for a few years. NOTE: If it should ever need replacement, the wire harness connects at the rear of the gauge with a quick-change multi-pin plastic connector, so you will not have to replace the wire harness, just the gauge.every time it is powered on.

product_title: Walker Products 250-24248 4-Wire Oxygen Sensor
review_body: I own one of the mighty 8.1 GM beasts and want to shed some light for anybody that is in the situation that I was in. All of the application charts and auto parts stores that I consulted will tell you that there are 4 (or even 5) O2 sensors on your vehicle. Mine is a 2001 Silverado 2500HD 4X4 with Allison and 8.1 motor. Mine has only 2 total period. I noticed my mileage was getting worse over the years and finally I got a \\"service engine soon\\" light. After checking the code with a scanner I got a O2 sensor bank 1 position 1 failure \\"no activity\\". I started researching O2 sensors to find that the life expectancy is 30 to 60K miles. Mine has 117k and they have never been changed. After deciding to buy them I could not get a logical answer from anybody or any website or blog that indicated which sensor to buy. Finally looked at the Wagner website and at least it had a fairly accurate diagram of the specs connector and dimensions. I say fairly accurate because the actual length as indicated on the diagram is wrong in length by 1 inch. I emailed Walker for a confirmation that my factory Denso part number is the direct equivalent for the Walker 250-24248 after I had already ordered the walker. I have yet to hear back from Walker. Got the new sensor and indeed it is identical in the measurements. If your truck has only 2 sensors then the upstream is the one you should  need. It came with anti seize compound so you wont need to buy any. I removed mine with a 22mm craftsman open end wrench without to much difficulty. Some force was needed to release the protective wire duct on the connector. A broad headed flat screwdriver will get it done. After you get the access to connector there will be a plastic slide lock that you can pull out to allow the connectors to be separated. Installation was much easier than removal. Truck starts and the error has not returned. I have yet to go drive it but feel confident it will be fine and I hope my mileage will increase. If it does I willbuy one for the other side. If not I will wait until I get a fail code from the bank 2 side (passenger). The parts store will try to sell you a special socket for $20 to do the work. I did not need it because the 22mm (or 7/8 SAE-kind of loose) will work and to tighten to the required 35 ft. lbs. I used a 22mm crow foot attached to my torque wrench with a 1 inch extension to gain clearance and it was easy at least for the driver side. If I get one for the other side I will follow it up with a review. You cant buy these big powerful 8.1 motors any more due to the fuel regulations so we have to keep them going.

product_title: 1992-1998 BMW E36 Coupe 2 Door 318i 320i 325i Twin Angel Eyes Halo Projector Headlights Black
review_headline: They look great, but have NO INSTRUCTIONS and DONT FIT PERFECTLY, and the angel eyes DONT GLOW
review_body: 2 year update: left side rings have gone out. When the headlight assembly is cold the rings have their normal dull glow, but as soon as the engine bay warms up the left side starts to flicker, then after 20 or so mins of driving goes out completely and doesn't come back on until the car has sat overnight. Through my trouble shooting I've determined the resistor/capacitor block is to blame, power goes in one side but doesn't come back out.  First off, everything is in translated English (translated from Chinese, or so it looks like) so the two pieces of paper that come with the lights are very hard to figure out, I wasn't sure if I had missed a piece or if something wasn't shipped, so I left the angel eyes off until I have enough time to hook them up.  The angel eyes have to be hooked up to another power source, but there are literally NO instructions in the box on what goes where. They are a little mishapen, and there's a small gap between the insulation and the edge of my headlight housing, but it isn't very noticable. Also, they are shaped in such a way that it's nearly impossible to screw the bottom screws on without getting underneath the car and using a special tool.  Takes a few hours to install the set, but once you figure out one the other is a lot easier.  Rattling after installation is hard to avoid, as the bottom screws are VERY hard to reach.  Still though, they look WAY cooler on the car than in the thumbnail.

Nonetheless, the dealer wanted quite a bit more for these items and you never know what you'll end up getting on "that" auction site, so I'm still happy - but I did take a star off since the product wasn't really new.

product_title: Stant 10501D Diesel Locking Fuel Cap
review_body:
With diesel fuel prices as high as they are nowadays I felt a need to protect my 40 gallon, ~$150 investment. This was cheap insurance out here in farm country. This cap is plastic so don't expect it to hold up to anything stronger than a human finger. My major reason for purchase was simply to deter the errant miscreant criminal opportunist while out and about not someone hell bent on stealing my fuel in my driveway. Anyway, the cap fits perfect and works well at sealing the tank off to the elements. Contact, rotation, and clicking when sealed of the Stant provide the same feel as the stock cap did. All is well there. The only odd thing after you put this on is what to do with the stock strap that holds the stock cap when it's off. There's no place to attach it to this Stant unit (note it slipped around a ring at the base of the stock cap). I left the strap on and slip it back over this cap after I've tightened it back down every time I fill up. You can't loosen the cap without taking it back off, because it's a little too tight but that's no big deal to me. I like having it on there for some reason and just set the cap on the truck bed when fueling up. Another note is you can put the key in, turn it, pull the key out and still be able to open the cap - so no leaving your key in the cap or turning your keys with the cap until it's off: good stuff.

The problem and reason for the 3 star rating here is the locking mechanism itself. It has become "sticky" over time and left me fearing it may not work in the very near future. I've had this on for over a year now I'd guess and I've shot some WD down there a couple of times, but the mechanism has gotten a grinding feel now whenever I turn the key. The key goes in no problem at all, but it only turns about 1/8 turn or less to unlock. This stoke of the key (my perception here) has gotten shorter and shorter over the time I've owned this thing. So when I put the key in it begrudgingly turns a fraction of a turn then it's unlocked. Hopefully I'm not at the ragged fringe of the unlock mech heading quickly toward total failure. Like I said it works... for now. I just might double down and try another one of these as this item is very well priced and seemed to work well when new. review_headline: BIG DISAPPOINTMENT.  DON'T WASTE YOUR HARD EARNED MONEY!!!

When it was time to install the headliner, I cut an X-shape in the headliner for the over head console, dome light, grab handle, sun visor, etc., per the instructions. Had to take my original headliner to an upholstery shop where they cover it and installed it for $60.00.  PLEASE FOLKS, DON'T MAKE THE COSTLY MISTAKE I DID.  Learn from my mistake.  I should have known when I read the other guys review not to purchase this.  Now I can't even get my money back.

product_title: W.A.O. Go Cart Throttle Cable"manco#8251" 75" Cable 68" Housing with 4 Free 8812bs
review_headline: Perfect repair for Lawnboy model 680542 replacing Toro 683041
review_body:
If that title made any sense to you it will be because you know this part is pure unobtanium from LawnBoy/Toro.

The LawnBoy part 683041 is the cable that connects the "dead man's switch" to the engine. The cable retracts a flywheel brake and grounds the magneto so you get a spark. When the operator releases the mower handle the cable no longer holds back the flywheel brake and disconnects the magneto from the spark plug. Without this cable it is messy to defeat these safeties and in the end you have a potentially lethal toenail trimmer that's hard to turn off.

Alas, the part is not obtainable from Lawn Boy (now Toro).

But if you have a soldering iron and a few basic tools this cable is the perfect replacement. All you have to do is shorten it.

Ok, it isn't that simple. Here's what you need to do:

1) Remove the motor gas tank so you can clearly see where the cable is attached to the motor. Take pictures or make a sketch because there's a big spring, a cupped washer to go over the end of the spring, and an odd slit washer to lock the cable in. The assembly is a bit counter-intuitive so take as many pictures or notes as you can.

2) Turning to your new Go Cart throttle cable assembly neatly cut off the ball of solder on one end. I simply melted the solder off with a husky (100 watt) soldering iron.

3) Pull the cable through the sheath. Now you have two pieces. Later you will reassemble by reinserting the cable from the non-threaded end of the sheath.

4) Shorten the sheath. Match it to the old one or hold it in place to figure out how long it needs to be. Error on the side of too long, however. I used a three corner metal file to cut the sheath. Follow up with a sharp knife to cut the inner liner neatly.

5) Clamp the sheath cutoff in a vise or locking pliers and yank off the ferrule at the end. Slide the ferrule onto the cut end of the measured sheath.

6) Reinsert the cable from the non-threaded end of the sheath.

7) Attach the loop end of the cable to the "dead man's switch" and mower speed adjustment on the handle. That thing on the handle is a festival of small parts that has to be completely disassembled. Be prepared for parts to fall out. Work carefully and document what you are doing. It's not hard or overly complicated -- perhaps a dozen pulleys, shafts and screws -- but it's not always immediately obvious where a part goes.

8) It's time to address the motor end when you've got the handle end fully reassembled. Wind the adjustment nut on the threaded end of the sheath until it mid point in the threaded range. Thread the cable back in place with the spring and cup washer in place so you can figure out exactly where the cable end should be. I clamped a small locking plier on the cable and found the length by trial and error.

9) Mark the length and disassemble the motor end again. Use some acid core solder and your soldering iron to build up a a roughly 3/8" ball of solder on the end of the cable. Use a big locking plier as a heat sink or you might melt the sheath liner when the cable gets hot. That proved to be an ugly task that had to be done twice. [ You might investigate if a brass "stop" (A little slug of brass with a hole for the cable and a set screw to clamp the stop on with -- bicycle and mower shops should have an assortment.) might work. I'd already made a new solder ball before using a stop occurred to me (doh!)].

Mine still works like a champ after all the spring mowings.

product_title: Classic Accessories MotoGear Motorcycle Saddle Bags and Tail Bag Bundle
review_headline: Works well for in-town and short trips
review_body:
I've been running these bags on my 2004 Suzuki GS500F for a few months now. In that time I've used them to carry groceries, rain gear, take-out, and luggage for a 1-day trip.

I have them setup so the 2 top velcro straps are under my one-piece seat. This acts like a security mechanism so that someone can't just unbuckle the bags and take them away. I have the front and rear buckles on each bag connected to the passenger peg frame extension and rear signal indicators, respectively.

Overall, I got my money's worth. It's nice to have storage space on a bike with abysmal storage options, and I can at least do my weekly grocery shopping when using these saddle bags with the accompanying top bag. We're talking a dozen eggs, half gallon of milk, some vegetables, fruits, a few steaks, a 6 pack of soda, and some toiletries.

The reflective striping works really well and has very likely contributed to my visibility when I ride at night. The bags have stayed together and don't seem to be too worn by sunlight exposure. At home, I leave the bike in the garage, but it will stay outside for at least 8 hours when parked at work or at a relative's home.

The rain cover mechanism is pretty clever. The bright neon yellow color of the covers is in your best interest as a rider, even though it will detract from the appearance of the bike. I have not yet ridden with these bags in the rain, although I believe they would do just fine. It wouldn't hurt to spray the outside of the bags (sans rain cover) with some 3M Scotchguard or equivalent product, though, to give you time to pull over and deploy the rain covers in the event of a random shower.

The downsides are the sag with weight and the inability to expand the bag for needed storage. When these bags are loaded down, expect them to hang a few inches lower, depending on the weight inside. On my GS500F, the exhaust is on the brake-side of the bike and these bags when unloaded have around 2 inches of clearance above the exhaust. The underside of the bags seems to be designed to handle heat, but I wouldn't trust them to hold up to being stuck in stop-and-go traffic on a hot summer day. The other gripe is that these bags could expand outward for more storage, much like the tank bag offered by the same company or like the pricier competitor's offering (Cortech 2.0 Tour Master).

Overall, I think it's appropriate to consider the design of these bags and what they offer. These are not hard panniers on a dual sport. They're fabric bags that will end up on a sport bike or a small cruiser. You wouldn't use these to ride all the way to Alaska, but you can use them to run errands around town, while saving gas, and enjoying the weather. The price (and value) is what is most attractive about these bags. To step up to Nelson-Rigg or Cortech, you'll have to spend more money and you honestly won't gain a lot more storage room.2 inches of clearance above the exhaust. product_title: Griot's Garage 11033 Glass Sealant, 8 oz.
review_headline: Worth It - If You Have the Time
review_body:
I've used this stuff, intermittently, for years. It definitely has a place in the automotive detailing pantheon. If you are the type that keeps your car sparkling clean, and waxes it religiously, a "slick" coating of petroleum-based magic (Rain-X is the same thing) over your glass, to help keep it water-stain free and dirt repellant, truly is the icing on the cake. But it definitely takes some time and commitment to get the coating right, with repeated applications. You can actually eliminate the need for using wipers by applying it on your windshield, but, realize that if you decide to start using your wipers, you will get a hazy mess for quite a few strokes. Classic car owners that don't drive in the rain all that often, and have flaky/ineffectual wiper mechanisms, love this stuff.

It's also very important to PROPERLY clean all the glass (not just if it's a windscreen you're dealing with) before applying this. Note that polishing your windshield on occasion is a good idea anyway, and is a huge factor in allowing your wipers to work their best. A reasonably cheap electric glass cooktop polish (like Wieman brand) works nicely.

When considering this product, you need to ask yourself if it's worth the effort. If you regularly encounter clinging dirt/mud or ice in your travels, it probably is. Because clean up will go much easier. Also, if your car is parked on a highly traffic'd urban street, rinsing the windows with plain water will get them perfectly translucent again, even if it's been parked for a few days.

Having clean glass is a safety concern, and so should be a priority. The multiple treatments and overall time it takes to get it right, though, means I subtract one star.

product_title: TMS 3 CFM Single-stage Rotary Vane Vacuum Pump R410a R134 Hvac A/c Air Refrigerant
review_headline: It sucks and sucks and...WORKS GREAT !!!!
review_body:
Perfectly packaged, a bit heavy, but quite a beauty overall. Amazon got it out to me two days early, which gave me extra time to figure it all out. (Documentation is P-poor.) The users manual shows the air-inlet fitting as "oil-fil" etc. There is already a larger plastic opening for oil nearby, so after a little brain-banging, I convinced myself that the fitting was where I would connect my service line. (Yellow hose from a "gauge-manifold.") The hose fitting is 1/2 inch, and the pump fitting is 1/4 inch. Amazon sells an adapter fitting for this so - buy it. (I couldn't find one in any of my local stores.)
The pump works like a dream. Make sure you bring up the oil level as required then hook it up. I was almost shocked at how quiet it was. (No neighbor complaints with this one.)
It pulled about 28 inches of mercury by my gauges, so no problem with the evacuation process. I shut all the valves and waited several hours before cramming some 134a down my system's throat. I followed all the instructions and.....NOTHING!!! The compressor refused to kick-in.
That's right, the low side pressure would not budge an inch during my first attempt, so very little refridge was being drawn in. The Hitchhicker's Guide advises...DON'T PANIC !!! so I didn't.
I reviewed a few more articles on the web, watched a few more videos on YouTube, and was just about to figure out how to put a jumper across my compressor-fuse to force it into operation, then remembered the short list of things that can cause a compressor not to cycle. I also knew that you can force-feed the low side with refridge without the compressor cycling. I guessed, that I simply needed to keep feeding the low-side more refrigerant until there was enough pressure in the line, to trigger the compressor's sensor.
When that puppy finally clutched itself and started turning, I nearly died. After that, I kept watching the gauges and kept feeding the system refrigerant, and eventually Istarted seeing the recommended pressures.
A quick feel of the interior vents and "Cap'n! there be coolin' in here!" What a great feeling. All it needs now, is to keep itself sealed and for no components to to explode.
So, it CAN be done, even with an old clunker like mine, but a little luck and resourcefulness helps too. My ride has 240k miles on it with nearly everything in the A/C system still original. (I bow down to the Gods of refrigeration.) "We stand on the (cold) shoulders of giants." :)
I place the miracle of Refrigeration right up there with heart surgery, rocket science and electric kazoos. Life would be hell without it.

Follow the product directions and make sure you thoroughly wash the area with detergent and dry before applying the scratch seal. Push the pen tip in 10-15 times to prime it, then just paint the stuff into the scratch. I only needed two coats to completely fill in the scratch. After the product has dried, you can follow up by wet sanding with a very fine grit sand paper intended for clearcoat finishes (3000 grit or finer). I buffed using a mechanical buffer and applied rubbing compound, followed by polishing compound. Nearly a perfect match to the factory clear coat, scratch is no longer visible. Great product, great price, does the job for minor scratches that have cut into the finish. Would protect paint/primer scratches as well.

product_title: 2 ThermoServ Foam Insulated Coffee Mugs 34 oz (1) Purple & (1) Blue
review_headline: Living in the tropics - a true test of dripability!
review_body:
We've been using these daily for about two weeks and love them! We drink iced tea all day long and live in the tropics without A/C, where humidity is usually about 80% or more, and have had extremely high heat for the past few weeks to boot. At least one day, the "real feel" was 106 F. I'm here to testify: Absolutely no sweating or dripping!

As others have mentioned, these replaced some probably 25-30 year old Aladin mugs bought from a Texaco gas station in the late 1980s or early 90s! Unfortunately, these had apparently deteriorated over the years -- were dripping from condensation like crazy. These ThermoServ were the only similar replacements I could find anywhere. The lid is shaped a little different but I like the new style better. It's thinner in the area that you drink from. The lid fits tightly with no leaks. Additionally, the ice is lasting much longer with these new ones than the old ones. I'd say it lasts at least 6 hours or so and by that time I need a refill anyway. The colors are more muted than shown in the photos which was another plus for me.

I do wish I could find a size around 24 ounces as these are very large. But they are what they say they are and are the size they say they are. Absolutely no dripping. I guess it is the foam between the inside and outside layers that does the trick.

A couple of caveats: If you are looking for a travel mug, this is probably not it unless you have very large cup holders. The bottom of the mug is just under 4" across (3 7/8" to be exact). Also, it isn't spill proof, though the openings are so small that any spills would be greatly reduced. They are much better balanced than most large travel mugs so tipping over is not likely.

I've tried several kinds of insulated glasses/mugs, and these are the ONLY ones that actually work in my extreme tropical climate. I'll be buying a couple more of them the next time I make an Amazon order. I've already put them in my shopping cart.my shopping cart.

review_headline: I think I got a defective one
review_body:
Well.. It is a nice pump. The power cable is detachable and uses the same connector that computers do so you never have to worry about a replacement.

My compressor seized on my Ford truck after 278k miles so I got all the parts and bought this pump to pull it down.

Unfortunately, after following all the instructions and filling it as prescribed with the included oil, it would only pull ~27 inhg of vacuum.

The truck held the vacuum with no leaks. Using some extra oil on the outside of every connection while the pump was running to insure that a connection wasn't leaking I determined the pump was bad.

I had to pay a local shop to pull the vacuum and it held till I got back home. I charged the system with the correct amount of 134a and it works well after about a week.

Robinair is a well known brand and this experience doesn't turn me off their products at this time.

product_title: Purolator L14477 Purolator Oil Filter
review_headline: I ended up with 8 quarts of oil on the driveway
review_body:
I had a major issue with a Purolator filter when I changed my oil yesterday. Model number is L1447 for my 2006 Toyota Camry. I had used this filter several times, in the past, for this car with no issues.

I changed the oil as normal, wrench tightened the filter and plug and put the oil in. I checked under the car – no leaks. So, I started the car. My oil light came on so I shut the car down. I got out and every bit of oil had come out into the driveway. 4 quarts makes quite the mess. I thought maybe I had not gotten it threaded correctly, so I took the filter off and reattached it. I checked the drain plug, it was fine. So I put oil in again. Same thing, except now there are 8 quarts in the driveway.

I went to Advance, where I had purchased the filter and took the filter with me (plus the old one I had taken off the car to start the oil change). They were very helpful. They confirmed, as I had on Google, that I had the right filter for the car and said it must be defective. They gave me a new on – a PL1447. I tried it and it worked fine.

I have an enormous mess on my hands. 8 quarts of oil plus 40 lbs of cat litter (and still may need more. Plus: extra purchased oil, a set of ruined clothes, a major need for a car wash and the likelihood that I will need to have someone pressure wash my driveway. I have reached out to Purolator for some reimbursement.

product_title: Griot's Garage 11033 Glass Sealant, 8 oz.
review_body:
I will come right out of the gate and explain that I found the constant application and re-applications and buffing to be tedious, time consuming and annoying. If you enjoy working on your car and have time to kill then this may be worthwhile time spent but if you are like my husband and myself then it leaves a lot to be desired when it comes to the wasted time.

The glass sealant works but you have to make sure that your windows are crystal clean or there will be a haze. We have had a few storms, hot days and pigeon attacks. The windows seem less dusty but the pigeon fecal matter now slides down rather than stay put. The windshield wipers do effortlessly glide, which I personally love. My only grip would be that this product seems to do exactly what our old RainX does! Seriously, there isn't much difference except for the fecal running. I am not sure what would motivate me to reach for this product over the RainX considering how annoying the application was. Maybe better results are yielded if used in conjunction with other Griot's Garage products?

Recommend if you are in the market for a great glass cleaner that allows your windshield wipers to work effortlessly. The rain just glides off and there is a longer period of dustless windows. I cannot with good conscience though, suggest that this product is any different than it's competitor.

product_title: Reese Towpower 44174 Class III Custom-Fit Hitch with 2" Square Receiver opening, includes Hitch Plug Cover
review_body:
We recently sold our Trailblazer and picked up a Honda Odyssey. While it has tons of room, I have a platform I like to take on vacation for the coolers, sand toys and beach chairs. I picked this hitch up so I could use the platform or pull the occasional rental trailer from our local tool rental place.

This has 6 holes that line up perfectly with the predrilled holes on the frame of the Odyssey. Some people say the you need to move the muffler and some people say you don't. I was able to install the hitch without moving the muffler. The trick is to maneuver the hitch on the right side of the van first and then move the left in place. Then the hitch can "hang" from the muffler while you get in position. Use a paint can or something to hold up the left side while you hang the 1st bolt on the right. Then switch to the left and hang it. Once you have a bolt on each side, the remaining two per side go quick.

TIP: Make sure you use a tap to clean out the holes. I can't remember the size, but lots of reviews mention the proper size.

30 mins and I didn't even have to jack the van up.

product_title: BAK 36506 Roll-X Tonneau Cover
review_body:
I bought this in Oct 2012, and wanted to leave a review for other 2012 Nissan Frontier truck owners. The things you are probably concerned about are:

- works with Utili-Track System / even the truck extender
- keeps rain out (i live in CA, but i have gone through the car wash once or twice a month with no leaking)
- Leather still looks great 2 years later.
- Very easy to use / very convenient
- Straight forward to install (if you watched the video on youtube)

So why no 5 stars?
The downside to living in California is the brutally hot summers. I park my car out in the open during the days and the internal temps can get to around 115-120 (maybe higher, that's just what i see on the temp display in the cabin). So one day i opened the back of the truck, and i can see that glue holding the the felt liner that is on the undersides of the tonneau must have softened/melted in the heat and caused the felt liner to separate from the metal portion of the cover. Ever since that day, the felt just hasn't been the same, it's out of place, and most times loose. This is still just a slight problem, as the cover still functions.

The 2nd problem is probably similar to the first. The rubber seal that you stick to the truck bed shifted due to the glue melting. so there wasn't a tight seal anymore causing a whistling noise that i eventually figured out. (it didn't make noise when the tonneau was rolled up, only when it was down. So i removed the tonneau and i saw the rubber seal drooping slightly into the truck. I just went to home depot, and replaced it with a 1 inch peel & stick insulation foam and put the tonneau back on, and haven't had a problem since.

As for keeping the tonneau looking shiny and new, i used Armor all the first couple months, but switched to using 303 Aerospcae Protectant instead after reading many reviews. This has less shine, but really does seem to be magic on leather and plastic.

http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004YJQE0S

I also wrote up a more wordy review when i first bought the product, and posted it on my blog @ survialpaladin dot com

If i ever need to buy a replacement cover i will most likely buy another roll-x from BAK industries, this simply has been the best cover i've ever used and the convenience it offers is well worth it.http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004YJQE0S

I also wrote up a more wordy review when i first bought the product, and posted it on my blog @ survialpaladin dot com

If i ever need to buy a replacement cover i will most likely buy another roll-x from BAK industries, this simply has been the best cover i've ever used and the convenience it offers is well worth it.

product_title: Raggtopp Convertible Top Care Kit - Fabric Cleaner and Protectant Twin Pack
review_headline: Performance of Raggtopp Cleaner and Fabric Protector
review_body:
My daughter purchased a 2007 Solara convertible, Blue in Tan Convertible Top, it does not appear the top was ever treated as no water would bead up at all- the top had dirt streaks as the crease points when the top closes. I used the cleaner with a brush and then cotton T shirt to work to rub out the dirt and it took a lot of effort to remove the dirt even after waiting for 15 to 20 minutes for the cleaner to work on the problem. I thought the dirt breaking power would be better - less effort.

On the protectant, it was an aerosol spray can and I was not able to do multiple coats as the directions advised - one can was not enough to do a top that has never been treated. I did some more Google searching for a local dealer as I wanted to do more coats and found the alternative product 303 Fabric Protector in a pump spray bottle and purchased from a local West Marine - 32 oz. I needed to use almost the whole bottle when applying in full sun to seal the top after having used the RaggTopp over the whole surface - 7 years of no treatment left the fabric very "needy". I saw a side by side YouTube video of the RaggTopp vs 303 and both seemed to cause water to bead up after application - 303 may have done a little better resistance and bead up. After applying Ragg Topp and 303, the first rain showed a very nice bead up on the fabric.

I liked the pump spray bottle versus the spray - you lose a lot more spray on a day with any wind at all. For next purchase, I would go with 303, I will have to try their cleaner as well.

product_title: Power-Trip Dakota II Men's Textile Sports Bike Motorcycle Jacket - Black
review_headline: Great Jacket.  Great Value.  Excellent Airflow, Solid Build, Amazing Waterproofing.  Could use more reflective striping.
review_body:
Power-Trip Dakota II Men's Textile Motorcycle Jacket
Pros: Lightweight, Sturdy, Excellent airflow.
Cons: Small reflective strip, Only comes in black.

I picked this up in February 2014 from the clearance rack at a local motorcycle shop. I commute on my motorcycle 5 days a week, and this is the jacket I wear. It is very comfortable, and bends in all the right places while feeling sturdy where I'd need it in a fall. There are three zippers to close the front of the jacket:

1) Zipper on the outer shell. Moderate airflow, moderate waterproofing.
2) Zipper on mesh front. Leaves the outer shell open, but holds the jacket closed. Excellent airflow! Not waterproof this way.
3) Snaps on waterproof flap. Innermost layer. Closing this and the outer shell leaves this jacket virtually waterproof.

At normal cruising speeds the airflow in configurations 1 and 2 is fabulous and keeps me completely comfortable. I live in Hawaii so the average outside temperature during my commutes is 85F (29.4C). I have ridden through pounding tropical rains in this jacket and my rain pants. I got home with a wet bottom and a bone dry shirt.

It comes with an insulated waterproof liner which makes the jacket much too hot to wear in Hawaii. Since I never wear the liner, I bought the jacket one size smaller than I normally would. At 5'11" and 185 lbs a Medium fits me perfectly.

My only complaints about this jacket are related to it's visibility, or lack of it. There is minimal reflective striping on the back. It is really just a narrow band of piping around one of the seams. The location of the retro-reflective material is good, I just wish it were an inch or two wider to increase visibility. I wish it came in other colors for the same reason. Since it is so narrow, and only comes in black, I find myself wearing a hi-visibility safety vest over the jacket at night.

I would recommend this jacket to anyone looking for a new jacket. It is comfortable, mostly waterproof, and durable. I expect it to last me many years and many miles.

product_title: Fulton 2060766 2" X 48" Zinc Surelok Transom Tie Down
review_body:
I bought this product thinking I was buying a Fulton Winch Company product. That's not exactly what it is. It says "Fulton" on a paper label on the package, but the Fulton brand name does not appear on the product itself. This product does appear on the Fulton web site, but Fulton's address or other contact information appears nowhere on either package or part. The product is sold with a "5 year warranty" according to the Fulton web site, but there is no warranty information or Fulton contact information for warranty claims. The actual manufacturer appears to be "Cequent Performance Products" in China, also no information on how to contact them. This does not inspire confidence.

The webbing is MUCH lighter weight than the webbing in the Boat Buddy straps I'm replacing, yet both claim the same 2500 lb breaking strength and 833 lb working load ratings- FWIW, both claims may be correct and I have no way to test them. The "Fulton" product lacks any feature to manage the excess length of webbing hanging out of the buckle, which many other tie-downs do have. The buckle assembly has a hard plastic cladding, not a soft/resilient plastic pad to prevent damage to the boat hull. The buckle assembly does not allow much tension to be applied to the tiedowns. The release mechanism has a plastic grip attached to the steel release, the plastic held in place with two small plastic rivets molded as part of the grip, thus maybe not replaceable.

All in all, not a satisfying purchase.

review_body:

This stuff essentially creates a film over the windshield to bead water droplets. It will also create that film over dirt. so, as you clean the windshield, the solution is also covering the dirt outside of where the wiper blades clean.

This leaves dirt stains in the corners of the windshield that are tough to get out. I went through an automated car wash and a hand car wash and they remained.
