product_title: Briggs & Stratton 498170 Carburetor
review_headline: Save yourself time...buy the carb now.
review_body:
My brother-in-law left an old Yard Machines 6 hp mower, circa 2001, sitting in our garage for 5 years. This year, I decided I'd get it up and running with fresh oil and gas because I hate a useless thing that takes up space. I filled it up, ripped the starter back and...nothing. Even after 20 minutes of pulling (and cursing) nothing. So, I took a look at the air filter. Clogged. That was obviously the problem. I picked up a new one on the way home from work the next day, popped it in, ripped the starter and...nothing. I gave the mower another once-over and the problem became clear -- the gas line was dry rotted and the engine wasn't getting any gas. Duh! I confirmed it with a shot of starting fluid to the carb. I pulled the starter and it started! But after 3 seconds...nothing. I replaced the fuel line (and spark plug for good measure). Repeated the starter fluid procedure and...3 seconds of run-time then nothing. I did consider taking it to a small engine repair guy but the last time I did that, I spent $70 and there was no way I was spending that on my brother-in-law's 13 year old mower!

So, I got on Google.

Someone said to tap the carb to un-stick the needle. I tapped it. Nothing. Someone said to clean the carb. I cleaned it. Nothing. Someone said to replace the carb so I got on the manufacturer website to order one and...$99?! You've gotta be kidding! So I came to Amazon. I found this one at a fraction of the price, ordered it, installed it in 5 minutes, primed the engine, pulled the starter and...the mower purred like a kitten. As good as new, or at least as good as I imagine this mower ran when new.

This carb is not as hefty as the one I took off the mower, as in it literally weighs less. It did come in a Briggs & Stratton box so I imagine that B&S has simply reworked the specifications for the carb to use a different metal. The metal choke arm is now plastic Specifications do change over time so I have no issue with that, especially since it worked on the first pull. The carb does come with the two gaskets that you will need. There are no instructions with the carb but, again, not so much of an issue. Swapping it out is as simple as removing the air filter housing with 3 screws, removing the old carb body with another two screws, removing the gas line and choke rod, then reversing the procedure to install the new one. It's seriously 5 minutes of work with a socket set and a pair of pliers and it's not that messy if you drain the gas first. There are no adjustments to make to the carb or mower to make it run. This is a direct bolt-on replacement.

I really wish I would have just bought the carb first since that was probably the issue all along. I was a little leery about ordering this one because of a couple of negative reviews but I was already invested in this mower with a new fuel line, air filter, etc., so I thought "what the heck?" I'm glad I did.

You can even keep it installed full time, and it can give you information like instantaneous mpg, time and distance traveled, or even capture and graph the most esoteric details of engine performance, and then email you the data so you can import it into Excel.

You do have to wait a minute or so for it to power up completely before using it, and you must pair it with your phone before using it. Pairing was a bit finicky as I had to turn Bluetooth on and off a few times on my phone before it would discover the device but that was a one time effort.

The device came with little to no documentation, and I had to go online to figure out a few things, but after the initial learning curve, it has exceeded my expectations especially for the price.

Not for the person who is completely clueless, but with a little effort, this will become one of the most valuable tools in your toolbox.

product_title: K&N 69-3513TTK Textured Black Performance Intake Kit
review_body: This is my first intake kit I've owned and installed on a vehicle.  It was a pretty easy install and the directions are pretty straight forward.  The only issues I ran into were: 1) I over-tightened the hose clamp for the filter on the end of the intake tube and bent the tube a little bit, but that was my fault.  2) I found that the support piece that bolts onto the lower 2 bolts of the throttle body caused the intake to have a twist in it, which caused the plastic throttle body to warp a bit, and made the intake butterfly catch on the throttle body.  You could feel it when giving the car gas from a stop, or on the road.  The solution was to drill another hole, beside the factory one, for the intake tube to bolt to the support piece.  3) I noticed a rattle that wasn't there before installation, when starting the engine, and when taking off slowly.  I found this to be the heat shroud for the cone filter bounces off the battery mount.  The solution will be to put a piece of rubber weather stripping or something between the two to silence the rattle, or possibly install an "L" bracket to fasten the two together.  I've only had the kit installed for about a month, so I really don't have a grasp on any MPG benefits, but that is probably due more to my driving as of late, as I'm usually running around 80mph to work (164 mi commute, round trip).  So far, my best mileage recorded has been right at 32 MPG, but I did get that a time or 2 before installing this kit.  I do definitely notice a slight HP boost, and louder intake noise during hard acceleration, which is not over powering or annoying, to me.  Although I have not personally seen up to a 3 MPG increase as some have seen, yet, I would still recommend this kit based on performance.

review_body:
5/8/2014
I just purchased these for my 09 Maxima SV and they were a direct perfect fit. I was very reluctant to buy this brand because I've never heard of them before but I did some research and found numerous other reviews on forums and people were surprisingly pleased with their products and brakes.

Because of the other reviews I found and the low price point I pulled the trigger and bought this package set for my car to replace all 4 rotors and brakes. The full package (came in 2 boxes) arrived in about a week and my buddy and I did the replacement ourselves. If you don't feel confident then just take it to a shop and pay the labor for them to replace it for you.

The package included 2 front rotors, 2 rear rotors, 4 front brake pads (2 per wheel), and 4 rear brake pads. These were pretty much direct fitment and needed no modifications for my car.

I only rated this a 4 star because I don't know how these will hold up down the road but I will try to keep this review updated as the months go by. So far I'm very satisfied and pleased with the rotors and brakes and I hear no grinding or scraping of any kind. They are quiet and the brake power feels good. The only issue to announce is that there is a very slight vibration when braking from high speeds but it is very negligible. Everyone did say that you do need to "break in" new brakes so I'm assuming these will actually get even better in a few months. I'm not an aggressive driver by any means and am a pretty conservatively driver actually so I'm not looking for any big braking power or racing brakes but even still these brakes are fantastic for the daily drivers like myself.

So far I highly recommend these; will provide update in a few months.

5/11/2014
It's been a few days since the replacement and I can tell there's a difference in the pads and rotors every new day. I didn't know but I guess brakes really do get better as you break them in a bit and I can tell that these are getting better and better. It has also rained here in Atlanta, GA the last couple days and I've had no issues with the brakes in the rain or when wet. I'm still very happy.

Everything is still holding up and no issues. There is still brake dust but it's nothing out of the ordinary. No issues to mention, still good.

Rode about 100 miles with these in light to heavy rain on about a 40 degree day. They kept my hands warm and dry for about thirty minutes,  however they became water logged from the heavy rain. My hands remained fairly warm,  second only to my torso with a thick leather jacket on. They took a while to dry which is expected of the material. On a dry day at lower temperatures they keep your hands warm well but finger tips begin to get cold after an hour or so. The only thing I don't like is how bulky they are and on longer rides they are uncomfortable, but that comes with wearing thick gloves.  Overall these gloves are great for the price and I will be buying a new pair when these wear out.  If you don't have bottomless pockets and ride year round I would recommend these. I will order a size larger next time to allow for glove liners so keep that in mind if you ride year round.

product_title: OTC 4676 Windshield Wiper Puller
review_body:
An absolute must if you need to pull off a windshield wiper arm on a 02 Camaro. If you raise up the wipers to wash the front window, you better remember to put them back down before you open the hood (or the hood will snap them off like twigs). Yep, got in a hurry drying my car one day after washing and learned that the hard way.

Also the wiper arm is pressed on, so there is no way to pry it up because there is the windshield right above it and plastic right below it. So, there is nothing to get any leverage off of that won't break easily if you try.

So a little tool like this is absolutely needed if you have to replace the wiper arm and it is pressed on. Do yourself a favor and don't break a $200 or $300 window, or other expensive part trying to pry the wiper arm lose....just spend the $12 and get the right tool to get it off.

product_title: Liqui Moly (20002) Cera Tec Friction Modifier - 300 ml
review_headline: Definitely Beneficial - Especially in Cold Climates
review_body: I added a treatment of Ceratec to my 2013 Honda Civic and 2008 Honda Odyssey.  For the Civic, it was added during the second oil change (6K miles) and mixed with Mobil 1 0W-20.  The engine is running smoother, quieter, and mpg appears to have increased.  I cannot tell if the mpg increase is due to 1) engine break-in, 2) Lucas fuel treatment, or 3) 42 psi tire pressure.  Currently, at about 13K miles and third oil change, I'm averaging 40 to 50 mpg and the oil is still beautiful and golden.    The Odyssey had 75K miles and the improvement in engine smoothness and MPG was more noticeable.  Also, the Odyssey is taking much shorter trips with mixed driving so the reduced friction benefits are more critical.  I would not hesitate to add Ceratec to any power equipment or vehicle.    Do yourself a favor and change the oil yourself - not to save money but to make sure its done right.  Get a magnetic oil drain plug, extra plug washers, Mobil 1 oil and Mobil 1 oil filters.  Ceratec really seems to be a quality and proven product which is very much worth the premium price.  On a smaller car you could probably get by by putting 3/4 of the bottle in the first treatment and the remainder in the next.  LiquiMoly should offer this in a more cost effective bulk package for fleet sales and multi-car families.    UPDATE:  Went to FUELLY to check the fuel economy of other 2013 Civic owners: [...]  The average seems to be 33 to 38 mpg.  I'm easily achieving 40 to 45 mpg in mixed driving - a 10 to 15% improvement.  It is possible that 5 to 10% of that improvement is due to the Ceratec treatment.

product_title: Powerlet (PAC-069) Powerlet Plug to Dual USB Adapter  2.1A
review_headline: Great adaptor, finally able to charge 2 phones or use GPS and charge phone without second outlet.
review_body:
Works well for my needs which is charging an iPhone or Sena BT communicator and powering/operating a Garmin GPS. This also works ok with other Sena, Bad Elf, and Samsung products. I imagine it would be fine with anything USB. Currently using it on a BMW GS and K16's original canbus equipped outlets.

I'm just glad to finally have something that let's me use regular USB cables but doesn't require any drilling/adapters/etc.

Construction is solid, the only minor issue was the petal-contacts needed to be pushed out a little to give it more purchase within the connector when I got it. Everything else is ok, it's solid regular powerlet.

Appears to be waterproof without cables hooked up to it. There's a little rubber door that I can remove with gloves on. This hangs in place once "unplugged" , which is a nice touch since odds of losing it are less. I wouldn't operate it in the rain with USB connections made (since nothing I have has waterproof USB plugs either). But seems fine to leave connected as long as the rubber plug is in.

The current rating is 2.0a (10w). As of the time of writing the specs are unclear if this is aggregate or each port. I believe it's aggregate, and users will see 1A per port with 2 devices connected or 2A per port with 1 device connected. Regardless, unless your charging 2 iPads you should be fine.

Yes it's a pricey piece but compared to the alternatives, this is plug and play, which still makes it a value for me. No playing with fuse panels or wiring, and easy to move between bikes, perfect.

One thing to consider is if you are between this and a powerlet cable (micro or mini USB/lightning) is that the powerlet cables will likely outlast your OEM USB cable when it comes to being whipped around in the wind. So if your on a naked bike and don't need 2 full usb connections/cables, the regular powerlet cord might be better.

Also if you do go the 2x USB cable route, make sure the cables are only as long as they need to be. The more cable, the more there is to whip around and scratch your ride, or get tangled on stuff.

product_title: Zero Gravity Double Bubble Windscreen - Dark Smoke
review_body:
I'm glad I finally took the plunge and ordered this windshield. I've been eyeing it for the longest time and finally made the decision to buy it. Installation took me about an hour, but I'm pretty new to working on my bike so it was more of a learning process than any issue with the product itself. The product was shipped in a large box marked FRAGILE and was very, very well-packed so as not to crack the plastic. The manufacturer is not joking......THE PLASTIC WILL CRACK WITH THE SLIGHTEST OVER-EXERTION OF PRESSURE!!!!! I managed to crack one of the fastening holes, but it hasn't affected the installation or use of the windshield yet (and hopefully it wont spread?!)

Overall, this is a great product. I recommend taking your time to install it and label all your screws!!! For my particular bike, I ended up taking off the entire front cowling to install the windshield, as the gap between the cowling plastic and the windshield is not enough to insert the new windscreen + the plastic female grommets that the screws go into. Keep this in mind when installing this windshield. Take your time, and, when in doubt, UNDER tighten rather than over tighten!!!

It would be extremely helpful if zero gravity posted a guidelines so one could use a torque wrench and tighten based off of inch-lbs instead of guessing!

Only time will tell how well it holds up, but it exceeds expectations for now.

***Updated*** August 10, 2014
So I have carried this air compressor in my camper all summer so far and it was worth every penny. I have used it to fill the camper tires, the truck tires and our bicycle tires. It fills them all quickly and easily. The built-in gauge appears to be accurate as well. I hope to get many years of use out it.

product_title: Jack Quick 12-Volt Brute Power RV Electric Tongue and Trailer Jack - 3650 lb. Capacity
review_body:
The unit arrived from Amazon on time and was well packaged. Installation was simple and went smoothly. Switches and lights work as expected. So far 5 stars for the hardware. I will update later regarding performance and reliability. The reasons for 4 stars vs. 5 were the instructions and the bull's-eye level.

Wiring Connections: The wiring instructions are inadequate for anyone not familiar with electrical circuitry. 1) Installation step 9 says to route the black wire \\"towards the battery\\" but never says to connect it to anything. Worse yet the next sentence says to \\"Attach the [same] wire lead to the trailer using cable ties.\\" This could lead someone to attach the wire to the frame as would be done with a ground wire. Farfetched? Perhaps, but Murphy's law prevails. 2) Step 11 says to connect the lead from the fuse holder to the battery's \\"+\\" terminal, but which lead? There are two leads one stamped \\"line\\" and the other stamped \\"load.\\" What it should state is, \\"Connect the `line' lead to the `+' terminal of the battery and connect the `load' lead to the black wire leading from the motor.\\"

Manual Crank: The instructions never describe use of the manual crank. It looks like there is a cap of some sort under the bubble level but does it lift off, unscrew, or do the three small screws around the level have to be removed? I am reluctant to experiment not knowing what will happen when I start removing screws or twist the cap and break something. Advice anyone? In my case I cannot use the crank provided with the jack because it interferes with the propane tanks, but I could probably use my electric drill with a socket.....if I could access the drive point.

Bull's-Eye Level: determining what is level in a camp trailer is subjective. Place a level anywhere in the unit and you will get a different indication. I use the grate over the stove burners as my level reference. Everything else can be a few degrees off and be unnoticeable. Once that is level I mount a bull's-eye level with epoxy somewhere on the hitch so that the bubble is centered. However, after mounting the Jack Quick 3500 the integrated level was too far off center to be useful (a half bubble right and up). Not surprisingly my hitch is not in a parallel plane with the stove. It would be far better if the level was included as a separate item so the end user could establish her own level reference and epoxy it appropriately.

Recommendation: A good product at a fair price.

2014/04/09 update.
Manual Crank: The manual crank is accessed by turning the knurled knob beneath the bull's-eye level one quarter turn ccw. This simple one-liner should have been included in the instructions. My 3/8\\" electric drill does not have enough torque to turn the 11mm nut. Fortunately, by removing the shroud from the propane tanks I have enough clearance to use the crank should manual operation be necessary.

Bull's-Eye Level: I suggest the following:
1) Remove the three Phillip's head screws surrounding the level and discard them
2) Remove the level
3) Level the unit using your chosen reference (stove, refrigerator, table, etc.)
4) Apply epoxy to the base of the level and replace it, supporting it with the bubble centered until the epoxy dries.

2014/06/22 Update. We just completed a 4-week 5,000-mile trip. The jack performed flawlessly.

product_title: aFe 49-46230 MACH FORCE XP 2/2.5" Stainless Steel Y-Pipe Exhaust System
review_headline: The Best Exhaust Solution When Lifting a Jeep Wrangler
review_body:
I bought a new 2013 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited Rubicon and purchased the AEV 3.5 Dual Sport Lift Kit, Bumpers, WARN Winch, and Tire Carrier. When you lift a Jeep the front drive shaft will come in contact with the factory exhaust cross over pipe. The aFe Y-Pipe for Manual Transmissions moves the cross over tube from underneath the front drive shaft to back behind the transmission. It's a perfect solution that simply removes any possibility of the front drive shaft coming in contact with the cross over pipe. It's made out of stainless steel so it won't rust and it fit's around the manual transmission perfectly. It's really easy to install. I was able to install this Y-pipe and the [[ASIN:B006YDHHAI Borla 140461 Stainless Steel Cat-Back Exhaust System for Wrangler 3.6L AT/MT 4WD 4-Door]] in about an hour. Jeeps are so easy to work on...LOVE IT!

PS,
The aFe Y-Pipe had no adverse affect on gas mileage and the combination of the aFe Y-Pipe and Borla Catback Exhaust sounds excellent. Unlike many Jeep exhausts the Borla has a resonator which eliminates the droning so often hear in after market Jeep exhausts. The Borla sounds factory quiet at first but sounds off under hard acceleration. Also after a few thousand miles of use the Borla changes to a slightly deeper tone but is still well behaved driving on the highway. You won't need to speak louder or turn up the radio yet she sounds off when you put the petal down or are off-roading. aFe & Borla... an excellent combination!

Note! There is a version of this Y-Pipe made specifically for automatic transmissions and this one for manuals so make sure you order the correct one.

product_title: B00F9LPIAC Battery Tender BTL09A120C Lithium Iron Phosphate Battery and Green Lithium Junior Battery Charger
review_body:
As everyone has already said, this is a great replacement battery to save weight on a bike. My bike's battery box in a Triumph Daytona 955i was almost like a bottomless pit with this battery installed. In fact, I did not have enough foam spacers to pack around this much smaller size battery to keep it from sliding around inside the battery box. The terminal nuts and bolts are too small and do not secure properly to the eyelets on the bike used by my old battery. I used the old nuts and bolts from the old battery which secure the cables to this new battery's terminals much better. I also secured an extender cable for my Battery Tender to the terminals, so I will have a quick and easy way to keep the battery (maintenance) charged during long storage periods. This battery has an extra set of terminals on left and right sides, both front and back (and plastic covers), so it can be mounted with positive and negative cables attached in either orientation.

Before initial operation on my bike, I inadvertently left this LiFePO4 battery attached to an old analog DC Voltmeter. By the next day, the battery was completely dead. Oh S***!!! I did not think that would put that much of a load on the battery to discharge it overnight, but I guess I was wrong. Nevertheless, the battery fully recharged in a couple of hours (using a 1.25A Battery Tender) and started my bike up just fine. The instruction manual warns not to allow it to fully discharge or drop below a certain voltage, so I dodged a bullet before it way too late by unwittingly discharging it all the way to ZERO!

Seems like a great product, worth the extra dough as a \\"high tech\\" replacement for the old \\"boat anchors\\".

review_body: I just wanted to write a review here, so that if someone is in my position and is looking for the correct fluid, here it is. I've seen on the Fiesta forums that people have used different types of gear oil, and while it might work fine, this is the correct oil according to the Fiesta ST supplemental owners manual. It is available online from Ford for free. This is the oil that states in that owners manual that must be used, and it will take 1.8 quarts, so you need to buy two of these. I haven't changed my oil out yet but it seems to use a hex/triple square bolt, so make sure you have a set of those on hand, and make sure you take out the filler bolt first before the you do the drainage bolt. That's all there is too it really, get some sort of a hand pump or something to put the new fluid in and you're good to go. If your Fiesta hasn't had a fluid change in the first 10k miles I would definitely recommend it, because it's breaking in and there are going to be a ton of metal shavings in it. It wouldn't hurt to get a magnetized drain plug as well, so you can pull out even more shavings.

product_title: Airtex E3621S Fuel Pump Sender Assembly
review_body:
Purchased and installed an Airtex (Model: 3621S) pump and sending unit assembly in mid-December, 2013. Verified the pump's operation immediately after installation. The Truck is only used to tow a boat and was not started until March, 2014, three months later. When I attempted to start my 1993, C1500 it would not start. I COULD NOT BELIEVE THE CAUSE...NO FUEL!!!!! The truck has not been started since mid-December, now when I needed it, it would not start.

Again, pulled the bed from the vehicle, removed the pump and found all the rubber-compound material dissolved. Before I purchased the Airtex pump I specifically asked if the rubber components were compatible with today's fuels...I was told they were. The reason I asked was because I read several accounts where the material decomposed, and wanted to be assured this has been corrected. Apparently NOT!!!

Additional thought: The assembly's tubing has rubber-compound "O" rings that seal the connection between the Airtex tubing/fittings to the vehicle's fuel lines; these "O" rings are also damaged. Remember, I only started the truck once...not much fuel in contact with these rings. The rings are the seal, the threaded fitting only provide ring compression to seal the fuel lines. If the "O" rings fail, in my mind, a potential fuel leak is possible. Hot exhaust and gasoline---not a good combination!!! Does the Columbia Space Shuttle ring a bell?

One star because I could not rate it lower!

product_title: ADIDAS miCoach Speed Sensor PC/MAC black
review_headline: Decent sensor but buggy syncing software
review_body:
I've used this for a little more than 8 months starting in September 2013. The sensor seems to be fairly accurate and consistent. The battery life was not as good as I was expecting. I've replaced the battery three times since purchasing this sensor. The sensor is water resistant, but not waterproof. I've had a few outdoor matches in pouring rain, where my boots have been completely soaked. I wrapped the sensor in plastic wrap before placing it in my boots to try to help it stay dry. Playing in deep puddles may explain the shorter battery life.

My biggest gripe with the sensor is the Adidas Micoach Manager software. In order to view your stats, you need to sync it with said software. Out of the past 8 months, I've had at least 2 major software issues - where I could not download the data from my speed sensor. I've lost data from about 4-6 matches, and I've had to wait 5-10 days for Adidas software updates so I can view my newest data. I've contacted Adidas MiCoach support 3 times, and they're friendly and responsive to my issues. Still, I feel that the MiCoach software updates should be tested more before being released to their customers. I feel like I'm helping debug the software for free. 70% of the time it syncs on the first attempt, 25% of the time I need to try multiple times, and 5% of the time it's completely frustrating/non-working.

product_title: Genuine Mazda Accessories 0000-8L-R02 Roof Rack
review_body:
Got this for our 2014 CX-5. The fit is exact, and is obviously a Mazda OEM part. One side of the bar is adjustable, to fit different Mazda roof rail widths. However, I'm concerned about the design of this product. The construction of the item is very good, even though there are some plastic parts, everything looks sturdy and well built. However, the way the bars are attached is very questionable in my opinion. What you do is slide one side of the bar into an exposed bolt head and rotate the bar down to the other bolt (which are the 4 screws you see in the picture). These screws are then inserted through the bar and screw down to the threads in the \\"receiver\\" which slides into the roof rails. However, the screw head supposedly doubles as a tie down (the head of the screw has a loop in it), but to me it looks like it's just plastic. I can't tell if there is a metal core to this very thin loop of plastic which forms the head of this screw (about 1/8\\" thick). But if it's just plastic, that's a terrible idea...to try and tie anything down and drive freeway speeds onto a plastic loop in the screw head. Even if it's metal, I say again it's VERY thin, and unless it's titanium or forged steel or something, this loop is very iffy IMO.

Also, when you do screw in the only screw that holds down the bar, it's very difficult to turn past a certain point. (Look at the picture, you can see the screw head design is circular (nothing to grip) and then there is only this small loop to grip to turn). The instructions say go until you hear a \\"click\\" but there is no clicking. Examining the parts, there is nothing to make a click, it's just a screw that threads into the receiver end. It also actually advises you to use a screwdriver to assist in turning the screw! Nice design, just have the user insert a sharp metal object into this screw head to turn it!. Several times I nearly scratched the crap out of our brand new car. Also, because of the proximity of the screw to the bar, it's very difficult to use the screwdriver to turn it. Afterward, I was not confident with how tight I could get the screw. When we decided to move the location of the bar, unscrewing it took minimal force. At freeway speeds and road vibrations, I'm very worried that this will unscrew on its own, causing the load attached to the bar to become unstable. We'll have to find out, but I am not happy with the design of this. There is only the one questionable screw on each side of the bar to hold it down. The other side just slides into a bolt head but is not permanently fixed. If the screw were to come loose, it's almost a certainty, by the design, that the bars will detach from the rails. In fact, once you loosen this screw just a bit, the entire bar can slide back and forth within the rail, as this screw also is the only thing to keep the bar from moving within the rail slots. There is WAY too much riding on this one small hard-to-tighten plastic head screw/bolt/tie down/retainer. There needs to be redundancy with things such as this for moving vehicles carrying loads, and this design sorely lacks redundancy.

They would briefly flash when I turned the switch from the OFF position to the Battery Load Test section, but not when I actually tested any batteries. After doing a web search, I found several comments stating that the fuse had blown, and found that to be the case with mine. This seems to be a common problem, judging by many of the reviews I have seen here. I purchased a package of 4 fuses from Radio Shack for about $4 and inserted one of them into the unit, which again blew after testing another few batteries. The third fuse is, so far, holding up but I'm glad I still have some spares available.
Update: According to the user manual, both of the Amps sections are fused for overload protection, so it appears that failure to follow correct procedures while using the Amps functions could result in a blown fuse, which apparently also renders the Battery Load Test LEDs inoperable.

product_title: Dorman 741-644 Cadillac/Chevrolet/GMC Front Driver Side Window Regulator with Motor
review_headline: Replacement was easy and fit well
review_body:
I ordered the regulator to replace the one in my 2001 Chevy Silverado passengers door. The part arrived just as promised by Amazon. Opening the box I found the regulator, a piece of paper with information type on it describing the possible changes from the OEM part. A small plastic bag with two nuts and a bolt in it. I removed the door panel. Taped the window and removed all the bolts. Removed the old regulator. Just as I figured the control cable had rusted and broken. I compared the new one to the OEM. On the bottom of the regulator where there was two bolts, there are welded studs on the new one.. Also, a support bracket mid way on the right side of the part is not present on the new one. It installed with ease. Studs lined up, all bolts lined up with no problems. Window clamps appeared to be the same as the OEM and tightened to the glass. Powered up and a few test runs all appeared to be fine. Time will tell.

The paper work explained the difference of the OEM and the replacement with pictures, its a copy, but readable.
I hope the missing support on the right side of the frame does not cause any problem later but time will tell. The paper work shows a picture and explains the missing point of contact.
If you want to review the removal/installation of the door regulator, there's lots of videos online to show you the proper way to repair your regulator.
The up/down speed appeared normal and non-labored
This is an easy repair for the mechanically challenged.
It took about an hour or so. Most of that was taking my time and removing the door panel, plastic and wire's and reinstalling them. Take your time and all will work out for this product.
The part was priced anywhere from $40.00 to $60.00 dollars cheaper then I found at Auto Zone or Advanced Auto. These are the two parts places around me.
I'll update if any problem with it, but so far so good...I HOPE to get years out of it.

Be a lot cheaper and easier than replacing valve seals if they're not too far gone. product_title: ATD Tools 7441 Underhoist Stand - 3/4 Ton Capacity
review_body: I purchased to of these for use in my home shop. The finish is nice, but the fitment was terrible. The stands fit together such that the base of the unit and the vertical shaft are two separate pieces. The vertical shaft is hollow and slides down over a nub or nipple on the base. There is a horizontal hole through both the base and she shaft which a bolt (supplied) is inserted to lock the two pieces together. Unfortunately, the outer diameter of the nub/nipple is not large enough to fit snuggly into the shaft, thus the shaft can rock back and forth. It's actually a joke how bad the fitment is, it's not even close. This is extremely unsafe, and should never be acceptable during the manufacturing process. I thought if I tightened the bolt enough, it would collapse the shaft enough to eliminate the rocking/wobbling. However, once I tried this, I ended up stripping the threads out of the weak grade bolt. I would have sent them back, but needed them for a time sensitive project. I ended up installing a Grade 8 bolt and nut, and welded the shaft to the base to prevent the unit from moving. They have worked fine for me since. I would imagine those that are purchasing these types of items would have the means to fix them, but it shouldn't be a requirement. I should have known the price was too good to be true.

product_title: Leather Honey Leather Conditioner, Best Leather Conditioner Since 1968. For Use on Leather Apparel, Furniture, Auto Interiors, Shoes, Bags and Accessories. Non-Toxic and Made in the USA!
review_body:
I have tried many other leather conditioners and this is by far the best product I have encountered.

It is much different than the milky, thin conditioners I have used in the past. The "honey" in the name is very appropriate for the consistency of the product. I used this on our large leather family room sectional and it has made an amazing immediately noticeable difference in both the couch's appearance and feel. I will use this product over and over!

A few side notes that are more operator error than product issue:

The product IS incredibly honey-like so it took a little bit before the small sponge I was using became saturated enough that it wasn't absorbing the product as much as it was spreading it on the couch. The bottle says "A little bit goes a long way", which I initially scoffed at based on the conditioners consistency. In my ignorance, I used quite a bit more of the product than I needed and, after 24 hours, the couch still had a clear, wet-looking shine to it. This was easily solved by taking a large towel and simply rubbing the excess off.

Again, that was operator error due to my experience with much, much thinner conditioners. I know better for next time. Just need to be patient with the process!

product_title: 3M 90100 Paint Defender System
review_headline: Not for the impatient or those who lack attention to detail...
review_body:
I live in the midwest and the product directions call for this project to be done when the temperature is above 65 degrees so I had to wait a couple of weeks until the weather was right for the application. After doing some extensive review of the instructions and reading all the comments on the system, I realized that I was definitely not up to the task at hand. I solicited help by bribing my son-in-law with dinner and a batch of brownies (not nearly sufficient in retrospect) to come over and do this with (for??) me.

My car is a 2010 Subaru Forester and it's in fantastic shape but I wanted to use this paint defender to protect the finish from dings and scratches on the front end of the car - the hood, front grill and mirror areas. The first task was to wash the car really well and to make sure that after it was dried that there were no dust or lint particles on the area that was being prepped for the coating. Doing it in the garage was the only choice, but I did worry that overspray was going to be an issue if it got onto all the other things I have stored in there! So definitely there is a LOT of preparation to doing this project and taking shortcuts or poor planning is going to give you more headache than joy.

After the washing came the taping and masking so that only the area to be sprayed was exposed. That was a lot more work than I bargained for, tedious really, but finally that was done to a degree of satisfaction. Then the coat with the synthetic wax protection has to be painstakingly applied. Ready for the spray -- terribly nervous. As suggested, a little spray of product somewhere besides on the car to make sure the spray was even and also to see how much was going to come out -- that does give valuable information. The amount of spray to actually use is going to be a judgement call. You don't want thick rivulets but yet it's hard to tell how thick the coating is going to be when you're actually doing it. Make your best guess -- you'll have to wait for the film to dry completely and then remove it if you mess it up, and maybe you won't have enough for a retry -- so that's going to be one of those factors that needs to be evaluated later. After the spraying, you wait. I didn't want to back the car out of the garage while drying as it was a windy day and I didn't want anything to stick to the film while it was curing so I left it inside overnight and hoped for the best. Then, in the morning, bravely and gently took off all the sheeting and kept my fingers crossed I wouldn't accidentally tear the coating while removing.

Well, it turned out OK. Not as smooth as I'd like and the closer you look, the less professional the job appears. I do think that having put it on that part of the car will help prevent the damage sustained by following salt and sand trucks in the winter and from fine gravel. Only time will tell how long it lasts and how the coating fares when going through the automatic car wash, etc. It's definitely an alternative to a more expensive shop done job, but I won't be wanting to do it again anytime soon. I can't say enough how much time and effort the prep needs to take, and if you get the least bit impatient or take short cuts, you're likely to have a mess on your hands. I was glad I had someone who would do this for me as I'd never attempt it myself -- that spray goes wherever there is no masking.

product_title: 1200 Peak Amp Power Source Kit
review_body:
I bought this unit to insure that a car I keep in storage would be ready to go when I wanted it. I figured that as beefy as this unit is, the air compressor would be sufficient for inflating four tires. Wrong. It gets to tire #3 and dies, I think from a thermal shutoff because the battery shows a good amount of charge (80+%) remaining. Contrast this with a friend's cheap Peak unit, which will do all four tires and keep going, and this unit seems to be a bit of a rip off.

Beyond that, there are multiple switches up front that aren't labeled. I wound up remedying that myself so I'd know which was the light, the inverter, and the jump start.

The unit may be okay for jump starting (which I haven't needed to do yet) but it's a bit weak in most other areas.

As an update, after using the unit for about the fourth time to inflate tires (which the unit shut itself off after two tires, as usual), the device will no longer accept a charge. Awaiting word from the manufacturer whether I'll be receiving a replacement or purchasing something more worthwhile.

I now have a 2006 KTM 450 EXC with a stock pipe, that could use a repacking, and new gaskets. Once the weather breaks, it will be nice to experience the improvements in drivability and performance one should expect fro mone of these FMF marvels.

Installation is simple, but it's tempting to mount the pipe without the spacers provided to obtain a closer fitment to the frame. Do not do this, and follow the instructions to the letter! Enjoy!

review_headline: Used this kit on a 2004 chevy impala 3.4l head gasket replacement
review_body: Used this kit to do a head gasket on my wife's 2004 chevy impala with the 3.4l V-6. Kit showed up on time and was half the price of was 150 dollars less on amazon then it was if the repair shop was to order it. If your doing a head gasket you will use almost every part of this kit. Only bad part is there are no instrustions with it except for the spot where you use a tiny tube of RTV (provided with the kit) to seal the heads to the lower intake manifold. But if your doing a head gasket yourself you should have enough smarts to figure out where everything goes. Only gaskets I didn't use was the valve spring replacement guides because I never removed them, even when I brought the heads into be machined, a thermostat gasket that looked like it came off a 350 small block and a few o rings. The only questions I wasn't %100 percent sure on was which side down for the head gaskets but I took my time and made my best educated guess based on how the factory ones came off because they are not labled "this side down". The other bad part of this kit was the O rings that came with it. They all just came in an unlabeled bag. Again I had to use my best judjment on which one went where. Replacing them on the fuel injectors was a bit of an issue because there are 2 per injector and they are different sizes. When reinstalling then injectors be SURE to get them as clean as possable and use some kind of O ring silicone to seal them up because mine leaked. Other then that pretty easy , very good quality kit and I would only use this high quality kit to do this job. Hope this helps

review_body:
I got these (4) to light up some pathways at night while trying to be ecologically sensitive.

All was good for several months then I noticed one was not working. Since I'd ordered a few extras, I replace it. Then a few more went out after another month or two so I dis-assembled one of them and tested the battery - it was bad. Same with all the other failing units. Upon closure inspection, the housing was beginning to weather quite a bit.

I guess the weather here in Texas was too much for these units. This gets to the challenge with solar - reliably storing the energy. Batteries and heat are not the best of companions. The plastic around the aluminum housing didn't fare much better. Note, I've had quality outdoor lighting for many, many years and these are the first units where the weather has degraded their quality so quickly.

The concept is great - low profile solar lightening where you need it - but this product doesn't quite measure up.

review_headline: Not a Good fit for TJ wrangler tail lights.
review_body:

When stop light/ turn signal are activated, there is not much difference between parking light and stop/turn signal brightness. That is not desired effect, you want as much brightness difference in my opinion. Overall bulbs are good but not for this application where you have a single light handling parking light/stop/turn signal duties. Perhaps reverse lights are a good match for this bulb.

Update 2/20/14;
I was contacted by the vendor, Speed Shop, they appear to be interested in more feedback, that speaks well of the vendor reaching out to customers. The item was shipped promptly and arrived in good condition, getting that out of the way; Here is the main issue with the product. It does not list the lumens in the low and high output, the bulb is bright, but with little difference between the two outputs. Here a real life scenario, as I tested one bulb in a typical OEM Jeep Wrangler tailight, I had the parking light on and turn signal on, I hardly could tell the blinker was on, there is what appears a faint difference. This is not a fast blinker issue, faulty wiring, low voltage, etc., my Jeep is equipped with the appropriate LED flasher unit. Look, it is not the vendor's fault for this bulb, the product advertisement should list the lumens rating and difference between the two outputs, or include a warning on the two outputs. I'm not sure if the other vendors would list them either. So buyer beware.

product_title: Nauticus PT9510-60 Smart Tab
review_headline: For the money the best thing I have ever put on my boat
review_body:
I never give 5 stars for anything but these deserve it. I have a 17' aluminum river boat that has some bad habits. It has what they call a delta pad. They have never been known for being really smooth on the water because they are supposed to run shallow. My problem is with two motors on back and a 30 gallon fuel tank it can tend to porpoise when you are running fast or in slightly rough water unless I keep the motor trimmed way down. Also because the boat itself is pretty light I really have to watch where I store things as it will tend to list to one side under power.

I took about an hour to put these one my boat mostly because I have a kicker motor I had to figure out a way around. I also had to drill slightly larger holes than the instructions called for an aluminum boat. I am guessing that because my boat is heavy gauge that there was less stretch in the hole. I ended up breaking one(They are #14 SS 3/4") and had to get a new one at Lowes.

I run my boat a lot and have tested lots of different props. I know pretty much exactly what it will run and how it operates on different conditions. When I put the boat in the river for the first time after the Smart Tabs the first thing I noticed was just how much better the boat came up on plane. Almost like someone was lifting it up flat with almost no bow rise. Touch the throttle and you were plane. I could also stay on plane at much lower speeds.

Next I had read some bad reviews because of turning. I made some really aggressive high speed turns and everything was great. Having the flat bottom the boat will sometimes slide out but this seemed to hold its line even better than before.

Finally I went out to find some rougher water and see just how fast it would go now. On the speed I half expected to lose some. In the end I was almost exactly the same top end. Where the boat is so much faster is acceleration and not having to slow down as much when you hit awake or slightly rougher water. I am also able to trim up my motor higher and keep it there. I am now able to run max RPM's and may put my higher pitched prop back on. If I do that I will actually gain some top end. I also might put in slightly less downforce the next time I go out and see how that works.

The only downside for me is I do sometimes run a jet lower unit on my boat and I will have to move these out of the way. They would get beat up in the river bouncing off of rocks. If you often beach your boat, as I often do, you need to be aware of how they are hanging down so you don't tear them off. I don't really know just how well they will hold up but even if I had to replace parts every couple of years it would be a bargain.

It would be hard to explain just how happy I have been so far with these. I took a 50 mile round trip down the river yesterday and could not wipe the smile off my face. It took a good boat and made it a great one. I have plenty of power but I am sure these would work great for boats that are slightly underpowered or overloaded.

product_title: Safety Seal KAP30 30 String Pro Tire Repair Kit with Storage Case
review_headline: Safety Seal 30 String Pro Tire Repair Kit
review_body: I've carried this Safety Seal tire plug kit in my vehicle for many years and along with my little 12-volt air compressor it has saved my bacon countless times in addition to saving more hours of grief than I could ever explain from jacking vehicles, removing wheels and schlepping to and from the tire shop. I actually needed to use this plug kit again just a few days ago, for the first time in years, to fix a nail hole in my truck's tire. It was a little bit of a re-learning experience, which was a surprise since I used this kit what seemed like every other day for several years running, but within a few minutes it all came back to me. I've always bought the actual Safety Seal tire plugs and the one I recently installed was probably ten years old, but still like new because I always kept them stored in an airtight plastic Ziploc bag. The day I made the repair it was below freezing outside so I warmed the plug with a heat gun to soften it before threading onto the insertion tool and installing. I find that these plugs are generally easy to install, although you sometimes do need to a little forearm muscle, but I'm sure most people could handle it. Overall, even though it is more expensive than similar kits from other manufacturers, I think this plug kit was a very good value and feel that one should always be kept in every vehicle along with a 12-volt compressor.

I attempted to solder the connections directly to the board, but still ran into issues, likely due to the excessive heat which was built up within the resistor.

product_title: OE Replacement Toyota Sienna Van Driver Side Mirror Outside Rear View (Partslink Number TO1320128)
review_headline: Glass vibrates even on smooth highways. Wiring harness must be spliced.
review_body:
I have a 1999 Toyota Sienna XLE. Non-heated mirrors.
The new mirror looks almost identical to the OEM Toyota mirror.
Installation is straightforward except the wiring harness plug attached to the new mirror is much smaller than the original and has only three wires compared to four wires in the original wiring harness.
The plugs do NOT fit together.
To make installation of the wiring harness easier, I taped the new wiring harness to the old one to pull it through the door channel (using the existing \\"old\\" wire harness as a \\"fish tape\\") and then spliced the blue, purple and yellow wires from the new wiring harness to the blue, purple and yellow wires on the old wiring harness' plug.
If you are not comfortable doing electrical wire splices then maybe this replacement mirror is not for you.
The new mirror responds to the position controls perfectly!
I think the seller should have mentioned that the wiring harness may not fit all models.
The field of vision is much wider than the old mirror so this will take some getting used to.
Will update if anything changes over time.

Update January 19, 2014.

After driving on the highway, I find that the glass vibrates even on the smoothest road surface. Totally distracting, annoying and unacceptable. I have to
uninstall and return this mirror. Cannot live with the constant vibration and subsequent distraction of the view in the mirror.

review_headline: It's pretty much what you expect
review_body:
Guys,
I've been looking forward to reviewing this. Let me start by saying I'm a complete amateur. Never painted before. First, I used around 6 quarts to paint a fourth gen Nova. I used this much because I had to do a complete color change, door jams, under hood, trunk, etc. There is a lot more to paint that way. I practiced on the under side of the hood and trunk. Basically, it took me about 8 weeks of weekends and one or two nights during the weeks to finish my project. I had a lot of body work to do, so the time it took me was pretty long because of the body work, my day job, and the fact that it was my first time painting. The second time will be easier, but make sure you block out a LOT of time and like they say, TAKE YOUR TIME.

As far as the paint goes, I knew from the reviews that lacquer isn't the best option for durability. For me, the car will be in a garage, so it's less of a concern. The paint was fine, it looks GREAT, and it was easy to work with. It was almost impossible as an amateur to get the technique right... so for me, it was important to have an easy to use paint for my first time. If I had tried to use a premium urethane, I think it would look horrible, and I would have wasted a lot of money. All in, I think it cost around $400 by the time I factor in primer, paper, masks, tapes, plastic (hanging up in the garage, and for the car itself), propane to keep the garage warm, fans... basically everything I spent to make it work. The last subject will be the paint fumes. It was a challenge to deal with the vapor as my garage is attached to my house. If your lady is queasy about smelling paint, or if you have kids... you may want to make sure you can do the spraying times when they won't be around for the day. Lastly, I had some inevitable problems with the gun getting clogged and shooting drops onto the paint job. This just seemed to happen at random times no matter how careful I was. I'd disassemble and clean the gun, and it would shoot drops onto the paint randomly. I think that part of learning is being ready to see or hear when the gun is starting to clog and stopping before you shoot drops onto your paint job. All together, I really like the results, but there were predictable challenges and mistakes. Even though the paint job isn't perfect, I did it myself, and the mistakes are mine. It was an awesome learning process that makes me respect professional painters even more. I think this is a great product for your first paint job. Good luck guys!

review_body:
I bought an 18\\" Walkstool Comfort many years ago and quite frankly beat the hell out of it. I used it camping, as a quickee seat while working on my car, at fairgrounds ... wherever I could pull out a comfortable seat out of nowhere. Its come in handy about a million times and the ease of stuffing it in a backpack or whatever contributes greatly to its utility.

Can't say enough good things about it... and like any well-used tool, it eventually wore out. After about 8 years one of the legs broke. Realistically I could have probably fixed it as the rest of it was fine (mostly) just that one leg was actually broken and they sell parts on the manufacturer's web site. If it wasn't for the fact I weigh 265 lbs I expect the product would have lasted even longer

So now I have a 22\\" Walkstool Comfort, just delivered by Amazon Prime today. I'll make a couple of quick observations and comment a little further on my poor dead 18\\" model and how you might make it last forever.

The 22\\" model is surprisingly large. I can't imagine someone using the 30\\" model but hey there are some really tall people out there. Best way to understand the height of these things is to measure where your office desk chair's seat comes up to. It turns out mine is 20\\", and I sort of wished I had thought of that before buying. While the 22 is perfectly comfortable as a full size seat, the 18 was perhaps a better working size: You are 4 inches closer to the toolbox you have sitting on the ground. Its also smaller, which is going to make it a bit easier to pack, although its pretty easy to carry around either way (they come with carry bags now which in my view is just something for you to have to remember to pick up... there's no need as the stool will stay closed up thanks to the sturdy strap that keeps it together.

As far as extended use goes, I did have an issue with my old one: Over many years the legs got stiff with respect to extending them. Further, to extend the legs you grasp the base of the leg and pull, and the rubber foot on the leg is what you use to gain purchase on the leg. Well, over the course of many uses and many years, those feet wear thru (the legs still bite just fine on the ground) and can come loose when you are pulling out a stiff leg. I always got the thing out but there were some cusswords needed to make it happen. I tried smearing a little grease on the leg and this was mostly effective, although a greasy leg can be problematic if you forget its on there. I used black lithium grease and I probably would have been better served using Mobil Aviation grease - the red stuff - which is impervious to the elements and very long-lived.

While my original didn't last forever, it did last a long time through very hard use. I'm glad I have another again.

product_title: ATP AT-205 Re-Seal Stops Leaks, 8 Ounce Bottle
review_headline: For power steering systems add 1/3 cup
review_body: The dealership told my wife they needed $1,200 to replace the rack because her 2005 Toyota Sienna has a very slow leak and a damaged rack boot. I replaced a damaged rack boot myself but want to stop the leak to keep the boot from being damaged by filling with power steering fluid. The 8 fluid oz bottle states to add 1/3 of it to the power steering system. Loosened clamp and removed the upper return hose from the reservoir and drained 4 ounces from it. Replaced hose and added 1/3 cup of Re-Seal followed by enough Dextron III AT fluid to reach cold fill line. This car takes AT fluid in the power system per the manual. Drove car for 5 minutes and then idled engine for 10. Will follow up with results.  4/10/2015 Followup 12 months later no leaks and have added no additional fluid. I also used this on a 1996 corolla that was leaking 8 oz every 4 days. Did a complete flush first. Added fresh fluid and 1/3 bottle at205. It leaked again 4 days later. Just topped off with 4 oz fluid didn't add any more at205. Has been leak free since for 3 weeks since. I suggest you always do a full flush if possible before adding the at205.

product_title: WARN 92100 ProVantage Plow Base/Push Tube Assembly
review_headline: If you're thinking about a ProVantage plow, READ THIS FIRST.
review_body:
Finding the right parts can be pretty confusing, so allow me to explain the ProVantage System.

The entire plow consists of four parts:

1. Vehicle-specific mount kit (One of many part numbers. Check [...] to find the one for your particular vehicle.)

2. Push tube assembly (P/N 92100 or 78100; depending on which type of mounting kit you use)

3. A Plow blade (P/N 78950, 78954, 78960, 80954, or 80960; two different styles (straight blade and tapered), three different widths (50\\", 54\\", 60\\")

4. Lift (usually a winch w/ roller fairlead. Alternatively, Warn P/N 84600 is a dedicated lifter)

For #1 and #2, there are two basic types: Center Mount and Front Mount.

Most vehicles have a center-mount kit available, many have a front-mount kit. If you have the front-mount kit available, I would recommend it, as it allows the plow to lift higher. I've found that it lifts high enough that I can reach over the front rack and turn the plow without leaving my ATV.

*** If you select a front mount kit, you need to select the front-mount push tube assembly, P/N 92100

*** If you select a center mount kit, you need to select the center-mount push tube assembly, P/N 78100

#3 is self explanatory, select from one of 5 blade options.

#4, If you're buying and installing a winch along with the rest of the components, make sure you read the instructions for the front mount. On mine, parts of the front mount kit replace a couple components on the winch mount kit, so right after you finish installing the winch mount, you've got to take it apart to install the plow mount. Because of this, I strongly recommend buying a WARN winch mount, regardless of what winch you put in it. Warn winch mounts should be compatible with Warn plow mounts.

Any decent ROLLER fairlead will work. DO NOT USE A HAWSE-STYLE FAIRLEAD. In addition to their regular fairleads (which will work acceptably) Warn sells a roller fairlead specifically designed for plowing, P/N 69373. This fairlead has a very large bottom roller to reduce the tightness of the bend and extend winch cable life. Warn also sells a 8' synthetic plow lift rope (P/N 68560) to save wear and tear on your regular winch cable.

I recommend a fast winch - you'll be raising and lowering dozens of times while plowing. Make sure you mount your winch control in a convenient location - you don't want to have to reach for it each time.

There are a few useful options available:

1. Power Pivot (P/N 79360) - Electric motor rotates the plow blade. If you're doing a lot of plowing, this might be useful.
2. Bucket Loader Conversion (P/N 83133, 84133, or 85133, depending on blade width) - converts a regular plow blade into a bucket loader for handling loose material (sand, gravel, topsoil, mulch, etc.)

There are a few hangups you'll have in certain situations. For instance, if you want to use an assembled plow on two different model ATVs, it may or may not work. The vehicle-specific mounting kit contains two \\"tabs\\" that bolt on to the push tube and allow it to quickly attach to the mount. The tabs for one model may or may not be the same height or spacing as tabs for another model.

If you're trying to have two plows for one ATV (one regular plow and one with the \\"bucket\\" conversion) you'll be missing a set of the aforementioned \\"tabs\\" for the second plow, and you'll need to contact WARN to obtain a second set. They've been sending them out for free, but contact them first to confirm.

Once you've got all the correct parts, assembly SHOULD be fairly straightforward. Unfortunately, you'll be reading from 3-5 different assembly manuals simultaneously, one for each of the parts you purchased, so it can be a little confusing. This is my only real gripe with the whole kit so far.

review_headline: Great Meter, good bang for the buck!
review_body: I was tempted to give this 4 stars instead of 5 simply due to the strong VO (Volatile Organics) odor when I first opened the package, (and for months afterwards).  However, I knew this would eventually dissipate, and it has.  I suspect that maybe it was the reason we got such a great little meter at such a great price!  I use this meter all over, in computers and electronics, household appliances, battery testing, continuity testing (yes, it does take that annoying second, but it does work!), automotive, you name it.  I have tested millivolts, milliamps, 1.5, 3, 9, 12 V, etc batteries, 110V household, even 220V on my pool pump.  It's told me what I need to know every time, and it is simply indispensable around here.  My old one was a piece of crap that I paid $35 for at AutoZone 10 years ago, that I was never sure I could trust, and finally chucked it and bought this little beauty.  Yeah, that strong organic smell was something else to start with, but I minimized my exposure to that (and my family's) and it's died down now, and I have a really great meter that I'm very very happy with.  The backlight is nice, the dial feels great and is easy to turn yet locks firmly onto it's setting, and both the meter face and the actual digital readout are all very easy to read.  The little stand on the back is very handy and also good and sturdy, and doesn't slide around on your work surface.  I'm very happy with this meter, and would not hesitate to buy another one, actually, it would definitely be my first choice.  Great deal, excellent quality, plug your nose for a few weeks and you'll end up with a really nice meter.

product_title: Nilight Driving Fog Light Off Road Led Lights Bar
review_headline: Great as long as you don't want to listen to your radio
review_body:
So as with all things you pay for what you get. These lights use the Cree LED's which are among the best LED's made. Unfortunately, the manufacturer of the whole system (NOT CREE) did not continue this with their circuitry. First a common misconception:

All LED's create interference or "noise".

This is not true the LED's themselves do not create any noise. The LED's driver circuit is what CAN create the "noise", I say CAN because a properly designed circuit is designed to eliminate any noise caused by the driving circuit. These circuits use more expensive components and are why some LED lights are more expensive than others. Although just because they are more money doesn't mean they are designed well either.

That is why I rated these lights as 2 stars, I don't "hate" them but I do not like them as they are. They are Super bright as expected, I can barely tell my headlights are not on when these are. If you are looking to purchase LED lights and do not know how to modify them and like to listen to the radio DO NOT purchase these. I can sit in my Jeep and be listening to a perfectly clear radio, when I switch these on I get pure static. And yes I have everything properly grounded.

product_title: Spectre Performance HPR8038 Air Filter
review_body:
I was skeptical at first to give the Spectre brand a go over the more known names like K&N or Airaid. Unfortunately, price was a huge factor as this was at the end of my tune-up of my 1996 Chevrolet 305 C1500 p/u and it's an easily changed product if it turned out I didn't like it.

Spectre has a long history in producing high quality products, this was something I was not aware of before researching the company. They even hold the land speed record of 415 M.P.H. at the Salt Flats using dual ram Spectre Air Filters about an inch from the ground bolted to a modified Cadillac engine. Definitely worth a google to see that thing run and get a look at their engine set-up.

HP Gains: Wasn't planning on any gains and while I do feel quicker throttle response I have not dyno'd this machine since dropping in the Spectre. Feels great tho and when it comes down to it, that's all that matters.

MPG Gains: Was just dropped in and have not ran an entire tank while using this yet, will update when I calculate, but I would wager a modest 1 to 2 MPG gain overall, if I can keep my foot out of it.

Longevity: Life-long product. Clean it every so often and recharge the oil per manufacturer specifications and it will last forever.

Price: Pay an initial $30 and NEVER buy another air filter ever again. Keep an oil recharge kit ($20) on hand and recharge it per instructions. Huge bonus considering a standard paper filter would have cost me as much if not a few dollars more and only last maybe 6 months where I live, if I am lucky.

Ease of Installation: Can't be any easier if it were done for you. Open the air-box, take out the old filter and drop kick it as far as possible before sliding this one on and tightening down the included clamp to ensure a snug fit.

If you are on the fence about buying a "permanent" air filter and aren't ready to drop upwards of $100 on an initial investment then buy this little $30 entry level filter and run it for about a year. If you are comfortable with the cleaning and re-oiling of a permanent air filter like these and want to upgrade from there you still can and don't lose any of the $30 invested initially. Don't believe all that you read by any of these companies claiming to rocket you to the moon with their filters, just won't happen. This is a modestly priced upgrade for a modestly expected increase in throttle response and MPG, which now days a 1 to 2 MPG increase is worth it's weight.

However, if you already know that you want to replace your entire air-box setup with an aftermarket air intake I would suggest trying the Spectre Air Intake Kit instead. Roughly costs around $160 and replaces a lot of heavy equipment under your hood for a much lighter product that just looks beautiful when installed correctly.

Other thoughts: Ensure that you're intake system is directing outside cold air to either the stock box or custom box and if it isn't you will want to invest in some additional hardware (very cheap) that Lowe's sells. Run a ram air line from the front bumper into the air box, be sure and screen off any openings to keep out critters and debris, and your car/truck will thank you for being able to breath again.

Deranged

product_title: Motorcraft FL820S Silicone Valve Oil Filter
review_headline: Would use this over most replacement filters
review_body:
This OEM oil filter is every bit as good as a large majority of more expensive filters. The only filter I would have chosen over this one for my Mustang was the Ford Racing filter which has substantially more surface area. Since I couldn't get one of those shipped quick enough, this was my second choice. These filters should be more than sufficient for most people's use.

When you read about these filters, you'll likely run into the thread-end bypass vs dome-end bypass debate. These filters employ a thread-end bypass while aftermarkets (like Fram, for example) use a dome-end bypass. It's claimed that the dome-end bypass can backwash over the dirty filter media in bypass, and that the thread-end bypass helps prevent this. In my research, I was unable to find much solid evidence supporting either on being substantially better, but with how well this OEM filter performs on top of the fact that it's thread-end bypass and cheaper than nearly all aftermarkets, I'd stick with this.

The reason I would have preferred the Ford Racing filter is the drastically increased filter surface area (and it does employ the same thread-end bypass). I swapped my car over to synthetic with this last oil change. I'm planning on running it for a short 2000-3000 mi run and swapping it again to clean it out, but when I replace it I'll likely go with 25k mile Amsoil. Now I have a hard time trusting the oil for a full 25k, but 10-15k feels fairly safe, and to do so I'd want an increased filter area, or to swap an OEM Motorcraft filter halfway or so. In my opinion, any other filter is mostly pointless.

product_title: Slime 40022 12-Volt Digital Tire Inflator
review_headline: Way better than the last one that I bought
review_body:
I bought a cheap generic unit at Harbor Freight for about $12 a few months ago. I paid about $25 for this one after doing more research since the Harbor Freight one was so terrible. Compared to that piece of junk, here how the Slime 40022 compares:

* Speed: The slime topped off my tires from about 28 to 33 in less than a minute or two. The cheap cheap I have takes somewhere between 5 to 10 minutes to inflate about 3 pounds.

* Noise: I understand that people would like machines to be completely silent, but I don't see how anyone could complain about the noise on this thing. The cheap unit I have is atleast 3 times louder and vibrates itself across several feet in large circles. The Slime moves less than 6 inches for me since it vibrates so much less.

* Cord length: The power cord has plenty of length for all 4 tires on my truck. The air line has plenty of length to reach the valve even when it is at the top of the 20" rims. For comparison, the cheaper unit would be dangling in the air if the valve happened to be away from the ground so sometimes I'd have to move the truck a few inches until the valve stopped close to the ground.

* Size and storage: The slime is about twice the size of the cheap unit, but still very compact. Much of the extra size is due to the built in storage for the cord and hose which prevents clutter in the trunk or under the seat.

* Accuracy: Digital pressure gauge provides readings to 0.5 PSI. This seems to be accurate compared to my high quality digital tire gauge when I run measurements before filling. Perhaps the reason some reviews complain about the accuracy is because the Slime runs for a bit after it reaches the target pressure. So when I set it to 33 psi, it keeps running for a bit before it stops and my tire gauge shows 34 psi. It is possible that the Slime fills it to 33.5 which might be rounded to 34 by the tire gauge, so perhaps they are both right within some margin of error. Either way, the cheap inflator had an analog dial that went from 0 to 200 and it was not possible to distinguish between 28 psi or 35psi. That terrible analog dial and the time to inflate just a few pounds was the reason I went looking for a new inflator.

Valve Connection: As other reviewers mention, this has a twist style connection instead of the usual flip style and comes with a couple of adapters. I've never used the twist style connection before, but I really like it so far. As others feared, I also thought I would have more leakage while twisting, but it turns out that I get much less leakage and it is much easier to put on and remove since you don't have to use any force to push it onto the valve like the flip style connectors (still, nothing is as bad as those gas station ones that require pushing the entire time).

product_title: Tobacco Pipe Lighter and Czech Tool - All in One
review_headline: How do you get fuel into these darn things?
review_body:
It arrived quickly, in very nice packaging, it's much prettier in-person than in the pic, and I looked forward to finally not adding to landfill with plastic disposable lighters. I bought the fuel, and set about filling it. And there, the nice experience ended.

I soaked my hands and lap and table with fuel, but never got any into the lighter. Well, some went into the lighter, but not into the fuel chamber. So, clicking it just set the fuel all over the mechanism and the outside of the lighter on fire. Not a pleasant experience.

As I kept clicking, hoping to burn off that fuel and hoping there was at least some inside that would light properly, the clicker got stuck. Uh oh. Kept clicking, it went back into place. Then got stuck again.

Never mind. Packed it right up, clicked away to authorize a return, and away it went. I need to just stop smoking to spare the landfill, I guess. Sigh. Maybe you'll have just the right size screw driver (tiny but strong, and should be included!) to make it take fuel into the chamber, and not all over the pretty thing. Maybe you'll be able to click it for years and get a perfect flame. I failed.

I really like this tool and Amazon has it for about half the price as the local parts stores.

review_body: I bought this for a 1995 Civic VX hatchback. It is essentially identical to the original radiator it replaced, which developed a leak along the seam where the aluminum and the plastic meet at the top. (It held on for 18 years or so, which is not bad.) Anyway, no issues with fitment in the car, but the OEM Honda radiator cap is not a direct fit. The TYC unit came with a cap, but I don't trust it -- after installing the radiator with the included cap, I went for a test drive and found a bit of steam escaping from the cap. In order to make the OEM cap fit, I did some filing on the plastic of the radiator at the neck and finally got it on there. About a week later, it seems to be holding pressure just fine, with no evidence of leaks. However, I would love to find an aftermarket radiator for this car that isn't necessarily designed for racing/tuner applications (with the associated price tag) and accepts the original Honda cap (part no. 19045-P08-014). Any feedback or suggestions would be much appreciated.

product_title: License Plate Frame Torx Locking Security Bolts & Chrome Snap Caps - includes 3 fastener sizes to fit all vehicles
review_body: OK, so these "theft proof" screws are hex-head, with a washer, and then you pop a plastic chrome-colored cover on to the washer, over the hex-head screw. Not theft proof, but definitely a deterrent. There will be easier plates to steal all up and down the block rather  than sit there and fuss with mine. review_body: I purchased this heater with the hope that the low ratings were from people who needed a larger heater. I quickly learned this wasn't the case. I installed the heater in my 06 Dodge Ram using heavy 8 awg wiring, which was rated up to 300vdc. The power wires were ran directly to the battery and I also installed an in-line fuse block, which was used just for protecting the heater and my wiring. I will say that the heater worked great for the first 3-days! On the 3'rd day, while driving to work, smoke started pouring out of the heater. Luckily I was able to pull off of the highway before it caught fire. To my astonishment, neither of the fuses blew!!! The heater just burned from the inside and is now trash. I guess if 3-days of heat is worth what you are going to pay for this heater, then by all means grab one quickly! I only gave this a 2-star rating instead on 1-star because for the 3-days that it did work, it actually put out good heat. For the record the heater was mounted to my dash with vilcro. There were no obstructions at all to block the airflow, so basically it just burned up on it's own. Thank the good Lord that I was able to pull over and throw it into the grass before my truck caught fire.

I feel I would've been better off getting a new pair of stock headlights, WAY less expensive and WAY better product. After all, buying light bulbs for the stock headlights is easy because everyone sells them, even Walmart. Although I haven't changed the light bulbs on these headlights yet, I'm expecting the light bulbs to be difficult to find and expensive as well.

These headlights are a complete joke. Don't waste your money on them and just get a pair of stock headlights, I assure you you'll be better off.
