product_title: Genuine Honda 08U45-TK8-100 Cargo Tray Liner for Select Odyssey Models
review_headline: 5-stars for what it does and what it is, 3-stars for value, 4-stars overall
review_body:
QUICK SUMMARY: My wife loves that she doesn't have to worry about grocery store items leaking or breaking and fouling the pristine carpet of the cargo space. We both love that the fit is perfect and you can store the 3rd row seats into the storage area AND reinstall the seating back again WITHOUT fussing with this liner. It stays put, and is easy to remove and clean.

BACKGROUND: We just got a 2013 Odyssey (close-out deal since 2014s have been out since summer). My wife loves having a new vehicle to drive, but she would ordinarily stress over getting the cargo area carpet soiled from stowing groceries or whatever in that storage space. Although maybe there are 3rd party items that do the same thing, it was worth it to me (barely) to spring for the Honda OEM liner, knowing that it will fit and function exactly as I'd expect.

WHAT I LIKE:

- Fits perfectly in the cargo area
- Easily removed for cleaning
- Protects the carpeted interior so it looks nice (important if you're going to privately sell your Odyssey)
- Storing the 3rd row seating into the cargo bay isn't impacted at all by having the liner installed
- It's nice that Honda hasn't changed the dimensions of the cargo area, so this liner works with all Odysseys 2011 and later (2011 is when the Odyssey was last redesigned)
- Notably, although it was delivered to us folded up, it almost immediately settled into cargo space once I installed it (while other reviewers have noted it took a few days for it to fit perfectly)

WHAT COULD BE BETTER:

- I'd have preferred the sides of the liner to rise higher than what it does, covering the entire sides of the indented cargo area
- The material itself seems a little too thin, and I'd think it would be pretty easy to get punctured if something pointy was carelessly stored in the storage bin
- Mostly, though, the price of this liner is far more than what you think you ought to pay. To me, it looks like it should cost between $20-$50, and not the nearly $100 price tag that it actually has.

CONCLUSION: You've just spent $30K+ on your new minivan. Spending an extra hundred to protect the storage bin area of your Odyssey is probably a sound investment, if only for the peace of mind you'll get by having it. Recommended.o me, it looks like it should cost between $20-$50, and not the nearly $100 price tag that it actually has.

CONCLUSION: You've just spent $30K+ on your new minivan. Spending an extra hundred to protect the storage bin area of your Odyssey is probably a sound investment, if only for the peace of mind you'll get by having it. Recommended.

I used the AGT 168 LEDs which I found from SpeedShop here on Amazon and they look great with their light - and will likely never burn out!  UPDATE 10/15/15:  I'm changing my rating. I had the right side burn out after about two years. They were great, so 2 yr life span not a huge deal considering the price. I'm changing my rating because the 4300k replacement set I received is a completely different color than the 4300k ones I ordered before. The new ones are distinctly more warm/yellow, I'd call it more like 3000k. Not too happy considering what a pain it is to get these installed. I slid the circuit board in the new case and then slid in the battery - the whole process was quite easy.
Then I tested it - the buttons were MUCH stiffer than the origional unit really hard to push. I then looked at the other two cases I had purchased and found that the individual buttons on each varied in stiffness - I selected the one that the two buttons I use the most were the least stiff of the three sacrificing the fact the trunk button on this case was REALLY stiff. product_title: Cobra Fi2000 PowrPro Tuner Digital Fuel Processor for Harley Davidson 2010-13 F
review_body:
If you haven't figured it out already, Amazon's automotive "parts finder" is a little... Off... So it's best to Check Cobra's website for bike fitment, and then shop Amazon using the Part Number Cobra provides for your bike on it's website..

Okay.. That said.. To the meat of it..

I installed the Cobra Fi2000 PowrPro Tuner (Auto Tune) 92-1615AT on my Aero at the same time I installed a new Cobra exhaust and new Cobra PowerFlo air filter on my bike - all this to help maximize performance... As-you-do :o)

First thing.. Once the unit is installed - I turned on the ignition, and the light blinked.. and blinked.. and blinked, and blinked, and never set up solid red (like it was supposed to).. I Started the bike with the light blinking.. seemed to run okay... A call to Cobra informed me that this can happen and it's no big deal..

Well...Okay..

I live up in the mountains of North East Arizona, so, after a quick "check to see if things were running okay" I took a quick 120 mile trip down the hill to Phoenix...

Just to reiterate, I had installed more exhaust, and more air than the stock setup and the Fi2000 PowerPro was purchased to take care of as much fuel as my new setup could handle..

Logic dictates that All of this "More".. Should result in an across the board and "stable" performance increase..

It didn't..

It seems as though I do get Much smoother power and better acceleration at around town speeds.. SO Much Better..

But at higher and interstate speeds, I either see MASSIVE Performance Gains, Or Lack of Power to even make it 55mph up a hill without dropping a gear.. (on the same stretch of road).. And I see these performance fluctuations every trip.

Something else I have noticed.. When there does seem to be a lack of power, the engine seems to act like it's burn is off - like it's drowning in gas or getting way too muchair.. It feels like it's "flooding"...

Keeping that in mind - At the same time I installed this unit - I also installed a "cobra classic slashcut deluxe exhaust"... Being a brand new exhaust, everything is shiny on it, including the tips.. Over time you can expect to see black exhaust (carbon buildup) (which is normal) on the slashcut exhaust tips...

One of the first things I noticed was that This buildup is occurring at an uneven rate, the exhaust tip leading from my front cylinder is Black with heavy carbon buildup, the exhaust tip from the back cylinder is almost new-looking "clean".. It's almost like one cylinder is producing more emissions than the other..

There also seems to be an occasional increase in engine vibration, like something is not "synching".. This happens occasionally during any trip and usually as it struggles through whatever is causing lower performance power fluctuations..

As I see it.. This unit has one very bad flaw, but that flaw is also it's selling point... And that is, that It reprograms itself every-time you start your bike.. This is bad because it has to learn fuel delivery every single time you start your bike, at all speeds, at all power demands, and at 80 times a second - WITHOUT FAIL.. It doesn't read your bike's performance and then tweak it a little over time to get the best possible performance to create a modified and consistent fuel map.. And this seems to be the issue..

Because Performance with this unit is Not ALWAYS as expected..Performance fluctuates.

Since installing this unit Gas consumption has varied up-to 14MPG running the same stretch of road.. I can either get a max 62MPG or closer to 48MPG.. I ride consistently - there shouldn't be that kind of variation..

Having said all that.. Overall.. This unit IS Capable of providing Much More Power with the new setup than my old.. It just isn't doing it consistently..

For safety's sake, consistency from your engine on a motorbike is Exceptionally Important.. So, For Safety's sake, I'm going to be replacing this unit with a power commander and get my bike dyno tuned by somebody who really knows what they are doing.

These are stainless steel not aluminum(i have seen some sites saying aluminum, not sure why). YOU MAY NEED TO PURCHASE 2 ACCESSORY HARNESSES FROM THE DEALER. Part no. 999q9-ay000 is what you will need to connect to the car(1 for each side, $10 ea.), unless you already have another accessory light installed, such as ground lights or the foot well mood lights, in that case there is already a harness there and you just tap into that. This info is in the instructions but just pointing it out before you tear you car apart and then need parts. Good luck and have fun installing, I know I did and the little bit of trouble I had was well worth the outcome, and my car looks a bit more awesome!

product_title: Keep It Clean SS4500 Setting Saver Delux Battery Memory System
review_body:
It kept my car computer and radio from losing its settings...BUT be careful. Upon plugging the battery back in and stepping back into my car, I smelled something strange...the 9v battery attached to it was smoking! Yanked this out and threw it as far from the car as I could. The 9v (an Energizer, not the cheapo special that this comes with) was still smoking and fizzling electrolyte for a good 10 minutes afterwards.
Since the smoking didn't start happening until after I plugged the car battery back in, I suspect that a diode was either not placed into this device (which would have prevented current from flowing back into the battery and causing the fun scare), or said diode had failed in a way that allowed current to flow back into the 9v battery. There was also nothing powered on that could have caused too much current to be pulled from the device, outside its intended purpose (car computer/radio memory).
Oddly, the device itself seemed unharmed by the incident, and thankfully there was no damage to the car, either; I'm sure it could have been worse had I not yanked it out immediately.

It doesn't appear that anyone else ran into this problem yet, and I likely did get a faulty unit. Regardless, though, BUYER BEWARE.

product_title: ELM327 WIFI OBD II Automotive Diagnostics Scanner for iPhone iPad iPod Touch
review_headline: Excellent tool for diagnosing and eliminating your "check engine" light.
review_body: Worked for me as promised.  As a Prime member, I received this item, as promised, within two days.  It arrived today and was incredibly easy to use.  I plugged it into my 2005 Toyota Corolla S and the red LED power light came right on.  I turned on my iPhone 5, went into settings, then WiFi, and there was the device showing up as an unlocked Wifi connection.  I simply tapped to connect, and my iPhone figured out the rest and connected me immediately.  I then downloaded and installed the $9.99 app "OBD Fusion" from the Apple App store.  I started the app right after the download and install.  The software found the device using the "automatic" protocol once I tapped the "connect" button.  I then ran some diagnostics on my car while it was running, then saved  a copy to my iPhone using the software.  It showed me the problem or why my check engine light was on.  Once I turned off my car, I was then able to use the software to clear the code.  The whole thing from start to finish took 15 minutes.  I am going to wait and see if the light comes back on over time, as the code indicated a problem that I had recently repaired, but the light stayed lit nevertheless.  If the light comes back on, I am confident that using this device and OBD Fusion again will reveal the cause of the trouble and allow me to address the problem myself saving me a lot of money.  I would have given the product a full 5 stars, but the hokey little (mini) CD that came with the device was the only source of any documentation whatsoever, and also contained an outdated app file.  The documentation did include a brief pictorial on how to manually connect with the device, but was unneeded as my iPhone configured itself correctly without the need for any manual intervention on my part.  A simple piece of paper describing how to connect both automatically and manually would have sufficed and been far more useful to me, especially since I recently began using a MacBook Pro laptop that doesn't even have a DVD/CD drive!  Luckily, I have other computers and an external drive that allowed me to access the files, but the mini CD was presumptuous at best by this seller.  Anyway, good device, works as advertised, and I also highly recommend the OBD Fusion app to use it with if you're going to try this with an iPhone.  It was a pleasant experience for me.  :-)

product_title: INTERFIL Fuel Filter
review_body:
Exact OEM replacement for a '93 Mazda MX-3. The filter isn't that easy to replace on this car, however, this filter is an exact match of the original part...including the small crimps on the filter that fit into the bracket.

The tips below assume average or better mechanical ability, and should only be attempted by someone qualified to make repairs or replacements of an automotive fuel system.

Disconnect the batter before attempting any fuel system work...this ensures the fuel pump is deactivated and no ignition or spark can be initiated through the car's electrical system.

TIP 1: The bracket on the firewall has two nuts fastening the bracket to another firewall mount...the bracket is held in place by threaded bolts that also have nuts exposed. The nuts on the bracket do not need to be removed, simply loosened to allow the bracket to be moved upward...each side has slots to hold the bracket in place. Once the filter/bracket is removed from the firewall, it is much simpler to undo the bracket band bolt and remove the filter hose clamps. Ensure you install the filter with the "out" side facing upwards (reverse of the label).

TIP 2: While you are replacing the filter, it's a good idea to blow out the fuel lines. The rear seat is easy to remove (release clips under each seat position hold the seat in place), and then the sound insulation can be removed. This exposes the fuel tank sending electrics and hoses. Remove the electric clip, remove the cover screws to expose the fuel hoses. Remove the fuel hose clamps. While the fuel filter is off, remove the return hose from the fuel rail. Have a partner slowly use compressed air to blow out the lines while you hold a waste canister and shop rag to catch the fuel (about 1/4 cup) in each line. Facing the rear of the car, the left hose is the return fuel line, the right hose is the filter line. Examine the fuel for debris...excess debris indicates a dirty tank.

product_title: Battery Tender Plus 021-0128, 1.25 Amp Battery Charger is a Smart Charger, it will Fully Charge and Maintain a Battery at Proper Storage Voltage without the Damaging Effects Caused by Trickle Chargers
review_headline: No more wondering if the truck will start
review_body:
We have a truck that is seldom driven. Over the last several years there have been occasions the battery was DOA when we tried to start it. Never knew when it was going to die. Didn't want to leave a trickle charger on it all of the time. After replacing the battery for the second time in too short of a time period I decided to try the Battery Tender. Very pleased with the results.
As I understand it, the Tender charges the battery to a full charge and then disconnects. When the battery requires additional charging it reconnects. As long as the green LED is on, all is well.
If for some reason the battery discharges even though the Tender is connected, the red LED will light. (I had this happen once when I left the key on and a fan motor running).
Also bought a Tender Jr. for the riding mower.
I now feel confident that the truck or mower will start any time I need it with out worrying about over charging the battery.

product_title: Actron CP9550 PocketScan Plus
review_headline: Huge problem with disconnecting terminal from OBD-II port: Blunder in Acron scanner terminal mechnical design
review_body:
Actron CP9550 suffers from the problem of great difficulty of disconnecting the female terminal of the device from OBD-II port on some cars, including Toyota models (Camry, Sienna, etc), Mitsubishi models (for example, Outlander), and possibly others.

This is a very serious problem for a tool designed for regular folks. Serious to the extent that I think that Actron is definitely negligent here: due to this problem you can damage you OBD-II port with repair costing more then the reader.

Here is how to solve this problem, which I researched after experiencing it on my car:

The female terminal of the Actron tool has a 5mm square cut hole about 3 mm behind the edge of the terminal. Outer edge of hole is lightly elevated but Acton committed a blunder by not making the inner edges of the hole round.

The idea of the hole is to engage a nub on the port to keep the terminal firmly in place (some advanced readers are used when driving a car), but the net result for this entry level device is completely opposite on the intention: it is so firmly attached to the car's terminal that it is almost impossible to detach. At least without reading this review ;-)

The best approach is to chisel the outer edge of the hole making it round before you connect the device. Or completely cut the retaining tab from the Acton connector so that now there is just a continuous \\"slot\\" instead of a rectangular hole. But if you got into this trap, don't panic: you can easily destroy you ODB-II port applying excessive force.

One simple way to detach the terminal it is to get a mirror, a good light and push a the screwdriver between Acron female terminal and the port while rocking the Acron terminal. You should not be in a hurry and as you improve the positioning of the screwdriver, your patience will be eventually rewarded. It will disengage.

Shame on you Actron from being so disrespectful of customers, as I have found theproblem clearly described in January 2011 review:

=== quote ===
The female terminal of the Actron tool has a 5/16\\" square cut-out about 1/8\\" behind the edge of the terminal. This engages a little nub on the car's male terminal when the tool's terminal slides over, so as to keep the tool's terminal firmly attached to the car's terminal. To release the tool's terminal, place your forefinger over the square hole and depress the nub while rocking the tool's terminal to and fro. The two easily separate. It is as simple as that.
=== end of quote ===

Here is another description of the attempt to release stuck terminal:

=== quote ===
I have a 99 Toyota and you are quite right about the Acton reader getting \\"stuck\\" in the car's port plug. I am too old to be scrunched upside down under the steering wheel and trying to release the catch clip with fingers or a small screwdriver! After I managed to free it with the screwdriver I cut the retaining tab from the Acton connector so that now there is just a continuous \\"slot\\" instead of a rectangular hole. Mechanical friction between the two connections keeps the reader attached well enough to do it's job.
=== end of quote ===

And if the person is not mechanically inclined, he/she can well destroy the ODB port:

=== quote ===

...Also if you have a car like a Toyota Sienna the port on the car will have a little nub that that will get stuck inside of the code reader's plug and there is no way of getting it out without wrestling the thing and using a slotted screwdriver to chisel it out. Then you end up scratching the code reader up and almost breaking you cars OBD port. We called the company and they said that it happens pretty often and that you pretty much have to break it to get it off. The Equus is designed so that it will not get stuck on the car.

=== end of quote ===

Again the simplest way to fix this problem is to chiselthe edge of the hole.

Other then that is a good, albeit overprice reader. The manual is well written and is not a translation form Chinese to English. They offer also some web site to help with diagnostic, which might be useful.

review_body: I've been researching wireless/bluetooth kits for my 2002 BMW M3 for almost a year. Wow, am I glad I did. This kit is amazing and does everything its supposed to. Installation took literally 20 minutes and most of that was spent wrestling my trunk liner away to expose the connectors needed for this unit. To be clear, this review is for the main unit and if you want bluetooth functionality you must buy the BT dongle as an add-on....but its worth it!  Once installed, my Galaxy S3 paired immediately with the car and within 10 seconds I was streaming music through my speakers. Steering wheel controls allow me to advance tracks. A very cool added bonus was that the steering wheel controls also work with Pandora and Spotify, something I did not expect!  Song titles, album names and artist names stream to my radio display ( although my head unit does not scroll, so most of the titles/ artist names get truncated; no big deal). The bluetooth kit also comes with a microphone for hands-free calling but I found that I do not need this. When I receive a call, I just put the caller on speaker using my phone and they can hear me perfectly. The caller's voice does come over the speakers.  All in all, a fantastic 21st century update for my ride that only cost me about $160.

They provide a lot better air flow then your stock/standard air filter that the factory provides.  With better air flow you get better gas mileage and horsepower.  It's not a huge increase, but it is a few points in each category, and with these gas prices anything can help.  The other huge benefit that I like is that it is a million mile filter, which means it will last forever.  You never have to replace you only have to clean it about twice a year, vs replacing your factory filter every 3-4 months.  They cost about the same.  I usually find my K&N filter between $40-50. The cleaning kit is about $20 and it will last for years.  I recommended these filters to many family and friends, and anyone who uses it loves it, and can tell/feel the difference.

product_title: DashMat Original Dashboard Cover Ford and Mercury
review_body:
I bought this to reduce the glare from the dash on the windshield. I guess Ford wasn't thinking when they built a car with a light beige dashboard - I certainly wasn't thinking when I bought it. In any event, the DashMat - which is basically a black piece of carpet cut to fit your dash - eliminates the glare. It comes with some fasteners to make it lay flat - I only needed to use them in a couple of places. The fit was pretty much exact and there's no curling or bulges - it lays about as flat as a piece of carpet on your dashboard can. Not the most attractive option, but it beat painting the dash and I've pretty much forgotten that its there. The only thing I've found is that it reduces the sensitivity of the headlight sensor so that my lights come on earlier in the evening. There's a cutout for the sensor, but I'm guessing just having the black rug around the sensor sides reduces the light going into it.

It does come rolled up in a tube, but mine was laying flat within a day or two.

Five stars for being exactly what I expected.

You have to use the key to open or close. No key, no close. Well, that's annoying. But worse - when you try to close the lid, it hits the latch. You have to hold the latch with one hand and move it to a middle position for the top to clear it. That's a two hand operation, and there is no reason for it to be this way. A simple plastic boss (a bump) would keep the latch clear of the top. So the design is flawed.

As a side note, I was at the American International Motorcycle Show and went to the Givi booth. As I am a product designer wanting to help, I explained the issue and offered a suggestion for a simple fix. I was told I was doing it wrong. I demonstrated the problem on a booth model. They said it was that way because it was tilted on the display. I challenged them to do it. They kept repeating it would work fine mounted on a bike. Frankly, I was astonished that they simply didn't care. So I think I'll be avoiding Givi products in the future.

Don't get me wrong - overall this is a good product with an annoying latch. If you are not the type to search for a better product, this one is pretty good. The base plate is solid, the product looks good and works well. But that latch is needlessly annoying because you can't hold a helmet in one hand and close it with the other hand. Minor, but annoying.

If you can take the time and effort, give Givi a pass and look elsewhere. I saw better models at the show by their competitors. Knowing what I know now, I wish I had not bought it. But it's not bad enough to throw away and get something different.... so far.

review_headline: Objects in photo are larger than they appear.
review_body:
These are solid Jack Stands and the photo doesn't do them justice. They are lightweight, robust and larger than you can discern from the description photo.

I unknowingly checked quantity 2 at check out, so I was a bit surprised when shipment arrived with 4 stands in one box. I was going to return a pair but after an easy assembly and since I was happy with the quality I decided to keep them.

I knew I wanted a pin style design vs the ratchet and these worked as designed. I've read several unwarranted comments about these Jack Stand on various forums which mostly stated they did't \\"appear\\" as robust as the 4 leg ratchet style stands, however none of the commentors actually owned or touched the stand. I am not a structural engineer and even if I was it would be impossible without controlled testing to say if these are inferior to its 4 legged counterpart. I do know the pin is found in the virtually all extreme heavy duty jack stands which is what I wanted to mimic.

I added some pics in the customer images section of this product which should help give a better perspective on the true size of these Jack Stands.

I don't think any product is perfect, nonetheless I am giving 5 *'s. Some reviewers deduct stars for the most insignificant things which I won't do here - although just one more link in the chain for the retaining pin would do wonders for inserting pin in highest position.

review_headline: Only last about 1 year, Amazon won't honor warranty
review_body:
It works, but only for about 1-1.5 years. Dorman has significantly changed the design of their window regulators in the past year. IMHO, much cheaper design and build quality, they have gone from riveted metal joins, to spot weld, the metal is noticeably thinner, and the motor is 1/2 the size. Yes, I know that none of these may affect quality or function, but if you have a Dorman regulator from 2+ years ago and compare it to a new one, you will instantly notice the build changes.

product_title: Dorman Jeep Grand Cherokee Window Regulator with Motor
review_headline: DOES NOT FIT JEEP GRAND CHEROKEE 2000 but here's how to make it fit
review_body:
IDIOT MANUFACTURER POSITIONED THE TOP RIGHT MOTOR BOLT TO USE THE CENTER BRACE BOLT HOLE.

What morons. Chinese obviously built this from schematic without realizing they were causing an unsolvable collision between the two points.

I am going back out to see if I can solve this problem by boring three new mount holes for the motor mount.

I hate lazy and incompetent engineers. SHAME ON AMAZON FOR NOT NOTICING ALL THE COMPLAINTS OF THIS VERY SINGLE FAILURE. THEY SHOULD PULL THEIR STOCK FROM THE MARKETPLACE.

Shame on me for seeing the first glowing reviews and failing to read deep enough in to observe the fit complaints. Maybe this is only a problem for the 2000 Jeep Grand Cherokee, but I assumed that all WJ series have identical stampings for replaceable components (an auto industry convention).

FOLLOW-UP: Made a cardstock template of Dorman's motor unit mount points and, using the WJ's top right factory mount hole in the door frame as the index point, bored two new lower mount holes, which will be about two inches below the factory lower mount holes. This approach keeps the motor within reasonable distance to the track frame and allows it to be positioned on the center door frame stile on the large flat central field. If you were to position it to the left, the right, higher or lower, the motor would have at least one mount hole off that flat central field.

Yes, my window now works fine, but NO STARS to Dorman, because of their product engineering failure.

Here's a YouTube video on replacing the regulator-motor (but with one that ACTUALLY FITS, so it is not a Dorman): [...]

Here's a YouTube video on removing and reinstalling the door panel: [...]

Both were useful to me. I used duct tape rather than painter's tape to support the window, passing it over a shop towel on top of the door frame to protect the paint. This leaves residue which needs to be scraped off,but I did not want to rely on weak blue painter's paper tape to support my window glass while I was working on the regulator-motor swap.

product_title: Ancra Red Gradual Release Big Bike Ratcheting Tie Down - Pair
review_body:
I have been riding and racing motorcycles since I was 7 years old, 31 years. When I was a teenager, I discovered Ancra straps, the original cambuckle tie down. Since then, tons of other brands and types have come out and I have owned most of them, some good and some are total junk. I have probably 30 Cam buckle type straps that I use in trucks, trailers, motorcycle lift tables, motorcycle jacks, at work hauling cargo, etc. This product, thier \\"Big Red Bike Tie Down\\" is a ratchet type strap, is fairly short which is great because you do not have a ton of extra strap to tie up, and are very heavy duty in a relatively small package. If you value whatever it is you are strapping down, ANCRA is the ONLY brand to use.

These Big Red Ratchet Straps are awesome. I originally bought these just to have a short set of ratchet straps available in my trailer for whatever. But I haul a Polaris Rzr 900XP 4 on a flat trailer a lot these days and was using a pair of these in the back to ratchet down, and a set of \\"cheap\\" ratchet straps in the front. It was actually a pain using the cheap, and long, other brand straps in the front because they just didn't feel as secure, and I had a ton of extra strap I had to wrap and tie up which took time every time I loaded the machine. So one day I am driving down the road and I feel and hear a \\"Boom\\". I slowed down, pulled over and looked around but did not see anything. When I got to the sand dunes and was unloading, I saw that the entire center of the cheap ratchet had blown out and the front of the Rzr was no longer secured in the front. I ordered a second set of these Ancra straps immediately and now I feel safe and secure, and I load faster. It is great of have a set of 4 of these around for everything I need. An investment that will serve you for years and years to come.

Again, these are fairly short - about 5 feet compared to longer cargo ratchet straps. They are \\"BIG BIKE\\" straps, not 20 foot long cargo straps, which for motorsports is awesome and exactly what you need, but if you are looking for the catch all 20 foot cargo strap, try something else. They are tough, strong and a quality product as I would expect from Ancra.

As I understand it, back in the day, Ancra came out with their first cambuckle straps to hold down small aircraft on the tarmac to keep them from blowing away in high winds. Being for the aircraft industry and holding down very expensive equipment in a small strap - they were obviously an awesome product. Then the motorsports industry discovered them and everything else that you ever used to secure a motorcycle became obsolete. Ancra is the one and only strap. And, they are no more expensive than any other strap you can buy. If the straps you are going to buy seem very inexpensive, think about it. Think about what you are trying to secure with that strap, think about what would happen if the strap broke as it did in my case when I did not use an ancra. Just buy the best and be done with it. You'll be glad you did.

product_title: ATV DROP REAR Cargo Carrier Basket Rack - UNIVERSAL
review_body:
The basket rack got here faster than I thought and that's the good part. It went together easy enough and fit on my ATV like it was suppose to so no problem there.
That's the end of the good news. It's junk. It broke the very first time I used it. I was taking my ground blind to set it up before rifle season opened and put it in the basket, one end was in the basket while the other end was sticking out over the top of the other end. The blind weights a total of just 17 lbs, there was nothing else in there. I'm 61 years old and my racing days are long over, all I did was drive from the farm house to where I was going to set the blind up. When I got there I saw the bottom of the rack had fallen out. The webbing is not welded on to any part of the frame, the ends of the webbing goes into a slot made of two pieces of metal that are then welded on to the frame. Just one end of the 17 lb blind caused the webbing to bend and pull free of the slots. That was Friday, Sunday when I was taking the blind back I put it in the other side and that bottom also fell out. Now I'm going to have it welded back on with some more support bars welded on the bottom.
It's no fault of the seller, it's a design problem. Ever if I had send it back and they send me another one it would still happen again. Any time the webbing is bend anywhere it will pull free. Sorry but it's not worth it.

You can get this right if you put the time into it and the pad is removable, so you could make a thinner pad.

product_title: Precision 510030 Wheel Bearing
review_body:
I've always been picky about bearings, since they are typically a pain to replace (remove front tires, brakes, pull knuckle, press old ones out, press new ones in, reassemble). For this reason, I try to stick with OEM or reputable brands, such as Timken, Koyo and such.

With that said, the price for these was very good, and after a bit of research I came to the conclusion that they were decent bearings (based on comments by people that had experience with them). So I bought two of these for the front of my Civic.

Unfortunately, the driver's side bearing failed in less than six months.
I don't want to rate it any lower than three (3) stars, since it *could* be a one time defect.

It has been, however, quite the inconvenience, since - as mentioned above - these are not as easy to install as - say - an air filter.

I wound up having to buy the Timken branded version, which cost almost twice as much.

BONUS: The Timkens I received were marked \\"Koyo\\", so turns out I am installing OEM bearings, after all.

product_title: Spectre Performance 9925 Air Intake Kit with Red hpR Filter for Ford F-150 5.4L
review_headline: POOR DESIGN DAMAGES MASS AIR FLOW SENSOR HARNESS!!!
review_body: I had this on my 2004 F-150 for about 1 year before I began having problems.  When I installed it, I noticed a tight fit between the Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor and the brake fluid reservoir.  I didn't think much of it at the time.  After 6 months, I got an engine code and went to a Ford dealer.  They told me my throttle body was bad, charged me $600, and replaced it.  About a year after putting it on, I kept getting a check engine light indicating "lean bank" 1 & 2.  This code refers to the O2 sensors.  Four different shops agreed it was not the O2 sensors.  After those visits and over $800 to have the fuel pump changed, the last shop finally recommended to put on the stock intake.  After putting it on... problem solved.  Check engine light gone. Six months later, a check engine light and "engine fail safe" mode.  Back to the dealer, who tells me for $950 they need to replace the MAF and the Throttle body again (after only 1 1/2 years).  I call foul and refuse the repair.  After a weekend in the driveway with my mechanic buddy, we find a loose wire in the MAF wiring harness on the side where it was rubbing the Brake Fluid reservoir.  We super glued the loose wire and everything has been fine.  I suspect when the throttle body was replaced the first time and the stock air filter was put back on, that the mechanic pushed the wire back into place without realizing it.  Bottom line, this air intake probably cost me over $2000 without me realizing it.  I sold used it for $40 online.  You get what you pay for.

product_title: Crack Eraser: Do It Yourself Windshield Chip and Long-Crack Repair Kit. Repair 60 chips and 10 long-cracks
review_headline: Here's why long cracks are problematical
review_body:
My goal was to fix a crack about 18 inches long in order to pass state inspection, and I failed. The longer a crack is, the wider it is at the old end, and when the crack reaches a certain width, dirt will start to enter. The age of the crack will also make a difference as to how much dirt gets into it. In my case, about half of the crack was still very evident after being filled. Perhaps first blowing out the crack with compressed air might help.

Two additional observations: 1) It was easier to use the device when pressing on the plunger without engaging the threads. Once the threads are engaged it is harder to feel what is going on. 2) The resin bottles are black, to keep out light, and it is difficult to tell how much resin is left in the bottle. I wasted quite a bit of resin for the first job (due to the learning curve) and if I started another job I would be concerned that I might run out of resin part way through.

product_title: Mobil 1 75W-90 Synthetic Gear Lube - 1 Quart
review_headline: This is a GL-5 oil; you may not want it for your older tranny!
review_body: Warning: this is a GL-5 oil. GL-5 is what most of you want...but, not everyone. If you are looking for a manual tranny oil, and the specs call for GL-4, this may not be what you want. I know the "company line" is that GL-5 is back compatible..but, that is just not always so.  For instance, Toyota calls for GL-4 or 5 in my 1996 Tacoma 5-speed. The truth is, it needs GL-4 to shift smoothly. Transmissions which are even older than my '96, like the old 4-speeds, clearly need to avoid GL-5 oils.  For applications which call for GL-4 or GL-4/5, I would get on line, find a dependable forum...and, ask users there what they are using.

product_title: K&N PS-1010 Pro Series Oil Filter
review_headline: Not as good as the HP series K&N
review_body:

The metal in the housing is thinner, its diameter is smaller, the flow-holes around the central mounting hole are smaller, and the width of the sealing gasket is not as wide. There is a sloppy amount of glue between the base plate and the outside housing. The term \\"contractor grade\\" came to mind as being a cheaper, barely functional product designed for a jobber, not the end-user with an eye on quality.

I've asked K&N to consider changing the wording of their product description to more accurately reflect the inferior quality of this filter compared to the HP-series.

Since I don't need the HP series \\"nut\\" on top of the filter, I thought I'd save a buck or two on a filter of equivalent quality otherwise. Poor economy.

-----------

UPDATE

I've received satisfactory responses from K&N staff in their marketing and in their consumer affairs departments. I identified myself as a longtime customer and expressed disappointment that the \\"PS\\" series failed to live up to expectations. product_title: INNOVA 3040 Diagnostic Scan Tool/Code Reader with Live Data for OBD2 Vehicles
review_body:
I didn' have a CEL , but my gas mileage seemed poor, so I wanted a scanner with the live data feature so I could see if my O2 & MAP sensors were changing. The 3040 verifies they are, at least over a 15sec refresh interval. An oscillscope would be required to tell if the sensors are\\"lazy\\" but at least I know the're (mostly)working.
The display is easy enough to read and has good backlighting. The live data is somewhat customizable. I was hoping to use the O2 sensor test feature but my car doesn't support that. The scanner only seems to show fuel trim as+/- percentages instead of L/hr.I was hoping to use that as a crude MPG gauge. It may just be my car's limitations or maybe I need to figure out how to read that. Other features may not be available to you depending on what your car supports.
The scanner seems well made & sturdy.
The cord is a little short as pointed out by other reviewers.
I could have gotten a bluetooth reader but fidgeting with a laptop in the car seems unwieldly.
I haven't updated or used the website features yet. There was no CD included as shown the picture. I guess you just download the software once you setup an acccount.
I did NOT want any \\"clone\\" grief, so the mfr rebate offer (for purchased from Amazon.com) was reassuring.
I highly recommend this tool. If you can live without live data ,then a less expensive tool is probably adequate.

product_title: Keeper 07208 Black Waterproof Hitch Rack Bag (11 Cubic Feet)
review_body:
1) You need to place the bag on the car first, and make sure the SEALED side (with no zipper) is at the FRONT of the car
2) You need to zipper it fully, and make sure the velcro is tight around the entire bag
3) For added peace of mind, use additional lashing straps - we used 2 - one going side to side, and one going front to back
4) Used on a dodge grand caravan sport minivan

okay on to my thoughts.... I am 5'1 and my daughter an inch shorter. It was 'fun' (insert sarcasm) trying to get this thing up, balanced, loaded, closed and secured on a minivan. But we did it. :) It comfortably held a VERY large suitcase (man that thing was a B getting up on the roof!), a smaller suitcase, duffel bag, and pillows comfortably, and could have fit more. We packed it the night before we left and it rained - and rained about half of our 8 hour trip doing 80 down the highway, including a 40 minute very rainy, uncovered ferry ride on rough water. No issues whatsoever. I would check it when we stopped, just to make sure the straps were still secure, and they always were. Nothing was wet in the bag when we got there. well, it got wet when we unpacked cause it was raining, but the bag had nothing to do with that LOL

The straps on the bag I found difficult to adjust. Difficult, not impossible. I did feel much better with the additional lashing straps I had on there, but I think it would have been okay without them, if done tightly and properly. You will hear noise if the straps are not secured - we used duct tape on the ends of the straps, and heard nothing.

If you put ANYTHING on top of the car, it will reduce your gas mileage. This is common sense and anyone who uses that as a basis for a negative review has issues or lacks common sense. I did not notice a significant difference in gas usage - we filled up at the same places we always do, and spent no more than usual on gas. I'm sure it was decreased (common sense) but as I said, as far as hitting my pocketbook, no noticeable difference.

Once we got to our destination, I did not remove the bag from the roof. I simply zipped it back up and used the lashing straps to hold it down. There's not a whole lot of driving anyways on a very small island, and I didn't want to wrestle having to adjust the straps on the bag itself and get it up and all that again. It worked for us.

Would I use it again?

Yes but I hope to not have to. I'm hoping to get a hard shell one for the next trip, but if I don't, yes, I would use this again and be confident in it.

4 stars because of the difficulty of adjusting the 'on bag' straps.as hitting my pocketbook, no noticeable difference.

product_title: ACDelco 88962315 GM Original Equipment Transfer Case Range Select Position Sensor
review_body:
Service 4wd light was on. I tried replacing the 4wd switch with [[ASIN:B009CCM6CC Dorman 901-072 Four Wheel Drive Switch]] but that did not resolve the issue. I then ran across reviews on the 4wd switch saying the range selector position sensor could also be the reason for the Service 4wd message. What do you know, it resolved my problem.

The install took about 2 hours, mainly because I had a few hiccups with removing the front driveline by myself. Because of the height of the stock truck, I only needed to crawl underneath. Removed the skid plate, front driveline and then the entire transfer case motor. After removing the 6 torx screws on the transfer case motor it opens up without a problem. Replace the range selector position sensor and remember to put gear back in the same place or you may have problems lining it up when re-installing the motor. I also opted to replace the [[ASIN:B0049OI3DE ACDelco 12384990 Transfer Case Four Wheel Drive Actuator Seal]] since I already had it open.

Not a difficult install for anyone halfway handy. And for 2 hours and $60 worth of products to replace, it sure beats a trip the 4 wheel drive shop.

product_title: MaxxHaul 70225 Trailer Dolly With 12" Pneumatic Tires - 600 Lb. Maximum Capacity
review_body:
I bought this dolly from Amazon in March to maneuver my double jet ski trailer and my 84\\" x 12' utility trailer around my driveway and in my garage. It helped to move the trailers to the very edge of the garage to provide the most room to park next to each trailer. Almost after the first use the triangular support frame bent towards one of the wheels. The dolly doesn't seem to have enough lateral support. Just recently one of the wheels began to wobble and finally broke free from the wheel hub - both the tack welds broke and the wheel is now loose from the hub. The dolly is completely unusable at this time. I now have to try to weld the wheel back to the hub and add some additional angle iron to bolster the triangular support structure.

Overall this would be an excellent product if it really held up to 600 lbs of force. It works to quickly maneuver trailers around tight spaces, but the lateral support is poor and my dolly broke after only a few months of use with relatively light trailers. I would not purchase this product again.

I always make certain that it's not my fault before I write a negative review of something, and it definitely was not my fault. This helmet leaks both noise and most-certainly leaks water. I really regret this purchase and I just had a defect. I am now stuck with a helmet that is potentially unsafe for me to ride with during even the lightest rain showers. ONE positive note, the flip down sun shade is nice. It really does block a lot of sun without me having to stop and swap in some shades. But overall, I absolutely do not recommend this helmet.

product_title: Monroe 40046 Specialty/Electronic Shock Absorber
review_headline: This is a high-end performance shock
review_body:
My car is a 02 Cadillac Eldorado (5,000 lbs plus), and I wanted to maintain the ELC, Electronic Leveling Control. The ELC is simply an onboard compressor that keeps the rear of my big car level, and riding fine. I am very picky about suspension, specifically the rear shocks/preload. It's more important than my 300hp Northstar 32 valve engine. What good is power, and 330 foot pounds of torque if you can't control the ride. Well, my past experience includes mostly the German Manufacturer, Sacks, BMW's OEM and Bilstein, one of the best aftermarket providers. Well, these shocks bolted into my Cadillac within 30 minutes each side. The top bolt had a some rust (nothing PB blaster won't over power) and one bolt down below. Literally 30 mins each side....and I'm the Forest Gump of mechanical skills. If your shop mechanic charges you anything over 50 bucks aside, then, your labor rate is way too high.

They eliminate any wheel hop, and ride the highways... nice and smooth. On the rural back roads, they are firm, but not harsh. If you are like me, needing excellent suspension without paying a thousand a shock, then, you will be feeling very satisfied with these luxury performance shocks. And Amazon's price is competitive. Enjoy your car...life is short. Get what you want, these shocks will not disappoint.
J.

product_title: RaceQuip 350 Series Black Single Layer Driving Gloves
review_headline: Great for high performance track driving
review_body:
I recently got into high performance driving clubs with my car. The first two times I took my car (to Pocono Raceway) had completely different weather conditions. The first time the weather started cool in the morning but quickly heated up by mid afternoon. This caused my hands to be quite sweaty. The second time I went, it poured rain for the first half of the day. On top of that, it was pretty cold. Having cold fingers while driving at speeds greater then 130 MPH isn't exactly 'fun'.

At first I wasn't sure if I should get single or dual layer gloves. Not really knowing how they would be different, I went ahead and bought the single layer gloves. They completely solve the cold/sweaty situation that I was having the first couple of times I went out. They're thick enough that they keep your hands warm, but don't seem to be too thick to retain heat. I believe it's the Nomex material that allows them to breath and prevent significant sweating. The leather palm provides excellent grip on the steering wheel. My car has a typical leather stitching steering wheel, but nothing really that fancy.

For those that take their car to the track on the weekends or a few times a year, I would highly recommend these gloves. It's just one less thing you have to worry about when you're driving at high speeds. This allowed my to put more focus on my technique and to be more comfortable.

review_headline: Starter would not fit, seller imposed restocking fee on returned part
review_body:
I ordered this starter motor for my Triumph TR6 only to find that it would not fit, even though it is stated that it is for that application on the sellers web site. When I returned it to the seller, Rare Electrical, they imposed a 20% restocking fee. Their rational was that it stated the model of starters that the part would replace, and my original starter was not listed. However, my confidence is very high that the starter that I ordered would not fit in any Triumph TR6 regardless of the year, or original starter motor. I know this because Triumph did not change the body of the TR6 throughout it's production so there would always be an interference problem.

I recommended to the customer service person at Rare Electrical that they check their information and remove the TR6 from the compatibility list so this doesn't happen to others in the future. Obviously Rare Electrical had the discretion to not impose the 20% restocking fee, but chose to do so. For this reason I cannot recommend that anyone purchase from them.

review_headline: Edit: Started fine, but not good for 2005 Hyundai Santa Fe
review_body:
I got a pair of these to replace the brake light bulbs on my '05 Hyundai Santa Fe. Excellent quality, bright, they work great! No hassles. The lifetime on LEDs should mean these are the last brake light bulbs the vehicle will need over it's lifetime.

In the future, I plan to replace any burnt out bulbs on the vehicle with LEDs, where possible. I may even do so proactively. It's nice to have one less thing to worry about.

Edit: Just after the end of the return window, the tail lights on both sides stopped working. The brake lights still worked, but no tail lights. Replaced them one at a time with standard replacement bulbs and those work fine. Tried swapping the LEDs back in, no tail lights. Since LEDs last a very long time, I'm guessing something in the circuitry in each bulb burnt out with the voltage/amperage the Hyundai sends to the tail lights.

I thought I was making an investment that would save me any future tail light bulb hassles, but instead these appear to be junk that can't handle the power input range that standard bulbs are designed to handle.

product_title: Burly Brand 14in Narrow Glide Ape Hangers Handlebars - One Size
review_body:
My Harley-Davidson Street Bob came with 12" apes. I am 6'4" tall and have long monkey arms. I purchased these 14 inch apes so I can extend my arms a little more plus they look great. The Street Bob (+ All Sportster and Dyna models) have a narrow fork assembly and these narrow bottom ape hangers fit perfectly. Burly sells these apes in black or chrome and in 12", 14" and 16" heights. I personally think the 16" ones are too tall. The 2 inches between 12" and 14" sounds small but there is definitely a noticeable difference in the height.

Also, the taller your handle bars are the more responsive the bike will become when pushing and pulling to turn. Too tall and things can get dangerous fast. Most US States do not allow your hands to be higher than your shoulders for that reason. I would not recommend anything taller than 12 inches to an inexperienced rider.

I love these bars and they look great on my bike. Installation was a pain in the ass due to all the wire and cable extensions that are needed. I've been working on cars and motorcycles since before I was a teenager and it took me 6+ hours to install. If you have little patience and/or have little to no mechanical ability I would highly recommend having the dealer do the install. It may cost 3 or 4 hours of labor costs but it is definitely worth it.

review_headline: Great Bulbs but Not Quite 6000K as The Description States
review_body:
These bulbs are definitely well-built with a major brand name on it, that definitely is not in question. The base is thick and sturdy with good wiring gauge that won't bend easily. They're also domed without exposed diodes unlike lower-priced bulbs that might be compromised if installed on the outside of the vehicle such as license plate light locations. In addition, they're not polarity sensitive meaning you can install them in either direction and they will still light up.

One important detail, at least IMHO, is that the color output is not of one that is 6000 Kelvin as listed in the description. I'm very particular about this since I have 5000K headlights, fogs, dome, map, license plate... (which these were meant to replace. 5000K isn't an option so I had no choice but to order 6000K) on my 2 Ford F-150s and these definitely do not blend in. They have a slight yellow hue to them when put side by side with a 5000K bulb so I would estimate that they're closer to a 43000K color. You'd think that at 6000K they'd be bluer than the 5000K bulbs but quite the opposite is true in this case. Still, if your intention is getting as much light output as possible and don't care about getting your bulbs to match these would be a great choice.

review_body:
I never wanted to mount my phone in my truck. I don't like unnecessary stuff on the dash. I'd rather spend two grand to have a built in factory GPS than a $200 portable one. It's stupid, I know. You also have to attach a little round magnet to the back of your phone or case. One friend found this annoying as your phone won't lay flat on it's back anymore. I don't mind it at all.

I have taken this all around the country and on rough rural roads and it has always stayed secure. I am also able to push the home button at the bottom of the phone without it coming off of the mount. It's extremely easy to take on and off when getting in and out of your vehicle.

Bottom line is this is the cleanest, easiest mount that I could find and the only one I'll use.

product_title: Slime 20088 4-Way Valve Tool with 4 Valve Cores
review_headline: decent quality at an El Cheapo price
review_body:
I picked up the identical kit for less than $2 at Walmart.
**edit 10/17/13: I see Amazon is now offering it at a competitive price; good job, Amazon!**

The old version I had was like this except for the driver tip, which was almost flush with the tool's body. That one is only good for installations where the tool can fit over a stem with full clearance.

I needed to replace a valve in my hand vac pump recently and this design with the longer driver did the trick on the cheap.

The included core fit perfectly and sealed up nice and tight. It's holding a vacuum, good as new.

The cleaning appendage of this tool fit the pump's brass bore threads well.

The alloy seems durable enough to endure many normal repair jobs.
After decades, the original core in my vac pump was practically welded to the bore -- I had to scrape seal remnants out after its removal. In the removal attempt, I applied quite a bit of reverse torque by this tool, enough that the valve plunger shaft backed completely out of the crimped cap and the core housing still hadn't budged -- I ended up tapping the empty housing out from an opposing access hole using a different tool. I probably could have grabbed the housing with the reamer part of this tool and yanked/twisted it out, but I didn't want to risk damaging the brass bore.
At any rate, this core tool withstood the torsional abuse, no problem.

product_title: Forever Black Bumper & Trim Dye Kit
review_body:
This products works pretty well and withstand a fair amount of time and washes (I need to retouch now after two years)
From my experience, the key

1. Prep the plastic to be painted appropriately (wash thoroughly with provided soap/solvent and let dry or use lint-free cloth)

2. Apply several layers (3 at least).
It dries quite quickly so by the time you get to the other end of the trim/molding you can start over on the next layer. Fewer layers results in patchy coloring which makes the modeling/trim look cheap.

3. Try to paint using long strokes rather than circular or other patterns.
Since the paint dries off quickly, you end up with blocks of black and boundary lines otherwise.
This is not important for first few layers when color is building up. But for the last layer(s), using a uniform, end-to-end long stroke is the difference between a professional look and a rain-spot dirty like look.

The one annoying thing I find (reason for 4 stars) is that the applicator (sponge) makes foam after a few minutes of use (or when already wet and pressed to release more paint). The bubbles create paint clusters that end up creating darker spots. The long strokes help a little with this by breaking the bubbles and sweeping them to the ends. Perhaps a finer sponge on the applicator would solve the problem.

I do recommend this overall. It has served well to me and I get new-looking trims and moldings with some extra care while applying it.

product_title: EasyGO (AM-UNIVERSAL) Universal Smart Key System with Proximity Entry and Vehicle Security
review_headline: Solid system if you're looking to add-on push start
review_body:
I purchased this system for my 2011 Chevy Tahoe. Just to give some background information, I work at Best Buy and have been MECP certified for over 3 years. I did a lot of research on this system before making the decision to purchase, there is a higher priced system that is more vehicle specific to my truck, but I prefer the proximity lock/unlock and didn’t need the extra remote start feature on it, because I’m going to add a Viper smartstart. I’ll admit that after reading the other customer review on his Denali diesel I had some doubts, but still decided to give it a try, reason being as an installer and working with different car alarms every day, I felt that the majority of the problems he was experiencing might not necessarily be the cause of the Easygo.

The instructions were easy to understand and laid out very much like VIPER alarms. All the wiring are labeled correctly with polarity, so if you have access to vehicle wire diagrams then you can easily locate everything, but I personally recommend you still meter test all wires for better safety. The Easygo is like a typical car alarm so I had to use a separate dball bypass module for the security and the factory canbus door locks all pretty standard stuff. No security alarm products tells you that you need to purchase additional bypass modules, because most are universal and not all cars will require them.

I did have a question regarding the steering and shifter lock, and had to send an E-mail to tech support to call me since they don’t list a phone number. A tech called me back within the hour and was able to answer all my questions and go over the process with me. That’s by far the quickest tech support I’ve ever received from any company and reading some of the other reviews for their other systems it seems their standard practice is good customer service.

The steering and shifter lock has a mechanical side and an electronic side. You will lose the mechanical side, so when the car is off you’ll still be able to move the shifter, but this is a GM design specific only to the trucks. The tech mentioned the vehicle specific kit comes with a key turn knob that lets you manually lock the shifter so it won’t move around when the car is off. The steering lock took 2 minutes to remove. I’m comfortable without having a steering wheel lock, because my store is next to an automall so we do quite a bit of alarm installs for dealerships and from personal experience, cars equipped with factory push start do not have steering wheel locks.

The install was fairly easy, since all door locks and triggers are picked up through the bypass module, there wasn’t a lot of wiring. Overall it took roughly 3 hours to do the system. It works like expected, you walk to the driver door and it unlocks, you put your foot on the brake and press the button to start the car. It’s pretty simple to use. The other review mentions that it only unlocks the driver side door and not all doors, that’s because factory has priority door unlock and the bypass module retains that factory feature, it’s not the Easygo. Any car alarm you install on these GM trucks will do the same thing.

As a side note to help out the other reviewer, normally to start a diesel you get into the vehicle and turn the key to ignition wait for the glow plug light to disappear on the dash and then turn the key all the way to start the car. With the Easygo system you can duplicate that by getting into your vehicle and without pressing the foot brake just press the push start button to turn on the ignition, then once the glow plug light disappears you can press down the foot brake and start the car. You shouldn’t have to shut it off and open the door to disengage factory passive arming, that sounds like the bypass module installed incorrectly and causing the problem.

This is a solid system and one of the best options out there if you’re looking toadd push start and alarm to your car. I personally would like to see more auxiliary channels for future expansion to add some more custom features. All said and done I would recommend this system to anyone and advice that you have someone familiar with alarm and remote starts to install it for you.

product_title: Cardone 18-B4919 Remanufactured Domestic Friction Ready (Unloaded) Brake Caliper
review_body:
I used these calipers to upgrade my 2006 Tahoe Z71 to the newer 2007 GM Brake system to solve the typical mushy pedal and poor performance associated with GM brakes. These calipers are for 2007 and up GM vehicles, but if you use these calipers and the mount brackets that are included with them with the newer 13.0\\" rotors as well (instead of the 2006 and prior 12.0\\" rotors) everything bolts up to the stock knuckle and it is a very easy conversion. The calipers themselves are good quality and the reman company actually took care of a couple of GM issues. For example, the stock calipers come with Torx fasteners for the caliper to bracket bolts. That is a terrible idea because with mileage and weather, the torx heads normally strip instead of breaking the bolts loose. These calipers come with those fasteners replaced with normal hex heads, which is awesome, and will be a big help the next time you need to do a brake job.

Now the bad news - Notice that this amazon listing does not specify whether this is a driver or passenger side caliper? I guess I failed to realize that there is a difference, or did not pay attention since this is the first time I have ever mail ordered calipers. The difference is the mounting bracket is keyed on one side so you can not mount the caliper mount bracket on the wrong side. Also, the brake bleeder must be in the up position to bleed the brakes properly. So I ordered two of the same side calipers. This is my mistake, but also I think a mistake in the way this item is listed because it does not tell you which side it is for. Since those are the only two differences, once I figured all of this out, I ground the keying tab off the one side, and then had to take the caliper off and position the caliper so that the bleeder was up instead of down and then place a piece of wood between the pads in order to bleed the side with the wrong caliper. In the end, it all worked out and these things stop great, but they just need tofix this listing and have these sold as right and left.

review_body:
Have appreciated Denso products for some years now. Especially oxy sensors and other components where Denso was an OEM supplier. Denso also had a good reputation for AC compressors with mfg facilities in US & Canada plus worldwide according to their website.

After having been particularly disappointed with the declining, and hit or miss quality of Delphi and some AC Delco products, I believed I had ordered some quality predictability at a premium price with this purchase.

Upon opening, this is a Genuine Denso product. However, some major concerns:
1) Made in China
2) 'Delphi' ink stamped on case and end cap. Very brief Denso label with model # only.
3) No label indicating refrigerant or refrigerant oil type.
4) Tape across S&D ports state to follow the oil balancing instruction included, but there were none, and Denso aftermarket website had none
5) Instructions included only covered the sealing washers and a rudimentary install procedure w/no mention of oil type or amt
shipped dry or ???
6) No warranty information or criteria for warranty replacement. Neither included or on website

Called Denso Tech support and they graciously acknowledged Denso was never a HT6 type compressor supplier to GM and that they sourced from other GM suppliers.
But to their credit they took all of this information - including the absence of documentation either in the box or from their website, logged with a reference #, and Thanked me for bringing it to their attention.

Ugh!!!!! Going with GM parts distribution (and not ACDelco) See my review for Delphi CS-0121. Just simply very disappointing.

And a big Thanks to Amazon once again, a painless return process in progress.

review_body:
In my youth, I used to work in the Wix factory where automobile oil filters were manufactured. I know how these are made. Given the choice between a Wix and a Fram filter, Wix will always win out in quality.

You should know that they made filters for many brands: they are all the same except for the color of the paint and the labeling on the outside of the filter. So back when I was working there, we made OEM filters for Ford and Volvo, and I remember we used to make filters for Gulf as well, among others. product_title: Lexus LS400 Replacement Headlight Unit HID Type - Driver Side
review_body:
First of all, let me say that AutoLightsBulbs was proactive enough to contact me before shipping, so as to ensure that I required an HID type replacement part (which I did).

I had hit a deer and smashed my original light on my 2000 Lexus LS 400. Since the damage was only to the headlamp and turn signal unit on the driver's side, I elected to perform the work of replacing the parts myself.

When I took off the original headlamp unit and replaced the part, I was able to confirm to my satisfaction that the product I received was in every respect identical to the unit it replaced.

If you elect to go the DIY route, be aware that you will still need the actual xenon headlamp bulbs that go in the unit, as well as the incandescent day-time running bulb (mine were fortunately not damaged, and were an easy swap — wiring harnesses also will be needed if those have been damaged). Also, as with any halogen or xenon bulb, do not touch the glass of the bulb with your bare hands, as the oils from your skin will cause the light to burn out in short order. If you have an auto-level servo motor on your luxo-ride as I do, then you'll need to remove the manual level adjustment screw/bolt from the center of the unit, and then manually snap the reflector part of the headlamp on to the servo motor (this is easier to understand if you look at it up close from the back — there's a plastic retainer clip inside the headlamp unit that the level-adjustment bolt snaps into with a "click").

The job took about 1 hour total. I'm very happy with the part. My car looks good again and is no longer a cop magnet.

product_title: Rain-X Latitude Wiper Blade 5
review_body: I have been buying RainX products for years and they have a good product and are a good company. When I had a problem with one I purchased for my old car I contacted them and they shipped me out a replacement blade, so when it came time to buy new blades for my newer 2012 corolla I bought the rainx fusion blade. This blade matched the OEM blade on the car with with metal casing and the packaging even said it was what was used for OEM on toyota's. I liked the metal casing design  because it would be a heavier blade and keep it from chattering on the windshield when I drive the freeway. So I went to my local store and bought a pair. I found that the 26\\" fit fine, the 16\\" (Passenger side) doesn't fit a 2012 corolla. There is a gap at the end between the windshield and the blade so it doesnt sit flat against the glass, enough so that it wont completely wipe the windshield and will chatter on the freeway. I took it back to the store I bought it at ...boys... and the mechanic looked at it and said it was installed right but the old OEM blade had more of a curvature and suggested the Latitude line, in fact he said besides an OEM that is probably the only one that would completely fit. I did try another fusion to see if the one I bought was defective and the second one had the same problem. I tried the latitude and it fit perfectly but it didn't have the metal casing. The latitudes are also more expensive. In the end I returned it and kept the old OEM on the passenger side (that blade was not streaking). When it comes time to replace them again in 6 months or so I will either replace them with the latitude or go to the dealer and buy a set. I know its more money but they fit properly. RainX should not advertise they are OEM for toyota if they are not, if they do list it they should list the cars it is OEM for.

product_title: Mossy Oak Two-Grip Steering Wheel Cover
review_body:
Version purchased: Browning Infinity
Installed on: 2012 Ram 1500 Laramie CC

This steering wheel cover is very attractive and is well built. I knew it would be a chore to install it from previous experience with other wheel covers. After reading other reviews, they helped remind me of this fact and to take it slow and stay patient while installing it. Slow and steady and you can get it on with only a little bit of elbow grease. It is a very tight fit, but I appreciate that mainly because that proves it will not slip or change position on the steering wheel. The Browning version also has superb ribbing in the style of raised rubber grips comprised of bullet casings surrounding the Buckmark logo on either side of the cover. My OEM steering wheel would occasionally slip under my grip so I am very pleased with the feel and thickness of the grips on this cover. Others have made mention of a foul or unpleasant odor.. I have not noticed any odor other than that of new rubber and that just proves to me that I did, in fact, receive a new, unused product. It is not anything I would complain about (and I have sensitivity to odors) but it will wear off after a few days of use.

Overall, this product is beyond what I was expecting from the pictures and description and I would recommend it to anyone wishing to add a touch of color to their interior or anyone looking to alleviate a slippery OEM steering wheel problem.

I can't even contact the manufacturer to let them know how much their product sucks because their contact information cannot be found anywhere. I am definitely done with this manufacturer.

product_title: Meguiars G10307 ScratchX 2.0
review_body:
Right to the point. Disregard the less than five star reviews! This stuff is amazing! I've owned about 30 cars so far and was once a professional detailed. Just tried it on my 2012 white f150. There were about 20 small areas that had fine scratches, scuffs, stained and marks. This product removed about 18 of them. Little or no pressure too. Some deeper ones requires a little elbow grease. They disappeared and yes I said disappeared right in front of my eyes! Only two would not come out as they were through the base coat, but they still looked far better. As for the application I followed the advise of some other reviewers. Put a dime sized amount of scratch x on a tight bundled part of a microfiber towl and rub against the scratch. When finished buff with a dry microfiber towel. No swirls, cloudy rub spots or any sign that you worked that area..amazing!!
Note: this product nor any product will remove scratches or nicks that are through the base coat. So if you can see the metal or primer it will not work. However it did remove many hairline scratches that I thought were into the base coat.
In short, my f150 looks like it rolled out of the dealers lot! Just like when it was new!!!

product_title: Jtech 2x 1157 BAY15D 7W Cree Q5 LED Pure Red Light Lamp Bulb
review_headline: Very bright, but don't work correctly in housing
review_body:
Bought a set to replace the lights on a small trailer. I installed them and the brake lights work beautifully, but driving lights do not work at all on either side. Just to be safe I reinserted the old incandescent bulbs, which worked just fine. I tested the LEDs by grounding them and jumping both leads separately, and to my surprise both brightness levels worked perfectly (and look great). The problem must be in the design of the contacts. The incandescent I removed (along with every other 1157 I've seen) have round, tall contact leads, whereas these LEDs have shallow, wide oval shaped leads. I believe the shape of the leads are preventing them from making a good contact with the socket.

I'll be contacting the seller to see if we can figure this out.

Edit: It seems that pressure applied to the end contacts is what causes the issue. This is true for both bulbs, and replicates itself on two separate trailers. I've sent in a request for return.

Another edit: Return instructions indicate that I must pay for return shipping. I've sent a request for a prepaid mailing label as well as a full refund for the original shipping cost.

product_title: Lucas 10008 Power Steering Stop Leak - 12 oz
review_headline: Worked Before, See if it'll Work again (Plus, alternative repair)
review_body:
This product worked for me on my 1983 CJ7 Jeep, stopped the leak completely. Now I bought a 1999 Mercury Couger. I just added this to it last night. I will see if it will work again.

Thanks to other reviews regarding there history and indirect advice about using it. I to have a Rack and Pinion leak. It's good to know to keep using the product for a week or two before giving up on it. I have another method of repair I can do at home as well if it fails or at least slows down the leak. I bought steel mixing Puddy (small tube next to the silicone supplies), you can buy at Walmart in auto section. I found the rack and Pinion under the car, as well as where it was leaking, (one of the treads that lead into the Rack and Pinion that connects the hose to the wheel shaft.) I am going to mix the Steel Puddy and clean the Rack and Pinion (Using Carb. Cleaner), and apply the puddy onto and around the treading where the leak is. Wait for it to dry (Hour), though I'll wait 24 hours to be safe. Then test drive it again.

product_title: Meguiar's Heavy Duty Headlight Restoration Kit.1
review_headline: Much Easier than it looks, If you are debating, DO IT.
review_body:
I debated between this kit and the [[ASIN:B00429NKWK Sylvania Headlight Restoration Kit]]. I went with this one primarily because I forgot to order ahead of time and my local auto store only had this one in stock, I also liked the fact that it had a buffing ball with a drill attachment. Both kits offer a UV protectant, which is a must.

I was expecting this to take 30-45 minutes per headlight and to be very difficult and arduous. I was wrong. It took less than 15 minutes per light and was rather painless. My headlights were pretty badly oxidized and this cleared them up extremely well. there are still 2 spots on the front of the lens that are a little fogged, but I think those areas are beyond repair and you can only tell when you get up close that they are there. The lenses are now clear and the light shines out much better than before. It makes the car look 100% better, the yellowing is completely gone.

I put off doing this for 6 months because I wasn't sure it would work and didn't want to waste $30, now that I've seen the results firsthand, I would have spent twice that on the kit. I'm not sure how well this will hold up in the long run, but even it only lasts a year, there is enough in the kit to do them 3 or 4 times, and it was easy enough I'd be ok to do it again.

If you are even debating buying this kit, DO IT, you won't be sorry.

review_body:
Firstly I'd like to address the size issue. Someone mentioned that the gloves ran super small so being 6'-2\\" ish and about 236 pounds, I figure hey, let's get the xxl size then, but when they came in, it was obvious that the xxl size was molded for some kind of gigantic Sasquatch. Not being a Sasquatch myself (although almost as hairy), I began to regret following that reviewer's advice. So I said to myself, hey, they're only like 5 bucks, lets get the large as well and see how they work out, and what do you know, they fit like... ummm... well, like a glove.

Now as far as quality is concerned... these are really great gloves, they're made out of super soft pliable leather and they are plenty warm, in fact the leather feels so soft that I am a little concerned that they will stretch out to the point of being a little large (i've only had them two days), so I am almost tempted to get a third medium pair just in case. But then I was like \\"hey, three pairs of the same glove in three different sizes in order to get the perfect size is starting to sound a little OCD\\" so I just upped my meds and I think I might be able to resist the one-click button for now.

One last point, I bought these to keep my hands from freezing off when I ride my bike in the morning at 80+ mph, which they do wonderfully, but please be aware that because the leather is so soft and relatively thin, they probably won't protect your hands very well in case of a spill on the freeway.

So to summarize, these gloves are warm, soft, and super comfortable but they probably won't keep your skin from shredding off in a high speed spill.
