product_title: Dorman HELP! Toyota Corolla Brown Interior Door Handle
review_headline: Does Not Match the slots and cannot anchor it.  Had to get a longer screw
review_body:
My original part has longer inserts for the slots. I took all this info to an auto parts store and they said I have the right part number for a 1997 Toyota Corolla but I would have to buy a longer screw to keep it tightened to the door and keep the screw driver with me. It is unable to snap into the holes because the inserts on this one are too short. The numbers on my original handle are 69206-12140 and then underneath it is 69278-12060L14. If your original part shows these numbers you will have to get a longer screw to hold this handle in the door. You won't be able to snap this in. I can go to a junkyard if I wish and try to get one that matches the old one but right now, I have made this work for me. I have a dark tan original handle and this is dark brown but there was no other color available.

For anyone out there who wishes to try to change out their car door handle, I am glad to help you. First take the screw off with a big Phillips screw driver, slide the whole door handle apparatus towards the front of the car and it should come out now by a few inches. Look to your left and you will see the rod which looks like a coat hangar. Pull the rod straight up and take a small flat head screwdriver and push the plastic overhanging the rod on top to the left. It can be hard to push but don't give up. I got it to move. Now lift the rod up out of the hole and get the new handle. On the new handle, move the plastic overhanging clip to the left (so it is in place to lock it later) and drop the rod into the hole. Now..while the overhanging clip is to the left, pull the car door handle back one time to lock it. The clip should now be hanging over top of the rod to keep it locked in. Align your door handle with where the old one was and put the screw in. Good luck!

review_headline: Great product, save $ over dealer/mechanic and install yourself!
review_body:

If you are even more like me, you checked at Toyota and other parts stores only to find that the part costs over $400 and was not happy about that. And even more like me? Went to the local parts yard only to find they don't have any 4Runners with this part.

Way better price on Amazon than the dealer or parts store. I received the part from Amazon in less than 48 hours (thank you Prime) and installed it in less than 30 minutes. There are plenty of 4Runner forums online that teach you how to remove the interior panel that you need to gain access. Do a quick search and you will see! After that panel is off it is quite self explanatory, I'd suggest disconnecting the battery before disconnecting the broken unit.

Hope this helps - I am certainly enjoying being able to use the rear door and not have it secured with a ratchet strap!

review_body:
This appears to be the exact replacement for the OEM part on my Saturn Vue, down to the product serial # being the same format as the failed switch I replaced. The good news is that it works as expected. Unfortunately, the bad news is that it works as expected as well. The switch becomes slightly warm when used, which leads me to suspect it may experience the shorting and eventual smoke issues that the last two switches had, as both of the previous switches displayed the same temperature change when new (it appears GM may have skimped on the wiring when they designed these switches, and went with too small of a gauge wire for the power going through that wiring). At < $35 shipped, though, this item is cheap enough, and easy enough, to replace.

Rating is for the quality of the OEM part. If you're looking for an exact replacement for a failed turn signal / headlight switch in your GM vehicle, this is likely what you're looking for, right down to the issues that caused the original to fail in the first place. :)

product_title: Polaris Mini Ranger 400 500 EV Winch Mount (Standard)
review_body: I just got a new Polaris UTV and wanted to fix it up with a snow plow. I already had my own winch, so didn't want to buy the one that the OEM had available. However, the OEM did not offer just a winch mounting bracket. I found this one on Amazon and thought I'd give it a try. It fit GREAT and was way easy to install. The materials and fabrication of the mount are very nice and it looks and fits like it's custom made for the job. If you're just using this to mount and use a winch only, you're done. A piece of cake. Nevertheless, I must give one warning if you are going to use the Polaris OEM snow plow mounting bracket. On each side of the UTV the Polaris plow bracket uses the bottom of three holes where the winch bracket also bolts on. You might as well just leave this bolt out (as well as the bolt in the middle hole) when installing the winch mount as you will later install a bolt through the plow bracket, the UTV frame and the winch mount bracket. This is NO problem, just letting you know. The only problem, if you want to call it that, is with the middle of the three mounting holes. The plow bracket will interfere with the bolt head for the winch mount that goes through this middle hole. It won't let the bolt lay flat on the UTV frame. But, not to worry. I just cut a thick washer in half and used it as a shim under the side of the bolt head opposite the plow bracket. Now the bolt head has support on both sides, sits flat when tightened, and problem solved. I made it sound way more complicated than it really is. Sorry.

review_body:

The Redline 75w90 GL-5 is used for the differential.
The Redline MT90 (75w90 GL-4) or MTL (70w80 GL-4) is used for transmission.
(This is correct to what I know and for the miata)

When buying this I was also curious to know what lubricant to use for the transmission turret and turns out you can use anything from what I've read on miata forums. I used the 75w90 for the turret and I haven't really seen problems with it yet, but technically you can add MT90 or MTL into the transmission turret. I read that someone used brake fluid to lubricant the gears inside the turret. Finding out for yourself would be beneficial.

The mirrors hold solidly, and there was little to no vibration (certainly nothing that rose to the level of bothersome) while travelling our bumpy Michigan highways.

The instructions are lame, so this might help. Put the soft material tape on the length of the stabilizer bar, starting on the end with the big bump, all the way to the outside of the big bump/end of bar. That big bump will sit on the outside edge of your mirror. When putting on the tow mirrors, ensure that that stabilizer bar is within the small tracks for it, and that the tow mirror edges are aligned to cover the edges of the vehicle mirror frame. When the outside edge of the bump on the stabilizer bar is level with the outside edge of the towing mirror, you are ready to tighten the knob.

product_title: Airtex E3973M Fuel Pump Module Assembly
review_body:
My application was a 98 Pontiac Grand Prix GTP, and the original fuel pump gave up the ghost.
Being an In-tank pump, I traditionally like to buy the Delco replacements since it's a "drop the tank" event.

Installation went like most aftermarket fuel pump replacements. You'll need to cut your factory harness plug off, and splice into the wires of the Airtex pump harness provided. The wires are color coded to match the factory harness, so it's pretty simple.
You need to use good force to push the pump down into the tank but use caution; the sending unit is plastic.
Read the instructions.

What I would recommend:
Buy a new tank snap ring or locking ring for your application. The 98 Grand Prix used a snap ring and it was quite rusted and fragile. Better to replace it when doing the pump. Use a good penetrant like PB blaster, and then compressed air to blow the chunks of dirt/rust out of the area to avoid dropping crud in the tank.

product_title: ARB Fridge Freezer
review_body:
This thing works great and the way I use it will pay for itself in about two - three months tops. The trick to it being a fridge and freezer at the same time is to turn the temp down just below freezing. Pack your "to keep frozen" items against the interior walls. They'll stay frozen enough for weeks. Pack your veggies, milk, etc away from the walls so they don't freeze. NOTE: Lettuce freezes to easy so stay away from that unless the unit is going to be used only as a fridge only.

Over the road trucker here and I just returned from a three-week plus tour out. I absolutely love this thing. Was able to enjoy home cooked type meals the whole time. Took chicken breasts, small steaks and hot dogs which all stayed frozen enough that I didn't "lose" a thing. Also brought along fresh veggies, carrots, celery, broccoli, that stayed good until it was all gone. Yogurt lasted until the end of the tour. Enjoyed ice cold water, milk (mixed from powder), and cokes the whole time. Brewed my own coffee so during the three weeks out I spent maybe $20 on food stuff, if that. And that wasn't even necessary.

Anyways this is a good buy. It takes just a little to learn how to pack it. Now the a/c in my truck was acting up during this hot July of running the West / Southwest states. I ran a lot with just the windows down and the ARB kept the temp it was set at. I was very pleasantly surprised. So far it's stood up to the abuse of bouncing around in a big rig. Fuses are hard to track down but can be found online. I haven't need one yet though. The only thing I'm going to changed is get an insulated pad to set it on since the truck floor gets so warm. No sense it working harder that it has too. That about does it. The ARB is tough and it works. Might consider the 80 qt but even in a big rig space is limited.....

product_title: TuningPros LS-099-B Lowering Springs Kit Blue Set of 4
review_body:
My goal with lowering springs was purely for aesthetics and not for a better handling car. This car is my wife's daily driver so it had to remain drivable without having to worry about driveways or parking stop scraping. The TuningPros springs not only fit the budget (half the cost of \\"name brand\\" springs), they have a close to stock ride, and lower the car just enough to give the car the perfect stance. I was leery at first because there were only a couple reviews on them. Fortunately the reviews I read were favorable, and I'm also writing a favorable review! :)

These springs are made out of the Japanese material equivalent that the H&R springs are made from. The Megan springs are made with same Japanese material as these TuningPros springs. Spring rates and ride heights are the notable differences.

$119 - TuningPros \\"blue\\" = 1\\" front .75\\" rear
$149 - Megan \\"orange\\" = 1\\" front 1\\" rear
$242 - H&R \\"black\\" = 1.4\\" front 1.3\\" rear

Here's a link to the material specs: [...]

Lowered vehicle using this DYI for reference. [...]

Front install was 1 hour from start to finish. Rear install was 30 minutes from start to finish. I only used an impact driver to remove the strut top spring perch. If you are somewhat mechanically inclined, and are not taking pictures of your installation, you should be able to do this install in just over an hour.

The lowering was exactly as advertised. Front was a 1\\" drop and the rear was .75\\". Both wheel wells are now 27\\" from the ground to the wheel well. The front started off at 28\\" and the rear was 27.75\\".

Ride quality is approximately 10-15% firmer. These springs are just a tad firmer than stock, which I expected because of the higher spring rate.

Bottom line: If you only want to mildly lower your Sonata, and want a quality budget set of springs, these are the ticket! They are perfect for a daily driver. I give these a 5 star rating for fit, finish, and quality.

If you want lower your Sonata more than 1\\", have a stiffer ride, and want to spend twice the price tag, then these might not be for you :)

product_title: 3M 32044 Imperial Wetordry  Sheet3
review_body:
In the state of Texas your car will not pass inspection once the headlights become to hazy. My wife and I have to park out side during they day when we are at work and with the sun beating down all day long the plastic head light lens start to turn yellow and hazy. At my last inspection of both cars the inspection station said that they would probably not pass for next years inspection. I checked with a couple of local shops and they were going to charge $50 per head light to 'restore' them. That's when I went on line to see if I could find a solution. I saw several home made remedies with tooth past and baking soda and then I found this kit. Thought I would give it a try for a quarter of the price of taking it to a shop.
I watched several videos on line, read the instructions that came with it a couple of times and started the project.
Worked great. You will need a drill, either electric or battery operated, and a little bit of time. If you are using a battery operated drill make sure all of your batteries have a full charge.
There was enough product in the package to do all four of our headlights. So instead of a $200 shop charge I bought this and did it myself. It took me about an hour to do the first two headlights. After I got the hang of it, I did the next two in about 45 minutes.
I purchased another kit to do my daughters car and did hers in about 30 minutes.

This is easy to do. Just follow the instructions. I would also recommend watching a video on it. If you go to the 'How To Center' on the 3mauto.com web site under the Vehicle Appearance section they have an instructional video.

You do need to use the painters tape that comes with the kit so you don't scratch the paint during the sanding process. Most of the videos have you putting two layers of tape all of the way around the headlight, including on the hood. On the three cars that I did I was able to raise the hood to get it out of the way and I didnot use the tape on the hood. Depending on your vehicle you may or may not have that option.

If you have yellowed hazy headlights this product will fix that whether it is for a state inspections or just to give you more light for driving.

review_body:

It did not take long to figure out that these are what I have been looking for for 3 decades. They are machined aluminum and encapsulated in solid rubber. They seal totally tight at either clockwise or counter clockwise rotation until it stops. I can produce a 40 foot stream of water with 70 pounds of pressure on a 5/8 inch hose and it can be turned from an narrow stream to wide spray patterns by rotating the outer shell. It can produce a very gentle low flow stream to water small plants and not wash them out of the planter.

These are so solidly built I could run over it with a tractor and I think it would survive. I can now add the last junky one to the bucket and sell the whole bucket at a garage sale for $10. This is a nice piece of merchandise that is rarely found these days.

Took the old actuator off by driving out pop-rivets.  Swapped the mounting bracket.  Original bracket was held on by 3 screws.  Only 2 screws came with the VDO actuator so I reused 2 screws from the original.  The original also came with a rubber sheath covering that I reused.  After installing I was expecting a brand new locking actuation.  To my surprise, the lock mechanism wouldn't even move.  It would start to move but the new actuator had less torque than the original actuator and it would stall out.  I am going to reinstall my original actuator; it had more torque. product_title: Superchips 2865 Flashpaq for GM Gas V8 Gas Truck/SUV and V8 Cars
review_body:
I bought this mainly to calibrate my Avalanche's speedo & odometer after lifting it, re-gearing it and putting on larger tires. First tip: pull your radio fuse if you have an aftermarket radio before connecting the flashpaq. Second tip: put a level on top of one of the tires and measure from the ground to the base of the level, use that and not the Manufacturer's listed diameter. Bringing it down 1/4" from actual measured size dialed in the speedo with the new gear ratio. I have a CAI and a cat back exhaust and after I got the speedo calibrated, I loaded the premium tune. Really did not notice any difference in performance, so I returned it to stock tune with options (new tire and gear sizes). An added bonus, I haven't had any ABS issues with the new setup (295/70R18 tires and 4.56 gears).

I guess the performance end is limited to a stock vehicle, so if you are buying this for performance gains on a modified vehicle, save your money. My speedo was about 18 mph over actual prior to using this, so it did the job I needed it to do. I will probably try the other tunes to see if they offer anything, but I'm not expecting much.

The only people who seem to mind are me and any dogs in the area but it's enough that I'm glad it's locked in the garage with my car and not somewhere I could be within earshot.

It charged my car's battery right up overnight and has been trickle charging for several days. It hit the battery with a bit higher voltage than the 1amp charger I had cobbled together, keeping it charging at 13.7 volts, which is about as much as an alternator would so it should keep the battery in tip top condition.

The cord is a little longer than is apparent from the photos but still not long enough to be used without an extension cord. My car's lighter adapter is pretty close to an outlet and it was just barely long enough to reach.

The box is smaller than in the photos as well but in my book that is a good thing. The last thing is there is no on/off switch. It's either plugged in and on, or unplugged and not.

product_title: Toyota Sienna Van 98-03 Sequoia 01-07 Outer Rear Liftgate Door Handle 6909008010
review_headline: It's METAL and Strong! Not Plastic!  Replacement Toyota Liftgate Handle Assy
review_body:
If you don't know how to repair this; then start at youtube.com. Watch some of the videos on how to: 1) Open your Toyota Sequoia Liftgate. And; 2) How to replace the broken handle.

I used this replacement Toyota Liftgate Handle, now I'm back up and running just fine. (I only used the actual handle, not the other parts of the supplied assenbly. See below.)

A broken Liftgate Handle is a big deal. Toyota made their's of plastic, and they break.

This handle isn't perfect though. The handle part is made of metal (Aluminum maybe?), and is very well made in this replacement assembly.

But; the rest of this assembly isn't as well made. The metal bracket that I got was bent and mis-shapen. I didn't want to bend & straighten, check & compare, repeat, repeat...

Not a problem though! Here's what I recommend:

Watch the YouTube videos. Learn 2 things: 1) How to open the Liftgate, and 2) How to remove & replace the handle.

Then: open your Liftgate.
(This may be the hardest part. Start by unlocking all doors. You'll need a slender, curved, "Index finger" shaped metal probe, to reach inside and "press" / "lever" DOWN onto the release bar, which is hidden inside the Liftgate. By slender I mean: .15" to .21" Dia, or 5/32" to 7/32" steel wire. Much smaller, and it won't be strong enough. Much larger, and it might not fit, and it will be hard to bend even with a torch. Be sure to "temper" the steel if you use a torch.)

Then: remove your broken stock Toyota Liftgate Handle Assembly.

Then: disassemble this replacement handle and remove the one part that breaks; the actual handle itself. Set all the other parts of the replacement Liftgate Handle Assy aside.

Then disassemble your old stock Toyota Liftgate Handle Assy, and install just the one new part, the actual handle from the "replacement assembly," into the old stock Toyota Liftgate Handle Assy.

The stock Toyota bracket, levers, springs, mounting studs, and holes, are already the correct size and shape to fit right back into the Liftgate. Just replace the handle; plastic handle out; metal handle in.

All the best to you.

product_title: Meguiars G12310 PlastX Clear Plastic Cleaner and Polish
review_body:
Rather than pay three times as much for a multi-step kit that can take up to an hour of work per headlight, I opted for this inexpensive and simple alternative. Not only did it WORK on my sister's 2007 Corolla's 100,000 mile, VERY yellowed and foggy headlight covers, it worked in just FIVE MINUTES PER COVER! And I used only 1/3rd of the 10oz bottle! So my cost was $2 and time was ten minutes. The covers went from under 50% light transmission to at least 90%. With the lights on at night, standing in front of the car, you can still see a bit off fogginess, but when driving the lights work great!

I used a small foam pad from a car wax kit for application and a small, slightly damp terry cloth hand towel. I used the towel to promptly wipe off any cleaner that got on the paint, and after rubbing generous amounts of cleaner on each lens cover for five minutes, I wiped the cover dry with the towel while the cleaner was still wet, as directed on the bottle. It can't get easier than this! Of course, the result can only improve if you want to spend more time scrubbing, or, if you want perfection, spend the money and even more time on those other kits.

See my \\"before\\" and \\"after\\" photos above!

ADDENDUM (11 Jul 13): I just found on EHOW dot COM that a 3 to 1 ratio of toothpaste to baking soda will do the same job. Wash lenses first with dish soap and afterwards with baking soda in water (rinse well after each wash). I'll try it and let ya know!

review_body:
I installed this on a 2012 KLX250S along with a 108 link (search item# B006O85URA here @ Amazon) chain. With my application this rear sprocket is the same as adding a 13t front sprocket to get that lower gearing which really helps. This rear sprocket requires a 108 link (520) chain whether you use the factory 14t or you put the smaller 13t sprocket on for the days you need even lower gearing. The 45t rear and 108 link chain is the best combo for the KLX if you do a fair amount of off-road because it allows you to easily swap back and forth between the 13t and 14t front sprocket depending on your needs that day. The 14t with this rear is still capable of speeds of 75-85mph which will get the job done if you need to hop on the interstate.

This review is specifically for the KLX250S which comes from the factory with 14/42 gearing

To find compatible (KLS250S) front sprockets here on Amazon:

search item# B005WJ9G6S for the 13t

search item# B0031721AG for the 14t (OEM replacement if needed)

product_title: Givi Silver T477 Roll Bag - Black

This is a step up from the ubiquitous Cortech sports luggage that unfortunately isn't very durable. The seams are reinforced and the material, while appearing to be similar to that in Cortech luggage, holds up much better. I've had mine for 2 seasons now and they're not suffering any of the rips or fraying of my old set.

I have 4 minor criticisms. First, I wish these roll bags would all have a reinforce bottom (removable) to help them hold their shape better. Second, the heat shielding on the bottom is a bit awkward and needs a soft later to prevent scratching your bike (although careful mounting will address this). Third, the Cortech luggage has an ingenious modular system that the Givi luggage lacks. So there's no built-in way to connect this back to the T479 if you have it. Finally, I'd like if the bag had a few internal pouches for storing small, loose items (fuses, ear plugs, etc.).

This is a good bag though and I'd recommend it. I use it as my afternoon ride bag to carry tools, water, etc.

product_title: Black Bull SBCNNS Red Vertical Blast Cabinet
review_headline: No rating - delivery refused; second delivery accepted
review_body:
THIS IS AN UPDATE. AMAZON PROMPTLY REPLACED REFUSED DELIVERY. SEE SECOND PARAGRAPH FOR MORE DETAILS.

I wish I could write a stellar review of this cabinet. I was very excited to find one so affordable, even if assembly is required. I purchased this bead blast cabinet in good faith, from Amazon LLC since the listing was one of a very few that did not have negative reviews on the condition of package at arrival. The package, when I received it, was utterly destroyed. Corners were smashed in, the box was torn multiple times and retaped. It looked like the whole thing had been ripped apart and some one put half an effort into fixing the box, and failed miserably. After taking pictures of the delivery package (which do no justice to its true condition), I refused the delivery without opening the package. There is NO WAY the item could not have been damaged. I am a regular Amazon user, and Amazon Prime Member, and was very disappointed. Much of this review is a copy of the email I sent to Amazon. I posted the photos of the package at time delivery was refused. I hope Amazon rectifies this situation, and I must come back and write the stellar review of a great blast cabinet and how it has helped me become more efficient and profitable.

Second delivery, the box was still damaged, though not as severely as the first go-round. I figured, may as well accept it and see what happens. The packaging of the item is efficient, if one realizes the outer box is 'sacrificial' if you will, to take the damage rather than the item itself. The blast cabinet was in good condition over al. A small bend in two flanges of the corner of the support table; nothing that couldn't be fixed with an adjustable wrench. Everything went together easily. Instructions assume you have some working knowledge of assembling. Opened box, laid out parts to determine all were present, arranged everything for assembly and put it together. In less than two hours I went from a damaged box and a pile of parts to a fully functioning blast cabinet. The second package wasn't horribly damaged, and the cabinet was just fine. Works great! Had a buddy at the shop ask if I paid a grand for it, so that's something. If they put some corrugated plastic inside the box, I'd bet even that damage would largely go away. Would be 5 stars if the first package hadn't had to be refused.

product_title: Smittybilt 98380 X2O 8 Comp Series Winch Synthetic Rope / Alum Fairlead
review_headline: Waterproof solenoid a bit of a reach
review_body:
This winch worked great the first time I used it. The second time I went out, I was surprised when I tested it and it only clicked in both directions. I used a hammer on the solenoid box(in accordance with the user manual), and I was able to get it to work in the spool-in direction. Since then, it has worked intermittently, and I usually have to hit it with a hammer a couple of times to get it to work somewhat.

Fast forward to today. I recently emailed Smittybilt customer service to request warranty support on the winch. I got no response and this weekend, I decided to open the solenoid cover and see what was wrong. The solenoid box was full of water! All of the contacts were corroded. I had envisioned that the \\"waterproof\\" solenoid would be a single solenoid that had sealed connectors. Not the case, as there were 4 individual solenoids, one of which was full of water internally. The \\"waterproof\\" gimmick must be due to the solenoid enclosure, but there are no o-rings on the penetrations, and the case is flimsy enough that you can deflect it and see into the solenoid compartment.

I opened the cover, used compressed air and brake cleaner and a wire brush to remove all the sludge and corrosion. I had to smack all the solenoids with a hammer for about 15 minutes to get them to cycle properly and consistently. Once all the moisture boiled out of the waterlogged solenoid, it started to work better. I sprayed the entire enclosure with silicone spray and then sealed the entire cover with permatex. I'm sure I'll be able to use it like it is for a few more seasons, but I'll be sure to have a hammer handy.

My next winch will have a little quality control on the solenoid. I will eventually upgrade these solenoids to a single waterproof unit from a reputable manufacturer.

product_title: Spectre Performance (58198) 1.5" x 19" Chrome Stainless Steel Flex Radiator Hose
review_body: This looks like an expensive braided stainless hose but is about half the price and worth even less. These hoses are undersized and I figured that out the hard way, after destroying one hose, buying another and then having to modify the Magna-Clamp to even get it on. I have been working on cars, trucks and engines for over 40 years and this Spectre Radiator hose is not recommended for any purpose. My hot rod has all braided SS hoses so I wanted matching radiator hoses again when I changed radiators. The old Spectre hoses had lasted awhile but were not reusable when I switched to an aluminum radiator so I ordered new hoses from Spectre. I spent hours trying everything possible to get the first hose on and eventually (after heat, lube, removing the tape, etc) I got the hose onto the water pump. I tried tightening the hose clamp and it slipped. The other 3 clamps (for the top hose and the other end of bottom hose) tightened with no problems but this one would not. That meant removing the hose since the clamp is not removable with the hose installed. The only way that hose was coming off now was to destroy the hose in the process. So I had to order another hose and another $50. This time I took the Magna-Clamp apart and had to split it on the back side since it was not going fit on the hose with the hose installed. I put the Magna-Clamp end on the water pump, forced the hose on then slid the rest of the Magna-Clamp with the hose clamp onto the hose. Of course no way is the Magna-Clamp going back together so I'll use Valco silver rtv on the back side (where it can't really be seen) to attach the end so it does not move around. I seriously regret having bought these Spectre hoses and would no longer recommend them for any application. I contacted Spectre but so far they are ignoring me, probably have no answer.

product_title: Fit System 62075-76G Chevrolet/GMC/Cadillac Driver/Passenger Side Replacement Towing Mirror Set with Turn Signal and Dual Glass
review_body:
I replaced stock small mirrors with these on my 2003 Sierra and I could not be happier.

The packaging- could not have been better. Product was very well protected and arrived flawless.

The item- both mirrors have wiring harnesses that are the same length as stock (about 18 inches- NOT as shown in the photo above), the connectors are the same colors as stock (one blue, one black), and the cable has barbed clips in the same spots as the stock harness so it mounts exactly the same. They come with the same foam gasket as the stock mirror meaning you can toss the old one. The mounting bolts have thread protector sleeves on them.

Installation- the instructions were perfect and include steps for removal of the door panel. Maybe could have been better for how to remove the connector to the door panel from the truck. There is one that has a flip over 'bail' that secures the connector to the door controls. This is of course for vehicles with power windows etc.

The mirror mounts with 3 studs and nuts (you re-use the nuts from your stock mirrors). Tighten them by going around to each one several times to slowly and evenly compress the foam seal/insulation.

The good- I have seen other reviewers complain about vibration and about the mirrors being tilted up (not level to the ground). Well, yes, at freeway speeds, the passenger side vibrates a tiny bit but I think this is because this is the first one I installed and didn't get it as snug as the driver side. I will re-tighten and update this review. As far as not being level to the ground- the stock ones are the same.

The not-as-good- I sit with my seat adjusted to the rear stop (as far back as possible) and with a slight recline. Even with this setting, I have to have the driver side top mirror adjusted completely 'in' to have it adjusted for me. I can't imagine if I were shorter and had the seat closer to the steering wheel how I would see behind me inthe drivers side mirror. Yet when I adjust the mirror all the way 'out', it goes so far that a gap opens up and I can see the wiring behind the mirror. Also, I had to turn off my memory seats so the driver side mirror doesn't arbitrarily adjust in and up each time I put the key in the ignition. This isn't the fault of the mirror, just pointing this out. I haven't decided yet which inconveniences me more: having to adjust my seat manually once in a while, or the mirror each and every time.

But- even so, these are a VAST impovement over the small stock speakers they put on my full size pickup.

product_title: TYC 4720322 Honda Civic Driver Side Power Non-Heated Replacement Mirror.309
review_headline: Didn't Fit my 98 Accord EX Coupe (US)
review_body:
I ordered this part because the Amazon site states it is compatible with my fiancée’s '98 Accord Coupe. When I first opened the package I was happy because it looked to be an exact match, and of good quality. It didn't come with mounting screws, but I knew this from a previous review, and wasn't too concerned since I planned to reuse the existing screws. I was very careful not to damage the screws while removing the old mirror, but was disappointed to find out that the screw holes are threaded differently than the original mirror. I went to a local hardware store the next day and picked up the correct screws, and went back to work on the mirror. Disappointment set in again when I realized the screw holes are slightly off (grouped closer together than the holes in the door). I measured both mirrors, and found this replacement to be a tad smaller... the biggest difference is the base (bottom third of the triangle), which measures an inch shorter than the original. So after wasting several days waiting for the mirror, and two days trying to install it, I'm back on-line looking for the correct part.

I'm puzzled as to why Amazon shows the mirror compatible with my car. My best guess at this point is that this part (4700331) is probably for a 4-door, and the error is Amazon showing it compatible with a coupe. I'll post more info when I know for sure. I emailed TYC today about the issue and am awaiting a response.

I didn't mark the product down because it appears to be of good quality and I assume my issue is with Amazon's compatibility list. I did take one star off for the lack of screws or any info about what screws are needed.

product_title: ANCO C-21-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 21", (Pack of 1)
review_headline: Good Quality Product - Won't Fit our Car
review_body:
We ordered this ANCO 21\\" contour blade for our 2004 Honda Odyssey. We thought that the various connectors meant that it would connect properly - but as it turns out it would not connect properly. So the review that follows is for the other contour blade we received, a different length, for our other car.

We got a single ANCO 22\\" contour blade to review, and we reviewed it side by side against a new regular ANCO (non-countour) blade on the other side of the front windshield. I own a Subaru Forester. The Contour blade was slightly clearer and slightly quieter. Both were just as easy to put on and remove.

I'm 44 and have been driving since I was 16. In those years I definitely learned early on the value of using a good quality windshield wiper. After all, it's a relatively cheap part which can help prevent a quite expensive (and harmful) accident. So definitely I would say if you're currently using a cheap windshield wiper blade that it's well worth upgrading to something good quality.

Do you need to go from normal ANCO to the contour ANCO? Again, I would say it's worth having the best you can get. This is about seeing the road in front of you in an already slick situation. You've got enough else to worry about in a thunderstorm or snowstorm. You don't need to worry about being able to see the road on top of everything else.

I'll update this when both wear out, to give notes on the durability of them, but I assume both will have the normal range of durability.

The ramp itself is decent quality, very sturdy, and has enough grip for the ninja to stick to. It is very light though and easy to throw in the truck bed, it folds up into approximately 4 feet long.

The one problem I have with it though, is that the description says it is 7'4\\" long, when in fact I was surprised to find that it is only 6'4\\" long. Luckily it seems to work for my mid-size truck, but I feel like it would be very difficult to use on a full size or lifted truck. As it is, I tend to use it on slopes where the ramp angle is lower, which makes it easier to get the bikes into the truck bed.

Overall though for my situation it is affordable and gets the job done, I will probably purchase a second one so that I can haul lawn tractors and atvs.

product_title: VERIZON FIOS REPLACEMENT BATTERY 12V 7AH SLA RECHARGEABLE BATTERY 12V
review_headline: Perfect fit into the Fios box
review_body:
The battery came with a 12.6 volt charge on it. It's the exact same size as the old (2 years) Fios battery.
Within a few hours, it was charged up to 13.7 volts. No alarms yet. :)

When removing the battery, don't try to unplug terminal lug wires. Pull out the small pig-tail plug near the center of battery (left side).
It has a little handle, you can grab.
Release the plastic hook clamp and pull out the battery. Now you can pull the wire terminals off the battery lug tabs.
If they are stuck, use a small standard screwdriver to 'drive' the connectors off the battery tabs,
by tapping the screwdriver handle with a tiny hammer (or a large screwdriver handle).

Being careful not to bent the new battery tabs, Install the pig tail onto the new battery.
The large red connector goes on the '+' /Positive/Red side.
Clip the battery into the Fios box, push in the small pig-tail plug and you are done.

I'm not sure, but I suspect the Fios box runs tests on the battery, if the voltage
isn't just right, it will set off the beep alarm. (Followed by an email from Verizon).
Simply un-plugging and re-plugging in the battery will reset it for a while. Sometimes for months.

One Year Later:
At the beginning of this month (April 2014), the FIOS box dead-battery beeper started up again!
I could not believe my new battery only lasted one year! So, I wanted to charge it up and test it.
So, I pulled it out of the FIOS box and connected it to a 12V solar charge controller.
Without a battery, the Beeping was continuous! So, I found the old battery that I had pulled out last April,
plugged it in and no more beeping! Peace at last..

So, it's been over three weeks now.. What's up with the old battery? Maybe it wasn't so bad after all..?.
Now my plan is to leave it installed and swap it out with the new one, when the beeping starts again..

review_body: I bought it thinking that it was going to be scratch resistant and it isn't. Like the previous review, I was also thinking that since it was a premium product, it was going to work better, but to start, it is hard to know what is the side that will be sticking to the glass. This multitool is the very best that I have encountered amongst those that will fit on a key-ring or key-chain.

Unlike the [[ASIN:B003WWRDDA ST50016]], which offers a nice selection of 9 tools but which won't stay on my key-ring, the ST53500 has not managed any escapes.

It is rather larger than earlier generations of this general line of tool, and you might want to look at the [[ASIN:B001AY2WLU ST53100]], or the [[ASIN:B004MDSPS0 MPCSTC]] if you think that a more compact tool might be better. (You could also consider the 6-in-1 [[ASIN:B0001EFSUC Mtcss]], or [[ASIN:B0001WOLUM ST56002]]. I don't think that they are as good a choice as is the 8-in-1 [[ASIN:B0001WOLU2 MPTBS]] or the 9-in-1 [[ASIN:B004MDSPS0 MPCSTC]]; the finer screw drivers have definitely been helpful to me.)

I admit that I have not got much use from most of the functionality that this tool offers beyond that provided by the [[ASIN:B004MDSPS0 MPCSTC]], but the two hex wrenches (in the jaws of the pliers) have been useful. (If Swiss+Tech made an 11-in-1 by adding those hex wrenches to at 9-in-1, then it would be a very nifty tool indeed!)

review_body:
This is a light weight durable Spoiler. You will not have to change your trunk springs. It bolts down to your trunk. Here are a few tips to assist you in your installation.

1. Do not drill 8 mm holes as the manufacture suggest. The drill bit is smaller. I took the screws to Home Depot and
they recommended a 4.32 mm drill bit. It was perfect. You can always go bigger, but I would not suggest that.
2. Honda has pre-set drill spots in the trunk on each side. Looks like 2 dots on your Trunk.
drill those out with the 4.32 mm metal drill bit. Your spoiler will line up perfectly.
3. There is a 2006-2007 video on You Tube--I suggest you watch it before you drill holes in your trunk.
4. Do not use the manufactures template to drill your holes. Honda already has drill spots marked in your trunk; use
these along with you 4.32 mm drill bit.
5. Use a little clear caulk on the holes once you drill them out to prevent rusting.
6. Don't rush, take your time
7. I was very surprised that the installation was super easy
8. Gives your vehicle a great sporty look--
9, Happy customer in Winston-Salem, NC

product_title: Firstgear Scout IV Leather Jacket
review_body:
Too bad they don't make them anymore, nor any textile version of the same design. The pockets and venting are ingenious. It has three pockets accessible from the inside: these include an side breast pocket of the usual design, closeable at the top by velcro; another interior breast pocket on the opposite side closeable by vertical zipper; and a dedicated cell phone pocket. On the outside it has the two flapped breast pockets, but these are not the usual shallow ordinary pockets. Instead, they open all the way down to the bottom hem of the jacket, on both sides. To either side of the main front zipper are two vertical vent zippers that open almost to the bottom hem, and inside, running along these zippers is a few centimeter-wide perforated lining that when fully unzipped allows an enormous amount of air to cool your torso. Inside these columns of perforated lining on each side is a long vertical velcro strip, that can be opened for full access to the deep front pockets. And inside both these front pockets are a variety (five in all) of medium and small pockets that secure all manner of cargo, all of which can be reached through the flaps or by opening the full velcro strips paralleling the vent zippers, with still plenty of room in the full deep pocket space for still more cargo. Not that you'd want to weigh yourself down with heavy gear, but the point is flexibility of purpose. The jacket has a two snap-two position collar, and hand pockets at the sides. It is made of sturdy cowhide, dyed black. The sleeves also have two snap-two position cuffs, with vent zippers running vertically from the cuffs, secured by webbing inside. The jacket is made of rugged cowhide, with nylon liner. It also has double and triple-layer reinforcement of stress points all around, with corrugated leather-covered elastic paneling under the armpits and along the bottom hem on the back and sides. It has medium-stiff shoulder and elbow pads. Mine is a nominal 4XLT, I think it was the largest size, and their actual fit is probably a size smaller than you'd expect in girth, but fine for tallness including sleeve length. The jacket is very well built and mine is holding together as good as new after years of use. Although the venting cools you off when moving, it is a full leather jacket and can be hot if you're stopping a lot in city traffic. But next time you're moving again, it airs itself out as well as you. I've never had to clean mine except to lightly sponge off sprayed mud and kamikaze bugs.

It was quite expensive, made in China; I think mine was over $ 400, so maybe they didn't sell enough to continue the line.

review_headline: E-Brake Pedal Dress Up Pad install tip.
review_body: The Emergency brake pedal doesn't fit my 2011 Challenger as advertised. Trimming will just ruin it so don't. I did install it on my car and it complements the other Mopar factory pedals. I removed the original pedal from the E-Brake assembly and mixed up some 3M 08115 Panel Bonding material from my Body Shop. This is an extremely strong epoxy used to bond sheetmetal panels in the automotive industry. A generous amount  of epoxy to fill the cavity on the back of the new pedal pad and stacked the glued pad to the top of the original pad. Be sure to clean the original pad with hot soap and water to remove any mold release agents and of course dry completely. Leave the stacked pads overnight to cure and trim any excess glue with an exacto knife. The next morning simply slip on the original pad to the E-Brake assembly and the piggy backed metal pad will remain on top!

product_title: CURT 13703 Adjustable RV Trailer Hitch
review_headline: Curt Manufacturing 13703 Class III Receiver Hitch
review_body:
Purchased this trailer hitch for the back of my 2008 Jayco fifth wheel trailer to be able to tow my boat. Upon delivery, I noticed that the box was damaged on the corners and had a few holes in the side. I could see the nuts and bolts protruding from the holes. After I opened the box. I had to collect all of the loose parts that somehow came out of the provided plastic bag. All the parts were contained in the box so I scheduled time for the installation.
My trailer is built on a I beam frame. In order to install the hitch at the rear of the frame, I had to remove the two rear stabilizers, cut the 4" square bumper supports off of the side of the I beam's and cut and relocate the rear support for the plastic belly pan. After grinding the surface smooth I placed the side brackets in the I beam and drilled the hole's (4 per side) and the holes in the draw bar. (2 per side) I had to sharpen the 7/32 drill bit after each use. After drilling the 12 holes I proceeded to install the brackets and draw bar. The bolts and provided mounting washers were easy to install. The four bolts in the draw bar took some work to get in a position to accommodate the over sized washers. All nuts were torqued to 75 foot pounds as stated in the instructions.
I had to install mounting plates for the 4" square bumper and welded them to the back of the I beam in the original location and re install the two rear stabilizers in a new location.
The installation of the hitch was relativity quick and easy. All of the preparation to accommodate the hitch took a while to complete. Use of grinders, cut off wheels, cold chisels and a wire feed welder.
The hitch is built strong and should not have any issues towing my boat behind my fifth wheel.

review_body:
I was going crazy, the bottom right tab would not go in, so I had a gap at the bottom right. Finally, I decided to remove the billet allen wrench screws so that I could get at it easier. The top and bottom screws, I found are just for looks, and don't need to be removed. Remove the other 4 and the outside comes off, then I was able to get the bottom right clip to properly clip on. Now it looks great. If yours is like mine and all 4 clips don't catch, don't give up.

While I'm at it, a couple of removal tips. The instructions are just silly pictures, this should help: As far as the taillights are concerned, the instructions look like you have to remove all the 4 screws, you only have to remove the 2 inboard screws. Also, don't try to push the filler in like the instructions seem to show, it won't move and will just frustrate you. Better to just pull the old opening out. The rubber gasket will come off the filler tube no problem.

More money than the other ones, but this one is a perfect fit ( no gap) now. I say pay a little more and get the real deal.

product_title: CPS Products TLJ2 R-12 1/4" Injector A/C Oil Refill 2 oz. Capacity"
review_body:
Not too much I can say about this. It's made very well out of high quality materials and works as it should.

I knew I needed to add some oil to my home's R-22 central air system after finally finding and repairing the leak that the "Professional" HVAC techs left me with after butchering up the system during a furnace replacement. I had puddles of oil forming on top of the furnace below where the refrigerant lines entered the plenum. The pinhole leak was due to a faulty (overheated) brazed connection and could only be seen (due to its location) with a mirror. It took me two years (off and on) to find it. By that time, and after several refrigerant top-offs and oil clean-ups, I knew at least a few ounces of oil had been lost. This tool was exactly the right thing for adding that oil during the re-charge and there were no issues or surprises.

Note to other DIYers:
If you have the equipment, and know how to charge an A/C system but are stymied by the high cost of R-22 and/or the inability to buy it, read on... I used a hydrocarbon (HC) blend refrigerant called "R-22a" that has resulted in my 17yr old system being considerably more efficient that it ever was with straight R-22. And it requires only 40% by weight compared to R-22 to achieve full charge (1oz. R22a is equal to 2.5oz. R-22). It's compatible with R-22 and mineral oil so it can even be used to top off an existing system. It has no impact on the ozone layer so requires no license nor certification to buy it. Just google R22a or envirosafe.

This year I brought the battery inside and put it back on the mower when the season came. The battery was down enough to not be able to start the lawn tractor so I put this charger on it... the charger green light came on which is fully charged... but it wasn't. I put my larger metered charger on and the meter needle went to change and after 3 minuets I cranked the mower... so much for the charger not being the problem. This is a defective charger and so far they will not replace it.
I gave it one star on behalf of the company not sending a replacement. I know you can get defective products from time to time but the company should make it good. I just wrote them again... lets see what happens this time!

product_title: 2004 04 Honda Accord Uncut Transponder Key
review_headline: It's a key. A few pointers...
review_body:
A key is a key. It doesn't have the cute little silver H on it, but I don't buy keys because they look cool and I want to show them to my friends...I buy them for their functionality...and this one works as expected...it opens the door and turns the car on...once cut and programmed.

Be mindful, if you have two keys and are making a third it's no big deal because they use two keys to program the third. If you only have one key you will pay through the nose. That being said...if you have it cut and programmed at the dealership you will likely pay through the nose anyway...and they are grumpy about not getting to charge you 4-5 times the price you can pick them up for on Amazon. (My dealership, for example, wanted $60 for this key or $90 for the one with a remote and another $35-50 to cut and program...and that's if you already have two keys! If you only have one key you can add another $40-50.) Some say that dealerships will cut and program as a courtesy...and perhaps some do if you buy one of their keys for $60-90...but all the dealerships within 50 miles of me will charge you out the waazoo.

My recommendation, buy the key here on Amazon and make a few phone calls to local locksmiths to find one that can cut and program these keys. It will be roughly half the price and in my opinion...totally worth it.

Despite these negatives, its just a hitch, the fitment was great and the hitch was $30 cheaper so I'm happy.

UPDATE: 4-3-14 Approx. one year after purchase. The welds failed today when towing a ditch witch, well within the weight capacity for this hitch. I have initiated a return request.

product_title: NPN ACC Cabin Filter for select  Volvo models
review_body:
Purchased a WIX 24821 from the local parts supply house last year. It looks exactly like the NPN ACC Filter and is not charcoal impregnated but instead has the BioShield® 75 coating which is suppose to be better than charcoal. The WIX Filter definitely has superior craftsmanship and filtered the air exceptionally well. The intake side was black and with a layer of debris while the underside was still in very good shape after 1 year.

The NPN's material seems to be good quality but the glue used to attached the seal and filter media did not work and any handling will cause it to come off or separate. Had to use Rhino Grip Double-Sided Acrylic Adhesive Strip to reattach 40% of the round seal and one entire end of the filter media to the black frame which separated due to poor quality and inadequate amount of glue. If the filter does not work well to eliminate odor from outside air it will be back to the WIX's again next year.

UPDATE: The BioShield® 75 eliminates outside air smell and AC Odor better than Charcoal. For around $4.00 more going with WIX again next year.

product_title: Chemical Guys Easy Grip Soft Hex Logic Applicator Pad 12345
review_headline: Perfect solution for cleaning bathtub grime
review_body:
I purchased this brush specifically for scrubbing soap scum in our bathtub and shower. It does a great job, used with Comet scouring powder, on an 18 volt cordless drill at about 500 rpm. This company also makes the same size drill brush with \\"firm\\" bristles (red nylon); this yellow nylon is \\"medium\\" firmness.

Durability: After 20 minutes of use, the bristles are starting to bend a little, but show no noticeable wear. It looks like I might get at least 20 bathtub cleanings out of this brush before it is worn out.

Ease of use: Not too bad, a little tendency to skip around, but no worse than I expected. If you have a drill with a side handle, like the 1/2\\" heavy-duty drills often have, it will be easier to control the brush. Overall rating: Highly satisfied, I would buy another one, and will probably buy the red-bristle \\"firm\\" model next. Cleaning bathtub soap scum is one of the worst chores in any home, this brush makes the task at least a lot faster and more bearable, if not exactly fun.

UPDATE: August 2013. I also purchased the red \\"firm\\" brush when it was briefly on sale for $14.00. The bristles on the red brush don't feel all that much stiffer than the yellow brush, so I guess either one will work about equally well for general purpose home cleaning. CAUTION: Use of these brushes on fiberglass (bathtubs) or acrylic (countertops) will probably cause visible scratches, especially if used with scouring powder. However, the ease with which they strip soap scum off a bathtub, compared to doing it the hard way, makes me willing to risk a few light scratches.

product_title: Trail Tech TTO Tach/Hour Meter - Silver 72-A00
review_body:
I bought one of these two years ago and installed it on one of my dirtbikes. I liked it so much I bought 2 more for my other bikes.
Today's machines require lots of maintenance and the TTO helps you keep track of your hours. I also like the Tach feature, although I can't verify how accurate it is and it's very difficult to read when you're actually riding. It's good to have a rough idea where you are, so you can keep off the rev limiter. I believe it displays max RPM when you shut down.
The TTO installs easily and will function for about 5 years(according to their rep). It's too bad you can't change the battery, but it's still a good value.
The TTO comes with everything you need. They also make several other more comprehensive devices, but they become more pricey and more tricky to install.
The installation is simple. The unit double-tapes somewhere flat on your bike. I chose the triple clamp under the handlebars. Next, you snake a wire under the gas tank and wrap it around the spark plug boot. I used a ziptie to hold mine in place. Takes about an hour if you remove the tank.
Like most riders, I don't really use the TTO for oil changes and air filters. I do that stuff (WAY too often) basically every ride. Like most people I know, I don't get a chance to ride every day or even every week. I therefore don't like the idea of letting the bike sit with used oil in it. The TTO is better suited for tracking engine hours for overhaul and piston changes etc. I've found myself trying to remember how many motos I did last summer and was scratching my head.

product_title: HONDA CIVIC SEDAN 2013 SPLASH GUARDS GENUINE OEM PART # 08P00-TR0-100A
review_headline: A few tips based for Civic 2013 Ex owners
review_body: I just bought these splash guards.  Someone was kind enough to provide some good tips on here, so I wanted to add a few more tips to supplement the previous poster's tips.  These additional tips might save someone else more time (By the way, I am not sure why Honda didn't make these splash guards standard on the EX--or make the side molding standard on the EX).  If your Civic is new, there is no need for the messy wax. Just a brief pressure wash at the local car wash and afterwards wipe the excess dirt off the front only with a paper towel or old t-shirt.  If you have a water hose at your residence, this will be an added convenience.  After becoming acquainted with the parts, which is done before washing, select a few tools(a short Phillips screw driver with a soft handle, and pliers) and drill your holes on the rear splash guards (see instructions and tip below). You'll ready to begin.  Budget 1-2 hours for this job depending on your skill level and location. The front splash guards only take 3 screws and less than 5 minutes for each side after you orient yourself to the areas in which you'll be screwing. For the front, nothing comes off the car.  Just pierce the three spots with a sharp-pointed object (such as a thumb tack or nail) and screw the screws right in.  Tip: Be sure the wheel is turned so you have enough space to tighten the screws firmly. Be sure not to strip the screws by using a drill (I did this by accident and hope they don't rust--but I brushed paint over my slightly stripped screw tips). The back mud flaps take some time and elbow grease. Start with the passenger side.  Remember, you should have pre-drilled the one hole on each rear mud flap (I don't know why it's not drilled for you.  The whole is used for one large black pop-in thingy). I had a stubby Phillips screw driver that was too long to fit between the wheel and the screw. After some frustration and feeling stuck, I eventually realized that I was going have to buy a micro stubby Phillipsscrew driver, or put the car on a lift, but fortunately I remembered that I could take the wheel off using the jack in the trunk--if needed.  As I was jacking the car in the air to take the wheel off to make room for the screw driver, I notice that jacking the the car alone created the space I needed.  Next, take the four screws out.  Don't be afraid to unhinge the bumper off of several clips. In turn, you'll be able to see your work area.  Next, expect slight frustration as you try to remove the one clip that connects the mini plastic flap to the interior liner. You're suppose to remove this using a small flat head screw driver.  If you can get up under there and perform that kind of surgery, then kudos to you.  I couldn't and had to find a solution.  Because the plastic piece will be trash, and you should have enough parts screws etc., get at the clip with a pliers and pinch of the back of the clip. This destroys the clip, but it is not reused.  Once you get that clip off and the plastic mini factory mud flap is out--set it aside for the trash or recycling bin.  Then, you should be able to quickly fasten the purchased splash guard to the car.  Be sure to tuck the top part behind the interior liner before you start screwing.  Then use your drilled hole (by the way, you should have pre-drill that hole using a 1/4 in drill bit and have taken a pocket knife and gently carved the hole just a tad bit wider--or use the 10mm bit as stated in the instructions).  Afterwards, you're ready for the driver's side. Use the jack again if screw driver space is needed.  This side is a repeat of what you did on the passenger side. However, you will find one more frustrating clip on the bottom of the disposable mini-flap. As you did on the passenger side, Y=you can carefully rip the extra clip off using a pliers, etc.  Net, you'll find a neatly attached drainage hose and clip on the disposable plastic mini flap.  Keep the clip to snap it on the purchased splash guard. The rest is thesame as before.  Afterwards, pat yourself on the back for a job well done. Now, your Civic looks better and is ready for the garbage on the roads.

product_title: RBP J0764-RX3 RX-III Step for Jeep Wrangler 4 Door SUV
review_headline: Does not fit 2011 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited model
review_body: The J0764-RX3 RX-III Step by RBP is built and packaged extremely well however it will not even come close to fitting a 2011 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited.  In fact it seems unlikely it could fit the 2012 or 2013 models either.  RBP includes 4 spacers to help it fit \\"newer\\" models but you would need more than a 2\\" thick spacer to get even close to fitting a 2011 model.  The shape of the step across the length does not conform to the body shape of the newer models.  Unless you are ready to do some extensive metal work and welding, I'd avoid considering this model until RBP does a design update.  Also be aware that the product is designed to hang low.  While hanging low makes it easier to get into the Jeep, it might be a problem for off-road use. It also fully exposes the pinch welds where the original rock rail attaches. Finally, the Amazon fitment selector indicates that this product will fit a 2011 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited, or it did when I wrote this review, but it definitely does not fit the vehicle.

product_title: Bosch ICON Wiper Blade
review_headline: A good value given their durability
review_body:
I've had these on my car for a little over a year and a half. (I know, because Amazon just reminded me of my prior order as I checked out the product page to order another set.) Only now are they starting to show signs of aging. Before these, I had wipers from Rain-X (two different kinds) and while they cost about 75% as much, they lasted 30% of the time. You do the math.

In case you're not familiar with them, Bosch is the company that actually makes the OEM wiper blades for many high end cars (like BMW, for one). In fact, you'd probably be surprised by how much inside your car is made by Bosch. So, you're not buying from a company that is just marketing cheap parts made in China and selling it with a lot of marketing. You're getting OEM quality with these, if not better. So, when considered in that light, as well, these blades really aren't that expensive.

So, the blades really do last, but will you be happy with them while they do? I think so. They hold the shape of the windshield well, and never flap or vibrate, no matter how fast you're going. The bracket is solid, and worked well on the J-hook in my car. Many other \\"universal\\" mounts didn't work so well, notably the ones from the aforementioned Rain-X wipers.

They don't streak or chatter, and even after having them on my car for over a year, they are only streaking a small amount.

Given that your eyes are the most important safety device on your car, you owe it to yourself to not skimp on wiper blades. But I'm pleased to report that despite the upfront cost, these are actually MORE cost effective than many other premium wiper blades, given that they are the only expensive wiper blades I've ever used that actually lasted longer than the cheap ones.

Tip: the A or the B after the model number (e.g. 22A) refers to the spring force of the blade (i.e. how hard it is to pull it straight). The B applies more force, and would be useful if you have a highly curved windshield. The fact that Bosch offers not just a variety of lengths down the inch, but also two different spring forces, is another indicator of the fact that these are not your average wiper blades. I found that having an A on the driver side and a B on the passenger side works best on my car. If in doubt, just try A all around, and then if you find that the blade is missing spots on the ends of the blade, return the A and get a B.

Last tip: Amazon's database is helpful, but by no means complete. If you think this will fit your car, but Amazon says it won't, ignore Amazon. They say neither blade I have on my car will work, and yet I'm extremely happy with them, as you can tell.ndshield. review_body:
I bought My Ford Focus about a month ago and noticed what seemed to be hiccups in the acceleration at low RPM's. I looked online for a new air intake and came onto this one from K&N. On top of fixing the acceleration, I was looking for a little more power and better fuel economy.

So far 2 out of the 3 have been fixed. Still working on getting the data for the MPG.

I did come across this on another site for about $230 with a coupon code so deals are out there for a great price.

It took me about an hour and a half to install and was pretty easy with the great step by step instructions they sent with it. After the install it ran with a little more whistle and growl coming from under the hood. Getting used to the new noise but if you have the radio on at about a 5 it isn't noticeable. The acceleration is a lot better between 1.5 - 3 RPM's and is finally nice and smooth. Once the motor is broken in I will start driving it a little harder.

I use a Mileage app on my phone to track my fuel economy and with stock everything I was getting 32.08 Avg MPG on 4 fill-ups (Standard Trans). I will be updating the fuel economy within a month for MPG with the air intake. My guess is that it will be around the same but hope for at least a couple MPG better.

UPDATE** 4 fill-ups later I am now at 35.025 MPG on average. One trip helped significantly because it was all highway and ended up with 40.7 MPG (Coasting and Drafting trailer trucks)

I will add a few more fill-ups and see where it falls to. I am definitely getting better MPG but depending on your driving the results will vary. ALL and ALL LOVE THE INTAKE**

UPDATE 2** 13 fill-ups later I am now at 36.718 MPG. Last Highway trip 42.92 MPG!!

product_title: Bosch Engine Crank Position Sensor
review_body:
Does you car rattle, but the engine mounts and the throttle body are good?
Do you have bad mpg, but have no CEL?
Has your car ever stuttered beyond 2000rpm and then suddenly stopped doing it?
Was your car ever unable to start when the engine was warm, but started fine after a while?

Any of these symptoms may mean that you need a new CPS sensor. CPS sensors often fail somewhere in the 100k mile range. If you are suspicious, just change it. It will save you from trouble on a road trip! I have also seen 1-2mpg enhancement on my SAABs after changing the sensor. The sensor is not expensive, so just change it before your car stops at the most inconvenient place!

product_title: Powerbuilt
review_headline: Looks like a great jack concept... but did not last. At least they had good service?
review_body:
I purchased a a pair of these in August 2012 and received them both in working order. I did NOT buy them from Amazon.com, which is probably a good thing in retrospect. I purchased it directly from the manufacturer's website for cheap (they only sell Powerbuilt tools). They were listed as new, not refurbished.

When I received them, one bottle jack had rust on the piston and on the base. I promptly called the vendor and they graciously replaced it, no charge whatsoever. They didn't even ask me to ship the defective one back. Overall great service there.

It's now February of 2013, a little more than half a year later. Having only used these jacks twice, maybe three times, they are now no longer working. I didn't see any fluid leaking but now the bottle jack is not functioning. These were stored in on the bottom shelf of an insulated garage. I was hoping to use them to jack my car up this weekend, but nope - they are now just regular jack stands.

I'm contacting the vendor again to see if they will warranty it. I'm hoping it goes well and I end up with two more units, but who knows -- maybe in another six months, I'll just have 4 regular jacks...

EDIT: The manufacturer replied back right away. They'll be sending me replacements. 1-star for the product, 5-stars for the manufacturer's customer service.

review_headline: Works well, but be careful installing
review_body: I installed this product approx 5 mos ago in my 2002 F250 pickup. Buy the longer wiring kit, or use your own (I used 4 conductor trailer wire) for the install. I put the front strobes up through the bottom of the turn signal housings, and the rear in the back-up lights. The factory wiring connectors are NOT weatherproof and corroded with the moisture and salt here in New England. (The front ones are up behind the headlights and the rear ones are up behind the tail lights)  I recommend you remove these wire connectors and solder and heat-shrink in this location at the time of installation or at least cover the connectors with liquid electrical tape. BTW, I installed the controller under the dash just below the steering column. The lights work great especially at night. Without indicator lights of the on/off and "mode" switches you can't tell what pattern they are in unless you get out of the truck and look. Overall a great product for the price, just wish the wiring connectors at the strobe ends were weatherproof.

product_title: Nissan Altima 2002 2003 2004/Murano 2003 2004 2005 /Infiniti Fx35/45 2003 2004 2005 2006 Halo Projector Fog Lights - Smoke /1 pair
review_headline: Nice looking halo fog lamp. recommend getting the clear one.
review_body:
I originally ordered these smoked Halo Lights for my 06 FX35. Ended up getting 2 sets of the smoked ones and then the Clear ones. I really like the clear set.

2 main issues:
1. The smoked ones are not a consistent shade of darkness. The set I received had one really dark one and one lighter one. I received a second set, and out of the 2 I was able to get a pair that had a pretty close shade. the company should (And maybe by now has) make sure the tint matches.
2. The smoked lights are pretty dim. The tinting cuts out a lot of the light (the darker ones were almost useless for a light.

If you really want to have a tinted pair, you're probably better off getting the clear ones and tinting them yourself.

Also these do not fit the 06 FX35 without modification. There are side wings that sick out, and prevent the light from going into the fog lamp opening. I had to cut them off in order to make it work. I believe there was a bumper modification between the 05 and 06 FX models, so I would guess it will work fine on the earlier models.

The installation instructions have a good wiring diagram. there are basically 2 switches, one for the halo and one for the projector lamp. I ended up running the halo to the DTRL/ACC circuit, and connecting the projector to the stock circuit.

I will try to dig up some pictures to add.

product_title: Sunforce 82156 60-LED Solar Motion Light
review_headline: Allow nature to help you save money - with one correction on the instructions
review_body: 3rd UPDATE Jan 29, 2015  So by now I have installed these 3 solar lights for around 2 years.  They are still working great.  The one in the backyard didn't come on one night after heavy rain as I forgot to cover it with clear plastic bag before hand.  But the next day, the sensor was working again - probably after it dried out.  Having tried them out myself, I bought 2 more in 2014.  Continue to strongly recommend these lights.     2nd UPDATE Sept 30, 2013  My two solar lights are still going strong.  My electric bills have been in the $30 something range.  I had a battery powered motion sensor light for the side porch but that went out after 6 months.  Bought a 3rd solar light to replace the battery powered one.  Still very happy.    1st UPDATE April 8, 2013  Want to share a couple of updates on these solar lights.  1.  I shared that with one Solar Light up, my electricity bill was down to $48.48 in Jan.  With both lights up for Feb and March,  electricity bills are down to $36.xx a month.  2.  These lights are rated weather resistant. I'm concerned about them getting trenched in heavy rain.  I moved the lights to under the roof on the outside walls.  But solar panels have to remain in direct sunlight (which means direct rain also) for the batteries to be charged enough to produce bright lights.  I had put one under the eaves of the roof, indirect sunlight does not produce as bright a light.  3.  I cover the solar panels with clear plastic bags during heavy rain to keep them from getting trenched.  Only once so far in So Cal.  4.  The lights are holding up very well so far. (2 and 3 months into setting them up)    ORIGINAL REVIEW, February 7, 2013  DEMONSTRATED SAVINGS  Let me get to the bottom line savings before I tell you about these products.  We installed the first one on Jan 5, 2013 and the second one about 20 days later.  Averaging our electricity bills for 2012 not counting the spikes when central A/C or Heat was used, the average monthly bill was $68.  After having installed 2 Sunforce solar lights and 1 battery powered LED light to replace the usage of 3 other lights, our Jan bill that just arrived is $48.48. LOWEST in all of the bills for the years 2010, 2011 and 2012. WOW!! So how did we do it?    BEFORE SUNFORCE LIGHTING SITUATION  We have 4 outside lights that come on every night at dusk and they stay on till the sun comes up again the next day.  2 of them are flood lights - 1 in front yard and 1 in back yard. The other 2 are porch lights - 1 in the front and 1 at the side.    AFTER SUNFORCE LIGHTING SITUATION  We installed the Sunforce solar light on Jan 5 and turned off the flood light in the front yard.  We also installed a battery powered motion sensor LED light in place of the side porch light.  Then we installed the 2nd Sunforce solor light in the backyard Jan 25 and turned off the flood light there.    OTHER ELECTRICITY SAVING MEASURES TAKEN  We also take a couple of other minor measures to reduce electricity usage thus costs.  I turn off the power strip where all the stereo, hi fi, Blu Ray, Karaoke and TV are plugged when we are not using any of these electronics.    I have 2 laptops and a light that plug to a power strip that I use everyday.  I turn off the power strip when I don't use the laptops.    CORRECTION ON PRODUCT INSTRUCTIONS  There are 3 dials for the Sunforce so you can adjust for how dark/light the light comes on, how long it stays on and for the motion sensor.  The instructions say to turn the dial to Maximum (the icon of the sun) if you don't want it to come on during the day.  And that's is wrong.  The way you should use the dial for light sensitivity is this - if you want the light to come on at night, turn the dial to the MOON icon.  If you want the light to come on during day light, turn the dial to the SUN icon.  Then you can adjust to anywhere between bright (SUN) and dark (MOON)    CURRENT RECOMMENDATION  So as you can see, these solar lights do help me save money so I do recommendthem.  The only area I cannot comment on is how durable they are.  I've read reviews that some die soon.  So I'll be watching out for mine and provide update if they die prematurely.

product_title: 2013-2014 Dodge Dart All Weather Slush Floor Mats

Nothing beats OEM Mopar parts. Like everyone else, I wanted to add sporty touches to my new 2013 Dart SE. You can get some beautiful, white letter aftermarket \\"Dart\\" logo floor mats, but get these instead (he said). Why? I asked. Because these rubber slush mats will protect the carpet and keep your new Dart new. Did I mention my mechanic is a genius? And totally right. Fortunately my sister had given me an Amazon gift card for my birthday which was burning a hole in my pocket. What better way to spend it than to protect my new Dart?

I ordered these through Amazon from Avondale Automotive in Arizona, which has amazingly fast shipping, and these new Mopar mats are even better than they look in the photos. They are thick, heavy, grooved black rubber with \\"Dart\\" in raised letters on the front two mats. The mats fit perfectly into the hooks in the Dart carpeting, which keeps them in place. They not only feel great, adding a spongy, resilient surface to rest your feet on, but catch rocks, dirt, leaves, mud and snow, and look great as well. Noir on noir. It doesn't get better than basic black, which accents the entire Dart interior scheme. Sporty and functional. Like everything about the 2013 Dodge Dart, it's win-win.

product_title: INNOVA 3320 Auto-Ranging Digital Multimeter
review_headline: Nice meter, but auto-ranging is failing
review_body:
I got this meter for Christmas 2011 (sadly, this probably wasn't my most nerdy gift). I've been using it a good amount since then, and it works for the most part. I really like the audio continuity finder.

Unfortunately, the auto-ranging function has been acting up for a few months now. When I try to measure the voltage across something, it will frequently beep at me and say it's overloaded. In essence, it isn't choosing the correct range for the voltage measurement. I tried new batteries, but the problem persists. Unfortunately, the voltage function is my main use of the meter, so this limits its usefulness.

I have since purchased a \\"lesser model\\" Equus that lets me choose the range (sadly it does not have the continuity finder). My advice: if you really want or need an auto-ranging device, spend some extra money to get one that is built to last. Otherwise just get a manually ranged one. It is trivial to manually choose the correct range for measurement. Don't ask a budget device to think for you.
