product_title: PPA International OLSMSRGB OLS Motor Series Multi-Color Starter Kit
review_headline: a kit to add LED color lighting inside your vehicle
review_body:
This is a do-it-yourself kit designed for anyone who'd like to add these color lighting effects to the interior of their vehicle. There are 2 panels of LED lights which you connect to the controller and power via a connection to a DC/cigarette lighter adapter or the vehicle battery. It's got a modular connection design, so you can connect additional LED panels and extension cables if you wish. There is tape and velcro for you to secure the cables, though the cables are hard to keep hidden and the controller remote requires direct line of sight for the signal to work. The installation instructions seemed a bit incomplete but overall were adequate for me to get everything hooked up. The cable connections have arrows for you to align and it is recommended to use electrical tape to secure the connection between the controller and the DC adapter [that connection is loose unless you do something to secure it]. For novices, using the DC plugin power adapter is preferrable to trying to hook the wires directly to a battery. Oddly, the kit recommends professional installation even though it seems to be marketed for do-it-yourself installation.

The main problem I encountered during installation was that it wouldn't power on until I opened up the remote control battery compartment and discovered that the battery had come installed upside down. Once I flipped it into the correct position everything worked fine and I got to enjoy the colored lights. This is a simple way to add colored lighting in your vehicle, while a true do-it-yourself veteran could probably obtain needed components to install something similar at a lower cost. This kit might contain either more than you need or less than you require for the amount of lighting that you intend to install, so it may not be the best option for everyone.

If you drive an average vehicle 25K a year it should be changed after four years.

product_title: Rand McNally TripMaker
review_body:
We purchased this GPS to supplement our TomTom, believing it would be more helpful as it was designed to deal with our size issues - 40' motorhome with tow vehicle, making us 66' total length. We left home Jan. 10th & are currently in Las Cruces, NM. So far, this nightmare has sent us down a road that ended in an 8' high underpass (wide enough for a car!), told us to go down another road to turn around that was a dead end without any maneuverability, taken us to an RV park that doesn't exist (and apparently never did!), and avoids telling us vital info such as stay in left lane (thanks.... we wound up in a right-turn only lane without any way to get off it until we left the freeway! Major issues finding our way back ON to the freeway!).

As for emailing Rand McNally? Don't waste your time.... 3 attempts to reach them, no effort on their part to respond. We also have a TomTom - which assumes we're a car. That being said, we've buried the TripMaker in a drawer & have gone back to using our TomTom! Over the years, I've emailed TomTom a few times & they've ALWAYS gotten back to me within 24 hours! Our unwanted detours are fewer, and the prompts necessary to keep us on the freeway are reliable! If I thought I could dump this Rand McNally nightmare back with Camping World, I would. Sadly, I think we've had it too long, altho' I may still give it a try. Over $300 spent for safety, and we've been worse off than before we started!

There are other issues with this GPS, but my primary problem with it is the safety concerns. When you have a GPS purchased specifically for an RV & for whatever reason, it's sending you down a road that's barely negotiable with a Smart car, why spend the money????

I have 5 RV'ing friends who were waiting for my review on this product before purchasing it themselves. 3 guesses what they'll be doing.... I've encouraged them to purchase something else! It's my guess Garmin or TomTom will have 5 sales thanks to me!

product_title: Meguiar's M39 Mirror Glaze Heavy Duty Vinyl Cleaner and Microfiber Cloths Bundle
review_headline: Best vinyl cleaner I have ever used!
review_body: A friend and I were invited to participate in an article for Muscle Car Review that was covering proper care and preservation of older paint jobs that was held down at Meguiars in Costa Mesa, CA.  The writer of the article decided to include a section devoted to vinyl care since my 27 year old white vinyl top on my '67 GTO definitely needed some TLC.  I had tried various commercial products over the years without success, and had even tried Simple Green and Purple Power that also failed to really clean the top.  Mike, the Meguiars tech, worked a small area at a time with very little effort until he had expanded the cleaned area out to about a one foot square.That portion of vinyl literally looked like new.  Since this was for a magazine article, that's where they stopped after getting the necessary photos for the article.  Although I was a little worried (OK, very worried) that the remainder of roof might never equal what a professional had done, I arrived home and placed my Amazon order for the #39 cleaner along with other products they had used on my paint with excellent results.  Well, the cleaner arrived yesterday, and we finished cleaning the roof by doing a small section at a time and working the cleaner in with a brush and then wiping off the cleaner and dirt.  While it was a slow process, it was not tedious or hard work.  Our finished result looked every bit as good as the spot cleaned down at Meguiars, and we cannot tell where they started and we finished the cleaning - and we know where the two joined up.  We did use a full bottle on the roof, but it really had a lot of embedded dirt that had to be removed.  I'll see if I can't post up a picture where we cleaned up to the tape with the other side of the taped area not touched yet.  We also found that a short, soft bristled brush worked best in getting into the pockets and lifting out the dirt.  On a side note, the guys also tested out the #40 cleaner on the vinyl roof and it was just about half as effective cleaning the roof.  I'm ordering more bottles of the #39 and going after my vinyl seats next.

product_title: Mossi Black Premium Leather Fingerless Gloves
review_headline: Mystery solved! Very nice "Raider" premium Made-in-USA deerskin gloves
review_body:
Several previous reviewers thought they received the wrong product because these gloves come carded as \\"Raider Premium Leather...#BCS-702\\" gloves.
So did we...who wouldn't?
So we checked with the company, BCS Brands, directly, and we were told, quote/unquote:
\\"The BCS-702 are indeed Raider Leathers...There was an error when listing this item. Our leather gloves are under the brand name Raider. Mossi is another one of the BCS Brands.\\"
Thus, the mystery has been solved: BCS Brands carries both the \\"Raider\\" and \\"Mossi\\" lines, but these gloves should have been listed under the \\"Raider\\" name.
The quality is still \\"premium\\"...in fact, they are made in the good old USA of deerskin, and they are very cool and functional...whether you're driving, riding or doing manual labor.
If anyone would like to reach Raider directly, their \\"888\\" number is:
888-965-3700.
We hope that this helps anyone looking at these gloves...which we highly recommend at this price point...they are good stuff...and their customer service has been responsive as well!

product_title: Tekonsha 90195 P3 Electronic Brake Control
review_headline: Works as good as i hoped
review_body:
Works great! makes the truck and trailer feel as one when stopping and light breaking through tight corners. I bought this to help tow a 12 X 7 tandem axle cargo trailer using my 05' F150, 5.4 with tow package. it connected easy using the 2 pin harness recommended by amazon for $20.00.

The display is easy to navigate, and settings easy to control. I opted to turn off the break surge selection, because I did not like the trailer breaking disproportional to the truck. With that off I hardly notice that I'm pulling a trailer. My only complaint is that the display is on all the time. If the truck is on the controller is on, even when I turn off the truck the controller stays on as long as the the walk away lights are on.

I mounted the controller in a low positioned dash pocket, centered underneath the cup holder, and secured it using hook and loop strips ( heavy duty Velcro) by pulling out the pocket I was able to cut a hole at the top of the pocket to run my wire to the back of the controller. That way when I remove the controller you don't see a big hole.
All an all im happy with this and would buy it again.

product_title: TagsForDroid 5 NFC Tags + 1 NFC Key Chain + Stickers (MIFARE 1K)
review_body:
Ordering these tags was my first foray into the world of NFC and they make a great starter pack. Five of the tabs are peel-n-stick and one's a keychain. Set comes with stickers to label each tag for specific uses. They are compatible with my Droid DNA and seem to work well *most* of the time. I've encountered recurring write errors on tag from new, but the rest seem to be fine. The tricky one requires that I first erase it first then re-write new instructions, whereas the others seem to allow this all in one step with the NFC Task Launcher program.

Tag reading on the DNA works fairly well, but if the tag isn't centered just so over the NFC antenna it won't work. I'm using an Androidified smoked/clear plastic case and it works through that. I'd be skeptical if it works through something thicker like an Otterbox, though.

Overall, a good starter pack at a good price if you're new to NFC.

review_headline: Perfect for 3.6DI V6 CTS Owners! Don't miss!
review_body:
Real quick, before you buy a cold air intake for your CTS 3.6, consider that this filter and your stock airbox are also used for the 6.2 liter CTS-V. That engine is nearly double the displacement of the 3.6 and the engineers with very expensive tools on hand determined it flows enough for the 6.2 liter.

A simple mod of the plastic piece in the front grill will deliver fresh cold air to your airbox intake and you can easily seal this with a foam seal around the intake.

Next, remember that these filters will NOT ruin your car or warranty from oil contamination. The only way this happens is someone incorrectly re-oiling the filter and the excess being sucked into the intake. Personally, I throw my filter away after a few years and just buy another new one, by them the price is the same as paper! This filter is about half the thickness of oem papaer filters.

product_title: Airaid Intake System
review_body: I left a review after I purchased this intake and now I have had the intake for over 6 months now and I have to say its worked out great.  I have a 2012 wrangler unlimited sahara with the 3.6 pentastar motor and the 6spd manual.  since installing the intake I have noticed a few changes as far as power and gas milage.  The jeep is definitely more responsive on the higher revs and the intake screams when I punch it in second or third which is basically why I bought it.  Second the gas milage varies.  at times its very poor  when I first bought the intake my gas milage dropped from 19.2 to around 17.9 driving normally.  Since then I have put about 10,000 miles on the jeep with the intake and gas milage is just about where it usually was at without the intake, which was 19-22 going about 65 every morning for 30 miles each way.  One thing I will tell you is that this intake boosts gas milage big time when going driving at higher speed.  I live in Connecticut and go to school in North Carolina and drove down about about a month ago driving at 80-85 mph and averaged between 23 and 24 miles to the gallon.  IN A JEEP!!  All in all I would definitely recommend getting this Cold Air Intake If you are looking for something that is going to boost performance as well as slightly better gas milage (depending on how you drive) I will tell you that if you drive normally you will not hear it inside the truck.  One of the reasons I purchased this model intake was because it was in an enclosed intake and when I didn't want to hear it I wouldn't.  Something I will recommend though is if you are looking for strong intake sound all the time do not buy this intake buy an AFE stage 2 system for the Pentastar.  My buddy has it in his 2013 unlimited sahara and Ill tell you it is awesomely loud.  Hope this was a help to somebody  and this spring I am planning on lifting the jeep with an AEV 3.5 sc lift and 35\\" tires and I will write another review then.

product_title: K&N PS-7013 Pro Series Oil Filter
review_body:
Had high hopes for this filter and love that it's made in the US. However, when removing it from my 2008 Mazda3 2.3L for an oil change, the filter had been crushed. I'm currently running the [[ASIN:B000SARC4Y K&N HP-7013 Oil Filter]], and will report back how that filter works on the Mazda3 at my next oil change. The OEM filters do not get crushed, so they are definitely a safe choice, and not too expensive if you shop around.

UPDATE: Just did an oil change and the [[ASIN:B000SARC4Y K&N HP-7013 Oil Filter]] worked well with no crushing. I recommend using that filter instead of this one.

Cons: My bike, Harley Dyna Street Bob, is loud, with V+H pipes. My bike sounds louder in this helmet than it does in my half helmet. product_title: Airhawk Medium Cruiser Pad - 14.25in x 15in , Size: Md AH2MED
review_body:
Highly recommend this seat pad. I was skeptical of how much it would help because it's inflatable and because it's an add-on to the stock seat. But I had just rented a stock Harley Electra Glide for a weekend in Wisconsin, after which I had a sore butt. So for my next trip I tried this seat pad. I rented the same Harley Electra Glide and attached this pad. What a difference! I put 2400 miles on that bike in 7 days, camped all around the Black Hills and rode interstates back to Chicago, and wasn't sore a bit! Frankly I was shocked. I owe much of my enjoyment of the trip to this pad - it would have been a way different experience without it.

It seemed to fit the Electra Glide well enough, even though that's a full-size touring bike. And it attached and detached from my rental bike easily enough. It stayed secure, so I really leaned into the corners, dragging my boots on at least 3 occasions. It didn't take long to get used to the feeling of sitting in air. Do pay attention to the instructions (and the other reviews) where it says to INFLATE PARTIALLY and do not inflate all the way! That's key to comfort. You sit "in it", not "on it". It just gets better the more air you let out of it.

I'm definitely keeping this pad to use on future bike rentals.

One of these went with me across a 5 foot deep rushing river where the hood was submerged for over 30 seconds while crossing. Zero hydrolock. I pulled the air box after we crossed the river and it was bone dry on the inside.

My only complaint, if I have one at all, is that with the kind of trail riding I do, I knock off the pre-cleaner at the top occasionally. This isn't a design flaw... more user error. The trick, I've found, is to face the snorkel backward when you're doing slow speed crawls and to add every tie points to the windshield. That kept this from happening as often on tight trails.

product_title: Champion RCJ8Y (863) Copper Plus Small Engine Replacement Spark Plug (Pack of 1)
review_body:
Gotta love the role these fiery little guys play in heaving snow off our cement. A magneto rotates on the engine flywheel inside our two little snow blowers. Every time that magneto passes the ignition coil, high voltage transmits to these spark plugs. The plugs emit a timely spark inside a small cylinder bored in the engine. That tiny spark triggers an explosion inside the cylinder. Here's where it gets really good... The explosion pushes a piston down, which rotates the engine's crankshaft. That spinning crankshaft rotates an auger with rubber paddles. Those spinning rubber paddles scrape the sidewalk---hurling snow up, through a chute, and off to the side. Why? Because these plugs sparked the whole darn process.

Would I recommend these spark plugs? I most certainly would---if your engine specs call for RCJ8Y plugs. ;)

review_headline: Spend the extra $75 for the factory ones
review_body: Purchased both 02 sensors for replacement in my NA 850 without the CA emissions system after getting a CEL for the downstream sensor. Cleared codes and drove car for a few days, CEL came back on indicating a low voltage read from both 02 sensors. Car was smoke checked, and exhaust manifold was replaced because the flex joint was broken (obvious air leak). After this repair, the exhaust was checked again, and got a clean bill of health from Boston Volvo. Car drove great for 4 days, CEL light came on for 1 day and then shut off on it's own (bulb not blown). Drove the car without a light for 5 more days until the CEL light came back on today, indicating low voltage fault codes from both O2 sensors. The 20+ year veteran tech at Boston Volvo says he has never seen an after market sensor with the same precision as factory, and does not recommend using them. Seeing as this guy has worked on 3 different Volvos for me, I'll take his word for it. If he's not right about these parts I'll certainly update this review to ensure due fairness.

product_title: Reese 33018 Class III Custom-Fit Hitch with 2" Square Receiver opening, includes Hitch Plug Cover
review_body:
Probably one of the biggest reasons I give this five stars is that after looking for a hitch reciever that mounts up a behind the bumper, I finally found it! The wife and I had just made a purchase from a local neighbor of a 1972 Venture pop-up trailer for our camping excursions. I made a local purchase at a Chrysler/Jeep dealer for a tow reciever to get the camper home and the parts tech ensured me this was what I was looking for. Nope. It mounted down below the bumper affecting my approach angle of the vehicle. I returned it and had to go back a second time to get my money back. I had already gone ahead and removed the bumper and cut out the area that the reciever comes through and mounted the bezel and attached the wiring to the harness inside the truck. So I was committed. I then contacted another dealership in NY. "Yup, I know what you're talking about", is what I got from this sales person. Nope. Same low hung hitch came in again, shipped across the country. The excuse, "Oh, I've had a problem with the manufacturer." Then after he contacted them about the problem he said that they have discontinued the production for safety reasons of collisions on the rear bumper. Huh?!? Now what? I'm going to need to get a new bumper?!? One key thing he told me was that the manufacturer was Reese. Now I had done research on line previously and probably skipped over this company for some reason or another. I contacted Reese and confirmed the part number and ordered it. The 7-way electrical adapter is already mounted and comes with a nice chrome trimming on the 2" square reciever and even a plug cap. The other hitches I ordered where much more expensive with none of this. I finally towed my new pop-up trailer home!
BTW, I ordered the hitch from NY on Nov. 11th. He sent me a pre-paid UPS receipt for a free return, which was nice of him since he assured me he had the right product. It is now Jan. 7th and am still awaiting my refund.

several days. Eventually the outlets dried out enough and they started working again.

product_title: 2×BT interphone bluetooth motorcycle helmet intercom
review_body:
I got this set from another vendor and so far it has some good points and some bad points. The good point is that the range is phenomenal. We were talking line of sight about half a mile when it went out. But as soon as a car or house or something got between us, the range was seriously decreased. It depended on exactly what it was that was blocking the signal. I also noticed that at the fringe distance the helmet itself would block the signal so I had to turn my head slightly to get a better signal. The official range is only about 1500 feet and its got that and more.

At the fringe, it starts breaking up and chopping. We were just testing it. Normally you would never ride that far apart.

I noticed it making screeching noises every now and then and it seems that it was a loose connection where the mic set plugs into the unit. I think this is what the other reviewer was talking about when he said he heard static. The unit is encased in rubber and its hard to get the plug in all the way so when I pushed a little harder, the noise went away.

Now the bad part. Its not especially easy to get this thing installed in your helmet. The little speakers need to be directly over your ear canal and almost in direct contact.

The speakers are very weak even at full volume. This may prove to be a deal breaker. We can get up to about 30 mph and then the wind noise in our own helmets becomes so loud that we can't understand one another. The noise canceling microphones do a really good job transmitting clear noiseless audio, but if there is wind noise in the helmet, you can't hear the other guy. We know this to be true because my riding partner stayed at the stop sign while I rode off at 60 mph. He said I was clear as a bell, but I couldn't make out anything he said. I don't know how to fix this. Possibly an inline amplifier or better speakers.

One other thing is that I couldn't receive phone calls with this even though a I could dial them. The unit would answer incoming calls involuntarily after 6 seconds, and then I get no audio and the other people can't hear me. I'm not ready to blame the product for this because it could be something wrong with my cell phone.

The volume needs to be about double for this to be a good product. I'm giving it only 3 stars because you can't use it over 30 mph. At those speeds, its easier and cheaper to just yell.

UPDATE: The screeching seems to be confined to making cell phone calls and not to the intercom feature. Wind noise continues to be a problem. We took these on a trip and battery life sucks. We got about 2 hours of continuous intercom use before they died from a full charge. But they will go about 4-5 hours with intermittent use. We tried charging them while on the bikes, but as soon as you plug the USB charger in, the unit cuts off. There is also no apparent way to swap the batteries for fresh ones. But all in all, they did work, but just not as well as I had hoped.

product_title: Schumacher SSC-1500A-CA Ship 'N' Shore 15 Amp SpeedCharge Charger with Battery Clamps
review_body:
I purchased this charger through a local store as a backup to the current charger I use on my boat's battery bank. I'm using a Black and Decker smart charger with 25 amp max, and thought that this new Schumacher charger might be able to do the same job. I was very disappointed with this charger within a few hours after purchase.

Average power consumption onboard is about 2 amps, and at night 7.5 amps, mostly due to heating and charging electronics. I plugged in the charger earlier in the day and let it charge the boat from 80% power to 100%, but was surprised that it wanted to continue its charging cycle after that. The fan stayed on and never shut down, an eventual failure waiting to happen. As soon as my power consumption reached 7 amps, the charger began emitting a beeping sound. I noticed slight power fluctuations throughout these events as my cabin lighting dimmed and returned slightly.

Perhaps the 15 amp fast charge/speed charge ship n shore charger is great for charging batteries, but it did not lend itself to being the heart of an active battery bank without complaining. I'll be returning this to the store tomorrow and seeking a more robust charger, possibly from the same brand as my current one.

review_headline: US Army Motorcycle Jacket - 6055.04/AR385-55 Compliant/ECE Rated
review_body: I have been riding motorcycles for over 14 years now, I have worn plenty of jackets over the years, and this one is up there with some of the best. It comes pre loaded with very comfortable, but highest rated (ECE) inserts on the elbows and back/spine. The elbows are adjustable so you can make sure the inserts sit correctly, and dont interfere with your movements. It has multiple air intakes with adjustable zipper for fully closed in the winter, and fully open in the hot summer. It has 10 channels for air movement (I counted them). The sleves do zip off, but aside from replacing them after a fall I don't really think its necessary. It has plenty of pockets (I have a CHL and I can easily fit any of the 3 concealed carry handguns, including one that is a compact and not subcompact fits on the inside). It has a pocket on the wrist that fits your wallet quite well. Making it much easier than digging in a pocket when you get to the front gate. I personally dont use the ID pouch on the chest because I have to use my CAC card and dont feel like loading and unloading it every ride, but with the sleve/wrist pocket you can carry your wallet in an easy access slot, or in one of the two chest pockets. This jacket is fully 6055.04 compliant, so it meets all DOD motorcycle riding gear regs, and its AR 385-55 Compliant. Which asks that it is a reflective (All US Army Lettering and Emblems are reflective, as well as the elbows where its slightly grey are reflective). It also has a number of 2 inch reflective markers on the back, and the US Army emblem on the back is refelective. This product also has a Official US Army Riding Gear tag on the inside. So if you need a jacket that is functional, meets the regs to ride with, and doesn't look goofy like wearing a construction workers vest, than this is the jacket you need. I love this thing, its very comfortable, cool when you need it, and it comes with a winter liner which (it was 40 degrees yesterday and I came home very warm). I especially like that it meets the ECE ratings (its track legal, and meets all professiona racing requirements), and its DOD/AR compliant but yet looks decent too.

product_title: Tekonsha 90195 P3 Electronic Brake Control
review_body:
I've had lots of brake controllers, had to adjust them every time I towed depending on the load on the trailer (if there was a load) and for the conditions (icy, dry, wet, etc) I forgot to adjust one of mine one time and my wife was driving and we almost had an accident because the controller was set too light and it didn't apply enough trailer brake and my wife didn't realize she just had to squeeze the handle to get some braking power. Yeah, that was my fault for not showing her.

Anyway, got a new to me truck and it needed a controller. I live in Alaska where things are way more expensive than they should be so prior to purchasing a local controller I shopped around. The trailer place in town wanted $250 for this product!!! Good Grief! The cheapest brake controller on the shelves was still almost $90, so for a few extra bucks I purchased this one. A buddy of mine had it and swore by it. Now after owning this one and playing with it for the last few months I completely agree with him. This controller is so easy to use! I haven't adjusted anything, have pulled six different trailers with different varieties of electric brakes (1 axle, 2 axle, really old and sticky brakes, really new and strong brakes, weak brakes, etc) and haven't adjusted a thing. It does the work for you. Plug in the trailer and let her roll. I've only grabbed the slider (manual activation) once per use to verify connection prior to leaving the parking lot.

This unit can tell how hard you are braking and automatically adjusts the trailer brakes to compensate. I've done three emergency stops where I had to slam the brakes and stop quick, This thing added maximum power without any inputs from me except for the brake pedal and did exactly what I asked.

Perfect unit to get for that spouse that's never pulled a trailer with brakes before but wants to assist in driving on your trip. With this she can drive, and you don't have to worry about reminding herto turn up the brakes on a hill, or turn down in traffic or adjusting for road conditions. Plug it in and let it go.

I love the fact this comes with two mounts and an easy to remove plug in the rear. Buy a second wiring loom and you could move this between vehicles if you would rather not buy two for your fleet.

Highly recommend this product!!!

product_title: CURT 13100 Class 3 Trailer Hitch
review_body:
Hitch was received with no dings, tears, etc in the packaging.

Hitch has a very nice finish to it; gloss black. Matches our black explorer just right.

Installation was incredibly simple and I am not one who readily performs any work on my vehicles. I'd rather drop it off at a garage and let them handle it. I was able to install this hitch by myself and with no lift. I'm a larger than average male (6'2, 230lbs) and I could fit under the regular clearance of the explorer with more than enough room to work.

The only time I experienced a 'tight spot' was when I was first mounting the hitch. I made the mistake of lying under the car in a position so that my head was towards the engine and my feet were towards the trunk. When I repositioned myself so that my head was to the passenger side and my feet was too the driver side, I was able to balance one end of the hitch on my shin while I bolted in the other end.

Items of note:
I had no idea what they wanted me to do at the 'reverse fish' part. I knew what HAD to be done, but I wasn't sure how exactly and it wasn't explained clearly at all in the directions plus the pictures weren't too clear either. So basically the fish wire has this spiral end that screws directly onto the top of the 1/2\\" carriage bolt. You slide the carriage bolt through the specified vehicle hole while also fishing the 1/2\\" spacer through the fish line too. Position the half in spacer so the opening lines up with the vehicle's opening and then fish the carriage bolt through! Lickity split, too easy.

18mm socket to remove original bolts on the exhaust hangers
19mm socket to install new bolts for the hitch.

I think the hardest part was removing the exhaust hangars...the first time. It was all hand strength there since I didn't have any specific tools nor a ton of room for leverage. The second time around I removed them, I used some WD40 and they slid right off. (I removed them the first time but realized I didn't have a 18 or 19m socket so I had to put everything back to run to the store haha)

Anyway, looks great. Saved about $400 by NOT going to Ford to have them put theirs on. Thanks Amazon!

product_title: Portable Air Compressor and 12' Extension Cord Bundle
review_body:
Construction looks and feels solid. It's quite compact and light for such a quick pump, quiet too. I expected much, much more noise (it's obviously not silent, but it's pretty quiet compared to some other air compressors I've tried). The hose looks like it's made from some sort of nylon braid, very durable. The chuck is made of brass and even has a free rotating \\"collar\\" (so when you tighten the chuck the hose stays stationary). Some other pumps I looked at in this price range had only plastic chucks, it'll only be a matter of time before that becomes a failure component. I have heard from other reviewers and other opinions on the Internet reflect this as well, that you should keep the car running while you use this pump because the power draw is a bit high, meaning you might have a good chance of blowing your accessory fuse if you just run the pump off the car's battery.

For the price, this is a tough product to beat. Construction quality is great, it pumps fast and quiet and it's all in a compact package. Buy it, use it, love it.

Oh and the 85P does not come with any means of storage other than the box it comes in, plan ahead for that. Personally I use a small tool bag I found at the hardware store and use carabiners to keep it from rolling around in the trunk. Some have had luck using the original packaging too.

product_title: AES Industries Door Spring Compressor Tool For GM Cars and Light Trucks
review_body:
I am in the process of restoring a 1990 Chevy 1500C whose driver-side door was sagging due to worn bushings and bent hinges. To replace the hinge bushings/pins the spring (which holds the door open) has to be removed in order to gain access to the bushings in the body hinges. It is easy enough to pry the spring off with no special tool. One can also find a number of jury-rigged devices on the Net to aid in its replacement. After uselessly fumbling around (who wants to spend money on a tool that they will use once in their life-time) I decided to spring for the 14 bucks and purchase this spring compressor. Wise move!

As I mentioned, removing the spring is no big deal: simply pry or knock it off. However, this tool simplifies that process as well. In order to compress the spring beyond its detents, one has to position the tool between the last two coils on each end (so there is enough travel in the arms to compress the spring adequately). In my application, there was no space between those last two coils so I had to gently hammer the ends of the compressor-ends between those coils. Contrary to a review here, the tool that I received was as described by Amazon, i.e., it has a 1/2-inch (not 7/16) nut. I used a box ratchet wrench which greatly speeds up the job. Once the spring is removed, just leave it attached to the tool. If one chooses to knock or pry the spring off, then to replace the spring, place the ends of the tool between the last two coils and compress it.

I got my first car in 1962 and this is the first time I have had to change door hinge bushings/pins. Although it is unlikely that I will have to use the tool again, based on my experience it is well worth the 14 bucks; I spared myself 50 bucks worth of aggravation.

Ed

product_title: 32oz. Optimum No Rinse Wash & Shine
review_headline: Incredible, there's no other way to describe it.
review_body:
I first heard about ONR a few years ago on a car forum. A professional detailer there used it to wash customers cars at locations he didn't have access to a hose. He used ONR on exotics like Ferrari's and customers would come out after he had only done the wash with ONR thinking he had already polished and waxed their car! My first use of ONR was on a cold winter day inside my heated garage. I used it on a black car that was VERY dirty with sand and salt grime all over the car. The paint looked silver instead of black and was as dirty as it gets in the winter. ONR worked perfectly to clean it all off, although the water in the bucket was coal black when I got done. Most importantly though was I couldn't find any scratches or even any micro swirls afterwards. Keep in mind too that this was with the first generation ONR and it's been improved upon twice since then. I never even pre-rinsed the car that first time, but now if my car is really dirty, ie. has a buildup so thick I can't see the color of the car underneath I'll do a quick pre-rinse with the hose or at the high pressure wash if it's too cold for the hose.

I truly can not express just how much I love this stuff. I very rarely give a product 5 stars as I feel almost any product can be improved upon in some way. I just don't see how ONR could be any better though. It's SO, so nice to be able to wash my car in a T-shirt and shorts inside my heated garage when it's 15F outside. I don't just use this in the winter in my garage though. In my city the price of water has shot up drastically over the last few years and will continue to rise for a few more. Using ONR has saved me a good deal of money over washing the traditional way as it only uses 2 gallons of water. As an added bonus, I use the damp towels I use to dry the car with to clean the inside of the car including the glass, radio face plate, even the dashboard and speedometer cover. You can make quick detailer with ONR and even clay bar lube for a LOT less than buying the pre made stuff from Meguiars. I use the quick detailer to clean up bug guts. I spray it on, let it sit 5 minutes and then simply wipe the dried on guts right off. I even use the quick detailer to clean my plasma tv! I love ONR!
The only draw back is no logo on the key. I am satisfied with it. After duplicated it and it works fine.

product_title: Forever Black Bumper & Trim Dye Kit
review_headline: Forever Black Review From A Pro Detailer
review_body:
I use this stuff quite a bit in my mobile detailing business. The results you'll get is all about A.) how discolored the area to be treated is, B.) The amount of discoloration variation on the area treated C.) the prep. work, and. D.) Realistic expectations if A. and B. are 'fairly bad' to 'OMG that looks awful and I can't stand it anymore.'

To be frank, the cleaner included isn't so great. Especially if there is relatively heavy wax/silicone/sealant build up on the area to be treated. My recommendation would be to first use the provided cleaner as directed; then, after rinsing and allowing to dry, use [[ASIN:B004UQQTQE Griot's Garage 11071 Rubber Prep - 16 oz.]] as directed. THEN (bear with me) clean again with the cleaner provided by Forever Black. Then, and in my opinion only then, will you have a properly prepped surface to apply the Forever Black dye.

To be frank, if there is a circumstance in which the Forever Black dye can only be applied once (one layer) with satisfactory results (even after all of the above prep work) I've just never run into it. For one, the applicator is overly porous foam: foam holds air: air makes bubbles: bubbles make imperfections in the application. Second, you've got to have next to perfect/new trim to start with for this product to not streak...and even then it streaks a bit. In the end, severely weathered trim will need about 6 or 7 passes for the people who are willing to buy this stuff to be happy.

Even though I use Forever Black quite a bit, I'm only giving it three stars for the following reasons:
1.) The cleaner provided... is not good.
2.) Forever Black (the company) absolutely must know that the applicator is sub-optimal.
3.) Unless your car is new or next to new, there is no way at all, not even close, no chance, that one bottle of dye treats 4 - 6 cars. In fact, you will be lucky to get all of the rubber, plastic and vinyl all the way around a single mid-sized sedan with one bottle of dye. (as a point of reference, one bottle of dye is exactly the perfect size to treat all of the rubber, plastic and trim on a severely weathered 2000 BMW 323i.)

Happy Detailing!
AJ
Best-Auto-Detail.com

P.s. I wanted to add that when using the dye it is imperative to resist the temptation to apply more and more dye to fix the streaking, PRIOR to each application/layer having had a chance to dry. If you do this, it will flake off sooner or later. Especially if the surface wasn't prepped as described above.

product_title: Dorman 741-348 Nissan Front Driver Side Window Regulator with Motor
review_body:
I'd never done this type of replacement before, but once I got into it, it wasn't all that tough. Having the right replacement part made the job easy. It arrived well packed and in great shape, plenty of lubrication already on it.

Now there's probably a pro Nissan certified mechanic out there that'll tell me I did it wrong, but here's how I accomplished the task.

Tools I needed were:
-small flat screwdriver (for prying the door handle off and releasing the wiring harnesses)
-large phillips head screwdriver
-10mm socket driver
-hobby knife (for the glue/caulk holding the foam sheet behind the door panel)

I found out how to remove the door panel on youtube, then pulled off the foam sheeting. That glue is so nasty you'll have no problem getting it to stick when you reassemble.

Once you have all that open, you'll see the four bolts holding the long regulator part, and the 3 bolts holding the motor part. figure out the height for the window so you can get at the two bolts holding the plastic window clip. access in the 06 xterra was almost all the way down.

window disconnected, I disconnected the power to the motor part, then undid the 7 bolts. pull the window up and out of the way, then wiggle the busted motor/regulator out the big hole in the bottom left. TAKE A GOOD LOOK BEFORE YOU DO THIS.

Image fresh in your mind, put the new part in place. There's little hooks built into the motor housing to hold it in place while you get the bolts started. Tighten all 7 bolts to the door panel.

Reconnect the motor and switch wiring harnesses, get the regulator in the proper position, reattach the 2 window bolts.

Now's a good time to make sure the window track is clean and it probably doesn't hurt to spray some silicon lube in there.

Now that it's all functional, reassemble and tell your wife how much money you saved so you can go buy yourself a nice present on Amazon.on.

product_title: Spyder Auto Ford Ranger Halogen Projector Headlight
review_body:
Installed on my 1998 Ford Ranger XLT Off Road edition compact truck in about an hour with the proper tools.

Few things dress up the front of a vehicle more than new headlights. These jewels not only modernize my old truck but also are a cool upgrade in lighting the nighttime roadway. Very acceptable quality - looking nearly as robust as the originals. You will need 4 wire taps for the non CFL LED Halo ring if you don't want to cut and solder into the parking light harness. You don't have to utilize this feature to make these headlights truly plug and play but the Halos are very aesthetic with the parking lights on. The covering lens is crystal clear and the reflector is brilliant. Low beam lighting is very crisp with sharply defined edges. High beam resembles the old softly defined light pattern of the original lights. I cannot say how well the lens cover will weather or if the reflector will keep its mirror finish but new, they look extraordinary.

Since the supplied instructions that came with my set were useless I will elaborate on the installation process: Changing out the headlights was not the worst job but definitely not a snap either. You need some degree of mechanical aptitude and experience to do this. The headlights are a perfect replacement fit but the design of the Ranger necessitates a couple of special tools, a little wiring skill and a modest amount of patience. Obtain good snap ring pliers and the special Ford aerodynamic headlight adjusting tool before installation. You will need to make the adjustment before venturing out on the road. Mine were default set very low and in the darkness brightly lit only 20 feet out front. Beyond the distinct edge of light was the blackness of night. So don't make the mistake of getting caught out after dark before making certain your lights are pointing correctly.

Tools: Long needle nose pliers, large capacity snap ring pliers and a Ford aerodynamic headlight adjusting tool. Optionally needed; long flat bladed screw drivers for removing the retaining clips (instead of the snap ring pliers) and soldering equipment instead of the wire taps.

Conclusion: A great product and very useful. A spectacular upgrade, especially if your originals are clouding and weathered.

product_title: Jump-N-Carry
review_headline: Great for camping with a CPAP machine - ResMed S9 Series
review_body:
This review will be most relevant for people who use a CPAP machine and would like to go camping with it. The main reason why I bought this product was because I needed a cheaper alternative to buy the ResMed battery pack (about $600) for my S9 series. The S9 series uses 90 watts, 110V AC.

After some research I settled for the Jump-N-Carry JNC300XL as a portable battery and the PowerDrive RPPD150 150-Watt DC to AC Power Inverter Strip w/USB Port and 3 Outlet. Total $112.00

On Labor Day weekend I went camping with my family at Samuel P. Taylor State Park in Northern CA - Just past north the Golden Gate bridge.

The first night, I was able to sleep 8 hours straight without any problems and some little battery left. Plugged in the portable battery to recharge at the bathroom and had a full charge for the second night. Second night using the CPAP machine, no problems. The next morning, one of my friends had problems to get his small SUV started. We used the Jump-N-Carry with the little charge left from using it the whole night, and my friends car started immediately. Wow! I was impressed. My wife said she had the best night of sleep camping ever. Probably because no more snoring.

I considered buying the Duracell unit with the outlets but decided not to for 3 reasons: 1.- It was still more expensive than buying these two pieces of hardware; 2.- Bigger, heavier and 3.- Some reviews mentioned some problems with the battery. If you want to use a single device you might want to give it a try but for me, this solution strikes the right balance on price, features and value.

If you use a CPAP machine and are car camping with a place where you can recharge your battery, this might be a solution for you.

product_title: Lisle 17942 Black Plastic 4.5-Gallon Drain Pan
review_body:
I bought this based on the reviews, but as another review said I am just kind of EH about it.
Things to consider that I had not.

#1 and the biggest flaw, no cap on the spout. Yes it may make it so that you don't spill when pouring or have a funnel BUT it also didn't fit in most of my jugs. Also, no cap = it drips out onto your floor after you're done pouring it. New concrete? Hope you like an oil spot on it.

#2 Open pan design means everything in the world gets into it. Granted, it's oil it's dirty and it's used, but I still don't like having everything collect and get dirty in my pan that I can see. Not to mention if you have pets and you leave it sitting around for a little bit then you're going to worry about them getting into it or spilling it etc.

#3 It isn't THAT thin. It doesn't fit under my 2004 Tiburon when it isn't jacked up. Do other pans? I don't know, but this one doesn't.

#4 It is WAY over priced. I don't know why I was suckered into buying a pan this expensive. As another reviewer said, I saw an identical one at a parts store for around $10. Quality difference? Nope. If there was then by the time you ruined that one you'd see these design flaws and want another. I accidentally doubled my order of these and never got around to returning it too so I'm stuck.

All that being said, it does seem sturdy. It does its job. It catches oil and has quite a large opening to avoid spilling which is nice. I'd just buy elsewhere.

product_title: Depo Power Non-Heated Mirror
review_body: There were two after market mirror brands.  I got the Depo brand because the other brand had some negative reviews.  It's a lot cheaper than the $145 or so that the Chrysler dealer wanted.  It came in a soft bag in a box with some brown wrapping paper for padding.  That's about it.  No instructions.  I found a video on YouTube about how to install a Chrysler van side view mirror.  There are two tricky parts.  One is that the cover for the bolts snaps into place - no screws.  Getting the old one off damaged it slightly but since I was going to throw it away, that was no problem.  The other tricky thing is that you must have a Torx T27 driver.  Luckily I had a folding Torx key set with this size in it.  So I just unbolted the broken one.  Then I had to disconnect the wire.  Unfortunately the wire retracted into the dashboard after I disconnected it.  So when you do it, make sure you have secure hold of that wire.  I had to take off a small side panel of the dashboard and reach my hand in there to feed the wire back through the exterior of the car.  Then I connected it to the new mirror, and bolted the new mirror on.  Then I snapped the bolt cover on, and I was done.  Pretty easy.  Actually I had my teenage son do it (so he'd learn something) and he did the whole job in probably about 20 minutes.  The mirror works and looks good as new - at least until my wife breaks it again on the side of the garage!

product_title: ACDelco 15961566 GM Original Equipment Parking Brake Pump Motor Switch
review_headline: This is often the AutoPark fix
review_body:
If you have a Chevy/Workhorse P30-style chassis Class A Motorhome (independent front suspension, coil spring booster bags, typically narrow front track) then you are likely cursed with the AutoPark parking brake mechanism. The big yellow \\"Parking Brake\\" pull button to the left of the steering wheel is telltale. There are older versions that still have a foot pedal but some have only the yellow switch.

AutoPark is a spring-loaded drum brake that grabs the driveshaft until a hydraulic pump lifts the pressure off those brake shoes and allows you to move. This switch is part of that mechanism's control. It often fails because the working pressure is very high and hydraulic fluid spills through this switch's diaphragm and renders the system unusable. Like a big rig's air brakes, AutoPark FAILS ON.

At best, as soon as you power down, the brake will engage until the system is repaired. At worst, the parking brake will come on while you're driving and depending upon how quickly it engages it will either start burning the AutoPark shoes and drums or stop you in a big hurry. (how fast I don't really know). Once you're stopped you're stuck until you either repair AutoPark, or mechanically disable it by pulling out a cotter pin under the RV - a job best left to the AAA guy...

Please take note that without AutoPark your RV has no working \\"Park\\" function in the transmission selector either, so you better have leveling jacks or jack stands, wheel chocks, and someone with a foot on the brakes or the RV could start rolling with someone still under it when AutoPark is mechanically disconnected.

Keeping this switch onboard as a spare is cheap insurance that might prevent you from being really stranded if/when your AutoPark fails. Not all failures are this switch, but it is said to be the most common cause. It can be swapped out pretty quickly by someone who can get to the control box that is typically under the RV along the frame rail.

Giving credit where credit is due: OldUsedBear is the defacto AutoPark guru!

product_title: ST Suspension 90603 Coilover Kit for Audi A4 (8D/B5) Quattro Sedan, Wagon and S4 (8D/B5) Sedan, (Set of 4)
review_headline: Excellent Balance of Comfort and Performance
review_body:
These coilovers made my 2001.5 S4 ride the way a premium sports sedan should. You do lose a little bit of the silky smoothness of the stock audi/sachs suspension, and there is slightly more road noise and tire impact transferred to the body, but this is more than made up for. Brake dive used to be moderate and now it is almost non-existent, body roll in corners is much more controlled, and most noticeably in a stage-3 car is that it no longer lifts in the front and squats in the rear the way it used to under full throttle, which made the car feel unbalanced and loose coming out of corners.

These are properly damped shock bodies, no bouncy ride on underdamped stiff springs like the generic chinese aluminum coilovers or poorly matched lowering springs and shocks. Also, no need to try to adjust and match the damping properly side-to-side or front to back, just install and enjoy the fixed damping. The car is not racetrack firm, but seems like it will still be very manageable on the track during lapping days.

The fit and finish is very good on these. Yet to see how the eletro-zinc plating stands up to winter roadsalt, I plan on coating them in corrosion inhibitor and anti-seize. I just couldn't justify the increased cost to move to the KW V1 for the same performance from a stainless steel shock. They are well packaged and height adjustment is easy, just don't overdo it with the tiny locking setscrew. The shock bodies are about 1/2\\" shorter than stock, and they provide a good range of lowered ride height, possibly as much as about -0.5\\" to -3.25\\" but I wouldn't try to push it that low. If you want to completely slam your car I'd recommend trimming the bumpstops, but it's not required for moderate lowering.

These do not include upper mount plates, you re-use the ones on your car. For the front to save disassembling the old ones and to have new rubber parts, I chose to go with new Moog upper springmounts and Uro upper strut mounts, as well as two new spacer washers (audi/vw # 4D0412369A) and I'm happy I did. Installing the rears involved a little hammering with a drift to open up the upper shock mount/control arm bracket, as the ST upper mount bushing insert seems slightly wider than the stock ones, but once done, it all just slipped together and bolted up. Remember once loosely assembled to preload any suspension to near ride height with a jack before torquing bolts to save your bushings.

It's been a couple months and I'm still quite happy riding on these STs, and their value proposition is undeniable. If you're equipping your daily driver for a sportier ride, light track use or even just to replace high-mileage stock suspension, these are great. For heavy track use on a budget they'd be okay but you should probably be going upmarket.

product_title: toyota CAMRY Headlight Assembly Left Hand
review_body:
The 1996 Toyota Camry headlight assembly was well packed and arrived in good condition. Lenses were very clear and OEM design. Both low-beam (9006 55W) and high-beam (9005 65W) headlight bulbs were included. Fit was good. Left/right aim adjustment is controlled by a plastic knob which can be turned by hand if you apply enough force. Height aim adjustment is controlled by a phillips-head machine screw easily accessable from the top. Headlight assembly spreads the light evenly and illuminates the road well.

Installation hints: Grill must be removed. There are two horizontal bolts recessed into the front of the grille with heads (10 mm hex) toward the front of the car. A 10 mm long socket worked well for me, but a regular socket with an extension would work too.
Side marker light must be removed to reveal hidden nut. Remove the philips-head screw at the outside top of the headlight, and slide the side marker light FORWARD toward the front of the car. The side marker light must be slid forward or the plastic pin may break. When the side marker light is removed, the 10 mm nut which holds the headlight assembly on can be removed. Then slide the headlight assembly toward the center of the car to remove the headlight-assembly stud from the fender hole.

I read that there is an installation video on YouTube.

product_title: Innova 3120f Code Reader / Scan Tool with ABS and Bluetooth for OBD2 Vehicles with OBD1 Coverage
review_headline: Very good Code Reader for the price
review_body:

I had previous positive experience with an Innova code reader, an older 3130, so I knew Innova made a good product. I also like that Innova code readers have emission testers as part of the units. I've used this on my truck and on a friends Toyota Truck, both OBD I, and it read the codes without an issue. Please note, this can't erase OBD I codes, but I've found out that no code reader can. This is a very good entry level OBD I - II code reader.

I do want to re-state, this is an entry level code reader. It does limited real time data but it has a good code database and support. If you want or need real time data, spend $4000 and get a code reader that does real time data. For my needs, this was $150 well spent because it has already paid for itself.

review_body: This product is great for those with aftermarket wheels and not enough clearance to fit your vehicle's OEM lug wrench.  For example I fitted my Toyota Corolla with different wheels and lug nuts and this product is absolutely necessary in order to remove the lugs from the narrow lug sockets.  Essentially the clearance to fit the OEM lug wrench onto the lug nut is not there.  This adapter is essentially a 2.5\\" spacer. Since I have an import vehicle I needed to perform a conversion for 21mm size lugs.  21mm translates to 13/16\\" adapter, thus the Gorilla model 1316 wrench adapter saves the day. review_headline: Easy Install and improvement in performance
review_body:
Installed on a 08' Accord Coupe EX-L V6. The installation was incredibly simple with easy to read instructions and pictures to assist in each step. Anyone one can do this with some basic tools. One thing I will add, before you do the install call or go to your closet Honda dealership and get your radio code. Once you disconnect and reconnect the battery after installation you will not be able to use your radio until the code is entered. Once installed the performance was amazing, the responsiveness was greatly improved and, like everyone else has stated, above 2500rpm the car sounds like a throaty V8. Even hitting the throttle while sitting still you can hear the CAI suck in all the air it can.

Now for the 4 star rating, after doing research and reading other reviews most people stated an improvement in gas mileage. Now I haven't ran a full tank of fuel through the car since putting the CAI on, I'm currently in the process, but so far I'm far from impressed. To me it actually seems like I have a lower MPG compared to the stock air box. But before I give up I'm going to run a couple of tanks through the car, maybe it needs to get use to it or something I don't know. I will post an update once I run a couple more tanks through.

All in all though I am happy with the purchase :)

review_body:
I bought this Turtle Wax ICE spray wax for the specific reason that it says on the bottle "Synthetic Formula Prevents Water Spots".
I have used this Turtle Wax ICE spray wax twice on my jetski and it is still water spotted every time I take it out of the water.

Before I took my jetski to the lake this time, I used 3M's Marine Cleaner/Wax first to remove any old water spots. Then I liberally applied the Turtle Wax ICE spray wax and wiped it off. I did this twice just to make sure I had applied enough. Got back from the lake and the jetski is water spotted everywhere. Obviously the jetski gets wet but not much different than a car in rain or splashing through puddles of water.

I would be satisfied if the water spots came off easily but they don't. I am going to have to use the 3M Marine Cleaner/Wax to get the water spots off again. But next time I will use Eagle One's NanoWax spray wax instead. That is what I use on my two other boats (20' and 16' both fiberglass) and the water spots come right off with another application of Eagle One's NanoWax spray wax.

The bottle of Turtle Wax ICE spray wax calls it the most advanced wax yet and that it has a "Synthetic Formula that Prevents Water Spots". Maybe I just got a bottle of water or they forgot to put in the ingredient that prevents water spots. I'll just use it on my lawn tractor as it rarely gets used in the rain.

product_title: Folding Hitch Bumper Cargo Carrier Tray for 2" Class III or IV Receivers
review_headline: I fold it up.  I fold it down.
review_body:
After 23 years, the demise of my F-150 left me with no options, the 2012 CR-V is not really suited to dumping firewood or bricks into the back for neither short of long hauls. This hitch mounted platform is better than I imagined, sturdy, folds up,carried more weight than I thought and mounted on/off readily. Although,with a little foresight I think I prevented a couple of concerns. One, I also purchased the dual hitch extension which raises the platform a good 4\\" and sets it off from the bumper another few extra inches which allows easy clearance in lifting the rear door of the CR-V. The height especially when loaded with a few hundred pounds prevented scraping the carrier when turning off flat roadways up into uphill drives and uneven terrain. I installed a class III 2\\"x2\\" hitch which fits a CR-V, giving better weight capacity than a class II 1 3/4\\". It's been great in moving firewood around from one side of yard to the other eliminating the wheel barrel.

Easy to assemble and not too heavy or bulky. Actually, just right. If I had ordered the 60\\" it would made the CR-V look weird and would be heavier to lug around while installing. Reviewed several makes with others of same style costing twice as much. Very satisfied with construction and gauge of metal.

Another concern, is thief while parked in remote locations. Since the cargo platform does attached readily and easily, means it is also removed readily and easily to be placed into someone pick-up. I guess it takes a thief to recognized a thief's opportunity. I purchased (2) locking hitch pins and now I no longer have any concern while hiking.

10 years ago I put GR2s all around in my wife's new used VW Golf. I ended up with the car, which has 240K miles now, a lot of it over forest service roads and even some cross country. One of the rear units started leaking so I bought a pair and replaced them. The leaking unit still had good damping but would have gone south soon enough. Tis is the only time I have ever had a failure in a KYB shock or strut.

My only beef with the GR2 is they duplicate stock damping. If you want more damping, go to the Gas-adjust model.

BTW don't order from Just Suspension, get your KYBs from Amazon or some other vendor.

And no, it was not covered under warranty

Finally, start the tape along one edge to remove and work slowly along plate as you press down, rather then taking both strips off before starting. If you use a soapy water you will have to press down to remove water once you have it positioned correctly(I used a towel and rubber mallet to gently remove water) but this method allows you the needed time to line up things perfectly---rather then instant adhesion with applied dry.

product_title: Xelement CF5050 Mens Black/Grey Cordura Armored Jacket with Removable Sleeves - Medium
review_body: I must say, this jacket is a great jacket.  The armor in the arms, back, and front seems to be well-thought through.  The perception of a \\"six-pack\\" abs is neat...when your carrying a small keg.  The removable arms are pleasing, albeit less safe, in an area where the temperature hits 40C-45C in the summer months (Yes, in Canada) for keeping cool.  The venting is helpful at speed, although it doesn't help when in heavy traffic, or as another reviewer said- wearing a backpack blocks the venting.  This jacket has done well in all temperatures so far, from 6C morning rides in rain and wind, to 45C in blistering midday sun with no wind on an open road.  The first issue I have, and it is a personal one, the zippers on the sleeves are plastic, not metal.  They bent and frayed quickly, I was always taking my sleeves off midday, then putting them back on in the afternoon or morning.  Is this a manufacture problem/defect?  Hard to say, but I'm going to put in a steel zipper just for my own piece of mind.  The second issue is lack of reflective material, again only my opinion.  I think if the grey material on the elbows and the back of the jacket was reflective, it may help in circumstances when your not on your bike/at the side of the road.  I'm going to say 4.5 out of 5 stars.

product_title: Firstgear Rubber Rain Gloves
review_headline: Much better than other rain gloves I've used
review_body: I've been using these gloves for about 2 months now, and they work very well.  I've had several other pairs of rain gloves before these, which were made from synthetic cloth-type material, and in a heavy rain the water would eventually soak through to my hands.  These gloves, however, are rubber, and completely waterproof.  They also seem thick enough that I think they'll last a good while.  The only problem is that, in reading other reviews which said to order a much larger size, I ended up ordering gloves that are somewhat too big (but still usable).  I normally wear a medium-size riding glove, and so I ordered these raingloves in X-large size, but they're too big.  I'd guess that you probably should order just one size up instead of two, like I did, (unless you're wearing the rain gloves over armored gloves, which are larger).  Update - after using these gloves for a couple of years, they tore.  They way in which they tore indicates a flaw in the material.  I keep these gloves folded over twice, then placed into the carrying bag they came with, and then put in a pocket in my rain jacket.  The rubber on these gloves became so soft (perhaps when it's warm, which it often is in Thailand where I live) that the rubber stuck together where it was folded over.  The first couple of times, I was able to pull the stuck sections apart without tearing them, but eventually they stuck together so badly that holes were torn when trying to separate the stuck sections.  Now one of the gloves has 3 large holes in it, and is pretty much useless. I'm thinking of ordering another pair (since they worked very well until they tore), and putting pieces of thin cloth over each glove before I fold it, so that the rubber won't stick together, but it would make them bulkier to carry.

product_title: Mothers 06108 Back-to-Black Trim Care - 8 oz
review_headline: OK for rubber door seals, did not hold on exterior plastic
review_body:
1st of all - I'm a fan of Mothers products and use a lot of them on my car... this is not going to be one of them for plastic anyway...

I purchased Mothers \\"Back to Black\\" at a local auto store and used it on my 2008 Subaru Outback 2.5 XT. There is a lot of exterior black plastic and rubber on this vehicle, so it took me a few hours to apply and buff it all.

I followed the directions exactly - The car and the trim were clean and cool to the touch. I Applied it, massaged it in, let it dry, then buffed it... and when I say buff it, you really need to buff it to remove any excess. It looked great, until I woke up the next morning and there was dew on my car. Well, anyplace dew had settled on the treated areas, it was streaked and I had oily runs on the adjoining painted areas of my car. I can't imagine what would have happened if it rained! I waited until later in the day when the dew evaporated, and re-buffed again, and the streaks went away somewhat, but were still noticeable. I've applied additional coats and still get the same results. This only seems to work on materials that will absorb it freely. I tends to stay slippery and somewhat greasy feeling on hard plastics (on my vehicle anyway).

It does not say on the container or their web-site, but here on amazon in the product description 'un-treated plastic'... I'm not sure what that means, I have not treated my plastic with anything but this product, but maybe Subaru treats the plastic at the factory ?
The product description also states that it needs to be re-applied regularly... I'm not willing to spend hours every time I wash my vehicle, or it gets wet.

This product wasn't a total waste, since it seems to work very well on my rubber door seals and the rubber seals around the sunroof, both of which are prone to oxidation and would be extremely costly to replace since they are normally only available from the dealer. So I'd give it 4 stars for it's performance so far on soft rubber. I'd give it 5 stars if it keeps them protected over the years with regular application (the rubber is easy to treat compared with plastics).

product_title: Motorcraft MCSOE76 Ball Joint
review_headline: Best part available for your worn out Taurus!
review_body: I'm a full time Auto Tech, and when I needed to replace ball joints in my parents' car, I knew that it was going to be Motorcraft parts or else I'd be doing the job again in the foreseeable future.  Amazon had the best price, so I bought them and got the job done.  If you've never dome ball joints on a Taurus before, you will absolutely want the large C-clamp shaped tool and also the Taurus/sable ball joint press adapter kit, both of which are available on Amazon or can be rented from a local AutoZone or O'Reilly Parts store. review_headline: It's exactly what it's supposed to be
review_body:
The cable is a 50 amp male to female extension cord (non-marine non-watertight right-angled ends). It is the exact same gauge as the existing cord on my RV. The ends/connectors appear to be relatively high quality. I saw no defects in its manufacturing.

I ordered this extension cord to allow me to work on my RV outside of its normal storage bay (beyond the reach of its normal cord). I used the cord on a 50 amp GFCI outlet consistently over a period of a month with partial to full AC loads (1 to 3 A/C units). There was no sign of overheating nor any issue. It worked perfectly.

Safety Note: Use common sense and caution. The ends of this extension cord are not watertight. For outdoor use or when there is potential of exposure to water/grounding (rain, etc.), only use this extension cord on a GFCI (Ground Fault Circuit Interrupt) outlet. I took additional precautions where the extension cord mated to the cord from my RV by elevating the connection off the ground and covering it plastic to reduce exposure to the elements.

Maintenance Note: One needs to be aware that because it's 50 feet of 50 amp wire, it is heavy and does not rewind around your arm like a 15 amp cord would. Because of its length and weight, it takes some time and effort to mechanically recoil the wire to its original size. This is to be expected.

product_title: Leatherique 32oz. Kit
review_headline: A lot of work but it works
review_body:
After much researching and reading wonder stories from different forums on the net I decided to take the plunge and buy this expensive 2 part leather treatment. It works, but it takes a lot of work and patience. I applied to my 4 yr old black Infiniti interior. My seats were very dry and ashy from spending time in a repair shop, and had a few white chalky stains (mixture of primer, body filler, and water from wet sanding) dripped on the seats that wouldnt come out even after a quick interior detail & leather treatment at the local carwash. Someone wiped down the interior and tried to remove the stain with some solution in a windex bottle that made my seats super hard (it totally dried out my seats). Anyway I applied generous amounts of the rejuvenator oil daily over the span of about a work week. It took like a day or two before the leather started to absorb the oil, and I just kept applying. After soaking in the heat/sun for a few days I then followed up with the prestine cleaner. My first thoughts were that the seats looked more like graphite (lead) from a pencil instead of black. They had a matte appearance almost like some of the color had been washed away with the dirt. I then looked at new G sedans on the net and in person and realized this is how the seats look when the car is new. Every stain or discolored area was removed, and the seats were pretty much butter soft and the car now smells like leather even from outside the vehicle. Every time I take off my shirt or jacket after driving, I smell like quality leather. Considering how much this stuff costs and how much work was involved, I think I'd rather use a good leather conditioner spray in between full treatments.
I was totally skeptical, but it worked wonders on my Infiniti G seats. I also tried this product on a 90's Acura and the results were unimpressive. Yeah it made the leather a little softer, and a little lighter in color, but the seats still had dirt in them, and they didnt get butter soft. They did get softer, but not buttery soft. Also the Acura didnt hold the leather smell as well as the Infiniti did. At this point I chose to save what I have left of the rejuvenating oil, and use a spray conditioner on that car. The rest is going in the Infiniti next spring. With no other treatment or maintenance, this stuff has my seats soft 5 months later. The leather smell has faded a good bit, but I feel like that will be restored with some Griots Garage leather spray and the leather scented tree air fresheners.
I notice Leatherique works better on leather thats not painted or coated. It works especially well on perforated leather. product_title: Lisle 63000 Fuel Tank Lock Ring Tool
review_body:
I do 99% of my own work on all of my vehicles, including replacing a fuel pump when necessary. This wrench is a must-have to work on fuel pump replacement and it will fit on many different type of cars where the fuel pump is located inside the fuel tank. That pump is mounted inside the tank and is covered with a access lid that requires this special tool to get the lid off. Any time you work with a fuel tank, empty of not, extreme care must be taken to avoid a very serious mistake, fire or explosion. Getting the protective lid off is tough and without this special tool, can be very dangerous. I like this tool because its adjustable to fit any make or model so you are not buying some very expensive tools that you may only use once in your life. This wrench adapts to any brand or style of fuel pump lid, making removing it a pretty simple process. Well worth the money I paid, although it was not very much considering how much dealerships charge for a model specific wrench. This wrench works great.
Caution: Usually the fuel tank around the location of the fuel pump will have a rubber like coating on it to prevent anything causing a spark. I would suggest not wearing any nylon clothing or shoes that could create a static spark situation. Usually when removing the fuel tank lid, you have removed the rear seat and are in the car directly over the tank. Disconnect the battery also. Once the lid is off, fumes and raw gas are exposed. A simple spark could prove to be catastrophic. Also, it is highly suggested you NOT perform this procedure within your garage. Do so with all doors open and in the open air, this to allow clean air flow and circulation to allow gas fumes to exit the vehicle. And have a Fire Extinguisher close by, or better yet, have someone standing near by with a extinguisher at the ready just in case. Do Not take this procedure lightly, it is probably one of the most potentially dangerous maintenance functions you'll ever perform.

product_title: UNI Multistage Competition Air Filter Kit for Kawasaki Teryx 08-11
review_headline: Uni Air Filter Kit UK-1901ST - fits my Kawi Teryx
review_body:
First off the picture is completely wrong for this particular application, it comes in a cardboard box to protect it. This kit fits my 2012 Kawasaki Teryx 750 UTV/side-by-side just fine. Mine was $76.47 free ship from Powersports Superstore (known to be the cheapest on the Net on their huge web site). But prices seem to vary. You might find the correct picture here:
ecx.images-amazon.com/images/I/71w42IYVKVL._AA1500_.jpg

It comes with the filter, an aluminum adapter and a hose clamp. The adapter is quickly inserted from the inside of the airbox, through the airbox and into the engine intake boot. It uses the existing hose clamp on the outside of the airbox and the provided hose clamp to attach the filter onto the adapter on the inside of the airbox. Uni makes great stuff as usual. I use their foam filter on my dual sport BMW 650 also.

Ok so WHY buy this filter? IMHO... This is the first and main mod that everybody with a Teryx needs (I am a new owner but have heard this over and over). I'm not talking a performance mod for racers, I mean anyone who rides in ANY dirt! The stock filter uses simply foam and pressure to fit onto the front and many people have had a lot of dirt enter the plenum intake to the engine as somehow it gets around the filter. This then is a $3000 engine rebuild and it is a common problem - people are seeing dirt get in, hopefully before it does damage but I am expecting this to fix it. My dealer recommend the K&N but I do not trust paper filters for dirt and am a firm believer in an oiled foam filter.

The Uni filter itself is a one piece design but has an inner metal mesh cylinder that is very stiff to support the foam filter. This mesh cylinder is a separate piece on the inside, which actually is removable if you gently work at it a bit. The filter consists of red foam with a black rubbery end cap on the rear end with molded tabs to fit into the 2 air box slots on the rear, and the front of the filter is also black rubbery molded with a big round opening into which you can see the inner metal cylinder.

To install, remove the engine cover to get at the hose clamp between the airbox and the engine intake boot. Rmove the OEM filter, you won't re-use any of it. Now loosen the hose clamp on the outside of the airbox, insert the Uni aluminum adapter with a little oil/grease on its embedded o-rings and retighten the outer hose clamp. They even include a piece of foam to further seal between the adapter and the airbox. I actually installed the adapter and filter (dry) and snugged the adapter up against the edge of the airbox before I tightened the hose clamp on the outside. Then removed the filter for the next step - oil and install it.

Now with the adapter installed and clamped in, you simply oil and install the filter, the filter has NO oil on it out of the box. I oiled the new filter liberally with NoToil spray filter oil (water based cleanup - get with the future it's great!) and worked the oil in well. Just a warning, if you use NoToil you must use liberally and work it into the filter, it says right on the can that it is not a \\"spray and go\\" type but rather use liberally and remove excess oil. It uses alcohol as a carrier to distribute the tacky oil then the alcohol dries up. NoToil is so great - have you ever tried to clean an air filter in the sink of a Mexican hotel room without blowing up the place trying to use gasoline? Now you can and NOT be dangerous at all or leave a mess - just some Oxyclean and warm water!!! But I digress...

I debated pulling the inner metal cylinder out the open front end in order to help work the oil into the foam better, but either way you must be gentle on the seams between the red foam and the black end caps as you massage the oil into the foam.

Ok so now just install the oiled filter onto the inside of the provided aluminum adapter and clamp it on with the provide hose clamp. Therear of the filter is a black molded piece with 2 tabs on it, and the whole filter has to be pushed forward firmly in order to get the 2 tabs to go forward and pop down into their slots in the airbox frame. Finally the airbox cover is installed and held on with the 4 clamps. This was the only part that seems a little difficult. The cover has a molding that pushes down on the back of the rear frame of the filter to hold it in. And at first it seemed to not align properly but finally I was able to seat the cover and get the 4 clamps on. The rear seems very tight but yeah it fits. Not a problem functionally as now you have a filter that will never leak dirt.

I would also like to get a sheet of Uni foam filter material and just lay it over and around the Uni filter as a pre-filter. I could then really easily and quickly clean that sheet.
