review_headline: Adds a more modern, luxurious look to your Mazda3
review_body:
These headlights are sleekly designed and the LED strips nicely emulate the high-end look of other luxury vehicles. In my application I had no fitment problems and I'm generally pleased with the build quality. I found the low beam projectors to have good focus and brightness. The high beam reflectors work well, but I think their light output appears more scattered compared to the Mazda3's factory headlights. Also, I did have to adjust the leveling of the lamps since (in my opinion) they're aimed a little low by default.

Things to note:

> If your car isn't already equipped with daytime running lights, you'll have to purchase an aftermarket DRL adapter/switch or (like I did) tap into your car's parking lights harness to power the LEDs.

> The LEDs aren't super obvious in bright daylight, but they do show up nicely in overcast days and look really slick at night.

> Both the low and high beams use H1 bulbs; meaning that the Mazda3's stock bulbs WILL NOT fit. However, these headlights ship with H1 bulbs already installed.

> The included bulbs look very yellow compared to the LED strips. So, if you want a truly luxury look, I'd recommend replacing them with bulbs of a higher color temperature (4000K - 5000K) or installing an HID kit. Personally, I went the less complicated route and installed these in mine: [[ASIN:B007OYVMSO Philips - Diamond Vision H1 (Pair)]]. They excellently emulate the HID look and don't require the installation of extra hardware.

Overall I think these are very nice, classy-looking headlights and a worthwhile upgrade for anyone who loves their Mazda3.

But be aware that due to lack of snaps or construction to account for this issue this jacket will ALWAYS be pressed against your neck when seated. I have to unzip the jacket more then half-way to accommodate this. This of course is not an issue with this particular jacket but rather the style of jacket.

review_headline: I needed my tech skills on this one.
review_body:
Disclaimer - my vehicle, that I bought used, had an aftermarket stereo in it before I bought the vehicle. How do I know this? - Because the person who had the truck before me CUT the factory wire harness off and used the bare wires to connect to it. At least he had the courtesy to put the harness back on..well he had to in order to get the re-installed factory stereo to work. With that in mind, here is my review.

The harness fit my connector like a glove.. MOST of the wires were correct (in the correct spot on the harness) in that they worked (speaker placement, power, negative lead). But others: the remote turn on, power antenna, and constant battery for memory function, didn't work or were not connected to any wire on the vehicle connector side. I don't know if its a case of the factory connector being altered in the past (see Disclaimer above), or if the wire placement on the aftermarket harness being incorrect. Either way I just wanted to get my stereo working and not take the time to exchange the item, so I 'rewired' the aftermarket harness by relocating the wire taps to the positions in the harness that matched up to the correct positions on the factory connector. Now it works perfectly!

Now, I could have received a fluke, a 1 in 1000 piece that was incorrectly assembled, but in the end I have no complaints since it fit my factory connector and had MOST of the wires connected correctly the first time connecting it.

product_title: Gibson 19677 Single Exhaust System
review_headline: I like this Cat back system!
review_body:
This review is for my 91 Ford Explorer, 4.0L, 4 door, 4WD on mostly stock with JBA headers and MagnaFlow Cat. 6 weeks and 1500 miles later...

First off, the quality of the whole kit is nice. All the hardware was complete including hangers and bolts. The tailpipe is 2 piece and a chrome tip and the fitment was good, but not great. The piping goes between the shock absorber and the sway bar link and there is only 1 inch space on either side before touch them. This made precise fitment really important. With 2 pieces it was a chore, but I am doubtfull and 1 piece would work with older sagging springs and general wear and tear on a 21 year old truck. I had to really take my time and go step by step working my way back form the cat connection to the tip. But I was rewarded with a nice setup that only required tightening up the clamps once to make sure everything was good and tight. The stock location hangers work perfect and the look is very nice exiting just behind the rear passenger tire. The tip is nice and fits snuggly.

The sound is great. Given I replaced my whole exhaust, I can't comment on how the muffler alone sounds, but as a system, I don't think I could ask for a better sound. Throaty, yet strong and full. It'll never sound like a v-8, but it doesn't scream hot rod either. It does not boom at any rpm, but there is a slight resonance that is most noticeable at 3-4K when on it and just above 1K. These 2 rpm bands make the loudest pressure inside the cab. Volume wise, really no louder than stock. My wife and kids like it fine, of course the old muffler was blown out and loud as heck, but when I made a field repair to the stock muffler, that lasted 1 hour on 3 hour drive, the Gibson muffler was better sounding WITH similar volume.

I've only driven with the Rallye 4000 pencil beams previously- but the pencils are too concentrated and becomes blinding on open highways with a pair. Just two super bright spots. Looks good- but impractible for serious drivers.

The Euro Beam doesn't give as much distance; but throws more than enough to safely travely travel at beyond legal speeds on open roads. Illuminates the side roads nicely enough (to hopefully be able) to avoid suicidal kangaroos who are intent to break all the headlights they can crash into. 'Side lobes' angle out around 45degress each side of the lights and are very nice at illuminating road markers and the crazy wildlife.

One Pencil and one Euro Beam is a nice combo. Although- I am currently considering selling the Pencil and switching to two Euro's.

A couple of negative comments:
1. Light is supplied with a 50Watt Hella bulb (as others mentioned in some reviews) not a 100Watt as per description.
2. No idea on how good the original 50Watt Hella bulb was out of the box- broken during delivery. The box looks to have dropped in transit (but that isn't anyones fault as) I expected that (as I live in Australia). Light was perfect! The 'parker/position lamp' was fine (despite being inside a plastic bag just floating around)! Typical. Even at $130Au delivered+$15Au for a new bulb it is great value!
3. When you order- also make sure your ordera H3 100Watt bulb- to get the most from these lights.

A terrific light for the price- even if you have to buy a new bulb to use it.

product_title: Samlex Solar SSW-350-12A SSW Series Pure Sine Wave Inverter
review_headline: Not bad for the money, but for a Samlex, could be much better.
review_body:
(Apologies for the long-winded review, but I needed to be thorough on this.)

Pros:
* Lightweight
* Mounting brackets
* USB port that charges smartphones and has proper AC adapter signaling (phone recognizes the power source to be a charger)
* USB charging feature works even when inverter is off
* Doesn't put out a ton of RF noise like a lot of other cheap sine wave units
* Good bang for the buck, especially when considering this inverter is a sine wave unit that's UL certified.

Cons:
* It's too lightweight - feels very cheap for a $100+ unit
* Unlike the PST series and other ones from Samlex, this fan is not temperature controlled, it is load controlled and the fan comes on regardless of what temperature it's actually running at
* Fan is quite noisy even at no load
* Because of the always-on USB, it can end up draining your car battery
* Waveform is quite distorted (13-15% total harmonic distortion when unloaded!) that gets worse as you put more loads on it
* Pretty poor voltage regulation especially under fast-changing loads like stereo amplifiers/receivers, etc. and sags much more than the ~5 volts in the datasheet
* Frequency tends to drift +/- 1 Hz
* Power terminals screw into the unit; other units are a \\"nut\\" where the bolt part of the terminal is on the unit itself - this makes attaching leads a bit of a pain
* Fuse is not external - if something goes wrong that it blows the fuse (reverse polarity or overload perhaps?) then the whole unit is toast
* ONLY comes with battery clips, no cigarette lighter plug
* Battery clips are low-quality - the insulating sleeves fell off my unit during transit, and the cords are flimsy
* Narrow input voltage range - the unit starts beeping well before my other inverters signal a low battery; unit only works from 10.5-15.3 volts DC
* LED indicators are quite dim even when viewed indoors

This inverter isan good model when considering the price of this unit ($100 or so for a fairly decent pure sine wave inverter). However, I found its output voltage performance to be quite disappointing as it put out a waveform that was substantially distorted (and caused a few of my electronics to buzz as if it were hooked up to a modified-sine wave inverter), and when put under load was even worse. The load-controlled fan is an annoyance since it not only wastes battery power, but also runs when there is no load connected to the inverter. The quality of a unit was disappointingly low for a Samlex brand inverter, but it still beats the pants out of a generic sine wave inverter and is so much better than a modfied-sine inverter.

Bottom line: It's a nice inexpensive pure sine wave inverter, but you get what you paid for.

Also, I have taken oscilloscope images of the inverter's waveform when unloaded, when put at 50% load, and when delivering surge power. The images are located in the image gallery for this item.

I got this to restore the finish on a white 2005 Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor that I bought from the local auction. I actually wrote in and asked Meguiar's if it could be used with their 105 compound. They said yes and I ordered the machine.

Unfortunately, the pads would not stay on at the higher speeds in order to cut through the scratches and there is no way it would cut 1,200 to 1,500 sand lines like they advertise it doing in many of their videos. So, I learned that issue on the trunk, and did the rest of the car with 3,000 and after several applications of 105 at the slower speeds got the car to shine and ready for the 205 polish.

I did write in to Meguiar's regarding the pad issue and they did send me a pad and a new backing plate. Unfortunately, they sent me the 5\\"-6\\" backing plate and NOT the 7\\" plate that this machine is all about, so what's the point? Locally, ONLY 8\\" pads are available in all the parts stores, so that's another issue, your pads must be ordered also.

I thought I did all my homework before I ordered this product and looked at videos and reviews all over the place. I guess I didn't pay enough attention because when I received the machine and reviewed specific videos on product use I noticed many of the Meguiar's training videos show Maguire's folks using a MAKITA ROTARY tool and a WOOL pad at high speeds! I think that should have been a CLUE!

Anyway, in my next life I am going to at least go down to the local auto paint supply store and see what they are offering before I buy online. While 3M stuff is not so prevalent in the auto supply stores around here and I haven't seen any \\"good\\" DA's with the pressure responsive motors and the speed ranges of the online stuff, I'm sure they must have a complete set of products that local professionals are using for about the same price ... less the aggravation.

I've used Meguiar's products since the Blue Coral era in the 70's and between this DA thing and multiple problems with their failing spray bottles I am moving on to other vendors.

product_title: The Klasse Kit
review_body:
Ok, so I am really picky when it comes to waxes and polishes. I have never used a sealer until now, so I was a little skepticle. I have used Meguiars Gold Glass polish for the last two years and loved it, except it did not last long. I also liked Turtle Wax Ice polish, but again, it did not last long. I decided to try this kit and am glad I did (so far. I have done two cars in the last two weeks, which I will talk about in more detail). Here's my review of each of the cars that I used it on.

1996 Nissan Almera (Also known as Tiffany)
I wanted to try this on Tiffany before using her on my other two cars because I don't like to experiment on more expensive vehicles. I washed and dried Tiffany, and then began the process of the Polish and then Sealant. The polish went on easy and came off easy, which I was happy about. I put the sealant on with what I thought was a small amount, and began to have problems. It was VERY hard to get off. Even using the applicators, following the instructions, and buffing until my arms were sore, I could not get the streaks off. So I then just put a small amount on a microfiber cloth and went over the car again with that, and it got the streaks out for the most part. Unfortunately, it began raining pretty much after I got done cleaning it off as best as possible, so I wasn't able to re-apply. However, it does shine amazing and beads up better than anything I have ever used. After two weeks of rain nearly every day, she still looks really good (for her age) once she has dried. I am waiting on a nice day to re-wash to get some of the dirt marks from dried on water off to see how well the sealant does it's job. Overall, not too bad, but could have been better (if I had watched some youtube videos before hand, but that comes with the next car).

2009 Kia Borrego (Affectionately called Bertha)
Before working on Bertha, I watched a bunch of videos on how to apply the sealant better than the directions said. It really paid off. I washed and dried her, then used a bug and tar remover to clean it even better. Then I did something I've always been too scared to try; I used a clay bar. I am now a believer in why people do this, and will do it at least once a year on each of my vehicles. It made the surface smooth and helped with the application/removal of the polish. And made for an incredible shine. If you haven't done it before, try it. It's not hard at all. Next came the polish. This was really simple and effective, just like on Tiffany. The shine was incredible afterwards, and thought about just stopping at that, but decided to give the \\"experts\\" on youtube a chance. product_title: Engine Oil Stop Leak
review_headline: Avoid This Like The Plague That It Is!
review_body: My '93 Toyota P/U, 22RE w/ about 248k currently, began skipping intermittently recently & after much diagnosis, I determined the head gasket was beginning to expire. Having recently began a new employment commute of about 54 miles daily, I wasn't too interested in purchasing a new vehicle only to have it become rapidly transformed into a high-mileage sled, but neither was I planning to invest any serious money into a 19 year old workhorse with nearly a quarter of a million miles on the ODO. After reading about this product & several others, I decided to give Bar's a try, figuring the greatest thing I could lose was the purchase price of this dubious additive with it's incredulous claims. After the first application, dogmatically according to the instructions, I noticed no change, so within a couple of weeks I dared to apply the product once more- & let me tell you a change occurred! My truck began to surge constantly, (from about 1-2k RPM's,) which it had never done before, then it began to run hot. After figuring the \\"miracle cure\\" must have contributed somehow, I finally pulled apart the thermostat housing to discover the thermostat to be completely clogged with Bar's Leaks residue- no wonder my engine was running hot! Next, I began to figure the idle air control solenoid was causing the engine's recent surging episodes, so after removing the coolant line that's routed through it for engine temperature/idle speed determination, once again, I found zero coolant flow & Bar's Leaks was the only change that I've made, leading me to conclude it as the cringing culprit that prompted this line to clog as well. Since no coolant was allowed to flow, it apparently caused the ECM to constantly determine that the engine was not fully warmed up, yet the combustion results indicated that it was, causing the confusion & hence the surging. At this point, I, of course, flushed my cooling system of this bedeviling, vile \\"ejecta\\" & much to my dismay, the idle speed is still higher than normal (though no surging exists- I assume the air control solenoid may have sustained permanent damage from this \\"experiment\\"), & to top all of that off, I still have a head gasket leak! My advice to anyone: if you need to replace your head gasket either do so or continue to invest in fresh coolant when needed, but run- don't walk, run- as far away from this product as you possibly can. I've thoroughly learned my lesson & I can only be thankful that I didn't damage a more expensive vehicle on this highly promissory, \\"snake oil\\" product. (By the way, I'm not in the automotive repair, parts or accessories business, neither do I sell cars or anything else associated with this product, so I have no ulterior motives except to simply inform others concerning my experience with this product.)

review_headline: Trimax wheel lock is tough but go even tougher
review_body: This combination wheel lock & chock is xlnt, and it was $20 less on Amazon than at my local trailer shop. But the Ultra Max model by Trimax (TWL100 for $100 more) is the way I should have gone because the lug nuts would also be secured without messing with locking lug nuts wheel locks, and the accompanying risk of not having the key when u need it especially if u use more than one tow vehicle. Btw, if u go w these lug locks note whether u need \\"cone\\" or bolt type. My Zieman motorcycle trailer for ex uses \\"bolt\\" type, so I had to pay rtn shipping on my incorrect order). Back to the wheel lock/chock, for an expensive trailer I might even use one one each side in a crime ridden area. However, my cheap Harbor Freight trailer, secured only with a thick chain & lock, was stolen from an apt carport. I learned an expensive lesson, remember to use a Reese (or Fulton coupler lock, avail at Harbor Freight) when detached from tow vehicle. Unmarked white cargo trailers are particularly high theft targets cuz they can be easily sold online or pawned without the title. (Google for other crime prevention tips such as welding on lic plates, branding through your county, etc.)

product_title: 2005 - 2010 Honda Odyssey Cross Bars
review_body:
These bars were very easy to install. I read a number of other reviews prior to purchasing the product. There were a few that cautioned the installation due to the difficultly in removing the end cap from the side rails on the van (Honda issue not these bars). While the end caps didn't slide off easily, I didn't have to spend more than a minute or so on each one. You need to insert a screwdriver into the hole to release the tab. Just don't be afraid of using a decent amount of force to remove the cap. They go back on super easy. I would recommend using a towel or something just under the back of the side rail so you don't scratch the top of the van when the cap comes off (which I did).

The only critical remark I have about the cross bars is that there were additional screws and washers in the installation pack that the instructions were silent on. After looking at the bars, it was easy to understand that they are for fastening the cross bar caps (you will figure it out). All in all, good product and easy installation. Took me less than 20-25 minutes for entire installation.

product_title: Fit System Chevrolet/GMC Replacement OE Style Power Folding Mirror
review_body:
Edit: 9/6/2012

Today the main portion of the mirror straight-up fell away from the rotating mount part that attaches to the door sail. The whole wiring harness snapped and the entire thing fell off the truck on the freeway. I am changing my review from 2 stars to 1 because of this gravitational defect. I do not believe that mirrors should deft physics and blow off a truck to explode onto the freeway. I did not recover the mirror and luckily no one was behind me. Based on the other reviews here, I recommend you steer clear of this mirror entirely.

Earlier:I thought the mirror wobbling was a couple bad mirrors shipped to the other reviewers, but lo-and-behold - my mirror shook like crazy while driving. I merged onto the freeway, and POP! the mirror part fell out of the housing and was hanging by the wire. Maybe fit system needs to actually put one of these mirrors on a truck and go drive it... then they would know what shoddy quality junk they are manufacturing. It would get one or zero stars, but I needed a mirror, and it looks like my original mirror on the passenger side, which is all they got right.

I managed to glue the mirror on the motor mount, which turns out to be the defect. The mirrors are attached with junky hook systems that break. Glue it down, and the wobble stops... it also keeps it from falling out of the housing. I would ask for my money back, but I managed to fix it and use it. I do not recommend anyone else buy one of these unless they are handy. It might be better to go buy something else. This mirror could have gone through someone's window and seriously injured someone. Please repair your mirror or redesign it. Put it on a truck and drive, then you'll see. Fit system - 1 star, only because I actually got the \\"correct\\" mirror, and it did \\"fit.\\"

product_title: E4 SAFETY CERTIFIED 15" Car Seat Belt Extender - Black - Type A (7/8" wide metal tongue) - Buckles Right In!
review_body:
My husband has a hip injury which prohibits him from sitting. This seat belt extender allows him to extend the shoulder harness in the back seat of our Toyota Corolla so that he can still wear a seat belt while lying down when I drive him to appointments. Since this device is portable, it can also be used to extend seat belts in taxis and planes, provided they have the same size metal tongue--in this case 7/8-inch wide.

For anyone who avoids wearing a seat belt because it isn't large enough, for whatever reason, an extender like this can save your life.

You have a choice of colors and sizes in this product. It is important to be aware that you need to measure the exact seat belt you will be extending because the seat belts in the front and back seat of your vehicle may not have the same size tongue.

Finally, we received outstanding service from this seller. I had ordered the wrong color, and they answered my email about it in less than an hour. The email was very friendly and written in a professional manner. Their shipping was really fast, too.

review_headline: The photo is inaccurate.  It's actually the NASA logo exactly, without the special effects.
review_body:

I was pleased to find that there is no such special effect in the design. It's exactly the NASA logo--aka the \\"meatball\\".

Another important thing to note is that it's a cutout of the NASA logo. There is no big square of white or clear background. The parts of the chevron which extend past the circumference of the meatball are not rimmed in white. But this is the part that loses two stars, because the parts of the chevron which extend beyond the meatball can very easily come off, and the only cure for that is to replace it. Also, the coloring of the sticker fades at least a little very quickly, which is a problem I've never had with any other car sticker.

The best way to apply this to your window is to first clean the glass with an alcohol swab--the kind you might find in a First Aid kit--let it dry, and carefully put it on nice and straight. If you're putting it on your rear windshield you can probably use the lines from the defroster to line up the \\"NASA\\" with to make sure it appears level in relation to the car which most likely isn't.

I will take a picture later and post it on this page to what it looks like.

review_headline: Firestone Air Bags on a Chevy 2500HD Duramax
review_body:
Recently had the Firestone 2250 installed on a Chevy 2010 2500HD Duramax crew cab that is used to pull a Montana Mountaineer fifth wheel. With the new trailer weighing more than the older one we thought we needed some extra lift since the hitch mount weight on this fifth wheel is 2,200 lbs before you add weight to the cargo compartment etc.

The Firestone airbags we bought were the manual add air since the automatic air compressor doubled the price. So it is easy to manually add the air and one interesting thing we discovered and discusssed with the factory tech rep was the air pressure. We had put 40 lbs in the bags and then when we dropped the fifth wheel on the hitch we checked the air pressure once again. It was almost 60lbs which would give us 3,000 lbs of lift and looked way to high. The factory tech rep said that the correct way to measure the air is when it is hooked up. So we let some air out until the trailer looked level and the truck springs were carrying some of the weight. Then when we unhooked the trailer we checked the air again so we would know what the air should be when unloaded since that is how we most often would put the air in.

Have yet to make a long trip with these bags but that is coming up so I will revisit this review. I will say that the air bags lift easily and it is actually easy to overdo the lift. So far they appear to be a well built product. The only concerns that we have at all is that the left air bag isn't quite as verticle as the right one but the dealer said that was fairly common and the factory tech rep confirmed that. Also the instructions say that the weekly air loss can be as high as 3lbs on a 50lb air pressure which only experience with the product will tell us.

We carry a small air compressor with us on our trips so adding air to the truck tires, trailer tires, and the air bags won't be a problem. Normally the air compressor resides in my wood shop and is a small Bostitch finish nailer unit which turns out to work great with tires.

I will start out with a five star rating on this product for two reasons: easy to use and the factory tech rep is very accessible.

product_title: Progressive Suspension 11-1110 20.5" Fork Spring
review_headline: A Great Way to Improve Handling and Braking
review_body:
I put these on a 1980 Yamaha XS850LG, the Midnight Special. I know the springs don't say that they fit the specials, they are only supposed to fit the standards (XS850G). But, another site selling the same springs told me they would fit and I took their word for it. The springs come with white plastic piping that you can cut to length to act as a spacer to accommodate different fork tube lengths. They even come with a chart to tell you how long they should be for all the different bikes they fit. The Special, Midnight Special, and the Standard were all on there, with different spacer lengths of course.

For some reason my stock springs were incredibly soft when I bought the bike. Any braking would drop the front suspension half way down and hard braking would bottom it out. I tried changing the fork oil and raising the fork air pressure to the max, but nothing would help. I knew it wasn't the shocks because the suspension didn't bounce. I put these on and everything got better. Hard braking lowered the suspension half way, and I have been unable to bottom it out. Amazingly, the comfortable ride the stock springs provided was still there. These new springs absorb bumps 95% as well as the stock ones.

Having taken a fair number of forks apart, I can tell you these are some of the worst. This is in no way the springs fault, just be prepared for some busted knuckles. The top of the fork will only come off if you depress the part with the air valve in it, then remove a C-clip that fits into a grove on the inside of the fork. It is hard to explain in words, but it is a pain without 2 people, and even then its hard. Best of luck, its worth it.

product_title: einszett Polish Wax
review_headline: Excellent product and very easy to apply.
review_body:
I applied this product to both my Silver BMWs and my Black Lexus. I must say that it made the job easier due to it's liquid properties. It is easy to apply and wipe off. Not much elbow grease or pressure required. This is recommended for paint in good condition. If you have have a lot of scratches and spider web lines all over your paint, you may have to the to green bottle which is the polish. This one is a hybrid wax/polish..

I did the following to all of my cars. 1. Wash and dry. 2. Clay bar 3. Used Einzett Polish/Wax (1 coat) 4. Used Einzett Glanz Wax http://www.amazon.com/einszett-930207-Glanz-Wax-16-9/dp/B000V0DYUW/ref=pd_sim_auto_1 did (2-3 coats) The reason I did this many coats with the Glanz wax is that you can actually layer this wax unlike many waxes where the next layer will take off the previous. The results will give you a lot of depth to your paint and will last longer until your next treatment.

product_title: Zone Offroad 3" JK Suspension System 07-12 Jeep Wrangler JK 2 Door
review_body:
Super fast shipping, got it in three days.

Not difficult to install, Did it myself in about 8 hours over two days. Would of been faster but i had to go to the store for tools that i didn't have.

Would recommend the following tools:
1. Floor Jack. Yes you could do this with your regular jack, but it would suck. A bottle jack would work great also.
2. Air/Electric impact driver 1/2\\". Yes you could do this install with only hand tools, but once again, major suckage.
3. Metric and Standard sockets and combination open end box wrenches. No you can't do this job without these.
4. 10\\" extension for your sockets. This was one of the items i had to go buy, so no i wouldn't recommend trying this without an extender.
5. A friend who knows a little bit about cars would be helpful. I wouldn't call myself a mechanic, but I am not afraid to get dirty, and wrench a little bit. And if I can do this solo, just about anybody can. But someone to help you retrieve stuff that you left on the other side of the garage is always helpful.

Would recommend that you read the directions a couple of times, so you know what you are getting into, you can download the install instructions from the Zone off road website. Also search on U-Tube for install videos, can't tell you how much that helped.

product_title: URO Parts 17 13 7 501 959 Expansion Tank
review_body: This expansion tank is a good alternative to the $107 part that my BMW dealership wanted to charge me.  Installing this part is very straight forward due to the quick release clips that connect the coolant hoses to the tank.  Please be aware of one issue!  This will save you from having to reinstall it.  The male ends or \\"nipples\\" on this tank, which sink into the hoses, have ridges or burrs that protruded from them caused from the manufacturing process.  This small relief in the plastic doesn't make for a perfect seal.  You will get small leaks from this and similar aftermarket tanks.  I fixed this issue by sanding these nipples with 600 grit sand paper and polishing off the ridges.  Use very fine grit.  You don't want to damage the plastic.  Once smoothed out, everything snapped together and I have no leaks.  For $2 dollars of sand paper this was a money saving project.  If this seems like too much fussing around, go with the BMW dealer product.  They take the little burr off for another $60.  I hope this helps someone successfully install this expansion tank the first time.  Good Luck!

review_body: First of all, this is a excellent kit. It came well packaged and was shipped very quickly. While the instructions were nothing fancy, they were precise and  \\"somewhat\\" clear. I did however run into 2 problems. For my application (2001 Lincoln Navigator) the HID bulb has a ring at the base which must be removed and then reattached along with the factory security ring in order to properly seat the headlights in the factory lenses. It took me about an hour to figure this out since it was not mentioned in the instructions. Also after the install was complete the high beams did not work. After I googled my problem, I found out that I had to cut and splice the headlight input connectors wiring in order to properly work with my vehicle. Now the high beams work like a charm. You basically have to switch the 3 wires around untill your high beams work. I'm sure there are several people with this kit who just gave up on having high beams because of this simple problem. The instruction sheet did provide a diagram showing the diffrent wiring possibilities, but did not give a clear explanation on exactly what they were talking about. In the end, it really was a pretty simple fix. The lights work flawlessly! They are very bright(6000k) and light up the night. The factory Navigator lens does a good job of focusing the light just right so I'm very happy. Great kit so far.

review_body:

The manufacturer knows this but still sells the product. Why? Because hopeful truckers keep buying it!

There are other options but none are simple and some are quite expensive. Power Hunt makes a 12v coffee maker that actually works, but you don't plug it into the cigarette lighter. It uses a proprietary power strip connected directly to the batteries and a special plug with a heavy power cord.

This manufacturer is ripping off anyone who buys this thing. Spread the word... it's a fraud.

product_title: Speed and Strength Call to Arms Motorcycle Jacket Gray (Medium 5265)
review_headline: Cool look, not a great fit though
review_body:
I was looking for a different style of motorcycle jacket, and the Speed & Strength Call to Arms fits the bill. I wanted a jacket that I could wear with both my cruiser and street fighter, and not be your typical black leather jacket. The color is a sort of field-gray or gray-green, and there are tons of pockets to hold your wallet, keys, phone, paperwork, etc. The jacket is a good all-around jacket as well. It includes a Velcro-attached removable thermal liner and well-placed zipper vents that allow a large amount of air flow. It's obviously not a mesh jacket, but the vents do a good job at keeping you surprisingly cool in the summer. I wanted a jacket that was not covered in logos, and this one has two rather small S&S logos: a medium-sized patch on one arm and a small S&S logo patch on the back just below the neck. I haven't attempted it yet, but you could probably remove the patches by cutting the threading with a small razor blade or seam ripper and some patience.

My only two complaints about the jacket are the cut and the armor. It is a straight cut, and not tapered like most jackets. For those with larger mid-sections it might be fine, but for those with a more athletic build the wide straight waist will be a problem. When riding, it will billow up and likely not provide much torso protection if you did take a spill. I had to taper the waist myself by sewing in a couple of darts on the back of the jacket to add a taper. It's still a little loose in the middle, but at least it stays down now while riding. Also, the shoulder armor pockets sewn into the inner liner are too big and too loose due to the mesh material. This allows the shoulder armor to move around freely and slide to the back when riding. A few more minutes with the needle and thread fixed the problem though. The jacket includes back armor as well, which is a good feature. However, it's rather small and only covers the upper back. I removed the back armor altogether and just wear a separate armadillo-style back protector that protects the entire spine.

Overall I do like the jacket. The style is cool if you are looking for something different. It does have some dissappointing fit problems, but with some strategic \\"surgery\\" you can fix most of them.

product_title: Universal Low Back Synthetic Leather Seat Covers with Embroidery Flame Logos Black and Red color
review_headline: Not a quality product, though nice look.
review_body:
First off, I have to say that I wanted to like this product. It looks REALLY good! But unfortunately, I can't recommend them.
Summary
Pros:
Looks Great
Low price

Cons:
Awful smell
Very poor quality
Short longevity
Poor back seat fit (05 Hyundai Accent)

Like you, I came across this looking for a relatively inexpensive car seat cover. I read the reviews and hoped that those with poor reviews simply had high expectations. Sadly, I was disappointed. Installation was pretty simple on the front seats, though one elastic cord did just rip right out of the seam when trying to tie underneath the seat. The back seat was very difficult to install and a poor fit. When stretching the fabric (not even very hard) the under layer (foam) ripped several times but didn't go to outer layer, so I wasn't really concerned. Even with the poor fitting back seat I was happy with the finished look.

Now, only 1 week later, I have already had the driver's seat cover rip. Just from sliding out of the seat, the whole back seam ripped out. Now it won't stay put and I have to constantly readjust it prior to sitting.

Bottom line:
Invest in better quality seats. These are of the lowest quality. the synthetic leather layer is paper thin, almost like it was painted on. and the foam is probably 1/8 inch thick and not dense at all. If you want something to cover seats in a broken down car, these are for you. If you want something to cover your seats and last more than a week, these don't make the cut. Save your money and buy something better.

product_title: LeatherNu Complete Leather Color Restoration & Repair Kit
review_body:
I got this leather repair kit to attempt to repair one of the armrests in my car which had significant wear after 10+ years of \\"arm resting\\" on it! The wear consisted of cracks and rips in the leather, several large ones in the front and many-many tiny ones extending to nearly the middle of its length. So significant was the wear that I actually got a new armrest, but I thought I should give it a try. I had absolutely no previous experience in leather repairing, by the way.

I will start by briefly mentioning the instructions: you first apply a repair compound to fill in the gaps/holes in the leather (dries clear), then you paint, and finally you use a sealer compound (clear) to protect the paint if the area is under heavy use (the armrest apparently is; this last step may not be needed for other applications). Pretty simple eh? Read on!

Let me just say that I tried the repair twice. The first time I got a disaster! I think another reviewer mentioned it, taping the texture paper overnight after you apply the repair compound (per instructions) results in a sticky situation! The paper is not easy to remove afterwards, and if you apply a wet towel on top of it for 10 minutes to help in removal (per instructions), you still cannot take it all out perfectly, plus the moisture transfers onto the repair compound and weakens it. Rubbing to remove residuals of the paper (per instructions) makes it even worse as you will likely take out some repair compound with it. Not good! I ended up scrubbing (not just rubbing!) the whole thing with water to remove everything and start over. But make a note, this way you will make the original damage a bit worse, as this removes some leather with it.

The second time I applied the leather compound and used the spatula and my fingers to apply and make it nearly flush with the original surface. Took me 3-4 passes, once every hour or so. I ended up with a smooth surface, without any leather texture (I attached two photos at this stage - the top ones).

The paint was a pain to match, took me 2 days of mixing or so! At least I had the time available while playing with the repair compound :) But you get lots of colors and some basic mixing instructions to get the color you want. You just need patience... lots of it!

I then painted the repair, all the way from the front to midway. The paint is kind of thick, and dries out fast. I used the foam applicator to blot and feather away the paint (per instructions). Which is nice in theory, but in reality you end up getting some foam residuals of your project. I ended up using the foam applicator as if I was lightly sanding the project to remove everything (almost) as the paint was still drying. I forgot to mention you also get some brush bristles while painting, which can be removed with the foam applicator, in expense for more foamy residuals! The end result looked just okay, and without any leather texture. It then struck me, to use the texture paper on the paint itself. So I did. I applied another coat and instead of blotting/feathering or whatever, I just took a texture paper and pressed it on the wet paint, took it off after 5-10 seconds, and let the paint dry. The thickness of the paint is enough to preserve the texture and the fast drying helps. The result was a million times better than before (I attached two photos at this stage - the bottom ones).

Then I applied a thin coat of sealer with the foam applicator. The end result is very useable, although looking up close and under certain light conditions, you can certainly tell it is a repair and that the texture is not as deep as the original leather. But from 2-3 feet away, it looks very decent. In the car, where the lighting conditions are usually low and uneven, and there are shadows, etc., it looks nearly perfect.

Overall, I believe this kit is a decent choice. It is a shame they do not provide youwith more texture papers (more of the same kind I mean - you get 3 different textures but only 1 sheet 2-by-2 for each), especially since these are so easy to deteriorate (and if you end up using water to remove them, you can forget about them). To be honest though, I guess on a smaller repair, doing it per instructions might be fine. My repair covered nearly all of the 2-by-2 surface of the paper (and as a result, more of the paper stuck on my project). But anyway, it is just textured paper, so they could have included more of it, in my opinion. The amount of the other materials you are getting is sure to outlast the amount of paper. For instance, after applying the leather repair compound on all this surface twice, I still have more than half of it left.

My feelings are kind of mixed however. For a small repair, you might be better off having it repaired professionally (how much more would it cost?) and save yourself the time! For larger repairs, the cost-effectiveness is much better, although you cannot make it \\"like new\\". product_title: 3M 39010 Headlight Lens Polish and Protector Bottle - 8.0 oz
review_body:
I use this in conjunction with 3M's Plastic Cleaner. I use it to restore the headlights on vehicles. The two work very good together to clean up yellowed / fogged headlights from sun fade.

Both the cleaner and polish are used in the same manor as you use when waxing your car. Apply in a circular motion, let dry to haze, then buff off.

For an even better appearance, start with some super fine wet/dry sandpaper. I use 3 grades, starting with 400 grit, then onto 1000 grit, and then to 2000 grit. Get them wet, and rub away the yellow. Rinse between grades. Now move onto the Plastic Cleaner and then to the Plastic Polish.

Unless you have actual sun damage on the INSIDE of your headlights, they will come out looking new. Re-apply the polish generally twice a year if your vehicle is stored outdoors, or once a year if garaged.

When I finally took it to the Ford dealer a year ago, they said they could put some \\"anti-friction\\" additive in it to fix it. Unfortunately, it didn't work. So, fast-forward to this weekend when I changed the rear differential fluid over to RP 75W-140 Max Gear lube. Lo and behold on the first test drive, there was no chatter whatsoever!

Overall, the truck seems to be smoother driving, but that just may be my way of justifying the expense. I have generally held B&D products in high esteem, but from this point forward will regard them with close scrutiny before purchase. This is a poor, poor product.

product_title: Camco RV Awning De-Flapper
review_body:
I have used the original De-Flappers for years, you know the little wimpy ones. I have had them pull off, break, get loose, even had the fabric straps break. I bought a bunch of extra ones thinking as the quote goes, \\"quantity has a quality all it's own.\\"

Then I got these monsters last camping season and used them a lot, I'm talking several weeks, in some high winds and also with an occasional heavy wet snow load up in the mountains. I could not be happier with these. I read one review saying they weighed too much. They do weigh a lot, but I don't think that is a bad thing. They weigh a lot because they are truly heavy duty. When you open the box and inspect the de-flappers the weight will be noticeable. It says right in the product description they measure 3 x 7.3 x 12.5 inches and weigh 1.8 pounds (each), shipping weight is 6.2. I can't understand how someone can order something where the weight is disclosed and then complain about the weight; oh well.

I also read reviews saying the knobs come off and I was naturally leary about this. If the knobs have a propensity to do this it has not been seen on my units and I put a lot of torque on them. I know that if the large rubber knob(s) does come off I will simply weld a piece of steel to the head of the bolt (example: link from a chain would work perfectly) and crank it down.

When others I camp with saw these de-flappers they purchased some themselves. If knobs have come off I haven't seen such.

I saved the little de-flappers in case I need them. I have never used them since I got these monsters. Wish I had gotten them earlier.

product_title: Blitz 11903 Rhino Ramp 8000
review_body:

The mats I'm referring to were a little pricey, but they were rugged and I had one of them set directly under my wife's car that she ran over for a year so I knew they could take a punishment.

On the first try I ran my Ranger up on the ramps with the mats underneath. I was a little worried that the ramps would deform the rubber mats but after 45 minutes I took the truck off and the mats looked like nothing had been done to them. I was surprised.

On another safety note, if you do use these ramps make sure to chalk the grounded tires with a good made RUBBER tire chalk instead of the cheap plastic ones. I actually have had the plastic ones slip on concrete just like the ramps did. I think you can find these on Amazon pretty inexpensive and it may save your life.

I didn't see where the ramps were \\"bulging\\" at the sides as some reviewers have reported, but then again, I used my light weight truck and others might of tried heavier vehicles on the ramps.

I liked the idea that these can be stored inside of one another and they are fairly light weight.

The cons are that the company needs to go back to the drawing board and solve the slippage problem for rear wheel driven vehicles.

product_title: Dorman 689-108 Camshaft Synchronizer
review_headline: I wouldn't use it if it were the last one on the planet.
review_body:
I thought it would be better to just get a new cam synchronizer than clean up a junkyard part, especially since these are so inexpensive.

Oh, how wrong I was... Although it is CLEAN, that is about the only thing that beats a 100k mile USED OE unit from the junkyard. The "half-moon" window ring was loose, and popped right off upon receipt, so I fixed that - not a huge deal, but "really"??? The plate to which it attaches, the one that attaches to the shaft, was not tight on the shaft either. Again, I fixed that. Then I test fit it. The shaft was loose in the bore, as the housing is apparently NOT bored straight; when installed, you can rotate this thing, and the aux shaft gets harder to turn (binding at the gear) or easier to turn, depending upon how it is clocked!!! The shaft play out of the box was 1-1.5mm - COMPLETELY unacceptable. I replaced the gear immediately, as the one on it looked like some cast crap that would ruin my aux shaft gear due to the jaggedness of it.

Needless to say, I was not going to install this thing on my engine.

I literally took a junkyard part (OEM Motorcraft) with 100k miles+ on it, cleaned it up, and installed it. On the JUNKYARD PART with 100k+ miles on it - the shaft play was NOT bad, the "half-moon" window ring was TIGHTLY installed, and even the gear was in decent shape.

I'm not one to bash a product, but this thing is literally not worth the headaches. I'm not a professional machinist, but *I* could produce a better part. If someone REALLY wanted to use this thing, because there was no other unit available on the planet, they could take it to a machine shop, have the housing bored correctly, insert a new bushing, then fix the window ring, and buy a new drive gear. That would cost about as much as a brand new Morotcraft unit - which would still be better built.

I'm going to take the housing (cast aluminum) to the recycler next time I go, to recoup 25 cents in scrap - which is all that this thing is worth.recoup 25 cents in scrap - which is all that this thing is worth.

Luckily, my lugnuts are also 21mm, so I was able to use one of my lugnut sockets.

review_headline: Perfect Fit and Easy Installation for the Lexus RX
review_body: The AR-14A is an EXACT replacement for the rear wiper blade on 2004-2011 Lexus RX SUVs.  Unfortunately ANCO does not provide written installation instructions, but installation was very easy. The wiper arm needs to lift off the glass at about a 45 degree angle. The plastic trim cap at the base of the arm needs to be removed by gently prying the cap away from the wiper arm. Once the trim cap is removed the wiper arm can be lifted off of the glass at a 45 degree angle. The wiper blade is connected to the wiper arm using a \\"Roc-Lock\\" connector. To remove the wiper blade, simply raise the wiper arm off of the glass at a 45 degree angle, then rotate the wiper blade so that it is perpendicular to the wiper arm and gently pull the old wiper blade so that it releases from the wiper arm. To install the new AR-14A wiper blade, push the AR-14A blade at a 90 degree angle to the wiper arm into the Roc-Lock connector, then rotate the blade so that it is parallel to the wiper arm. Finally replace the plastic trim cap at the base of the arm and you are good to go! The replacement took about 5 minutes and did not require any tools. ANCO has an installation video at [...]

When I see it has less than 3 green lights (indicating a full charge) I will charge it to keep it ready at all times!  In my opinion it is a GREAT product, does what it says it will do, and very cheap insurance even if you never use it----but you probably will when you least expect it! Update:  4/7/17--------The  Jump-N-Carry 300XL is still going strong!  Charge it every 3 months weather it needs it or not----the only way to keep these chargers ready and full!  Not only have I used it as above, but I have helped other people to restart their cars when their batteries went dead, and got them on their way, all over the country at least 11 times since I got it!  All of them (mostly stranded ladies) were amazed what this little jump starter did for them and were very appreciative someone helped them!  Very happy to do that, and very easy with the 300XL!

product_title: DeoxITX10S Oiler, precision oiler oil 25 mL - X10S-25C
review_body:
DeoxIT is a high quality manufacturer, so for a few bucks more I opted for their oiler. This is standard silicone though, not a fancy hybrid of chemicals (like some of their other products). Since it's DeoxIT, you can expect high quality silicone, which is why I bought this one specifically.

I use this for fine instrument mechanisms, specifically some expensive dial calipers, O-rings for fuselages on outdoor equipment and the like.

If you are reading this review and looking at various oils, keep in mind what it is you want the oil for. Petroleum-based lubricants (WD40, BreakFree CLP, etc) will lubricate quickly and efficiently, but can break down composite materials. Teflon-based lubricants (DuPont, etc) are great for dry/film properties, reduce metal friction, but don't lubricate as well. Silicone (this) will not harm materials, has a lower lubricity, but will persist longer than any of the above. This is a great oil for clock mechanisms, swiss actions, and preserving polypropylene (and similar) composites from cracking.

product_title: Genuine Honda 08L04-SZA-110 Crossbar
review_body:
I installed these crossbars on our 2009 Pilot today. Here are a few notes:
* Popping off the end caps on the roof rails was a bit of an ordeal. I did not have the plastic trim removal tool referenced in the instructions. I worked with two small flathead screwdrivers, trying to be careful not to deform the plastic as I pried up the edges. But ultimately I found you do have to push pretty hard to get the covers to pop off.
* As someone else suggested, the installation is best done by two people pushing the crossbars forward in unison. If one side gets ahead of the other, it is easy to get the bars wedged.
* Neither my helper or I could not find any markings on the roof rails to align the crossbars. I pushed the front bars forward as far as they would go, kept the back bars as far back as they would go and used a tape measure to make sure they were even.
* As noted by another reviewer, the screws require a T-15 torx, not a T-30 as indicated in the instructions. Also, the screws were not self-tapping and in my case they were too big for the holes in the rails. I had to drill out the holes using a 5/32 bit in order to be able to get the screws in.

All in all, the installation was not too bad. Total time invested was less than an hour, the majority being spent trying to pry off the end caps on the rack, and also running back and forth to my shop to get the proper tools (torx driver, drill, etc.)

The only other thing is that if you want to put something heavy in the cargo area I would recommend laying down some plastic or something because the friction of the mat with the content you put in the cargo area might damage the mat. Or will at least be hard to slide in and out.

product_title: Robinair (11910) Digital Gauge - Low Pressure
review_body:
About the same size as a standard gauge, they (HP & LP) easily fitted on my Imperial Eastman 4 valve manifold. The gauge has a hard PVC casing with rubber cover that appears to be robust and should take a knock...or two.
I use kPa and deg C. The displayed pressure and temperature is easily set and is only required on the initial setup. The refrigerant can be changed easily with a press of a button. The LCD display is large, clear and easy to read looking directly at the gauge but is sometime difficult to distinguish when looking on an angle, even with the backlight on....but no real issue. When setting control cut-in and cut-out pressures, there is a small delay in the change of pressure displayed, so not ideal for this application. For general use the gauges are great, not having to pull out a PT chart to obtain an accurate SST or SCT. I don't know how accurate the PT conversion is for Zeotric blends such as R407c, and if the Bubble point and Dew point charts are used.
I'm very happy with these gauges and would recommend them, but only time will tell how robust they are.

product_title: CURT 13575 Class 3 Trailer Hitch
review_body: I read some of the reviews about this product and decided it was a good buy, even though I prepared myself for having a hard time installing it. Well, there is a trick to install it by yourself without having to remove any original vehicle parts. But to make everything easier, first lower and remove the spare tire. It will give you plenty of room under the car to work the screws. Now here's the trick: don't try to line up the hitch and lift it. It will not go pass the muffler protectors. The key here is to lay the face of the receiver (square hole) on the floor, which means that the sides will be pointing up. Lift the hitch into position and turn it 90 degrees towards the front of the car once you clear the muffler protectors. Install the screws and you're done. By the way, this trick  is NOT in the instructions that came with it so I had to learn it by myself. Now, this is heavy so having an extra couple of hands will definitely make your job a lot easier. Other than that, a sturdy, well made product. And as always, Amazon delivered earlier than scheduled. Ten stars: five for the product, five for Amazon.

product_title: Mr. Gasket 2842G Teflon Tape
review_body:
A few quick words on teflon tape -

This stuff is recommended by the manufacturer for use on fuel lines using their fuel line componets (elbows and barbs, etc). It works really well for that, and about any other use where you need an airtight seal between threaded fittings.

However, It should be noted that the tape needs to applied correctly. This means applying tape in the correct direction, as well as using the correct amount. There is a such thing as too much of a good thing. While this may not be important in water applications, it IS important in fuel applications where a piece of teflon tape breaking loose could lead to fuel system failure, and possibly severe engine damage.

For direction, you basically want to wrap the tape in such a way that the act of threading the two pieces together doesn't tend to unwrap the tape. For standard threads (which most everything is) - if you are looking directly into the male fitting (the fitting to be wrapped) you want to wrap in a clockwise direction.

Also, if you have to use more than about 1.5 to 2 wraps of the tape, something else is wrong (possibly damaged threads or something). Furthermore, if using the stuff on a fuel application, don't wrap the last few of threads of the fitting, as you don't want any loose tape sticking out to possibly break loose and mess stuff up.

Hope this helps someone out there.

product_title: TRANSFORMERS - AUTOBOT - Car, Truck, Notebook, Vinyl Sticker Decal #1036
review_headline: Now my Truck is an AUTOBOT!!!
review_body: I bought two of these stickers, and put one on my hood and the other on the rear window of my Ford Explorer.  My truck is a bit of an old beater, olive green, so I like to think with this sticker it is now old Ironhide.  The sticker has held up perfectly so far, but buyer beware, if you are going to put one of these on your car, you must follow specific procedures that the seller will not provide instructions for.  I used to put vinyl stickers on a variety of surfaces for my last job.  Here is what you need.  A soft edged tool made of plastic.  Then you must carefully wash the target surface and ensure that it is completely dry and clean.  The decal comes between two layers of stickers, one layer will peel away leaving the sticky side of the decal facing up from the non sticky layer.  Then you must CAREFULLY apply the sticker to the desired surface - CAUTION - you only get one try!!!  Then using the soft edged tool you must press out any stray bubbles from the decal portion of the sticker.  This required patience and being gentle.  Once you are confident that you've fully adhered the decal you peel off the other side at a hard angle while using the soft edged tool to press any stray edges of the decal that still peel up.  Caution here is required because it is easy to rip the vinyl decal.  Then as you peel away the sticker leaving behind the vinyl you will step back and admire how awesome your desired target looks with its new ornament.  I have had this sticker on the hood of my truck and on the back window for a little over a week.  It was harder to apply to the back window, but now they are both still good as new, and we have had temperatures ranging from freezing to 75 with direct sun.  There is a layer of road dust on these stickers that can be easily washed off, but once again, it is always wise to be gentle.  I highly recommend this product and seller to anyone who wants a great vinyl decal at a great price, both stickers cost me less than 5 dollars as the seller combined shipping, and they look cool!  Everytime we drive now I am always careful to command \\"AUTOBOTS - TRANSFORM AND ROLL OUT!\\"

product_title: TMS T-NS-MRC001 500-Pound Heavy Duty Motorcycle Dirt Bike Scooter Carrier Hitch Rack Hauler Trailer with Loading Ramp and Anti-Tilt Locking Device
review_body:
I can't believe these aren't outlawed. They shouldn't be allowed to be sold to the public. Let me explain something about trailer hitches. Most hitches, unless they are on a pickup or large SUV, are class I or II. They aren't rated to carry more than a 3,500 lb trailer with a tongue weight of 250-350 lbs. If you step up to a class III or IV hitch, you can get up to 5,000-8,000 trailer capacity, and up to 500 lb tongue weight. With additional equipment, like a weight distributor set up, you can carry up to a 10,000 lb trailer with a tongue weight capacity up to 1,000 lbs. Now, that's all TRAILER carrying capacity.

What you aren't being told, and most of the general public doesn't understand, is that a 500 lb trailer tongue weight (in other words, the tongue of your trailer as it sits on your vehicle's hitch, weighs 500 lbs) puts less stress on your hitch than if you have a 500 lb platform hanging off the back of your hitch. The stress of bumps and sways as you're going down the road with a trailer is distributed throughout the trailer's frame. If you have one of these platforms hanging off the back of your hitch, ALL that stress in on the hitch, and they ARE NOT rated for this. And remember, to get up to 1,000 lb capacity on your class IV requires a weight distributor, and this unit connects to your hitch AND the trailer tongue. You can't just hang something on the hitch and think you're good. You need some other connecting points. The only way to make these work is to have some straps or something that would connect up to the top of your tailgate, and from there, down to the back of the platform. And I'm pretty sure you don't want to drill holes in your tailgate to install some hooks.

Some of the cargo baskets you see to carry a suitcase or a cooler or something might be okay, as long as they don't weigh more than 100-200 lbs, depending on the class of hitch you have. As a rule of thumb, and this might be stretching it, is to divide your trailer tongue rating in half, and that's your max for using a platform of ANY kind. I really think hitch manufacturers should add this weight capacity on the sticker that they put on their hitches.

product_title: IceDozer Mini Ice Scraper
review_headline: What the Predator would use to scrape his windshield!
review_body:
...at least that's what I thought when I first saw it.

I'll try to be brief: the scraper is certainly unique - the handle is a large nub on the very top of it, which doesn't allow you to get a lot of force in the scraping motion over a traditional ice scrapper.The big downside of the handle is that your fingers have to curl under it, leaving them exposed to the snow and ice you are trying to clear. Not great if it was just a light frost and you are not wearing gloves.
The little rubber-like strips are supposed to allow for brushing away of snow, but the brush is such a small diameter that, again, a traditional scraper/brush combo outperform it by far. The scrapers themselves are on the underside, and are separate tiny blades that are staggered along with the arrow portion of the overall design. One of the ends is supposed to crack thick ice, but I don't see that happening (in fairness I have not tried this feature out so I cannot say for sure). a big downside to this is that it doesn't seem to work well on a lightly-frosted windshield. Oddly, it doesn't seem to really remove it no matter how hard I press on the thing. It is a bit better at thicker ice.
One cool feature it has is a little notch that clears off wiper blades. I have since bought another, much cheaper traditional ice scraper but have kept this around solely for that feature alone.
All in all, while it looks interesting as all get out, traditional designs have had better results for me.

product_title: Sylvania H7 EB EcoBright Replacement Bulb, (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Not an ECOBright bulb, more like an ECO-DIM one.
review_body:
There is a lot of hype on the pakaging:
Save Energy - from 9 to 21% wattage savings
Uses 9 percent to 21 percent less energy than traditional lamps and saves from $2 to $19 in gas over the life of a pair
25 percent brighter compared to aged standard bulbs
Pack includes two EcoBright H7 12.8V, 50W

Take the hype for what it is:

Understand that these bulbs are dimmer than standard H7, they save energy the same way a 60W bulb uses less energy than a 75W bulb.
Standard H7 bulbs use 55W, this is only 50W (9% savings).
A SilverStar Ultra High Performance halogen headlight (H7) is 65W!

They are not 25% brighter than a regular bulb, they are dimmer, at least they are clear that they are brighter than an OLD regular (55W), forgot to mention that they measure the regular H7 as it is about to fail (to get a favorable comparison).
Is like saying that your new VW has better fuel economy (or pollute less) than a 1955 Mercedes on its way to the junk yard.
They may last longer has they do not run as hot.

Is a trick restaurants and other businesses use with their incandescent illumination (use 130VAC bulbs instead of 120VAC on a 120VAC circuit) to get a longer life even if it is at the expense of lower illumination.

I'll used them only on the low beams and I do most of my driving in town. So for me they are OK.
I have tried their Silverstar Ultra in the past, they are brighter, but lasted 1/4th the life of a regular H7. Funny that that fact is clearly stated on this and regular H7 packs, but not on the SilverStar or SilverStar Ultra.

review_body:
It simply works and works great!

I have mine set up for two batteries, and that means the charger has four wires, a positive and negative for each battery, so my two battery system needed a \\"two bank\\" charger.

Multiple battery installations require one pair of wires from the charger to each individual battery. Generally you can get one to four \\"banks\\" on a charger. Each one charges a 12 volt battery at ten amps.

It is well sealed with epoxy, weather proof, temperature proof, and has two green leds, quite bright, that come on when the batteries are at 100% capacity. Two different leds show a red color while still charging, so it's hard to get mixed up.

This unit drops amperage in predetermined levels several times during the charge, ending at a trickle charges after the batteries are fully charged. This prevents overcharging, overheating, and lowering of battery fluid levels from heat, during the charging process. It also has the feature that cleans the plates in the batteries, which helps the battery life a lot and extends their peak performance. I don't know how it works...I don't care, as long as it keeps those expensive marine batteries alive and happy.

I wanted a battery charger smarter than I am, one I could plug and forget, even during rain, wind, heat of summer, to below freezing temperatures, and that's what I got. It has worked flawlessly.

You can find cheaper charges, but eventually that savings will be lost on more frequent battery change-outs, or worse, battery failure out on the lake. Just buy the best, and forget about having to worry whether it's doing its job correctly, and having to run out and undo the leads when the battery is full, to avoid overcharging.

I am impressed with the fact that this charger has a programmed chip inside to calculate, control, and vary the charging cycle amperage to accommodate the state of each individual battery. While it's best to use batteries with the same amp hours of capacity, some of us can't go out and drop over a hundred dollars on a new battery just to match capacities. I've mixed 90 amp hour and 115 amp hour batteries, and have had no problems whatsoever with this \\"intelligent\\" charger.

I'd recommend this charger. I'm very happy, and trust it to perform without fault for as long as I have it. review_headline: Westin Bull Bar 32-3605 installation for my 2011 4Runner

Best bull bar you can get for your SUV!

I will discuss the installation here. My estimated installation time is 5 hours (in stead of 30 minutes indicated in the manual and their advertisement). The Bull bar comes with 2 special brackets, which connect the bull bar to the front frame of the vehicle. Each bracket has 5 holes. 2 holes are used to bolt the bracket to the bull bar (bolts included). 3 holes are used to bolt the bracket to the frame of the vehicle (the 3 bolts are from the vehicle).

In order to see the \\"3 bolts\\", a plastic cover needs to be removed (5 screws). The bolts are very tight. I have to use my 18\\" wrench. My 8\\" wrench can't loosen them. The socket size is 12mm as I recall (could be wrong here). I bolted the left bracket using the 3 bolts. The space is limited and it is very difficult to tighten the bolts. A bigger piece of plastic cover (attached to the bumper) can be removed. Maybe removing it will make the job easier? So far, I spent about 1 hour and I figured I want to pay someone to do the rest.

I called a local garage and they quoted $75 to install the bull bar. It is a good size car repair shop with 90 years of history and a huge tools/parts section (5 times bigger than the tools/parts section in Wal-mart). I left my 4Runner with them for about 4 hours, and was told it is done. I got my 4Runner but found they forgot to put one of the bolts on the left (attaching the left bracket to the bull bar). I told them to put that bolt on and cut the plastic covers to fit to the vehicle. Note, after the brackets are installed, the small plastic covers can't be put back any more. After about 1.5 hours, I got my vehicle again. They did install that bolt. Again, the space is limited and to install it requires a lot of efforts. That's why they spent 1.5 hours just to install 1 bolt and 2 plastic covers. Well, they need some time to cut the covers too.

In order to check the small plastic cover, I have to look from under the vehicle and to my surprise they only installed 1 bolt instead of 3 on the right (attaching the right bracket to the car frame). Remember, I installed the 3 bolts on the left. So, another 1.25 hours passed, they finally finished everything.

As I said removing the bigger plastic cover may increase the installation speed. So, a VERY experienced installer may finish it in 30 minutes (I still doubt it though).

product_title: Silblade Flex Black Silicone Ultimate Wiper Blade
review_body: I have been using SilBlades on all my vehicles for the past 3 years.  The performance of the wiper blades are excellent and have not let me down.  I have read some of the recent reviews that indicated they did not fit well and fell off.  I had difficulty at first until I learned the trick to install them.  Once they are properly installed, they will not fall off.    The trick to install these on a J-arm is to first realize what actually holds these blades onto the  wiper Arm.  These wiper blades are held onto the Arm by the two ears that must extend past the crook in the J-arm.  This is almost impossible to do unless the wiper is rotated to allow the two ears to be beyond the plastic mount.  What this means is that the two ears are in free air allowing the ears to move outward while pushing the blade onto the J-arm.  Once the blade is pushed all the way on, the plastic mount prevents the ears from moving locking the blade onto the arm.  I hope I explained this well enough as I would hate to see anyone else return the product as it is well worth the money.

product_title: PIAA 19223 10-Watt Xtreme White Miniature Dome Light
review_headline: It is all about the color rating
review_body:
I purchased several sets of PIAA extreme white bulbs of differing sizes, tried them, returned some to Amazon then purchased some of what I returned again. Why?

PIAA, Hella, Sylvania etc. seem to market the non-HID or Xenon automotive bulb products primarily by wattage and light temperature (Kelvin). I do not normally find a lumen rating which I would prefer since my objective in upgrading bulbs is to see further or brighter. My 1991 BMW uses traditional halogen bulbs everywhere so I hoped for better-than-OEM. Here are my conclusions after installation and usage.

I find \\"wattage\\" as in 55w=110w misleading. I do not believe, and my opinion, that the extreme white bulbs illuminate any further than the original 55w halogen bulb. I placed one PIAA in one of two fog lights and observed equidistant visibility with it and the stock Hella type 9006 55w bulb. Thus, \\"lumen\\" would be the measurement I would have preferred rather than watts.

The Kelvin scale color temperature is what you are really benefitting from. I tested with an original, probably 3200k bulb on the right side, a 4000k 'extreme white\\" on the left side and big difference! The whiter looking 'extreme white' or any 4000k rated bulb or higher will look 'brighter' but it simply is a higher Kelvin scale color. I probably agree with the marketing suggestion that a whiter white may help you see more clearly in the dark, not necessarily farther out.

But here is the catch and why I returned some \\"extreme white\\" bulbs. Placed behind a color lens such as a side marker or turn signal, the color is not 4000k but becomes yellow or red. So, I see no benefit to the premium price for a 4100k bulb in this instance. To its credit, PIAA does not seem to suggest the low wattage bulbs for such application are any higher wattage than the stock bulbs.

To be clear, I suggest 'upgrading' to a higher kelvin-rated bulb only for clear lens applications such as backup lights, fog lights and headlights if your car uses older halogen bulbs in the 3200k range. The benefit is a whiter white that helps visibility with its contrast, not its lumens. I returned the side marker lights and wedge lights that fit behind color lenses. I re-ordered the wedge since I acquired new headlight assemblies that had a wedge bulb in addition to H1 bulbs not in the original BMW fitment. With the new headlamp assembly and PIAA extreme white bulbs, there is a decided color difference perceived as brighter but not illuminating further out.

I just returned from a 1400 mile trip using the PIAA extreme white bulbs. The road side signs seemed to pop out. I did not have any angry \\"you are too bright\\" flashes from on-coming cars. The higher Kelvin-scale bulbs are worth the upgrade for clear lamps, not colored lamps.lbs in the 3200k range. The benefit is a whiter white that helps visibility with its contrast, not its lumens. product_title: resqme The Original Keychain Car Escape Tool, Made in USA (Blue)
review_headline: Great "Just In Case" tool to have
review_body:
I bought 4 of these. Myself, my wife, my father and mother. I love to be prepared and think this is a potential life saver. When received, I test fired each one into a stack of newspaper to ensure the pin fired. Each one left the pin indentation in the paper. I will not \\"dry fire' them again as to not wear out the spring mechanism. The belt cutter is well protected from accidental injury and the safety clip covering it is firmy seated.

My placement of them in the cars is my preference and you may find other places better suited. I figured that if I even needed it due to a vehicle accident in my car, the airbags will be deployed and I may be disoriented. So attached to the keychain wasn't a good option in my eyes as the airbag will obscure it from view and if I'm inverted, it may be difficult to locate. Therefore, I 'zip-tied' it to the celing handle of my truck over the driver's window. This puts it inches from my head and in plain view. I also ordered the bright yellow for visability at night as I figured the black may be harder to see if in the dark or under water.

I also have easy access to this if I come accross an accident scene and I need to get people out of a car(s). By 'zip-tying' it using the blade cover to the Oh S#!t handle, a quick yank will release it from the handle leaving the blade cover in my car. After I use it, I can just snap the tool back onto the blade cover which is still fastened to the Oh s#!t handle.

product_title: Dorman 594-176 Harmonic Balancer
review_headline: Lighter than OEM, but worked fine.
review_body: Purchased a Dorman harmonic balancer, arrived fast with 2 days shipping, was about 50% of the cost of Pep Boys.    The actual part was maybe a pound lighter than the factory harmonic balancer.  I was initially concerned that it would cause the check engine light to come on.  However, after installing it no issues, and no check engine light.  So works for me...  One thing of note, a lot of people propose different workarounds for removing and loosening the harmonic balancer bolt and avoiding using the special factory tools.  Be very careful if you try to insert a bolt or pin into the two holes in the balancer and use that to prevent rotation of the crankshaft.  This is a cast part, and can break under the large loads required to properly torque the bolt.

review_body: If you own a 1996-2000 Chrysler / Dodge / Plymouth minivan with 3.8 engine, you must have this conversion.  My belt would leave me stranded every time it rained.  I installed this conversion and have not had a problem since.  OEM designed pulley system on these engines are a very poor design.  OEM idler and tensioner pulleys are smooth and nothing keeps the belt from moving sideways.  This conversion has grooved pulleys that hold belt in place. I also used a crowsfoot wrench with long breaker bar to move tensioner pulley far enough to install new belt.  It seems to be a tighter fit than the OEM belt.

Not only was the fan noticeably powerful but the temperature is now cold, in fact, we felt cooler cabin temp while driving backed up streets during the infamous San Diego blackout of 9/8/11 where the temperature around those days hit 100s.

The product seems solid enough.

product_title: Powerbuilt 647074 Ford Fan Clutch Wrench Set
review_body:
Worked fine... some tools of this class take some damage in their intended use, but this wrench set was in new condition after several uses. I got a few hints from others, I will pass them along here:

1. The very wide wrench is intended to be used on the end of a 1/2 inch ratchet or breaker. The jaw of it is meant to encompass the 4 small bolts holding the water pump pulley, thus preventing the engine side from turning. The longer one goes on the fan clutch shaft, pretty obvious.

2. Some engines will use a left handed thread here... you may find a warning on the fan shroud.

3. Depending on age and condition, this connection may be very tight. Verify you are turning the right way (left handed threads sometimes!) and you may have to put a 1/2 drive ratchet or breaker on the long wrench too. That's why the square hole is there.
