review_body: The Solar BA5 Electronic Battery Tester is easy to use and does test functions as stated. I used the CCA test for my battery to tell if I need a replacement soon. The only negative I will say is that the led screen is a little hard to read. The red output is hard to see when it's a nice sunny day outside; a dark blue output would be more readable in my opinion. Other than that is great!

product_title: 2001 GMC Yukon Keyless Entry Remote Fob Clicker with GM P/N: 15732803 (Please read description) With Do-It-Yourself Programming + eKeylessRemotes Guide
review_headline: shipping problems but they were on top of it
review_body: Programmed it without any issues.  Works just as expected.  It was accidentally shipped elsewhere.  I contacted the seller and they had a new one on its way within the hour.  Got it two days later! No reason to take any stars away for that.

product_title: Masterbuilt HWEBR HITCH-HAUL Web Tie Down System
review_headline: Good overall but could be better.
review_body: I got this net to go with my hitch-haul with rails. The net is a good size and works well. However the issue is with the hooks. They are made of plastic and the hooks are too small for the bars/tie down points. The bars + carrier + net are all the same brand so you would think that they're all made to work together. The hooks on the net are a bit too small, so when you hook them onto the rails or the tie-down spots the hooks get twisted. If it wasn't for that I would have gave a 5 star rating.

product_title: Panoramic Rearview Mirror
review_body:
1. It will work well enough for you if you can get used to the differently-proportioned reflected images inherent to curved mirrors; similar to the \\"Objects in Mirror are Closer than they Appear\\" notice on the passenger-side mirrors of US vehicles.
2. If your sun-visors' contours match the sides of the stock mirror closely when they flip-down, well, this longer mirror will get in the way. OTOH if your visors are nowhere near the mirror, such as in some vans, then this will do you nicely in covering all the [rear] angles.

product_title: AMC-400 Lightweight Aluminum Motocross & Dirt Bike Carrier for 2" Hitch Receivers
review_body: Very easy to use. Removal is just as easy. Holds my flat trck bike with no problems. Well worth the price. Great product!!

product_title: Akebono EUR946 EURO Ultra-Premium Ceramic Brake Pad Set
review_body: I bought these pads because of claims of quietness and little brake dust.  Both are very true.  Almost no brake dust after a few weeks of use.  Also absolutely quiet in my installation. I will say that the initial bite is a bit less than other pads, and the online reviews state this as well.  It takes a bit more pedal force than before.  Overall very pleased.    Updated November 12, 2010    The initial bite issue I report has since gone away as the pads and the disks broke in a bit.  It took in my case over a month.  The car now stops the same as the stock BMW pads.  Very pleased.  These pads show so little brake dust it is amazing.  If I look at the rear wheels that have stock BMW pads, and the front it looks like I just washed the front wheels while the rears are filthy.  I most certainly will be buying these pads again.  They are still silent.

product_title: Toyota Replacement Fog Light Assembly - Driver/Passenger Side
review_body: Purchased to replace a factory fog light assembly that melted, this fit right into my 2006 Tacoma. Great match to the factory light on the drivers side!

product_title: Actron CP7830 Hand Vacuum Pump
review_headline: Actron CP7830 Hand Vacuum Pump Review
review_body: It came promptly. It is made to last - Not plastic! We are using it with an adapter to vacuum pack dry products such as beans, nuts, and grains in mason jars. It also builds your muscles.

product_title: Kat's 11611 600 Watt 51mm Frost Plug Heater
review_body: First one lasted 2 months. Second one lasted 1 month. The element will blow. The second one I put on a timer, so it did  not even run all night. It probably had less than 40 total hrs on it. You get what you pay for. I guess for 10 bucks you can't expect too much. Bought my last one of these.

product_title: Security Chain Company Radial Chain Cable Traction Tire Chain - Set of 2
review_body: Just received my new snow-chains(SC1026) made by SCC or Security Chain Co. So far everything looks great for something under 35 dollars with next day delivery.     The construction of the chains is appropriate for the price. Don't expect long-term use of this product. They're made using stainless 3/16 inch cable and mostly all metal hardware, minus the plastic hooks for securing the excess cable during installation.    Maximum speed is 30 mph and minimal bare pavement driving is recommended. They include a one year limited warranty which is voided if chains or improperly installed or driven at speeds in excess of 30 mph.    Overall these chains are great for and emergency but i wouldn't recommend them if you'll use them frequently. The model I purchased fits a variety of tires sizes and that was the most important feature to me being that i use multiple vehicles. I hope that i'll never truly need to use them.    Buy if you just want to be prepared and not spend over 40 dollars. My opinion is you won't find any other chains in this price range that are this well made.     Kev.

product_title: Animal Print Steering Wheel Cover and Shoulder Pad - Zebra Pink
review_body: Nice covers . . . wish there had been more choices, but am happy with the product.  Looks exactly like the images shown.

product_title: Bosch ICON 426A Wiper Blade, Up to 40% Longer Life - 26" (Pack of 1)
review_body: Quite simply the best wipers I've ever owned.  Great performance & easy installation.    The only complaint I have is the connecting point sits high on the wiper, so your wiper arm will sit higher than with OEM wipers.

product_title: 3M 39008 Headlight Lens Restoration System
review_headline: Result is not permanent, protectant sold separetely
review_body: I actually bought this kit plus the Turtle Wax T-240KT Headlight Lens Restorer Kit.     Quick rundown on the differences:    3M Headlight Lens Restoration System   * $12 after rebate  * drill attachment  * dry sanding method  * comes with a small bag of polish compound  * lens protectant sold separately    Turtle Wax T-240KT Headlight Lens Restorer Kit  * $8 no rebate  * no drill attachment  * wet sanding method  * comes with a bottle of polish compound  * lens protectant included    I first use the Turtle Wax kit on my Camry because the haze is less severe than my Honda Del Sol. After polishing and a swipe with the included lens sealant, the result was simply amazing. I then tried out the 3M kit on my Honda. It was tricky to get even sanding due to protruding area on my headlight. The result was good once I finish compounding but not good enough compare to Turtle Wax kit. Maybe Turtle Wax has better polish material I don't know but one thing is for sure, once I swipe with the leftover lens protectant (Turtle Wax calls it sealant, it's like a piece of wet tissue), the result just simply takes my breath away.  Without the sealant, my headlight looks dull even after polishing, if 3M includes some sort of sealant in this kit, I would have give it 5 star and very much prefer this over Turtle Wax kit.

product_title: Medo BRP22 Big Fresh - New Car Scent
review_body: This new car scent used to be the best, but now....NOT!  It is horrible...I even wrote the company about it.  I wish they would bring it back...its smell was GREAT, but now it smells like windex...i have just about tried everything else and it does not bring a smell even close to that...i have one last bottle of the new car scent and I won't even spray it (just smell it) because there are no originals left...sucks!  The only other car scent I know that is refreshing is a collision shop that my friend owns...and he won't give the scent unless i need a job every red moon...sucks...some kind of friend...  but anyways why would they change the scent? i used to buy at least 2-3 times a week which result in a profit for them...but who knows?  we need more people to petition to change it back immediately...  i tried critically thinking about every issue...maybe it was harmful...maybe they used some of the old techniques of the \\"new car scent\\", but whatever...i want it back...that is what made me love my baby (car) because of that smell...i have to agree with almost every review that is against auto expressions newest car scent product....  If anyone comes across a similar scent... please let me know...thanks!

product_title: Motorcycle Jackets - Classic Biker Leather Jacket 34
review_headline: Well worth it - excellent heavy jacket for riders
review_body: It weighs a ton and came stiff as a board, but with liberal applications of leather conditioner and mink oil, it's softening up.  It's warm, no air leaks, and I have full confidence it would take quite a bit of punishment before tearing or abrading, even in a spill.    The zip-out lining is a bit light and is only a vest - no complaints on this, just an FYI.

product_title: mobile case
review_body: Valeo is standard equipment on pricey cars. They are far superior to wiper blades with brackets.  They last longer and really clean the windshield without streaks or smears. Cost more but worth it.

product_title: Drive Accessories KT-1011-15S/L, Nissan, 15" Silver Replica Wheel Cover, (Set of 4)
review_body: I bought mine for $22 at Autozone. This is a very good product since I can adjust the ring to fit tightly my rims. Unfortunately I knew this trick only after I loss one of the 4 wheel covers. I lost it a yesr later. So bad I cannot find a 14\\" on Amazon.com to replace the lost one.    Very good product. Easy to remove, easy to adjust.

product_title: 1992-1999 GMC Suburban Headlight Assembly (Composite Type) (1993 1994 1995 1996 1997 1998 92 93 94 95 96 97 98 99) - One Pair(Both Driver and Passenger Sides) - DOT Certified Headlight
review_headline: Great price, but the quality is lower
review_body: These headlight assemblies worked great.  I have to admit, I was leery about the low price, but I took the risk based on the Amazom.com name and it turned out ok.    The assemblies work well, were easy to install and just needed headlight aiming when complete.   The gauge of the plastic framing/housing is lighter than the original thickness, but that doesn't seem to impact the effectiveness at all.  It sure is great having clear bright lights again, and being able to see the edges of the road.    It comes well packaged, and includes standard Phillips halogen bulbs as well!    Note that more product details can be found on Amazon under the product listings for the individual passenger or drivers side.  Curiously, the Amazon listing for the 'package' set of both doesn't have as much detail, and i might not have purchased except I found the packaged set only after i had already discovered the more informative writeup for an individual side.    However, a month after installation, both sides now have condensation on the inside.  I double checked that the new bulbs supplied with the unit were snuggly installed.   So,  I guess it must be a poor seal between the front clear plastic lens and the back reflector part of the assembly.  That's sad.

product_title: WINEGARD GM-MP1 Carryout(R) MP1 Manual Portable Satellite Antenna
review_body: Great space saver while traveling and camping. Quick and easy set-up. Can't blow over. Small and inconspicuous. Seems easier to acquire the satellite.

product_title: K&N 33-2207 High Performance Replacement Air Filter
review_body: I've had K&N filters before and I'll continue buying them in the future.  This filter is of the same high quality as all the other K&N filters I've used.

product_title: Monroe 171580 Quick-Strut Complete Strut Assembly
review_body: If you are the mechanical type and like doing the work on your vehicle yourself, then the Monroe complete strut assembly is for you. It doesn't get any easier than this product. Just remove your old strut and replace it with this complete assembly, job done.

product_title: Classic Accessories 73727 MotoGear Motorcycle Tail Bag
review_body: This bag is just the right size for my V-Star 1300.  I needed just a little more room for overnight trips, and the space suits me well.  I was very disappointed with the straps, and the way they \\"loop\\" around a piece of the bike.  The long back strap split across the fender on the first mile, and I had to throw it away.  I followed the recommended instructions (which state that the straps are adjustable for any motorcycle), but the recommendation was flawed for a cruiser.  However, there are still four other straps.  I'm not returning it, because I figured out how to secure the bag to the frame without tearing up the straps, but it's not as easy and quick as the description says it is (unless you want your stuff to go flying off while you're on the road).  It does fit nicely on the back seat (I don't have a sissy bar or back rest), and the rain cover is a great idea.  I'm keeping it because I don't keep it on the bike all the time.  Overall, a decent purchase for the price.

product_title: Ford Logo Oval Decal
review_body: Ive ordered this item twice and both times its out of stock if its not in stock take it off the site

product_title: A Set of 2 Universal-fit Hawaiian Front Bucket Seat Covers for SUV / Truck Seats with Armrest - Blue Hawaiian Hibiscus Floral Print
review_body: I have vinyl seats in a Ford E350 and spent a lot of time researching a seat cover that was affordable that would fit.  These slid over the back of the seat nicely, but the portion that covers where you sit does not wrap entirely around the base and the few elastic loops meant to help secure it don't hook effectively to any part of my seat.  So, for the price and it not being a custom product it works.  Unfortunately I'm going to have to do some tweaking so that the bottom doesn't slide around but actually stays tight on the seat.

product_title: Motorola H680 Bluetooth Headset
review_headline: It is great for what i use it for
review_body: I love it!! but there is a slight static sound when using it.  I bought this to use for Play station online, I can't even hear the static when gaming so it doesn't bother me at all.  But if you're one of those people who are wearing a headset 24/7 waiting for a call, and a small crackle sound will drive you nuts.  Find a different headset.  Oh, and it is an awesome fit.

product_title: CURT 13506 Class 3 Trailer Hitch
review_body: The hitch itself is very solid and sturdy.  Installation was definitely not as easy as advertised for my 2001 Ford Escape, I have the model with the OEM class II hitch/integrated bumper.  The holes in the hitch were just a bit off so I ended up having to file them to open them up a bit to allow the hex bolts to line up with the OEM holes.  I imagine if it werent for the OEM hitch they would have been fine.  I was told about 80 minutes for an average do it yourselfer, took almost three hours because I had to file the hitch and try to mount it a couple times and then drill the two center holes.  Frustrating installation, but the hitch feels solid once its mounted.

product_title: Beck Arnley  024-1247  Timing Belt Tensioner
review_body: What I wanted and ordered was a timing belt pulley. What I got was a balance belt pulley. Big difference. They should research what they have before selling it. Now I've wasted money and time.

product_title: INNOVA 3721 Battery and Charging System Monitor
review_headline: Essential if driving an older car
review_body: Well, this monitor did the trick, for now all I do is plug it in the cigarette lighter, and voila, I can tell if it's charging. As said, most times it's charging, but now I have the security of knowing if/when it's not, and I don't have to spend over $300 to get a new starter motor but at least the mystery is solved.  The monitor also indicates the battery voltage when the motor is not running there's a nice diagram  that comes with it that tells you what's good and what's not. If you have a suspicious electrical charging system, I highly recommend it. I have a 9 year old toyota truck that has a questionable system. It charges most of the time, but I never knew when unless I actually got out and put a voltmeter on the battery with the engine running.

product_title: Energy Suspension 16.18109R Master Set for Honda Civic Si
review_headline: Best Buy. A must for Racers
review_body: This product does everything it says it will do. I never had such handling before. Really good for high speed driving.

product_title: ANCO 31 Series Wiper Blade
review_body:
I bought this item for my 2003 Toyota Camry because Consumer Reports recommended it. Easy installation. Recommended.

Update 1/22/11: You'll need a 19\\" and a 24\\" for your Camry. Wipers work well. I don't contend with snow, sleet, or frozen stuff on windshield since I'm in sunny Southern California, so I cannot speak for those conditions.

product_title: Schumacher SE-4020 10/40/200 Amp Wheel-Style Charger/Starter
review_headline: The best solution for the price

I found my reaction times slowed greatly. I also think there should be something to secure the windshield to the hood as there is only a strap that goes side to side that does not prevent the windshield from flapping in the wind. product_title: Apex RLB-2301 Universal Roof Crossbar
review_body: While I agree with other reviewers that that the product is in general terrific (i.e., sturdy, fits easily, water proof) and has a good price, it has one serious setback in that it does not have a lock.      I realized this in the middle of a trip, when we stayed at a hotel.  When I was checked to make sure my roof-box was locked, it suddenly dawned on me that someone can very easily remove the entire assembly and carry it away.  It does require two people to do it, given that the total weight is high (i.e., 35 pound for box plus baggage plus racks) ... but still, it is cause for concern.    If someone has figure out a good solution to this problem, please post.

product_title: Cruiser Accessories Tuf Flat Shield Novelty / License Plate Shield
review_body: Exactly as portrayed, excellent quality clear license plate cover and it arrived in only 3 days!      Thanks,    DM Yohe

product_title: Autel MaxiScan MS300 CAN Diagnostic Scan Tool for OBDII Vehicles
review_body: This works like a charm. The price is right and it doesn't take forever to boot up or have to have information plugged in like a scan tool with more features. It's great for pulling codes in the lot quickly.

product_title: Blue Kirby Lanyard with 2" Pink Plush
review_headline: Adorable addition to any cell phone!
review_body: Yes, lanyards come with everything nowadays, but sometimes, it's worth shelling out a few bucks to get something cute for your phone. This is one of those sometimes. Made by Banpresto (the makers of many high-quality video game plushes), this little lanyard will brighten up whatever you wish to attach it to. The plush is very high quality and feels like it's built to last. The lanyard itself is made of a silky, satin-like material. It's comfortable to hold, and makes an excellent strap. Admittedly, it's a bit large to use for a cell phone, but I like it all the same. This would also go great on a DS or other small electronic device.     Be aware, however, that you'll get a random Kirby, not necessarily the Star Rod wielding Kirby pictured. I got a very fierce-looking Fighter Kirby. Still adorable all the same!

product_title: Pure Lye Drain Cleaner / Opener, 2 lbs.
review_body: I could have gone down to the hardware store on the corner and bought lye for my soapmaking, but even with the high hazmat shipping cost across the country, it was still cheaper to buy from these guys.  The Buy-5 deal took $15 off and made the shipping affordable.  The lye is great, dissolves well and doesn't leave caustic pockets in my soap.  Fast service, good product.

product_title: Covercraft C80002RB Ready-Fit Car Cover Evolution Retail Box Evolution-Tan
review_headline: Great fit, nice material, and worth every penny
review_body: Covercraft makes some great covers. The material is dense and soft. This fit my Miata perfectly.

product_title: PACTS High Visibility Wheel Chock

product_title: Raider Open Face Helmet (Black, Large)
review_body: I found the sizing measurements form the manufacturer website.  I ordered the proper size for my husband's noggin accordingly... however, it must run small!  He could barely get it on his head! I had to send it back & we will be ordering the next size up as soon as the return is processed.  It is a really nice helmet especially for the price.  Just way too snug!

product_title: Champion Power Equipment 46534 4,000 Watt 4-Cycle Gas Powered RV Ready Portable Generator With Wheel Kit (CARB Compliant) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: The other day we had no power. I went to the garage and got the generator. I hooked it up and we had power in the hole house. We have two refrigerator. No problem for the CHAMPION GENERATOR to handle.

product_title: Walker Products 250-24301 4-Wire Oxygen Sensor
review_body: Two things to know before reading this review:  1)  I am an incurable miser...in extremis!  2)  This sensor HAD to work as I had to smog check my car to renew its registration...just before leaving for a 3-month trip!    I have a 1999 Ford Contour SE Sport 2.5L V6 and \\"mistakently\\" ordered this part (should be 250-24302!) because another website said it was meant for a failing pre-cat.  Turned out to be the cheapest O2 sensor (w/FREE SHIPPING) on Amazon, something near to every Pinch-Penny's heart!  When I discovered the discrepancy by consulting Walker's website, I promptly searched for more info.  This sensor apparently is meant for the Ford Econoline E-series vans.  I also found that so-called \\"universal\\" sensors would substitute equally well for my car and the vans.  I presumed, therefore, that the only difference would be the connector. I fretted about this until it arrived and found alternate sources for the correct part should my assumption prove fatal.  As you can probably tell by the 5-stars everything worked out great!  Removing the part from my car it looked identical to this one (same threads, same configuration, same wire length, etc) EXCEPT for the connector.  Furthermore, the connector was easily disassembled and swapped so that in 5 minutes, I had it ready for installation.  It even came with anti-seize compound!  Because of Ford design the part was difficult to access but well worth the effort: the car runs better now and passed smog with amazing numbers!    I wouldn't recommend my substitution but I'm convinced this part would work adequately for its correct usage, too.  I also ordered the CORRECT post-cat (Walker 250-24001), which worked well.

product_title: Spectra Premium TD84 Distributor
review_body: I got my item on time and it worked right out of the box. No issues yet!

product_title: Camco   Vinyl Spare Tire Cover
review_headline: Fits well, looks good, and durable
review_body: I bought this to replace an old spare tire cover for my tent trailer. It fits well, looks nice, and was easy to install. The quality looks good, I expect it will last a number of years.

product_title: 1998-2003 Toyota Sienna Plastic Liftgate Tailgate Handle
review_body: It was the perfect part for the job to fix the back hatch handle on my 2003 Toyota Sienna. I saved over $200. looking up the directions on the internet and fixing the broken handle myself.

product_title: Power Medicial WheelChair Mobility Carrier Rack Ramp
review_body: This is a great carrier. The price is the best I have seen anywhere. I can now take my power chair with me where ever I go.  Thank you Amazon for having this carrier at a great price!   For someone who is disabled & having to live off Social Security finding a carrier at an affordable price was impossible until Amazon made it possible.  If you need a carrier this one cannot be beat.   Thank you, thank you, thank you!

product_title: Dorman 77493 Exterior Left Hand Door Handle
review_headline: Nice Replacment US made door handle
review_body: Bought and installed both side door handles from Dorman on a 97 Sebring.  After searching the internet to find best product and best price...I chose the USA made Dorman handles off Amazon.com.  Researching the Dorman product I found that they had redesigned the handles fix OE short comings (ie breaking off in your hand)  The Passenger side feels solider in hand installed, but both seem to be superior to the the over-seas junk.

product_title: Specialty Products Company 74910 Cam Knock Out Punch
review_body: Great little tool..Very well made and a must have tool for wheel alignments..I was able to punch out those factory metal inserts in minutes.

product_title: ACURA Legend 1993 93 / / Hood / Lift Supports, Struts. Units Are Pair (2) Priced L & R
review_body: The struts arrived a day earlier than anticipated.  They were easy to install on my 95 Legend.  Cheap OEM replacement; pair was about 1/3 the price of one from Acura.    When installing these struts, you might want another person holding the hood for you, especially if you have a heavy hood like a Legend.  My assistant was a baseball bat, and it didn't listen very well.

product_title: Trimax MAG200 Resettable Combination Bent Pin 5/8" Receiver Lock
review_body: This is a great product. I hate to have different keys for every lock so finding this combination lock pin is great. I have a tow bar setup so I wanted several to lock the very expensive bar and hitch assembly for security. This fit the job perfect.

product_title: Gel-Gloss Auto Leather Conditioner and Protectant - 16 oz.
review_body: This is a great product and I received the shipment right away.  This product is good for faucets with a special finish.  I have a black painted faucet made by Danze company.  I have never been able to find a product to clean it until now.  Faucet brite cleaned off the scum with a protective coative.  The faucet looks like new.  Before this product, the flat black paint was starting to chip off.  Fortunately, I was able to get a new faucet, and now I can have a clean faucet.

product_title: AMP Research 75300-01A Bedstep
review_body: This is a neat idea.  It works good and is strong enough. It makes it easy to step up in the bed and folds up out of the way. I had to adapt it to my avalance though.  I would like it better if they made one to fit my truck.

product_title: PerTronix 1146A Ignitor for Delco 4 Cylinder
review_body:
When I went to my local marine shop to get points for my Mercruiser Stern Drive was I ever in for a shock. The point and condenser set I used to pay $3 to $4 for was now $44. I decided it was time to make the switch. I have installed Pertronix systems in two of my classic cars without incident so I ordered the replacement for my boat. Installation was simple and quick. Since I take my boat to places where a stalled engine could be dangerous I didn't want anything unreliable and so far I have not had to swim home. Just be careful to check and re-set your timing. When I installed this device it radically changed my timing.

Just in case something happens I kept the old system on board.

product_title: Motobrackets 269680 Upper Fairing Stay Bracket for Kawasaki ZX-12R fits 2002 2003 2004 2005
review_body: Well, I received my Motobrackets fairing stay today and have the following to report regarding these aftermarket parts:    1) It looks and weighs ALMOST the exact same as the Kawasaki part.    2) The welding is definitely not as tidy or clean as on the Kawasaki part, but it's definitely strong.    3) The part came painted a flat black, as opposed to the Kawasaki part's gloss finish.    3) I needed to drill out the upper bolt hole as the two pieces were not lined up properly when it was welded and there was a slight overlap that was preventing the bolt from passing through (2 second fix, no biggy).    4) one of the gauge cluster brackets (upper right) was placed slightly off line when welded in place, and although it was easily bent into proper placement, the flat black paint cracked and flaked during this process (Flat black touch up paint applied, problem solved.)    All in all, the fit was better then I had expected regarding the reviews I have seen, and for half the price of OEM, once it was installed, I could not tell the difference from the original part and I'm happy with the purchase. In the world of aftermarket, this is a TRUE knockoff part, identical in looks, but definitely cheaper in build.    I'll be going this route again if I need another one, which I hope is NEVER, haha.

product_title: Surf City Garage 103 Dash Away Interior Detailer Spray - 24 oz.
review_headline: Great car interior cleaner by the pros
review_body:
Designed by pros to clean ALL of the interior of your car, I was happily impressed that it not only brought the original look to my Corolla but helped get out some spots on a seat. The smell is \\"vintage car cleaning\\" smell which isn't bad, but good, and leaves no odor at all, but when I was cleaning, it made me feel like I did decades ago giving a new car a better cleaning. Detail of where I'd wiped it on the back dash showed up when I was in direct sunlight and I could see both the uncleaned surface and the majority that I'd Surf City'd. Supposed to work on soft leather, too, but that ain't in my ride.

Cleaned pedals and trim nicely. Easy to apply (spray, but shake well first) and a use mean, clean towel.

Cleaned the lighter gray interior of another Toyota, too, and I could see the change. While we'd been using harsh household stuff recently, this is made specifically for a car and boy, nice work. All in all, a much smarter purchase than multiple cleaners out there! Nice to have my original interior back and all out of one bottle!

product_title: Meguiar's W7006 Mirror Glaze Professional Soft Buff 6.5" Foam Cutting Pad
review_body: This pad and the yellow polishing pad are perfect. Cell foam material is durable, wash and reuse. This pad worked perfectly on my Home Depot's Ridgid Random Orbital Sander with the hook and loop pad. Don't spend $140+ on a so called \\"car\\" random orbital polisher. The Ridgid is basically the same thing...yet only costs $60 and I can use it for home improvement work after my car is done. Meguiar's Scratch X 2.0 also works good with this pad to remove minor scratches and blemishes. Use Ultimate Compound for heavier oxidization.

product_title: mobile case
review_body: Installation was a breeze. This blade is about half as wide as the OEM blade and not as rigid. product_title: Rally Pack By Dowco - Motorcycle Tank Bag w/Window - Magnetic Mount - 1 Year Warranty - Water Resistant [ 50108-00 ]
review_body:
Under $40 and free shipping might make you suspect this is cheap quality, but nothing could be further from the truth.
I have used the bag a lot on longer trips, and don't even use the extra strap to attach around the steering column, it doesn't move!
And I mean fully loaded (I'll get back to that) at 70mph, round corners in all weathers on my FJR 1300, it's really great.
When I arrive, a gentle but firm tug under the magnets and voila, it's off, and then stores completely loaded into one of my hard luggage bags.
With a large map pocket on top (accessed from inside), for rallies, and unfamiliar terrain, a smaller front zip compartment for cell phone, sunglasses etc, and then the main zip compartment, it's really great, looks good, and fits really well. I haven't tested it in really heavy rain, but it has stood up so far to a few showers, maps and contents dry inside.

I've been using mine mainly over the summer, so I put inside the bag:

My Mesh Armored Jacket's detachable liner for cool evenings
Froggs Waterproof set
Spare maps
Bottle of drink
Helmet Lock & Cable
Snacks, spare gloves, glasses case

With these contents it's padded out nicely, but it's still easy to see over, and once you line it up on the tank and fold out the sides, there's a nice \\"thullunk\\" as the magnets latch on and it's not going to budge. This also means it's really easy to lift off for gas stops, without having to fiddle with straps and buckles. The only thing it doesn't have is a special window or housing for a GPS, no biggy for me as I don't use one, and if I did I could place it in the map pocket and thread the wire through the zip. Those who use GPS a lot might want to look at other bags.

A real winner, and a great price - 5 stars

product_title: Portable Air Compressor and 12' Extension Cord Bundle
review_body:
After using this compressor for over a year (and extensively throughout the summer), I feel reasonably confident saying that the VIAIR 85P is a well built unit, country of origin aside. Should this unit fail in the future, I will update my review accordingly.

It performs admirably, and the pressure gauge is consistent if somewhat inaccurate. It always reads +2PSI higher than it should. This makes it easy to know when the desired pressure was reached. Please note that I am comparing its accuracy against a known high quality dial gauge. It is remotely possible (though reasonably unlikely) that the VIAIR 85P is correct, and that my previous dial gauge is incorrect. Given that my dial gauge matches with other high quality gauges, I feel reasonably confident that it is the former.

The screw on brass chuck works well. It was a convenience to not have to hold it in place, though threading it on with cold, stiff fingers, or hands in gloves might be more difficult than holding an air chuck on. Notably, the valve is permanently attached to the hose. You will not lose it, but then again, you are limited to which attachments you can add on. Thankfully, the compressor comes with a few attachments so you can use this compressor with a basketball/football/soccer ball, inflatable mattress, etc. Unfortunately, I was unable to get a standard air chuck to attach.

The only other item of note is that the 12V adapter does not work with a MINI. This is not a fault of the air compressor as there are many other 12V accessories that are known to not fit a MINI. Many cars of German origin use a 12V socket that is sized slightly different from the rest of the world. If you were planning on using this with a MINI, plan on picking up a [[ASIN:B00065L2D8 12V hookup]] directly to your car battery. Additionally, you will need to find a 12V hookup that is rated for a relatively high (15A) current.

product_title: Bosch ICON 419A Wiper Blade, Up to 40% Longer Life - 19" (Pack of 1)
review_body: I purchased these Bosch Icon wipers on October 2009.  I based my purchase on Bosch's claim that these blades are long lasting, quiet, and had uniform pressure across the blade that resulted in reduced blade lift off.  After a year, my blades exhibit none of these characteristics.      I replaced both wipers at the same time and they deteriorated in the same fashion and time frame.     Fall 2009, the wipers worked.   By spring 2010, wipers were smearing and streaking.  By winter 2010, wipers had deteriorated and large parts of the wipers were not making contact with the windshield and they stutter, skip, and squeak.     I'm not very pleased with Bosch.  Premium wipers should not be smearing and streaking after one winter and their life expectancy should be greater than one year.      Purchasing or repurchasing these blades every year does not make sense to me and does not reconcile with my expectation that premium wipers should last at least 2 years.       Thus, I'm switching to another brand and I'm going back to the oem wipers if my new ones do not work out.

product_title: INNOVA 3100 Diagnostic Scan Tool/Code Reader
review_body: First I am a woman, a nurse, not a mechanic.  My check engine light once again came on-just in time for my cars yearly inspection. The local lube/inspection outfit ran a diagnostic on it, (I flunked the inspection since the check engine light was on) The diagnostic showed code P0171, \\"running too lean\\". That was the same code I had received 2 years previously, same car, which ultimately cost me over $400. to be repaired by a local supposedly \\"reputable honest repair shop\\".  It turned out the $400.+ was to clean injectors and change filters.  I was determined this time I could do something about the issue and definitely save some money.  So I purchased this wonderful tool, ran the diagnostics, received the same code. I personally changed the air filter-was needed, and added [[ASIN:B0006305RY Lucas 10020 Upper Cylinder Lubrication & Injector Cleaner 5.25 oz.]]to my gas tank-spent less than $20.(not including the cost of this tool). After 2-3 days of driving with the injector cleaner in my tank and changing the filter, I cleared the check engine light with this wonderful tool. Did a full drive cycle (what entails a \\"drive cycle\\" is listed in the service manual for your vehicle) returned to the inspection place, and passed.  The techs there asked me where I went to repair the issue, (they had nicely recommended an outfit), told them I did it myself!  They were impressed, and I was thrilled with being able to take care of this issue myself. Couldn't have done it without this great little tool. Very easy to use and understand. Highly recommend for anyone!

product_title: R134a with SubZero Synthetic A/C Booster, Reusable Recharge Hose and Inline Gauge, 19 oz. (345)
review_body: I used this setup to evaluate how charged my system was.  Then I let out some pressure from the system as I would have been over pressurizing the car not doing so...     1. It is important to know that the gauge has to be dialed to the approximate outside temperature at the time you add coolant... It's a cheap and easy dial, set it and use it for reference.      2. Disconnect the hose from the can, attach the hose to the car and validate the hose will not come off. It's the air tool style  connector, tug on it, if it does not come off your probably ok.      3. Start the car and turn on AC.  Once the car is engaging the AC pump hook up your can to the hose.    4. Close the valve all the way, this punctures the cans seal.    5. Slowly open the valve, opening and closing will let your AC pump suck in the coolant a bit at a time...    After 5 mins your can is empty... turn car off and disconnect hoses... You may need an additional can.... but I did not...     Unless you got other problems with your cooling, you can now enjoy your work, and the money you saved doing it yourself.       Good luck all... Rory Siwik

review_body: I was excited to get my new Plantronics Discovery 975 headset. I am still experimenting with different earpieces and adjustments because what seems to be most comfortable for my ear means that the earpiece is not as snug as I'd like. However, every now and then, I get a connection accompanied by a clicking noise. I don't use the headset very often and have experienced the clicking a couple of times. That concerns me a bit since the Plantronics 975 is on the pricey side.     If you are looking for a small headset that is light-weight and barely noticeable when you wear it, then the Plantronics Discovery 975 is great. If you work in a noisy environment and need your headset to operate at a high volume for the best clarity, I cannot recommend it.

product_title: FIAMM 72112 Freeway Blaster LOW Note Horn
review_headline: Loud as heck for the size
review_body: These things are awesome.  I bought two along with some relays and relay sockets so I could get them enough power directly from the battery to do serious audible damage.  Make sure to buy this one with its mate, the 72102 high tone.  After wiring in the relays, these went in my 2000 Civic perfectly.  They replaced the crappy horn in there, and I used the wiring to tie into the relay signal hot wire.  Then, I grounded the relay to the body by tying it into the ground wire from one of the horns.  The horns come with these little wire slide connectors that you can clamp onto your wires.  I used wire nuts to tie all the wires together - I suggest you do the same.  I was able to mount them facing away from eachother with grounding connectors in between the mounts using a single bolt that held the old Honda horn.  This was ideal, and very clean - no drilling required!    I suggest finding yourself a 12V DC 4-pin or 5-pin 40 Amp SPST ISO Micro Relay for this project.  Also, it really helps to have a 5-Pin Wire Harness Relay Socket.  This will give you all the wires you need directly from the relay.  These are really cheap items, and you shouldn't have trouble finding them.  The 4-pin relays work fine with the 5-pin sockets.  Then, educate yourself on how relays work, and wire that bad boy up!  I got my relay and relay socket on ebay.      Overall, I'm very pleased with this product.  Buy it now if you want to be heard on the highway.

product_title: Viair 00073 70P Heavy Duty Portable Compressor
review_headline: Update - Received Ahead of Schedule and Works Fine
review_body: Update 6/5/2011: Have used it 6 or 7 times the first 4 times it worked fine. The past 4 months one of my tires has had a slow leak that they could not find. About every 6 weeks I find that the tire is down to about 15 pounds pressure. Now it trips off about half way to 32 pounds and I have to let it sit for 10 minutes before it will reset and run again. This happens at least twice each time I use it now - Frustrating?     Purchased 9/21/2010 I have used it to top off tire pressure on my car. Easily reached all the tires on my full sized 4 dr sedan. Was easy to use. The user manual was not very helpful. But the other reviews were very helpful and took the place of an adequate user guide. Important things I learned from the reviews:     1. Be sure that the car is running before you turn the compressor on. Some people have blown fuses when the engine is not running.   2. It is better to use a power outlet other than the car lighter if it is available.   3. While the compressor is running the tire pressure gauge will register a little high. If you turn off the compressor it will hold and show an accurate reading.   4. Some people found that they lost some air removing the air hose from the tire valve stem. I did not have that problem.   5. The compressor did start dancing across the garage floor as one review had mentioned but a light touch on the compressor handle kept it from moving.    A problem that I did have (not with the compressor) was when using my tire gauge to confirm the tire pressure I lost air getting an accurate reading (my bumbling). My solution was to put about two pounds above what I wanted when I filled the tire and bled it down to what I wanted.     The compressor looks and feels like it is well built. The storage case that comes with it is compact and easy to use. It takes up very little space in the trunk of my car.    Very pleased with my purchase and glad I decided to spend the extra $20 over the cheaper ones available.     [[ASIN:B0012WHBSO Viair 00073 70P Heavy Duty Portable Compressor]]

product_title: Bon-Aire Original Ultimate Hose Nozzle
review_headline: not yet proven to be the "ultimate hose nozzle" . . .
review_body:
The sky high ratings intrigued me, so when the Bon-Aire \\"ultimate\\" nozzle was available as a Lightning Deal, I bought one to see if it lived up to the hype.

The product appears to be very well constructed, and is quite a bit larger and heavier, than your typical cheapo nozzle. You adjust the flow of water by turning the spray head at the front. Water flow can be cut off at either end of the range, as the flow pattern goes from off, to a gentle sprinkle, to wide spray, and then narrowing into a beam, and then off again. Because of the larger sized head, the \\"ultimate\\" nozzle has a larger area of coverage, and can deliver a larger volume of water.

The nozzle does a decent job of diffusing water flow, producing a nice gentle flowing fountain of water suitable for watering potted plants or delicate flowers. When adjusted more to a spray, it is well suited for vegetable gardens and general use. This is however, nothing unique as far as sprinkler nozzles go.

Fully open, the front aperture is about 0.12 inches in diameter, which produces a thicker stream of water than your typical cheapo nozzle. Sometimes a thick stream is advantageous, but you will be using more water, and the increased water pressure may stress your plumbing. Unless your system has high volume, and good water pressure, you may not be able to take full advantage this nozzle.

The nozzle appears to be solidly built, and seems to work as advertised. Unfortunately the aluminum parts on mine have a reddish finish, rather than green, which looks cooler. Although it can deliver a higher volume of water, the assertion that it is the \\"ultimate\\" is perhaps an overstatement. It does a good job, but not that much better than the various cheapo nozzles and spray guns. The economy models typically don't last very long, so if \\"the ultimate\\" proves to be durable, it might be worth the premium cost. It's a bit heavy, and encourages using more water, so at this point I like it more than love it.love it.

product_title: Blitz Enviro-Flo Accessory Pack - Spout, ID Tag and Flex Tube, Model# 81101
review_headline: Blitz Enviro-Flo Spout - It Leaves You In Doubt
review_body:
INSTALLATION: All you have to do, to attach the spout to the can, is line up the threads and rotate clockwise, until you have clicked into the child safety feature. To make sure the seal is as tight as possible, I like to tighten it to the very last click on the spout.

Though, it seems to make a good tight seal onto the can, when in operation, I find it leaks, just above the spout cap.

OPERATION: The Enviro-Flo spout, has a \\"Store\\" & \\"Pour\\" mode. When in \\"Store\\" mode, it is not supposed to leak, but as I said, it will. To operate, all you have to do, is move the switch on the left side of the spout, down to \\"Pour.' Once you have done that, you have to press down on the back end of the spout to release the fuel flow. To stop the flow, all you have to do is release your thumb, and it will automatically shut off. It has a nice 2.5-gallon per minute flow rate, which I like.

MY EXPERIENCE: My experience with the Enviro-Flo spout, leaves much to be desired. Though, I do like the ease of use, and the child safety features. However, the can seal in the cap, is inadequate, and thus, spills gasoline.

CONCLUSION: In my opinion, Blitz needs to go back to the drawing board. These are the best sounding horns out there. They are loud, sound great and perform every time. In no way are these cheap horns in terms of quality or performance. I will use these on every car I own and recommend them to everyone who asks.

UPDATE: On my factory Nissan keyless entry, the horns sound funky and wimpy when locking the vehicle due to the short burst and most likely low voltage singal sent to the horns for the keyless system. It sounds aathmatic.

product_title: Flowmaster 430402 40 Series Muffler - 3.00 Center IN / 2.50 Dual OUT - Aggressive Sound
review_headline: Not what I was looking for
review_body: After a lot of research, I was originally going to go with the 50 series, but I ended up second guessing it and choosing the 40 at the muffler shop.  I knew that was the wrong decision for my 4.3L V6 Chevy S-10 on the way home.  The sound from the outside at idle and with a blip of the throttle is deep and mellow.  I wouldn't call it overly loud at idle, and I actually did get some complements on the sound.  Where I never quite got on board with it was the resonance inside the cab.  It is hard to describe, but while cruising, the constant \\"bwwahhhhh\\" sound was just the right pitch to get on my nerves in that small space.  I was late to a friend's house once, so I was rushing to get there.  When I arrived, he told me that he heard me come around the bend a mile up the road!  This was reinforced by the fact that several people have told me through the years that they could always hear me coming and I experienced it myself when people returned the truck after borrowing it.  If I had it to do over again, I'm would definitely have gone with something quieter for sure.  Something that didn't make it so that you have to yell to be heard by your passenger and had a better sound at cruising speeds or while under load.  On the other hand, if you've got a teenager, and you want to know when they come and go, get these!  Part of my issues could have been due to the small truck that it was on, and the fact that the muffler had to be located directly behind the passenger seat.  Just to be thorough, I had a single pipe into the 40, and two coming out.  The pipes exited straight out the back, on either side of the license plate (halfway between the edge of the plate and the corner of the bumper).

product_title: BMW Oil Filler Cap M E32 E34 E36 E38 E39 E46 E90 M3 M5 NEW
review_body:
This is a beautiful appearing filler cap for late model BMWs. It's made of solid, polished steel with the \\"M\\" logo engraved and enamel filled in color. It was supplied with an allen wrench that allows re-positioning of the retaining bar so that the logo will read correctly on any engine.

It's very well made and looks great. It comes with a thick gasket.

A few cautions: Unlike the original cheap plastic filler cap, this one retains engine heat so you should use a glove or a rag when removing it from a hot engine to avoid being burned. Also, the adjustable locking bar is retained by only one allen screw. If that loosens, it can drop into your engine. Once you set the position of the locking bar so the logo reads correctly, I'd strongly recommend applying some red loctite to the allen screw threads to safely lock it in place (as a precaution).

Final cautions: Adding \\"M\\" parts to your engine can increase horsepower and may void your factory warrantee. This device should be used by mature drivers only and must be kept out of the hands of children (anyone under 300 months old). It's best to keep your rpms below 4500 for the first 1000kM or until you get used to all the extra torque this oil filler cap will provide! You may also see a reduction in fuel consumption of at least 32.5 percent while using this oil filler cap (power has its price - if you can't pay, don't play). But, after all, since you drive a \\"Bimmer\\" why should you care about fuel consumption?

product_title: Battery Tender Jr. Battery Charger
review_body:
I have a motorcycle which does not get used as often as I'd like during the riding season. Also, due to cold and snow/rain, the bike is mostly garaged from late December until mid March. After a season or two of this, I finally killed the old battery by not keeping it properly charged.

When I bought the new battery I also bought the Deltran Battery Tender Jr. My reasons were two-fold. #1 I didn't want to be disappointed by a dead battery when I found time for a ride. And #2, the new battery was not inexpensive, so the cost of a Battery Tender Jr. just made sense.

I recently went though a period of not riding for two or three weeks but had time to ride yesterday. The bike fired right up and had a full/strong charge. I check the Tender's light most every day and it's been solid green all along.

The bottom line is this: If you have a vehicle which sits for days at a time, your battery will eventually fail. Once the battery fails chances are the vehicle will sit even longer which can lead to other problems (bad gas, carb problems, dry seals, etc). If you put the vehicle's battery on a good quality, \\"smart\\", trickle charger you'll not only get the full lifespan from the battery, you'll be able to use your vehicle when you wish.

Dan

review_headline: 1 year later...It's a temporary fix at best.

UPDATE 8/29/11:

I still feel the same. Over the past year I have spent alot of time trying to maintain the finish left by the 3M kit. I find that I need to polish it every month to keep it looking decent. I still do not recommend this product, simply because it does not come with some type of sealant to protect the plastic lens after it has been sanded. The polish is just not enough and only holds a temporary shine. Hopefully 3M will add some type of UV sealant and really complete this kit.

-----------
For the most part I take very good care of my cars. When I purchased this 3M product, I was looking at getting rid of some crusty sun damage that had emerged on the upper portion of my headlights (Garaged 2001 T&C). Everything was conveniently included in the kit and I had a drill with extra batteries, plus a professional polisher to boot (if needed) to get the job done. I taped the instruction sheet to the hood before I started working to assure I followed everything to the T. The entire process probably took about 2 hours. I was determined to get the perfect milky look on the lenses before going to the polishing stage, and to be honest, all that sanding was definitely taking something off (GOOD? or BAD?).

I finally get the the final polishing stage and I am excited to see the gloss coming back to the headlights. Unfortunately, by the time I was done I noticed something that wasn't visible in the pictures and advertisement...
While the most sun damaged portion of the lenses did look better, it wasn't anywhere near as good as a new headlight. It did look clearer but very hazy and it made the undamaged portion which was glossy, now appear dull and hazy like the top portion of the lens. I felt I had taken the bad and made it better, but also took the good and made it worse.
So overall, you get a dull clear look, but at the sacrifice of completely STRIPPING AWAY ALL FACTORY SEALANT/GLOSS.
This kit is only for the most pitifully damaged headlights. In fact, any kit that tells you to sand your headlights should raise a red flag. It only means you'll need to tend to the lens more often after you use the product. That means more polish to buy and more time to polish again and again because it will dull up again and again after the polish wears of.ut also took the good and made it worse.

product_title: Tufoil Engine Treatment 32 oz.
review_body: I've used Tufoil since I first heard about it on Paul Harvey News in the mid 70's. At the time I had a 72 Dodge Charger with a 318. On the second start after the first addition of Tufoil I noticed a difference. The starter sounded as though it was turning with little resistance which sold me on the product. I drove that car to 286,400 miles with no engine problems before getting a new used vehicle. I used Tufoil in it - an 84 Dodge Shelby Charger with a 2.2 L. Bought the car with 18,000 miles on it and drove the car to 406,000. Again no major engine problems. I was still getting 35 mpg and was only using a quart of oil every 2,000 miles which is the interval at which I did my oil changes. The only reason I got rid of the 84 was due to rust and deteriorating structural integrity. I was hoping to at least get to the half million mark, but the car was becoming unsafe due to the aforementioned corrosion. I would highly recommend this product to anyone looking to prolong their engines life span and increase their gas mileage. Combined with diligent routine maintenance it works - plain and simple.

product_title: Battery Tender Plus 021-0128, 1.25 Amp Battery Charger is a Smart Charger, it will Fully Charge and Maintain a Battery at Proper Storage Voltage without the Damaging Effects Caused by Trickle Chargers
review_headline: Works great charging Piaggio or Vespa scooters
review_body: I had my Vespa dealership recharge my Piaggio BV250 battery after winter storage.  They actually used this battery tender to charge it for me.  However, they only sold the Deltran Tender Jr (0.75 Amp).  This charger has a faster charging time than the 0.75 Amp.  My batteries charge in about 4-6 hours whereas the Jr take about double that (though exact timing obviously depends on how depleted your batteries are).  I've used this charger since then and it's been great.  It's simple to use: plug it in, connect the clamps or leads to your battery and wait for the green light to light up (indicating a full charge).  There are two sets of connecting cables (one is a clamp and the other a screw on) which is good depending on your need.  One benefit of these two cables is that they actually fit into each other and can be used to connect your battery to your bike WHILE your battery is outside of your bike - I had to use this feature because I accidentally shut my seat (lock is battery powered) when the battery was out and had to connect my battery remotely.    If you have a Vespa or other scooter, I would highly recommend getting this charger.  In cold weather, scooter batteries die in about 3-6 weeks of inactivity.

product_title: Accu-Gage H60XA (5-60 PSI) Swivel Angle Chuck Dial Tire Pressure Gauge with Hose
review_body: At this price this gauge is unbeatable. The heft of the unit is perfect, and all the swiveling parts are very precise and feel like they will last for years. When used on a tire it gives very accurate and repeatable results, and according to the website is accurate to within 1.2 psi. Most of the hardware on the unit is made of brass, and I'm uncertain of what the back panel of the gauge is made out of (it's painted with a black glossy paint). The parts are all machined with a great deal of precision and fit together with no visible gaps, nothing wiggles or rattles.     There is a release valve to seep out air on the stem above the dial, I find this feature a lot nicer than using a cheap gauge where you check the pressure, take the gauge off the tire then use the back of the gauge to release air then check again. Basically it saves time and frustration when trying to get an exact pressure in the tire. The rubber hose connecting the chuck to the dial has a nice fabric around the hose to help prevent the rubber from getting nicked or ripped. The viewing window is plastic, but it isn't thin and doesn't flex. As far as plastic goes it's pretty nice. The actual plate with the numbers to measure tire pressure (white panel with numbers and tick marks) is fitted very well and isn't warped (a problem I've had with cheaper gauges). Another nice thing about this gauge is that the brass fixture coming out of the dial can be unscrewed and cleaned (there's a small rubber flap in there to catch dirt) if you use this on a dirty tire.    Overall this is a really nice tire gauge, and it's made in the U.S., so I had no hesitations on buying it. Its accurate to within 1 PSI every time. The quality of the gauge matched with where it was made and it's lifetime you break it they fix it warranty makes this product a great buy.

review_body:

review_headline: Top quality- or so I thought

I would bet if you cleaned it once every 2 years, it would last forever. Dont forget to vacuum out the crud on your tanks bottom at the same time. Often the lower element is operating in a mass of calcite.

Okay, Disappointment: One of these burned out in just 3 months or less. Looks like their MFG' process is poorer than their promises and ideas. I'll report back if they honor the warranty.

The MFG. which is Camco, says True value stores must handle warranty issues and then get a credit from them, they will not deal with the end user. But this Rons hardware just does not care and will not intervene or offer a replacement or credit - I supose its too much work for them to get a cresit from their supplier, so its easier to just screw me.

My lights are flush with the hood at the top, so I popped the hood, taped around the sides and bottom, and took nice steady slow passes.  Don't be too timid with the drill.  The P500 is pretty grabby, so hold that drill firmly.  I would have liked one more p800 disc for each lens, but two was adequate.  Be sure to use plenty of water with the gray foam disk.  I used an old corded Black and Decker single speed drill that I keep around for an auger in the garden.  Worked great.  It would have been annoying to recharge my cordless during the job.  I highly recommend this kit.

review_headline: It works!!! yes, its true...but only for what it SAYS it works for
review_body: I researched this item before purchasing--needless to say with all the negative reviews i wasn't expecting too much. Though it comes with an extra tip in case the first one hardens, I have yet to replace the first tip.  the Pen actually goes a long way--I've already gone over all the scratches (and there were a LOT) and there's still plenty left over.  To make sure the tip didn't harden further, I put electrical tape over the edge of the cap to make sure air didn't get in, but I don't know if that was necessary, just precautionary. It is a CLEAR COAT SCRATCH REPAIR PEN, not for paint repair (duh) and it works PERFECTLY.

review_headline: heavy, loud, powerful, helps develop `Popeye' arms . .
review_body:
This buffer has plenty of power to get the job done, and appears to be well worth the money. Some minor assembly is required. There is a `manual' but it does not contain any instructions, instead it mostly covers general safety. Assembly is fairly simple. You first attach the curved top handle, either with or without, the straight side handle. The handle can be installed for either right or left hand operators. The buffer is top heavy, so installing the side handle is highly recommended.

This unit comes with the accessories to get started right away. For buffing, it has a wool pad, and rubber backing pad. For sanding, a Velcro backed hard plastic disc is included, but you will need to provide the sandpaper inserts. A special wrench for locking down the rubber backing pad is included.

Controls are pretty basic. There is a throttle switch on the bottom of the handle, with a lock button to keep the motor running. The speed control dial is on the top of the housing, and goes from 1 to 6 (maximum). The buffer starts to whine at around level 3, and gets screaming loud at full speed, when ear protection is definitely recommended. The amount of vibration will vary according to the task, and motor speed. When sanding or buffing fine dust is typically produced, so you may want to wear eye protection and a dust mask.

If you are into weightlifting, using the buffer on a vehicle may not be too difficult, but for those not so physically fit, managing the weight and vibration, could be a challenge. Because of the tool is about 18 inches long, your hands end up positioned about a foot apart, in order to keep the torque generated by the buffer under control. Just a little inattention can result in losing control, or dropping the buffer, and you don't want to hurt yourself, damage your paint job, dent your vehicle, or damage anything else.

The supplied wool buffer is quite thick, and does a pretty good job, but you do need to apply pressure for it to work. For the average sedan, buffing the hood and trunk should be the easiest. Things get harder when you do the sides, or curved or irregular surfaces, and have to both support the weight of the buffer, and apply pressure to the surface. Buffing non-flat areas usually requires changing angles, and varying the point of contact, and amount of pressure applied. Users will need to find the grip and techniques that work best. Buffing will require some finesse at times, and if your muscles are straining, this is when accidents can happen, or you can hurt yourself. Doing the roof can be tricky as well.

The listed weight of eight pounds, may not sound like a lot, but if you are bracing your body, locking your forearms, and squeezing hard on the handles for an extended period of time, you may find your muscles a bit sore, or in `shock' from the vibration, if you overdo it. Just go easy when using it for the first few times.

The pictured buffer has a blue plastic housing and black handle, but the unit also comes with an orange plastic housing. It has a ten foot cord with a twin blade plug, and comes with a set of spare brushes. The buffer does produce very good results, so if you have a strong back, and the upper body strength, it could be a very cool buy.for it to work. product_title: Arai Helmets Faceshield - Light Smoke 1423 034427
review_headline: Best reason to buy an Arai helmet
review_body: Arai's shields are the best available in my experience for one simple reason: they don't scratch as easily as other shields I've used, including other presumably hard-coated shields such as Shoei. For this reason alone I can expect to get 1-2 years of near as-new use out of an Arai shield even when riding 20k miles per year through bugs, ice and wind-blasted grit. Other shields scratch simply as a result of fairly careful cleanings and in my experience can be expected to have dramatically shorter useful lives. To attempt a quantification of my point, I'd estimate that Shoei's shields require double the care to provide perhaps half the life of an Arai shield, at least in my use, and an un-coated shield like the Kiwi shields I'm familiar with might require double again the care for again half the lifespan of the Shoei shield.    I recommend the clear and dark smoke shields. Even the dark smoke shield can benefit from being used with sunglasses under under very bright conditions, so I wouldn't bother with the light smoke.    Venting is not a major factor for me. I usually ride with the shield cracked to get the desired airflow. Another nice feature of the Arai shields is a fairly heavy and durable first detent position. On some shields the detents wear out quickly and the shield will close by itself as a result of airflow after some use.    The shields are in my opinion the best reason to buy Arai helmets. Many excellent helmets are on the market today. For real-world, more-than-occasional use, however, Arai's top-notch shields make all the difference in terms of usability, enjoyment and cost per mile ridden.  Comment

product_title: Milton Dial Type Air Gauge 0 60 Psi (MILS902)
review_body: Here's my round-up of tire pressure gauges.  Prices vary a lot on Amazon.  Usually much cheaper if purchased directly from Amazon (free shipping) than from an affiliated seller.  So be careful which seller you pick.  If Amazon is out of stock, you may want to wait a week or two. Prices below are what I paid, including free shipping.     In Jan 2009, I bought two gauges:  (a) Moroso 89560 ($40.04), an analog dial gauge, and (b) Accutire MS-5510B ($38.41), a digital dial gauge.  I have separate reviews for these two units.  Both are good units with a flexible hose attachment and a bleed valve.  They are fine in the garage, and fit any tire, but are bulky to keep in a glove compartment if you want to check pressures when you're on the road (for example, if you suspect a leak).  I just bought three compact units.  All three are analog dial gauges:  I don't want battery-powered units stashed away in a glove compartment (extreme high and low temps, and who wants a unit with a dead battery in an emergency?).    Same review posted for the following:    Milton (MIL) MILS902 $21.63  Professional Products (PP) 11101 $9.88  Auto Meter (AM) Auto gage 2343 $16.50    All five gauges have a range of 0 - 60 psi.  My tires run from 28 - 35 psi.  Main features to consider:    (1) Accuracy.  Accuracy is specified with respect to a calibration source.  Since I don't have a calibration source, I can't comment on accuracy.    (2) Resolution.  (a) Accutire.  Digital readout. 0.1 psi resolution.  (b) Moroso.  2-1/2 in diam dial.  Can estimate to nearest ½ psi.  (c) MIL, PP, AM.  2 in diam dial.  Can estimate to nearest 1 psi.    (3) Reproducibility.  Repeated 6 readings for each gauge.  Expected some air loss for each reading.  No noticeable change for analog gauges.  0.5 psi drop total after six readings for Accutire (it's not leakier, it's only because of the higher resolution).    (4) Agreement.  Ran 5 sequences of the 5 gauges in different order.  All gauges agreed within +/-1 psi.  This is good news.  MIL consistently 1 psi lower than the others, but this is fine.    (5) Mechanical.      (a) PP and AM appear to be the same gauge, with two minor differences.  Don't know if the innards are the same though...can't open the cases.  Both weigh 150 gm, so probably the same inside as well.  Heavy sheet metal body. Heavy metal neck, chuck, and valve.  Heavy plastic dial cover (hard, not tough, plastic though).  Tick marks and numbers on AM dial much sharper than on PP.  PP comes with fitted plastic case; AM doesn't.  Case is low quality though...hard, not tough, plastic; snap fit.  Good for stashing in a glove compartment or tool box.  But probably will crack and open up if dropped.      (b)  MIL. Heavy metal neck, chuck, and valve.  **Extremely el-cheapo and flimsy plastic body and dial cover.**      Common features (MIL, PP, AM):      (1) Have a neck with an angled chuck.  Non-swivel.  PM, AM neck 2 in length.  Milton neck about ¾ in longer.     (2) Have bleed valve. Smooth operation.   After gauge is removed, pressure reading is supposed to hold until bleed valve is released.  (PP, AM):  Reading holds even after 30 sec.  (MIL):  Reading starts to drop once the gauge is removed (not acceptable).      Common negs:      (1)  None come with a boot. Should be standard.  A boot is available, but Amazon doesn't sell it directly.  An affiliated seller wants $2.99 + $6.95 shipping.  That's more than I paid for the PP gauge itself.  I have a couple of 25+ yr old Brookstone gauges that have finally deserved a decent burial.  Their rubber boots are still in good shape after all these years, and they fit my new gauges just fine.      (2) Gauges without a hose are tricky to use.  Many wheels now have spokes, and the valve stems are recessed.  Worse, my wife's car has short rigid tire sensors:  the stems don't flex at all.  If you get a gauge with a straight chuck, the neck is often too short and you can't seat the chuck (the gauge body gets in the way).  So theseunits have an angled chuck.  The design is idotic though, because the bleed valve is on the same side as the chuck.  Depending on the tire, the bleed valve presses against the wheel when you try to seat the chuck.  Not good.  There is no swivel head.  So if you position the gauge to clear the wheel, you may end up with the gauge oriented such that you can't read it.  In which case, it's critical that the bleed valve doesn't leak...that way you can get a valid reading after you remove the gauge.  You, of course, lose the capability to overfill the tire a bit and then bleed the pressure to the right value as you look at the dial.  So these operate more like stick gauges.  In this respect, none of this group of three is totally satisfactory.      Summary:  Of the three, though, I'd go with the PP.  It has the lowest price and has a storage case.  It's essentially the same as the AM.  It's not worth the extra $ to get the sharper graphics on the AM.  The MIL is the most expensive, is the flimsiest, and my unit came with a leaky valve.  I returned it.  Five stars to Amazon for free return shipping and processing a refund within several days.    Note added 8/22/09:  Prices fluctuate a lot.  Go with either PP or AM.  If one is significantly cheaper when you order, go with that one.

review_headline: Didn't expect to like it so much
review_body: When I first put this jacket on, I liked the 'look', but had to adjust to the weight of it (light), and the armor twisting. I'm used to a heavy armored leather jacket, so this took a moment. The moment passed.      I'd gone to the Harley-Davidson dealership in Coeur d' Alene Idaho to try it on, imagining I'd need to order a lg. \\"LONG\\". Have to hand it to Harley to make a size available for the taller rider. At 5'11\\", a long was indeed needed. But the trying on allowed me to know if I'd want to commit at all.     Once in my hands, it wasn't until I took a ride in serious weather, extremes of heat, chill, and rain, that the attributes of the 3-in-1 came home to roost. This is a great all weather jacket. Riding is some extremely wet weather in British Columbia, I never got cold, or wet. In the wind, over several mountain passes, it held my own heat in even without the inner vest. And as the vest detaches, it can be worn separately.    And since it was the only jacket besides my leather that I packed for the trip, this jacket was a great deal more comfortable walking about in the towns where we stopped. The leather has it's place, but this jacket is more versatile and didn't wear me out carrying it, or wearing it after dismount.      I didn't expect to, but turns out I love this jacket.     And while I stayed warm and dry with the 3-in-1, my boots are another story.

product_title: PLX Kiwi MPG Trip Calculator and OBDII Scanner
review_headline: Great Idea. Buggy Unit. Dismal Customer Relations
review_body: SUMMARY: Great concept and much-needed product. Unfortunately, my unit failed after 10 days. Replacement/refund process a three-month ordeal.     THE GOOD: This product represents a much-needed tool for drivers to educate themselves in fuel-efficient driving techniques. It works. After ordering, I received the unit in a timely manner and found it easy to install. The user interface was somewhat clumsy, but I was able to get my Kiwi MPG up and running in a few minutes by reading the instructions. Once installed, I found the Kiwi MPG very useful for determining instantaneous and average fuel efficiency of my 2004 Toyota Tacoma.    THE BAD: Unfortunately, the unit failed within the first 10 days of use. Symptoms were that it would not shut down after the vehicle was shut off. Rather it continued to operate and got very hot. Shortly after this symptom commenced, it failed altogether and just gave an error display. It was still functional if I shut it off manually and rebooted every time I started the truck, but clearly it was not working out. Unfortunately, since this was purchased through a second party seller, I had to deal with the seller rather than Amazon directly.     THE UGLY: After contacting the seller by email, I was instructed to send the unit back for a replacement, which I did. One week passed, then two...and ultimately five weeks and still no replacement. I contacted the seller via email again and was assured my replacement was on the way. More time passed and still no replacement. After this, I was able to locate a phone number on the web and after several tries over a number of days eventually contacted the company. I verified that they had received my return and again, I was assured a replacement was on the way. Again, weeks passed and no replacement. Subsequently, I left a message with a different person on the phone and eventually my call was returned by someone high up in the company who was at a trade show at the time. He instructed me to call the original person I had spoken to weeks earlier and tell this person that he should \\"take care of me\\". I did and the person agreed to process a refund. More weeks passed, no refund. I called this person again and he told me he'd have to check with their accounting department and get back to me. He promised an email within a few hours explaining the status of my refund... no email appeared.     At this point, it was crystal clear that PLX had no intention of refunding my money. I contacted Amazon directly and inquired about my options. My first inquiry was met with (direct quote)     \\"Unfortunately as they are not responding to your calls and emails there is nothing we can do.\\"     I was not satisfied with this answer from Amazon and sent a more impassioned follow-up which included more details about my quest for a replacement or refund. My second claim was just approved and today Amazon sent an email confirming that I will be getting a refund for the purchase price from them directly. The squeaky wheel gets the oil I guess. Thus, assuming Amazon follows through, my long and painful saga appears to be over. My original purchase was on July 19th, 2009. The date of confirmation of a refund by Amazon is November 22nd. This was my second experience recently with uncooperative second party sellers through Amazon. I'd like to acknowledge here that Amazon did make it right in both cases. They deserve kudos for this.      Judging from the other reviews on this page, a lot of people have had good experiences with the Kiwi MPG. I suspect most people will have a similarly good experience. However, one should go into this purchase with their eyes open. If you do need to send the unit back for whatever reason, you are in for a painful ride.

product_title: Dorman OE Solutions 615-178 Intake Manifold
review_body: After over 100K miles (and days after having replaced a coolant leaking intake manifold gasket) on the second plastic cross over manifold on my mustang I noticed a small crack near the passenger side temp sensor that was weeping coolant and upon disassembly a three inch crack in progress where the cross over was getting ready to burst.     I did not want to pay the outrageous prices ford dealers charge for NPI aluminum cross over intake manifolds nor do I like any of the solutions to use a PI manifold on NPI heads (due to cost and/or engineering reasons depending on the method) so I went with the dorman hoping for the best.     On the plus side the manifold is made in the USA, it fits, and the install of the manifold itself doesn't have any special issues to deal with. It's far cheaper than what ford dealers charge for the NPI manifolds. (Ford PI manifolds can be found for just a little more than what this Dorman manifold costs)      On the minus side the molds that make the pieces at the intake ports were designed with a parting line inside the ports. The resulting draft creates material that will block some of the airflow or cause less than ideal flow. There was also some flash in there on the part I got. I removed this material with an xacto knife and a dremel to smooth out the ports. This clean up made it much more like the ford manifold. It was far less material than seen on dorman manifolds for other applications and probably would not make much difference, but I didn't like it so I took care of it.     The included alternator bracket does not work on a mustang. It interfered with the tubes that go across the top of the manifold. My dremel and a bench grinder were used to cut away the big 'plate' that was on the dorman bracket but not the OEM one. Also be aware that if your car has COP the coils are held in place by thread cutting screws instead of having threaded inserts. Mine doesn't so that wasn't an issue.     I haven't driven the car much with the dormanmanifold on so I can't say if there has been any change in power. it seems to be about the same, maybe a little less, but from what I could find on the mustang and crown vic forums that the NPI dorman vs. NPI ford is the same power wise.    Also of note, if leaking coolant has caused any additional wear-and-tear on some of the spark plugs or the coils have gotten weak with age (or both in my case) upon re-assembly misfires of some degree will make themselves known even if there were no obvious problems previously. If misfires show up after wards check the gap on the plugs that were flooded with coolant and the coil packs. Also check for boiled down coolant sludge inside the spark plug boots.
