With the rainy season upon us in Northern California, I decided to go for broke and buy the best non-OEM blades available. The Bosch ICON's are it.

The installation was more simple than I had imagined. No adapters or figuring out how to open the brackets. It took me more time to remove the old blades than to install the new ones. The first thing I noticed about the ICON's was that they were not straight, but were slightly curved due to the tensioned springs. Ingenious! They fit nice and snug against my windshield. The next thing I noticed was that it was bracketless. Apparently more and more new cars are coming with bracketless wiper blades. Aside from being more visually appealing, the design is supposed to perform better. Awesome! The last thing I noticed after installation was that they fit perfectly! No more cutting the edges off with scissors. Woo!

Right after I installed the ICON blades, I fired up the wipers and shot some wiper fluid out. WOAHHHH...WOW! Whisper quiet and clear as crystal! I don't ever remember my windshield clearing so well, not even with the OEM VW blades. My wife drove it in some heavy rain recently and she commented how great they worked.

The price for the Bosch ICON is pretty steep, but still cheaper than many OEM blades. I am actually keeping track of my install date to determine how long they actually last. For the moment, I could not be happier with them and am waiting for the blades on my other car to go bad so I can replace those with the ICON's too. In foul weather, arguably only your brakes are more important than your visibility. The ICON's are well worth the investment.he investment.

product_title: Autel MaxiDiag US703 Diagnostic Scan Tool
review_headline: Great bang for the buck.  Easy to use and reads ABS codes
review_body: The scanner powers up quickly and overall seems a bit faster than the Actron.  It's easy to use; as a guy I've yet to open any kind of manual for the Autel, yet was able to read by my check engine and ABS codes that are popping up on my vehicle.  In playing with the Actron the other day I pulled up the screen to read all live data at once and scrolling down was very, very slow and the tool would lag when it was asked to display the next page of data.  The Autel 703 scrolled through all the live data without any lag.  I haven't exported any data to a PC yet so I can't tell you how well that works.  On screen descriptions were provided for both PCM codes and ABS codes.     I have an Actron 9185, which is the same as the 9190 without all the OBD 1 connectors for pre-1996 vehicles.  The Actron is a great tool, but I needed to read ABS codes and the Autel was about $50 more than the Actron ABS reader only, and the Autel 703 reads ABS, Airbag, and Tranny codes, so for the extra few bucks I figured it's worth a try, and I can always sell the Actron.   I paid about $50 more for the Actron 9185 than I paid for the Autel 703.       The tool is new and there don't appear to be any updates on the manufacturers site.  I do expect Actron to have more frequent updates based on other online reviews.  The Autel 703 DOES NOT come with the connectors to connect to pre-1996 vehicles though the software supports them.  I have not seen the cables for sale anywhere.      As a hard core DIY mechanic that likes to troubleshoot and fix almost everything with my vehicles, I would recommend the Autel 703 because of the number of systems it reads, and at a lower price point than other products.

product_title: EZ - Air Tire Gauge
review_headline: Excellent for checking pressure, ok for monitoring tire inflation
review_body: I'm one of those people who some times has trouble getting the alignment just right with the traditional \\"stick\\" tire gauges with the angled chuck.  The EZ Air Tire Gauge makes the procedure a cinch, though -- straight in and out, with no more than a puff of air from the tire when you attach or detach it.  The gauge itself seems pretty accurate and the entire assemble feels quite rugged.  For use as a pressure gauge, I'm QUITE satisifed with it.    It also has a connector at the other hand that lets you inflate the tire through the gauge.  It works with the air hoses you find at most gas stations as well as the screw-on connectors on, for example, the TyphoonMax TX300 portable compressor units.  I haven't used this with the gas station air lines myself, but I have used it with my TyphoonMax compressor.  The gauge will not give a steady reading while the compressor is on and inflating the tire.  The gauge needle vibrates quickly up and down in a blur between two readings while the compressor is on, but you can still see the pressure increase looking at the lower reading of the blurred needle.  You can also just switch the compressor off from time to time to check the pressure for sure.  It's certainly much easier than swapping back and forth between the compressor and the gauge.  The connector on the EZ gauge is probably the only real complaint I have.  While it attaches and detaches easily from the tire for quick readings, the spring-loaded piece that actually holds it in place on the valve stem (when you need hands free operation, like for working the compressor hose) will some times not grip very securely and you'll have to jiggle or remove and retry it.  It's never taking me more than a couple of tries to get a secure fit, though.    Finally, as a minor nit (but I feel worth noting), the gauge is oddly shaped and it may be hard finding space in, say, your glove compartment or other confined storage space.  It isn't BIG, just...oddly shaped.

product_title: Schumacher SSC-1500A-CA Ship 'N' Shore 15 Amp SpeedCharge Charger with Battery Clamps
review_headline: Does the job, but noisy fan
review_body: I bought this charger at WalMart.  This charger does the job very well and is very automatic.  I really like the % charge and voltage displays; they really let me know what is going on with the charging process.  It's very easy to use.    However, I have a few minor issues:   - The fan is noisy and always on, even when in float maintenance mode.  Schumacher at least should update their firmware to turn the fan off when there is no need for it, and maybe they should find another fan that isn't so noisy.  Besides the bother of hearing the fan, having it on always means that the charger will collect dust inside if left plugged in for months at a time (through the winter connected to a camper battery, for example).  The dust will ultimately cause overheating when a battery is charged.   - The paper manual describes 6 different battery type choices.  3 of them, including 6V and deep cycle, are not actually available to select on the charger: the charger cycles between Standard, AGM, and Gel.  Since I needed to charge a deep-cycle battery, I wasn't sure which to pick.  However, I was able to download an updated manual from Schumacher's web site which was updated to match the charger and explained that starting and deep-cycle batteries could be charged with any of the settings.  This made sense, and I charged my battery successfully.    I also agree with the reviewer who said that the desulfation cycle should not be fully automatic.  There should at least be an alarm chirp or something to remind you to keep a close eye out on the battery.    OK, so these are all pretty picky points.  Overall, this is a very good charger and I recommend it.

My husband had been scraping it off with a credit card. (If the credit card company found out, they'd probably charge us a fee for that \\"service\\"!) I went ahead and ordered this ice scraper because it's cheap but I wish I'd either not bothered or else forked over a little more money for a better one. This doesn't work much better than the credit card. Despite the wide blade, it only scrapes off very narrow strips of ice, so you have to scrape it across the windshield dozens of times to clear a small patch. Unfortunately, it's not worth shipping back.

product_title: OTC 7180 Universal Bearing Cup Installer
review_body: I was installing cups in the 3.8 inch to 4.5 inch range. I could find no other products claiming to do that. I did several and the OTC 7180 made a bearing cup installer out of me. A hard faced dead-blow hammer worked nice, but not essential. I'm not a pro, just someone who wants to be able to service this kind of thing to keep going.

product_title: Anytime Tools 11 pc FEMALE E-TORX (Star) SOCKET Set w/RAIL E4 - E20
review_body: I've been using these for a year and they came in handy. Also, the quality of the product is EXCELLENT!

product_title: Autel MaxiScan MS300 CAN Diagnostic Scan Tool for OBDII Vehicles
review_body:
The MaxiScan powered up after being connected.
It appeared to be scanning the different categories.
I received the message \\"link error\\".
I checked the firmness of my connection, but kept getting the same message.
I followed all included instructions.
I tried 6 or 7 times to no avail.
I am returning the unit on Monday.

product_title: Xantrex XPower Powerpack 600HD Portable Power Source
review_body: I bought the unit in November of 2007 for a campout my family was having. The unit worked very well. I ran a laptop and external hard drive off of it for almost 3 hours and still had enough juice to jumpstart my car with it the next day before recharging. I think in most ways it is better than a generator as you don't have to refuel it. Just plug it in to a car DC outlet or a standard AC outlet and let it charge for 2-6 hours and you're good as new. An excellent buy itf you don't have huge power requirements.    Pros- Virtually noiseless, lightweight compared to a generator, good recharge time for a battery.    Cons- Less capability than a generator to supply power, shorter life.    Overall rating- 4 of 5 Stars

product_title: Complete Tool Screw Driver Torx Kit to Repair Replace Apple Iphone-2g,3g,GPS,Ipod
review_body: I bought this kit to use to open an Asus netbook for some modding.  Shipping was way too high.  The lip of the blue tools broke off almost immediately.  The suction cup is a joke.  It wouldn't create suction on any part of my ipod. (I tested it out of boredom while on a conference call.)  The screwdrivers are throw away items.  I found I was better off with a cheap plastic disposable paint scraper (dull the edge with some sand paper) and my own screwdrivers.

product_title: Actron CP9175 AutoScanner Diagnostic Code Scanner with Freeze Frame Data for OBDII  Vehicles
review_body: Before I bought this product I tryed a diffrent brand scanner from a friend.  It could not get past my aftermarket security system on my car.  After doing some research I bought the Actron CP9175.  This is an amazing scanner for what it can do at a great price.  It has no problems with my aftermarket security system, and I like how it displays a brief discription of the problem along with the error code.

product_title: PhotoBlocker Reflector Cover by Phantom Plate
review_headline: It's a piece of plastic covered in glitter!
review_body: OK... let's be clear.  If you buy this product, you're buying a piece of plastic that's covered with glitter.  Nothing more.    As you might expect, it's hard to see through a piece of plastic with glitter glued all over it.  I suppose that's why cameras can't see it.  Unfortunately, nobody else can, either.  If you drive with this item, expect to be pulled over and ridiculed by the police.  It may very well work on high speed cameras, but it would be just as effective to just throw mud on your license plate - the principle is the same.    Save your money.

product_title: Gorilla Automotive Acorn Lug Nuts 24
review_body:
I got my set about 12 years ago. They've started to rust a bit, but unfortunately they still seem to be the best choice out there. I know they've saved my wheels at least twice.

When I got mine, they didn't have the large sets of 20-24 locks, so every nut is a lock. I called the company directly to order 5 sets of Gorilla Guard locks, all keyed alike. They were very helpful, took my order, and I had them the next day. Just recently when someone managed to get one lock off, I called the company to replace it. I was contrite as I had lost my key code and asked how this might be done. The woman who answered the phone was rude and argued with me. As if to say how dare I, a mere consumer, call them. Then she said I'd have to call back next week to speak to the replacement person anyway. When I called back, explaining I no longer had my key code, but had a good pic of the inside of key I could email her, she flatly refused. Said I had to physically send one of my other locks. The replacement would cost $12.
A new set of 4 only cost, like $16, so I asked if they could sell me a set after they determine the correct keying. Nope. I can buy four new locks, but each one will cost $12. She said that's how they do it. Take it or leave it. So for pity sake, don't ever lose your key code and hope you never need customer service from Gorilla Automotive Products.

review_body:

product_title: INNOVA 3130c Diagnostic Scan Tool/Code Reader with Fix Assist for OBD2 Vehicles
review_body: I purchased this tool on friday and recieved it on monday. I had been getting a check engine light on my 99 Accura cl and every-time I took it to Autozone it came up as an \\"exhaust leak\\" code. I had replaced the exhaust from the cat back and had not replaced the catalytic converter. When I pluged in the 3130 a \\"PO420 Catalyst system Efficiency below Threshold\\" code popped up.I changed the cat and cleared the code with the 3130 and have not had the problem again. I am very pleased with the code reader with the exception of it will not plug into a USB port on my computer, you have to purchase a seriel to USB adapter for $10.00 which is hard to find in your local Best Buy or Radio Shack. They carry a $39.99 Special Adapter which is over-kill.Thank-you Amazon.Com for providing fast shipping and Reasonable prices on Items I need!!! I have several Honda vehicles and tried this code reader on all of them including a 2007 Civic Si and it works on them all.

product_title: Black Magic 2-In-1 Leather Care
review_headline: not a pro, just a car nut
review_body: i've used lots of products, but for the last 3 years i've been using this stuff consistently and it is the best stuff on the market.  i've always used on lexus's light color leather (2 different vehicles) and this has been the best stuff to keep my leather smooth, clean, and smelling good.  the other reviewer sort of speaks the truth but i know what he is referring to so allow me to re-explain.    when you spray this stuff on if you leave it set for a minute or more it will sort of lighten the leather underneath a little.  in my past experiences using this product it is because the leather is actually dirty or had gotten darker than the original color...  if you spray this stuff on and then just work it in you do not get any spots, you just get super smooth clean good smelling leather.  i am almost always a McGuire's or Mothers product consumer but for some reason this particular Black Magic leather cleaner beats the others in my opinion.  Just don't spray a bunch of it on and walk away to make a phone call without working it in first.  On the flip side if you have any stained spots or darker spots or blemishes on your leather i have found that putting a little extra bit of this product on it and leaving it for a minute or two will actually clean/ lighten the area back to the original leather color.  if your leather seats are showing deep wrinkles and creases this stuff will actually help to restore them a good deal..  i have seen this first hand after a couple cleanings/ massagings of the seats with this product.    my favorite part about this cleaner is that it is not greasy at all, its not dry, just pretty much a perfect middle for my tastes at least.  it kept my 10 year old lex's leather (gs) looking good till the day i sold it and now it is keeping my 3 year old lex's leather (ls) clean hopefully for at least another 7 years.

product_title: Lund 95053 Genesis Tri-Fold Tonneau Cover
review_body: Update: Almost 10 Years and 185,000 miles later it still works great!  The elastic straps that hold the buckle are getting slightly stretched out and a little brittle, I'm not sure how much longer they will hold out.  The tarp is starting to show some small cracks where the hinges are and the seals are pretty much gone.  It might not be completely water tight if I went through a car wash now but it still keeps the rain out.  I'm considering checking out how well Lund would honor the "Limited Lifetime Warranty" for the cover since it's cracking slightly at the hinges. I'm still very satisfied with this purchase.  I take the cover off and put it on several times each month.  All the clamps still work fine and hold it tightly to the truck bed.  A friend bought another brand of the same type cover last year because he liked the functionality of mine.  His is already curling up at the corners and flaps like a flag in the wind.  Update: I have now owned this for right at 5 years and 110,000 miles.  All the stuff I said at first is still true. I have not replaced the seals, although they could use it, but it still doesn't leak.  Even in heavy rain or on the interstate.  Folded forward it takes up about the same amount of room as a toolbox would. I have driven with it flipped forward and latched many times at interstate speeds and while it does lift some, it has always held. When closed, it doesn't flap any more now than when new. (it doesn't really flap much at all)  I have had several people who bought one after seeing and using mine.  I have had it off the truck many times. It folds and stands neatly in the corner of the garage. It's never been off for more than a day or two though.  My 5 year old daughter has gotten on top of it and crawled around a couple of times recently with no effect and she weighs about 45 lbs. I have had multiple items that punched into it pretty hard while I was driving (such as bicycle handlebars)and they did not puncture or damage it either.  I even drove off without latching it one time and it flew up into the air and came almost completely off the truck without damage. So it can stand up to quite a bit of abuse.  I think this thing may just last me another 100,000 miles. I am so glad I didn't spend more on a hard cover that would be much harder to work with.  Original Review: I have had this on my truck for a few months now and have been very satisfied.  The day I got it I installed it in about 15 minutes (from getting the box off the porch to admiring it on the truck). It fits very well, looks nice, and comes with extra seals which I didn't even use.  The next weekend we left on a 600 mile trip and put all our stuff in the bed.  It poured down rain so hard for about an hour that I finally pulled over because of visibility.  When the rain subsided I checked the bed and there was not a drop of water back there!  I have since taken it through a couple of wand pressure washes and haven't seen water in there from that either.  The tarp does slightly flap at highway/interstate speeds but most all soft tops will.  This one isn't bad about it at all.  The tarp is thick and well supported enough that I have sat a few things on top of it for a minute or two (the heaviest being my emergency kit which is about 12" x 18" and weighs about 10 lbs.)  I installed a Bully tailgate lock at the same time to make everything more secure.  I guess if someone really wanted in they'd just cut the top and get in that way, but if you really want maximum security, go for a hard top. I wanted convenience, things to be dry & hidden, and the ability to take it off easily by myself when I need to use the bed for something bigger.  This one is lightweight, can be placed on or taken off in literally about 2 minutes by yourself, and I can drive with it open and only covering 1/3 of the bed.  The only thing that would make me happier is if someone gave it to me for free, but I'll gladly buy one for my next truck too.  Mybrother, after seeing mine, is about to order one for his truck as well.

review_headline: Dyanmat retro fit into a '69 Corvette
review_body: My project was to replace the rear carpeting in my '69 Corvette coupe.  The front carpets were replaced about 5 years ago at which time I used another thermal barrier product which was state of the art.  I can't remember the name of the product but it consisted of a metallic layer bonded to to a plastic air cell layer.  This product work quite well as a heat barrier but was not all that good as a sound barrier.  After purcahsing the new rear carpet set I discovered Dyanamat through friends and after talking to professional car restorer.  I am very pleased with Dynamat as both a sound and heat barrier.  The install in a Corvette was a bit of work as the Dynamat must be cut in to complex shapes to cover the odd contours in the car.  So even though the interior of a Corvette is small the amount of Dyanmat that is required is the same as a larger vehicle. After cutting the complex shapes there is a larger amount of wastage unless you want to cut it up smaller and \\"puzzle\\" it together. Bear in mind that the \\"trunk\\" of Corvette is actually part of the interior.  Over all installing Dyanmat into this type of vehicle is well worthwhile even thought it is not considered a stock restoration.  The results and the benefits are far superior in terms of performance. AS for the cost, it is a not a factor as the cost of the stock sound barrier from a restoration source is the same as the DYnamat.

product_title: Wheelmate Laptop Steering Wheel Desk
review_headline: Danger: This product is not safe.
review_body: While shopping online, I stumbled across the steering wheel desk and instantly purchased the item, thinking it would help keep my things organized on trips between the office and home. Upon the first day of using the steering wheel desk, I could already notice a serious decline in my attention to safety while driving. My first example came when I was in a rush, taking a short lunch, driving to a mcdonalds (I know, I'm so bad) to grab something and eat on the way back. As I had fries and a cheese burger sitting on the steering wheel desk, I thought to myself \\"this is much safer than reaching blindly into the bag for items while driving, now it's all in front of me.  WRONG!  I went to make a left turn and one of my mcnuggets went astray due to the outward force of the turn and became lodged between the desk and the steering wheel where the wheel connects to the air bag.  So instead of a left turn, I continued straight into a gas station at 35mph, which doesn't seem very fast, but when you're hitting the gas pump, it's obviously fast enough to push the thing over and cause gas and oil to spray up from the ground beneath.  And of course, when metal grids against metal, there are sparks, so a fire began as my minivan continued to speed over the pump.    I was stopped when I slammed into a pillar of the station's awning. That corner of the awning came down immediately, smashing my vehicle like a fiery pancake, thrusting glass, flames and metal fury out from inside my minivan of inevitable cremation.     But I wasn't dead...    Something rigid, almost indestructible, kept my the hoof from collapsing in on my head and body full of precious organs I will need for the rest of my life. That's right!!!  The Steering Wheel Desk!  And underneath its saviour-like umbrella of unrelenting passion for my safety lane an opening to for which I could escape to safety.    I would say I owe my life to the Steering Wheel Desk if it hadn't taken my mcnugget into a headlock while I needed todrive. You should avoid this product.

product_title: Blueant F4 Stereo Bluetooth Interphone Motorcycle Kit (Helmet not included)
review_headline: Blueant F4 Stereo Bluetooth Interphone Motorcycle Kit
review_body: Just received two of these and installed them on mine and my wife's helmets, easy install.  This is the third set of headsets I have purchased for my Goldwing.  First I tried the J&M corded model.  Could hardly hear my wife even when the bike was not moving, plus the cords are a pain.  Then I got the first version of the Interphone for Motorcycle (one speaker) much better product, no cords and worked well; however, I am hard of hearing so when riding I could never hear when a phone call came in, if I slowed to a stop I could then have a discussion; yes I know that is the safe way to use the phone but you can't pull off and stop if you never hear the call come in.  Now I have the new version the Interphone F4.  I have not used it on my bike yet because it is too cold to ride; however, when playing my Ipod around the house I have to turn down the volume because it is too loud.  That never happened with either of the others.  There is a problem with these headsets if you use IPHONE or ITOUCH, even though both of my apple devices are bluetooth stereo models they will not work properly.  When you switch from intercom back to music they will not restart -- lots of fussing to make them come back on again.  I contacted interphone and was told Apple does not support the \\"A2DP protocol\\" to make the Apple products work properly you need to add an adapter to them that does support the A2DP protocol.  So... I happened to have such a device that I use in my shop to broadcast my XM radio to my bluetooth headset.  I synced that adapter with my headset then plugged the adapter into the Iphone and \\"bang\\" it works perfectly with the interphone f4.  Bottom line, I am very happy.  Even though I have not tried these on the road yet, I am positive that I will be able to hear much much better than any other previous headset I tried.  Also, note I am hard of hearing so I am not a great judge of sound quality but these speakers put out a lot of sound, both highs and lows.[[ASIN:B0030U4XXM Blueant F4 Stereo Bluetooth Interphone Motorcycle Kit (Helmet not included)]]

product_title: RainX Fix a Windshield Do it Yourself Windshield Repair Kit, for Chips, Cracks, Bulll's-Eyes and Stars
review_headline: Product Works - Good Materials, Good Product Design!
review_body:
I concur with the other reviewers that one should read the instructions well before attempting the repair.

I used the repair kit to repair one 1.5 inch diameter star-burst and two small nick/chips - one of which was in driving view.

I ensured the car was in the shade and cleaned out the crushed glass out of the rock impact area with the included blade. I cleaned the repair area with soap water and a glass cleaner till it was squeaky clean.

I secured the repair assembly, with the 4 (good quality!) suction cups, to the windshield centering the housing over the rock impact area. I screwed in the resin delivery tube into the housing till it's rubber tip was flush with the windshield and centered to the damage area. I then added a few drops of resin (is same consistency as 3-in-1 oil) into the delivery tube and finally inserted the pressure tube which forces the resin into the crack by opening the rubber tip. I let it cure for about 10 minutes after which I placed a drop of resin on the center of the crack and placed the clear plastic sheet on it and put the windshield in direct sunlight - waited another 10 minutes and removed the plastic sheet. I scraped the excess resin with the blade.

I was very happy with the results - the damaged area, filled in with the resin, was see-through, not smoky like I have seen other windshield repairs. The cracks filled to the extent that the crack was accessible. The resin could not repair a \\"fracture\\" as there is no way for the resin to reach in between the fracture. The resin did obliterate the crack lines where it did reach.

The end result is that the star-burst is still there but less visible, both the nicks/chips are reduced significantly (90%+) and I can make them out only because I know where they are. The one in my driving view looks like a small pit instead of a chip. The only thing I am waiting for, this winter, is to see if the resin holds up to the heating/cooling.

It took me about 1 hour to repair all three areas.

The product is designed thoughtfully and is effective. The quality of materials is good. The really great thing about this product is the fact that the resin cleaned off with soap/water and did not harden on the skin. I could clean out the delivery and pressure tubes which means that they can be re-used......there is enough resin/plastic sheets left to repair a few more cracks.

DON'T use more that a few drops of resin...a little goes a long way!

I gave one-less star for false advertising. The company surely knows that fractures in glass cannot be repaired and should not advertise an \\"after\\" photo which shows a windshield with no hint of having been damaged.ooling.

product_title: Hopkins 11838 FloTool 15-Quart Oil Drain
review_headline: Only Decent Choice Out There But Could Be Improved
review_body: This is the only readily available choice for a self-contained pan with capacity for more than one oil change - so I guess it's better than nothing.  Both the little center hole cover and the drain spout cap have inadequate threads to make a decent seal and will either strip or break (as mine did) if you try to snug them up so they won't leak.  How difficult would it be to mold in sufficient threads into the thing so the cap would make a snug fit?   15 quarts might be its rated capacity, but if you put even 10 quarts in it and move it around at all, oil will slosh into the drain spout and start leaking through the cap.  It must be stored in a flat position so it takes up more garage floor space than if stored in a vertical orientation (like my old Sears one that isn't made any more).  On a positive note - the round, open drain pan that Blitz USA makes (purchased separately) fits in an inverted position onto the top of the 15-quart container and makes a perfect dirt/debris cover.  I like it and would/will purchase another - but there is much room for improvement.

product_title: Turtle Wax T376KT Color Cure (Blue) 16Oz
review_body: I used the blue color cure wax with chip stick.  Surprisingly, the chip stick did do the trick on some of the smaller scratches and paint nicks, but some of the larger scratches remained unhidden.  The key to using the chip stick is to use it when your vehicle is hot, such as in the direct sunlight (the opposite of what you should do with the liquid wax).  The chip stick melts into your scratches and with a light buffing blends nicely into the paint surface.  I was a bit disappointed with the wax itself.  The \\"one-color-fits-all\\" is quite misleading.  My vehicle is a dark shade of blue.  The blue wax is a medium shade (at best).  The lighter blue did not match well with my vehicles paint and now I have the small scratches (in which the wax remained) that show up as light blue.  I'm considering an experiment, buying the black color cure wax and mixing the two until the wax color more closely matches my vehicle's color.

product_title: Mr. Clean Starter Kit
review_headline: Buy this product for the filtration system, nothing else
review_body: The AutoDry system is nothing new.  I'm sure all you car enthusiasts already know that deionized water dries without spots.  This system does what it advertises, but you're pretty much paying for the deionized filtration system in fancy packaging.  And don't buy into the \\"Mr Clean AutoDry only works if you use Mr Clean soap\\" bs.  I simply wash the car with Zaino, rinse with unfiltered water, and top it off with Mr Cleans filtration system.  If you decide to get this, simply throw away the supplied soap, visit your nearest pepboys and pick up some quality carwash soap.  Mr. Cleans' system is only useful for its deionized filtration system.

product_title: Jeep Wrangler 3" Budget lift kit, TJ 1997 & newer
review_headline: This has nothing to do with the product...only about the description
review_body: Do not believe for a second that bump stops are not important. If you took off your bump stops or didn't get bigger ones when you got a lift with bigger tires...you are going to get yourself in a lot of trouble. With out the \\"100% unnecessary\\" bump stops (according to the description), as soon as your suspension flexes...your tire is going to bust your fender. Yup, you heard me correctly. The bump stops job is to stop your axel from going up too high during articulation...no bump stops...your axel, along with the tire, keep going up...and the only thing in the way of your tire...is your fender. If you don't believe me ask ANYONE who knows ANYTHING about 4x4s. Don't kid me wrong, the kit seems like an OK deal...just don't forget to buy some bump stops...or you can even make some bump stop extensions with some old hockey pucks and just buy some longer hardware. Oh, one last thing...i promise...I'd think twice about using shock extensions...you might as well just buy new shocks. Have a good day...and keep on Jeepin'!
